0.ways_to_identify: At enrolment, the ownership-change filings (CMS-855S change of information) for dozens of previously dormant DME suppliers show foreign-national nominee owners, shared addresses/phones/bank accounts, notary and corporate-record reuse, and IP/device overlap in the billing portal — all visible before any claim pays. Post-enrolment, each acquired supplier shows an abrupt jump from near-zero to very high claim volume within weeks, beneficiaries scattered nationwide with no geographic relation to the supplier, beneficiaries whose identities appear simultaneously at many unrelated suppliers, and no matching ordering-physician encounter history. Supplemental-insurer exposure is detectable by cross-plan matching of the same beneficiary/HICN-item combinations paying under crossover logic.
0.features_to_create: Build an enrolment graph keyed on supplier TIN/NPI linking owners, authorized officials, addresses, phones, bank routing/account, EFT forms, notaries, portal IP and device fingerprints; fire a pre-payment payment-suspension and site-visit review when a control-change event coincides with graph clustering across multiple suppliers or foreign-nominee indicators. Add a new-owner velocity edit: for any supplier within a defined window of an ownership change, hold claims for prepay review when weekly billed dollars or unique-beneficiary count exceed the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers, when beneficiary residence is outside the supplier's normal service radius, or when no corresponding ordering-provider encounter exists in claims history. Feed crossover files to supplemental insurers so the same suspension propagates, and run an identity-abuse detector flagging beneficiaries billed by an unusual number of unrelated DME suppliers in a short period.

1.ways_to_identify: This is an annual round-up press release, not a single case: no defendant, amount, service line or conduct period is identified, so no case-specific pre-payment signal can be reconstructed. The nearest payer-side route is the generic portfolio surveillance that the underlying cases would each have triggered (billing-volume outliers, kickback-linked referral concentration, and drug-diversion/pedigree gaps).
1.features_to_create: Maintain a standing provider-level outlier engine (billed dollars, service mix, beneficiary sharing, referral concentration versus same-specialty peers) with auto-escalation to prepay review, plus a pharmaceutical pedigree/supply-chain check that compares dispensed NDC volume against wholesaler acquisition records. No case-specific control can be designed from this release.

2.ways_to_identify: This is public-corruption, extortion and grant-embezzlement conduct against a municipality and its violence-reduction grant program; there is no health care claim and no payer adjudication point, so no prepay claims control applies. The detectable route is grant-side: nonprofit subrecipients whose expense reports include payments to intermediaries or entities tied to the awarding officials, and vendor/official relationship conflicts disclosed (or not) at award.
2.features_to_create: For grant and contract programs, build an award-time conflict screen matching subrecipient officers, addresses and bank accounts against elected officials, their relatives and their affiliated entities, and hold disbursement pending review on a match. Add a drawdown analytic flagging subrecipient payments to pass-through individuals or newly formed intermediaries with no service deliverable; no payer claims edit applies.

3.ways_to_identify: This is street-level diversion and distribution of oxycodone obtained from physician offices, prosecuted criminally; there is no billed claim by the defendant, so it is not catchable at adjudication of his claims. The payer-adjacent signal sits with the source practices: controlled-substance inventory/dispensing records that do not reconcile with acquisition, and PDMP patterns showing individuals collecting oxycodone across multiple prescribers with cash payment and early refills.
3.features_to_create: Build a PDMP/pharmacy analytic at the beneficiary level computing distinct prescribers and pharmacies for schedule II opioids, cash-pay share and days-supply overlap, firing a review referral and prior-authorization lock-in above the calibrated percentile. For practices, reconcile DEA-222/wholesaler acquisition against documented administrations and dispensings and open an inventory audit on unexplained shortfall; no prepay claim edit reaches the street sales themselves.

4.ways_to_identify: Day Habilitation billing is unit-based against OPWDD-required service documentation and staffing ratios, so the payer can compare billed units per participant per day against the provider's staff schedules, attendance records and habilitation-plan-authorized units before paying. The failure-to-return element is visible when the provider's own internal review findings, self-disclosure log and 60-day-report activity show no corresponding adjustment or voided claims after an identified overpayment. Retention is otherwise a post-payment finding reachable via credit-balance/self-audit review.
4.features_to_create: Prepay edit at the participant-day level: deny or pend Day Hab units exceeding plan-authorized units, exceeding attendance-record days, or implying staff-to-participant ratios inconsistent with submitted staffing rosters, with a documentation request for service notes on pend. Add a provider-level reconciliation job that compares certified self-audit/internal-review findings and CIA reportable-event submissions to actual voided/adjusted claims and refunds, firing an overpayment-recovery and enrolment-condition flag when identified dollars are not returned within the statutory window.

5.ways_to_identify: Single-use device reuse shows up as a mismatch between procedure volume and the practice's purchase records for the disposable device — the payer can require and audit invoice/serial-number support against the number of procedures billed. Medical necessity is testable at adjudication from diagnosis support, prior-visit indication documentation and abnormally high per-patient procedure frequency for the same gynecologic procedure versus same-specialty peers. Infection-control and reprocessing violations typically surface post-payment via survey/complaint data, which should trigger retrospective claim review.
5.features_to_create: Build a supply-reconciliation check: for procedures dependent on a billed or bundled single-use device, compare procedure counts per NPI per period against distributor purchase volume obtained via documentation request, and pend claims when procedures exceed devices purchased. Add a prepay frequency/necessity edit at the patient level for repeat gynecologic procedures without qualifying diagnosis or interval documentation, and an automatic prepay-review flag when licensure, survey or infection-control adverse findings post to the provider record.

6.ways_to_identify: Time-based psychotherapy codes let the payer reconstruct each rendering clinician's day: summing billed session minutes per NPI per date produces impossible workdays, and the missing AM/PM convention leaves multiple 45-minute sessions colliding in the same hour. Copy-forward notes are detectable by textual near-duplication across a patient's sequential visits once records are requested, and appointment/EHR timestamps or facility sign-in logs contradict the billed durations.
6.features_to_create: Prepay edit computing, per rendering NPI per service date, total billed time-based units and detecting overlapping session time windows; deny or pend claims when summed minutes exceed a plausible workday or when time windows overlap. Add a documentation-request trigger and note-similarity analytic (hashing/near-duplicate scoring of progress notes across a patient's visits and across patients on the same date) with downcoding to the shorter-duration code or payment suspension where duplication and duration collisions co-occur.

7.ways_to_identify: Billed nursing time units per licensed nurse per date can be summed across all patients and compared to payroll/timesheet hours, which the provider must retain; totals exceeding hours worked or exceeding a feasible shift are visible before payment. Overlapping units for the same nurse across different group-home residents at the same clock time is a second adjudication-time signal, as is billing skilled nursing on dates a licensed nurse was not scheduled.
7.features_to_create: Prepay edit at rendering-nurse-per-date level: aggregate all time units billed across residents, flag totals above a feasible shift ceiling or with overlapping time windows, and pend with a request for timesheets/payroll and shift schedules. Add a periodic reconciliation comparing billed nursing hours to submitted payroll hours per facility and per licensed staff, generating overpayment recovery and prepay review when billed hours exceed paid hours.

8.ways_to_identify: The FDA-clearance element is checkable at coding/coverage setup: a payer can validate that every implant or instrument catalog number billed maps to an active 510(k)/PMA record and refuse coverage for uncleared codes. Device failure signals are visible in claims as an elevated short-interval revision/removal rate for the specific implant identified by UDI/device identifier on the hospital claim, and the kickback element is visible by matching Open Payments consulting/travel/entertainment transfers from the manufacturer to the volume of that implant used by the surgeon.
8.features_to_create: Build a device-identifier gate: require UDI/catalog number on implant and high-cost instrument claims, validate it against FDA clearance and GUDID at adjudication, and deny when no active clearance exists. Add a device-outlier surveillance job computing revision-within-interval rates per device identifier versus comparable implants, triggering coverage review and post-payment recovery; and an Open Payments-linked analytic flagging surgeons whose use share of one manufacturer's implant exceeds the calibrated percentile while receiving above-peer transfers, routing to prepay review.

9.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic as the companion matter: uncleared devices can be caught at adjudication by validating the billed device identifier against FDA clearance records, and premature-failure risk is observable in claims as an above-expected revision or removal rate within a short interval for one implant's UDI. The kickback inducement is observable by joining Open Payments consulting fees, travel and entertainment from the manufacturer to the surgeon's implant-selection share and case volume.
9.features_to_create: Require and validate UDI/catalog identifiers on implant claims against GUDID/FDA clearance status, denying claims for devices with no active clearance and pending those with mismatched identifiers. Run device-level revision-rate surveillance (revisions per implant-year by device identifier versus peer implants) that opens coverage reconsideration and recovery, and an Open Payments-to-utilization correlation flag on surgeons for prepay review and a documentation request on medical necessity.

10.ways_to_identify: Standing/automatic orders show up as near-identical ordering patterns: the same test billed for a very high share of a referrer's eligible patients, in tight batches, often without the diagnosis staging or treatment-decision context that makes a genomic assay reasonable and necessary. Referral concentration to one lab plus Open Payments honoraria, meals and gift-card style transfers from that lab to the ordering practices is visible at claim time by joining lab claims to transfer-of-value data. Signed-order documentation requests reveal pre-populated forms lacking individualized clinical rationale.
10.features_to_create: Prepay edit for genomic/prognostic assays: require a qualifying diagnosis plus documented treatment-decision indication, and pend claims where the ordering NPI's share of patients receiving the same assay, or the batch-ordering pattern of same-day identical orders, exceeds the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers. Add a referral-integrity flag joining lab-to-referrer Open Payments/marketing-payment data with referral concentration, triggering payment suspension and a request for the signed order and clinical notes.

11.ways_to_identify: This is estate/bank fraud exploiting an incapacitated elderly person; no health care claim was submitted and no payer adjudicated anything, so there is no prepay claims control. If the victim was a plan member, the adjacent signal is a recent claims/encounter history documenting cognitive impairment diagnoses that contradicts a contemporaneous competent legal execution, and abrupt changes to a member's authorized representative or payee.
11.features_to_create: For payers that hold representative-payee or authorized-representative records, flag changes of representative, address or beneficiary designation for members with recent dementia/cognitive-impairment diagnosis codes and route to an SIU/adult-protective referral before honoring the change. Otherwise no payer-side claims edit applies; the control belongs to the bank's elder-financial-exploitation monitoring.

12.ways_to_identify: Same conduct as the companion entry at the sentencing stage: an estate/bank fraud with no health care billing and no payer adjudication point, so no prepay claim edit exists. The only payer-adjacent signal is a member with documented cognitive impairment in claims history whose representative, address or designation changes abruptly in favor of an unrelated third party.
12.features_to_create: Implement a member-level elder-exploitation flag combining recent cognitive-impairment diagnoses with changes to authorized representative, mailing address or payee, holding the change for SIU and adult-protective-services review. No claims-payment control otherwise applies to this case.

13.ways_to_identify: The ordering physician has no prior or contemporaneous evaluation claim for the beneficiaries whose DME and genetic tests he ordered, and his orders span states far outside his practice location, arriving in high-volume batches — all checkable against claims history and geography at adjudication. A single NPI ordering for far more distinct beneficiaries than same-specialty peers, concentrated to a handful of DME suppliers and labs, is the core signal, as is an ordering rate that implies more encounters than a workday allows.
13.features_to_create: Prepay edit on DME and hereditary-cancer panel claims requiring a payable evaluation encounter by the ordering NPI with the same beneficiary within a defined lookback; deny or pend and request the order plus the encounter note when absent. Add an ordering-NPI velocity/geography model (distinct beneficiaries per day, beneficiary-state dispersion versus the physician's licensure and practice ZIP, concentration to few supplier/lab TINs) that fires payment suspension for downstream suppliers and labs above the calibrated percentile.

14.ways_to_identify: Identical mechanic: orders signed with no examination, so no evaluation claim from the ordering NPI exists for those beneficiaries, and beneficiary residence is dispersed nationally rather than clustered near the physician. Batch signing produces implausible orders-per-day counts and extreme concentration of one physician's orders into a small set of DME supplier and lab TINs, all visible pre-payment from claim linkage fields.
14.features_to_create: Require a documented, payable encounter between the ordering NPI and beneficiary within a lookback window for braces/orthoses and genetic panels; otherwise deny or pend with a documentation request for the order and clinical note. Build an ordering-physician surveillance job scoring daily distinct-beneficiary order volume, out-of-state beneficiary share and supplier/lab concentration, and auto-suspend payments to the linked suppliers and labs when scores exceed the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers.

15.ways_to_identify: This is SBA pandemic loan fraud with no health care claim, so no payer adjudication control applies; detection belongs at loan underwriting. Pre-disbursement signals were available: employee counts and payroll on the application could have been verified against IRS transcript data for the certified-as-filed 941s/Schedule C, and multiple entities sharing owners, addresses, bank accounts and applicant IP would have clustered into a single applicant ring.
15.features_to_create: At underwriting, require IRS transcript verification of the payroll figures and filing status before disbursement, auto-declining or holding where the application payroll exceeds transcript wages. Add an applicant-graph check clustering applications by owner SSN/EIN, address, bank account and submission IP, holding all related applications when one entity in the cluster fails verification; no payer claims edit applies.

16.ways_to_identify: Non-dispensing is detectable by reconciling billed NDC quantities against the pharmacy's wholesaler acquisition records — a pharmacy cannot dispense more units of Latuda, Humira or Invega Sustenna than it purchased, and this invoice-versus-claims ratio can be demanded before or shortly after payment. Additional prepay signals: high-cost specialty drug claims for beneficiaries with no supporting prescriber encounter or diagnosis history, refills without corresponding prescriber activity, and beneficiaries residing far from the pharmacy.
16.features_to_create: Build an invoice-reconciliation control at pharmacy-NDC-period level comparing billed units to wholesaler/ARCOS-style purchase data, firing prepay suspension and an invoice documentation request when billed units exceed purchases beyond tolerance. Add prepay edits requiring an active prescriber encounter and consistent diagnosis history for high-cost specialty NDCs, plus refill-pattern checks (refills too regular, no beneficiary cost-share collection, beneficiary-to-pharmacy distance) routing outliers to review.

17.ways_to_identify: BLS non-emergency transports are only payable when the beneficiary's condition contraindicates other transport, so the payer can test each claim against the beneficiary's concurrent claims history — ambulatory status, absence of a facility admission or dialysis/outpatient service at the destination on that date, and no supporting condition codes or physician certification statement. Phantom trips show up as transports with no matching destination-facility claim on the same date, implausible trips-per-vehicle-per-day, and repetitive origin/destination and mileage patterns.
17.features_to_create: Prepay edit for non-emergency BLS: require a valid physician certification statement and a same-date destination service claim, and deny or pend when the beneficiary's history shows ambulatory status or no qualifying condition. Add a supplier-level analytic on trips per vehicle/crew per day, repeat-transport counts per beneficiary versus peers, and destination-claim match rate, triggering prepay review and a documentation request for run sheets.

18.ways_to_identify: For the signed-order scheme, the ordering NPI has no encounter with the beneficiaries, and the claims themselves contain disqualifying facts the payer already holds: date of death preceding the order, and amputation/limb-absence history contradicting a brace for that limb. For the unbundling matter, panel component CPTs billed individually for the same beneficiary and date sum to more than the panel code, and respiratory/UTI panel use far above same-specialty peers with routine rather than indication-driven ordering is visible at adjudication.
18.features_to_create: Prepay edits: deny orders/services with a service date after the beneficiary's date of death; deny limb-specific orthotics where history shows amputation or absent limb; and require an evaluation encounter by the ordering NPI within a lookback for braces and genetic panels, with per-order payment suspension of the billing supplier/lab above the calibrated ordering-velocity percentile. Add a component-to-panel rebundling edit that aggregates same-day same-beneficiary component tests into the panel code and pays the panel rate, plus a medical-necessity edit requiring a qualifying diagnosis and documented indication for multiplex PCR panels.

19.ways_to_identify: Kickback-driven ID lending shows as concentrated clusters of plan members from one employer and worksite all treating at the same small set of providers, with high visit counts, no cost-share collection, and services (acupuncture, podiatry) billed on dates the member was on shift or geographically elsewhere per timekeeping data the plan sponsor holds. Members whose dependents also suddenly appear at the same providers, and providers whose patient panel is almost entirely one employer's members, are visible pre-payment from claims.
19.features_to_create: Build a provider-panel concentration analytic per provider TIN computing share of claims from a single employer group and referral-recruiter clustering of member IDs, firing prepay review and payment suspension above the calibrated percentile. Add a member-level utilization edit (visits per member per period for acupuncture/podiatry versus peers, no copay collected, service dates conflicting with employer timekeeping/shift data) that triggers verification-of-services letters to members and a documentation request for treatment notes before payment.

20.ways_to_identify: The tell is a single member ID appearing on high-frequency claims from a small cluster of unrelated providers (acupuncture, podiatry) with implausible visit cadence and no referral or diagnosis continuity, plus the member's own employer-plan enrollment showing he lives/works far from the billing addresses. At adjudication the payer can see repeated same-code visits, no supporting E/M or imaging trail, and the same handful of member IDs recurring across the same provider group - a hallmark of member-recruiter kickback rings. Member-verification letters or EOB attestations ('did you receive this service?') would have surfaced the phantom encounters before payment.
20.features_to_create: Build a member-provider concentration model: per member per rolling period, count distinct visits and providers and flag members in the top calibrated percentile of visit frequency for modality codes (acupuncture, chiro, podiatry routine foot care); simultaneously build a provider-side check for share of revenue concentrated in a few member IDs from one employer group. Firing combinations route the provider's claims to prepay review with mandatory records and trigger automated member verification letters; sustained non-response suspends payment.

21.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic as the companion case: employees selling their member IDs produce clusters of members from one employer, all billed repeatedly by the same acupuncturist/podiatrist with impossible service frequency and no clinical progression. A payer can detect it prepay from member-level visit-density outliers within a single employer group and from provider panels whose members are overwhelmingly drawn from one employer, plus geographic mismatch between member residence and clinic. Member verification mailings and interviews confirm services never rendered before further payment.
21.features_to_create: Implement an employer-group/provider affinity edit: for each provider, compute the share of claims from a single employer group and the distinct-member count, and flag providers where a small number of members from one group drive the top calibrated percentile of paid dollars. Pair with per-member visit-frequency caps for modality codes that trigger prepay documentation requests and automated 'services received?' verification; failed verification triggers payment suspension and SIU referral.

22.ways_to_identify: The decisive signal is a drug-purchase-versus-units-billed reconciliation: billed J-code units for infused/injected biologics vastly exceeded documented acquisition from wholesalers/specialty distributors (4,829 vs 369 units), which payers can test using 340B/wholesaler invoice requests or supplier data at credentialing and audit. Prepay, the practice also showed level-4/5 E/M concentration and per-patient drug unit volumes above same-specialty rheumatology peers, and drug-administration codes without matching visit documentation. Invoice-to-claim reconciliation is normally a post-payment/audit route, but high J-code volume can trigger it prospectively.
22.features_to_create: Build a buy-and-bill reconciliation control: per provider per drug NDC/J-code per period, compare billed units against invoice/acquisition units obtained via a mandatory documentation request for practices whose billed units exceed the calibrated peer percentile; a shortfall places the provider on prepay review for all J-codes. Add an E/M distribution edit flagging upcoded level concentration versus same-specialty peers and an edit requiring administration-code/visit-note pairing.

23.ways_to_identify: This is a Stark/AKS financial-relationship problem visible at enrolment and credentialing: the lab's contracts with contracted pain practices tied 'productivity' bonuses to referred lab revenue, which a payer can detect by requesting compensation methodology in provider agreements and by comparing each referring practice's lab-referral volume to its own bonus/ownership disclosures. Prepay, the referral pattern shows near-100% of a practice's toxicology/lab referrals routed to one lab with volume far above same-specialty peers. Full proof of the compensation formula usually requires audit or self-disclosure, so this is a hybrid prepay-signal/post-pay-audit control.
23.features_to_create: At enrolment, capture structured disclosure of physician compensation arrangements and lab ownership/referral relationships; auto-flag any arrangement where compensation varies with volume or value of referrals for legal review before claims are paid. Add a referral-concentration monitor: per referring NPI, compute share of lab/toxicology referrals to a single TIN and referrals-per-patient versus peers, and place outlier lab claims on prepay medical-necessity and relationship review.

24.ways_to_identify: Impossible-day arithmetic is directly computable at adjudication: sum the time-based psychotherapy and E/M service minutes billed under one rendering NPI per date and flag days exceeding plausible working hours. Cross-checks catch the rest - claims dated while the physician was abroad (compare to travel/absence, or simply to zero-activity gaps), service dates overlapping inpatient stays for the same member, dates after the member's date of death, and E/M plus psychotherapy add-on billed where only medication management occurred. Rendering-provider licensure files also expose services actually delivered by unlicensed staff.
24.features_to_create: Build a per-rendering-NPI per-date time accumulator across all time-based codes that denies or pends claims once billed minutes exceed a calibrated daily maximum, and an eligibility-conflict edit denying professional visit claims dated after date of death or during an inpatient facility stay for the same member. Add a code-pair edit requiring documented separate psychotherapy time when psychotherapy is billed with E/M, and a credentialing edit blocking payment when the rendering NPI lacks an active license for the billed service.

25.ways_to_identify: There is no claims-payment component: this is fiduciary theft from an ERISA master trust by a third-party benefits administrator, not provider billing. Detection sits with plan sponsors, carriers and the fiduciary controls over the trust account: reconcile client remittances received against premiums actually forwarded to carriers and 401(k) recordkeepers, and monitor withdrawals exceeding the contractual per-employee-per-month administrative fee. Carrier-side premium delinquency/lapse notices and unremitted 401(k) contribution reports are the earliest external signals.
25.features_to_create: For payer/carrier operations, build a premium-remittance reconciliation monitor per plan sponsor comparing expected premium (enrolled lives x rate) against funds received from the TPA, firing on shortfalls or late remittances and auto-notifying the sponsor and DOL-referral queue. In TPA vendor oversight, require monthly trust-account attestations and compute administrative withdrawals versus contractual fee x covered lives, suspending TPA authority to disburse when the variance exceeds the contract.

26.ways_to_identify: No payer claim adjudication is involved - this is embezzlement of tribal healthcare funds through sham vendor contracts, so the controls are grantee/vendor financial oversight rather than prepay claim edits. The observable signals are a new vendor receiving an outsized share of an entity's disbursements, contracts for 'employee referrals' with no deliverables, common addresses/officers between the vendor and an executive-controlled shell, and executive-related-party disclosures omitted from conflict-of-interest filings. Follow-the-money review of vendor payments versus documented services is the post-payment route.
26.features_to_create: Build a vendor-integrity screen for funded entities: match vendor TINs, addresses, incorporation officers and bank accounts against officer/board related-party registries and flag any vendor whose payments exceed a calibrated share of total disbursements or lacks itemized deliverables. Fire a funds-hold and mandatory independent audit for contracts with no measurable output (referrals delivered, encounters produced) before further draws are released.

27.ways_to_identify: The claims picture screams before payment: billed amniotic/skin-substitute graft units per patient and per applicator size at the top of the national distribution, near-exclusive use of the largest-size product from one distributor, application to hospice-enrolled and homebound elderly patients, and grafts billed without wound-measurement documentation or any prior conservative-care trail. Payer data also shows an ordering-clinician cohort of NPs whose graft volume vastly exceeds same-specialty peers and orders originating from non-clinical sales-rep referral patterns. Concurrent enrollment in hospice for wound-related care is a direct eligibility conflict checkable at adjudication.
27.features_to_create: Build a prepay edit on skin-substitute HCPCS codes requiring prior authorization with wound measurements, photographs, and documented conservative care; auto-deny sq-cm units exceeding documented wound area and deny applications for members with an active hospice election for a related terminal condition. Add a provider/product-concentration monitor (units per patient, single-distributor share, per-NPI graft dollars versus peers) that triggers payment suspension and referral when multiple flags coincide.

28.ways_to_identify: This was a cash, off-claims consumer scheme - no insurer paid claims - so payer prepay controls largely do not apply; the detection route is licensure/credential verification and consumer/FDA complaint monitoring plus advertising surveillance for cancer-cure claims. If any such operation ever enrolls, the credentialing screen catches a nonexistent Karolinska Ph.D. via primary-source degree verification and an unregistered 'smart chip' ultrasound device with no FDA clearance. Post hoc, cash-only pricing, membership/confidentiality agreements and absent medical records are the audit signals.
28.features_to_create: Enforce primary-source verification of every claimed degree, license and board certification at enrolment and re-credentialing, auto-rejecting unverifiable foreign institutions, and screen billed diagnostic devices against FDA clearance/registration data with denial of claims for unlisted device technologies. Add a marketing-surveillance feed that flags enrolled or applicant entities advertising cure claims or unapproved therapies for credentialing hold and state-board referral.

29.ways_to_identify: This is benefit eligibility fraud against VA/SSA with derivative Medicare entitlement rather than provider billing, so the control belongs at eligibility determination: verify claimed decorations (Purple Heart) against DoD service records and verify submitted medical documents directly with the issuing clinician rather than accepting claimant-supplied copies. Cross-agency data matching would show the claimed total inability to work against IRS/SSA wage and self-employment earnings records. Continuing-eligibility reviews with earnings matches are the post-award route to stop ongoing payment.
29.features_to_create: Build an automated document-authentication and records-match step in disability adjudication: hash/verify claimant-submitted provider letters against primary-source clinician confirmation and validate decoration/service claims against DoD personnel data, holding award until both clear. Add a recurring earnings-versus-disability match (SSA/IRS wage and 1099 data) that suspends benefits and derivative Medicare entitlement pending review when reported activity contradicts the certified limitation.

30.ways_to_identify: One ordering NPI generating orders for DME braces, topical compounded creams and hereditary cancer panels across many states and many unrelated suppliers, with no prior or subsequent office visit for those members, is directly observable at adjudication. Telehealth claims are absent or reduced to a single brief code, the beneficiary-to-ordering-physician distance is large, and the same NPI's order volume sits far above same-specialty peers. Supplier-side concentration on a single ordering physician confirms the telemarketing pattern before payment.
30.features_to_create: Build an ordering-physician surveillance model: per ordering NPI per month, compute distinct beneficiaries, distinct supplier TINs, states covered, share of orders lacking any evaluative encounter with that NPI within a lookback window, and rank against same-specialty peers; outliers trigger prepay review of all downstream DME/genetic/compound claims. Add a hard prepay edit denying DME, cancer genetic panels and compounded creams when no qualifying face-to-face or telehealth encounter with the ordering provider exists, and suspend suppliers whose orders concentrate on flagged NPIs.

31.ways_to_identify: No claims payment is involved - this is a grant-integrity/False Claims Act matter about non-disclosure of research misconduct allegations in NIH applications and progress reports. The detectable signal is institutional certification of research integrity in eRA submissions contradicted by pending misconduct allegations, image-duplication detected by forensic screening of figures in cited publications, and journal expressions of concern or retraction notices tied to key personnel. Whistleblower/qui tam and ORI referral are the realistic routes.
31.features_to_create: For grant-making payers, build an automated pre-award integrity screen: match key personnel and cited publications against retraction/expression-of-concern databases, PubPeer-style image-integrity flags and ORI/institutional misconduct disclosures, and hold award or continuation funding pending certification review when hits occur. Require an affirmative, machine-checked disclosure attestation each progress report, with funds suspension for undisclosed pending allegations.

32.ways_to_identify: Not a fraud case - this is a press release announcing a U.S. Attorney appointment, with no claims, payer, provider or loss. There is nothing for a payer to detect and no billing pattern to model.
32.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies; exclude such announcements from case-derived rule mining so they do not pollute training or rule inventories.

33.ways_to_identify: Two checkable signals: the facility's cash/self-pay price for the same COVID test CPT (published under price-transparency and cash-price posting rules) was lower than what it billed the federal plan, and its E/M level distribution for drive-through screening encounters was concentrated at high levels inconsistent with a swab-only encounter with no exam or MDM. Both are computable at adjudication from the claim plus the provider's posted cash price file.
33.features_to_create: Build a cash-price parity edit: ingest each facility's posted self-pay/cash price file, compare the billed/allowed amount per COVID test CPT, and pend or reprice claims where the plan is charged above the posted cash price. Add a site-of-service E/M edit that denies or downcodes level-3+ E/M billed with COVID specimen-collection codes at drive-through/mobile places of service unless records documenting exam and medical decision-making are supplied on request.

34.ways_to_identify: Same-date presumptive plus definitive urine drug testing billed reflexively for essentially every patient is visible at adjudication as a code-pair pattern with near-100% concurrency and no documentation that presumptive results were reviewed. The VA billing shows analyte-by-analyte CPT 803XX unbundling instead of the appropriate definitive panel code, detectable as an abnormally high number of drug-class line items per specimen versus peers.
34.features_to_create: Build a reflex-testing edit: per patient-date, deny definitive drug-test codes billed with presumptive codes unless a documented review of presumptive results and patient-specific medical necessity is supplied, and monitor per-ordering-NPI concurrency rate against same-specialty peers for prepay review. Add an unbundling edit that aggregates 803XX analyte lines per specimen and reprices to the appropriate definitive panel code when the analyte count exceeds the panel definition.

35.ways_to_identify: The core signal is licensure verification: the license numbers she used belonged to other people, so an automated primary-source match of name, date of birth and license number against Maryland and Florida nursing boards (and Nursys) fails immediately, as would degree verification with Florida State. Payers and facilities can also detect one license number active concurrently at many unrelated employers and staffing-agency placements, and the pharmacy side shows a controlled-substance fax whose prescriber signature and DEA/NPI do not match the prescriber of record.
35.features_to_create: Require automated primary-source license verification (Nursys/state board API matching name+DOB+license number+image) at hire, at staffing-agency placement and at each payer credentialing/revalidation, blocking claims that list an unverified caregiver and firing an alert when one license number appears at multiple concurrent employers. On the pharmacy side, build a prescriber-authentication edit that pends faxed controlled-substance prescriptions where prescriber identifiers, DEA registration or signature template do not match the on-file prescriber, with callback verification required.

36.ways_to_identify: Identical mechanic to the companion case: stolen nursing license numbers and duplicated license images pass only because verification is document-based rather than primary-source. Automated Nursys/state-board matching on name, DOB and license number, plus image-duplication detection across submitted credential files, catches it at hire and at credentialing; concurrent employment of one license number across ~40 facilities is another computable flag. Facility Medicare/Medicaid claims for services by an unlicensed staffer are then blockable before payment.
36.features_to_create: Build a credential-integrity service: primary-source license verification with identity match, perceptual-hash comparison of uploaded license images against previously submitted images to detect reuse, and a cross-employer concurrency monitor that suspends a caregiver record when one license appears at implausibly many simultaneous employers. Tie facility claim payment to an all-staff verified-license roster, pending claims naming unverified staff, and add prescriber-signature authentication for faxed controlled-substance orders.

37.ways_to_identify: The document describes witness murder-for-hire arising from an unrelated indictment and gives no billing, payer, provider type or loss detail, so there is no claims-payment mechanic to detect prepay. The only payer-relevant hook is that a provider under indictment for health care fraud should already be on payment suspension.
37.features_to_create: Build an automated adverse-action feed (indictments, arrests, exclusion and state-board actions matched to enrolled NPIs/TINs) that triggers credible-allegation-of-fraud payment suspension and prepay review of all pending claims for the affected provider and its affiliated TINs.

38.ways_to_identify: A fabricated medical degree and residency match letter fail primary-source verification against the medical school, ECFMG/NRMP and the state medical board, and the impostor held no physician NPI or DEA registration of his own - so pharmacy claims carrying his prescriptions would show prescriber identifiers that do not validate or that belong to other physicians. Signals at adjudication include prescriptions where the prescribing NPI/DEA does not match the name on the script, self-prescribing (prescriber and member are the same person), and one prescriber identifier used from geographically inconsistent origination points.
38.features_to_create: Build a prescriber-validation prepay edit for pharmacy claims: reject or pend when the prescriber NPI/DEA is inactive, mismatched to the prescriber name, not licensed for the drug class, or identical to the patient (self-prescribing), with callback verification for faxed controlled substances. At facility/ambulance privileging and payer credentialing, require automated primary-source verification of degree, residency match and board licensure before any privileges or claim payment tied to that clinician.

39.ways_to_identify: This is a pure code-eligibility error checkable on the claim face: Q3014 originating-site facility fee is payable only when the patient is at an eligible facility, so any Q3014 line paired with a home place of service (POS 10, or a professional telehealth claim indicating patient home) is unpayable. The payer also sees the same practice appending Q3014 to essentially all telehealth claims, a distributional outlier versus peers.
39.features_to_create: Implement a hard prepay edit denying HCPCS Q3014 when the associated telehealth encounter's place of service or patient-location modifier indicates the patient's home, or when no eligible originating-site facility NPI is present on the claim. Add a provider-level monitor of Q3014-to-telehealth-claim ratio against peers to trigger recovery review and a compliance-certification/documentation request for outliers.

40.ways_to_identify: Prepay profiling of the practice's psychotherapy code mix would show a distribution skewed to the longest-duration codes (e.g. 90837/60-minute and high-level E/M) versus same-specialty peers, plus implausible daily service-minute totals per rendering NPI once billed units are summed against a workday. Cross-checking the rendering NPI on the claim against state licensure/supervision files would also reveal therapy billed under credentials of staff not qualified to deliver it, and time-in-day overlaps for the same clinician.
40.features_to_create: Build a rendering-provider/day feature that sums implied service minutes from all timed psychotherapy and E/M codes and fires a prepay edit when the total exceeds a feasible clinical day; add a provider-month code-mix outlier score for share of highest-duration psychotherapy codes versus same-specialty peers, above the calibrated percentile, routing to prepay medical-record request for session notes with start/stop times. Add a credentialing cross-edit rejecting timed psychotherapy where the rendering NPI lacks an active licence/supervision link on file.

41.ways_to_identify: At authorisation time, the certifying physician's signature and NPI can be validated against the physician's own claim history - a certifier who has no evaluation/office-visit claim for that beneficiary in the lookback window, or who suddenly certifies for many unrelated agencies, is a forged-certification signal. Beneficiary absence from the country is visible by matching member IDs against travel/immigration or by the total absence of any other in-country claim activity during the service span, and by referral concentration linking one referrer to a handful of agencies.
41.features_to_create: Build a certification-integrity edit: for each home care authorisation, require a paid face-to-face encounter claim from the certifying NPI within the lookback period and flag certifier-agency pairs whose referral volume is concentrated above the calibrated percentile; suspect certifiers get signature-verification and documentation requests before authorisation. Add a beneficiary-activity check that suspends payment when home care is billed for a member with no other in-state claim or encounter footprint during the service window, and hold enrolment of members whose PII was submitted without a verifiable contact/consent record.

42.ways_to_identify: This is a federal loan (PPP) affiliation/size certification case, not a claims-payment scheme, so no payer adjudication control applies. The detectable signal sits at loan underwriting and forgiveness review: the applicant's corporate parentage and worldwide employee count are visible from Dun & Bradstreet/ownership registries, foreign parent filings, and payroll tax filings for affiliates, none of which were reconciled against the 300-employee certification.
42.features_to_create: Nearest applicable control is an ownership/affiliation screen in the enrolment or funding pipeline: resolve applicant EIN to its ultimate parent via corporate-registry and ownership-graph data, aggregate employee counts across all affiliates including foreign entities, and block forgiveness/payment pending manual size review when the aggregated count exceeds the programme cap. The same ownership-graph resolution should be reused for payer provider enrolment to detect undisclosed common control.

43.ways_to_identify: The signal is a lab whose share of CBC-with-differential (85025) versus CBC-without (85027) is far above same-specialty peer labs, and, more decisively, a mismatch between the ordering provider's requisition/order data and the code billed. Payers can compare the lab's billed panel code against the order captured in the electronic requisition or the ordering physician's own diagnosis/order pattern for that member and date.
43.features_to_create: Build a lab-NPI monthly ratio feature (differential vs non-differential CBC, and analogous upgraded-panel pairs) scored against peer labs, firing a documentation request for the signed requisitions when above the calibrated percentile. Add a claim-level prepay edit that denies or pends the higher-paying panel variant when the linked electronic order or requisition on file specifies the lower-level test, and sample-audit labs with no retrievable order record.

44.ways_to_identify: At enrolment, the nominee-owner pattern is visible by matching the applicant's addresses, phone numbers, bank routing/account details, prior enrolment records and business filings against those of excluded or previously revoked individuals - here the barred principal's identifiers would tie to the lab's address, equipment lease or payment account. A nominal owner with no relevant licence, no industry history, and a modest fixed monthly income stream also shows up as an ownership record inconsistent with the operational footprint.
44.features_to_create: Build an enrolment ownership-graph screen that resolves every listed owner, authorised official, address, phone, EFT bank account and managing employee against exclusion/revocation lists and against identifiers of previously revoked entities, and auto-suspends payment pending on-site verification when any link is found. Add a post-enrolment monitor that flags EFT accounts receiving payments where the signatory or transfer beneficiary differs from the enrolled owner, and re-verify ownership when reassignment or ownership change is filed shortly after a related party's suspension.

45.ways_to_identify: At point of sale, PDMP and pharmacy claim data show a member filling repeated high-MME oxycodone quantities with early refills, cash or single-prescriber sourcing, and no supporting pain-diagnosis or procedure history - the classic diversion profile. Prescriber-level review shows a small set of patients receiving near-identical high-dose oxycodone regimens with no imaging, therapy or specialist claims.
45.features_to_create: Build a member-level controlled-substance monitor computing cumulative daily MME, refill-too-soon intervals, prescriber/pharmacy counts and absence of supporting diagnosis claims, firing a prepay edit requiring prior authorisation once the composite score passes the calibrated threshold. Add a prescriber panel feature flagging clinicians whose share of patients on high-MME oxycodone without supporting workup exceeds same-specialty peers, for prepay review and PDMP referral.

46.ways_to_identify: This is employer payroll-tax and premium-remittance theft, not billing of claims, so no claim-adjudication edit catches it; the insurer's own premium-receivable and eligibility systems carry the signal - premiums stopped arriving while the employer continued to submit enrolment and the group was cancelled without employee notice. Post-payment/administrative route: reconcile group billing arrears against active member eligibility files and IRS payroll filings.
46.features_to_create: Nearest applicable control at the insurer: an automated premium-delinquency to eligibility reconciliation that, when a group's remittance lapses, triggers direct written notice to each covered employee and freezes the employer's ability to file new enrolments; pair with a rule that any group cancellation for non-payment generates member-level notification and a claims-hold advisory. No payer-side claims edit applies to the unremitted payroll taxes; that is an IRS filing-mismatch control.

47.ways_to_identify: Orthotic-brace claims from these suppliers would show ordering physicians located far from the beneficiary, no prior or contemporaneous office-visit claim from the ordering NPI for that member, and a handful of prescribers concentrated across many unrelated suppliers - the signature of purchased, telemarketed prescriptions. Undisclosed ownership is catchable at change-of-ownership review by matching new owner identifiers, addresses, bank accounts and phones to a currently suspended provider.
47.features_to_create: Build a brace-claim prepay edit that requires an evaluation claim from the ordering NPI for the same beneficiary within the lookback window and pends claims where prescriber-beneficiary distance and prescriber-supplier concentration exceed calibrated percentiles, with an ABN/medical-record documentation request. Add a change-of-ownership screen resolving new owners, managing employees and payment accounts against sanctioned/suspended-provider identifiers, auto-suspending payments pending verification when a link exists, plus a growth-velocity trigger on brace HCPCS volume for new suppliers.

48.ways_to_identify: No claims-payment component: this is grant-application non-disclosure of research misconduct, detectable at grant peer review and progress-report stage. The signal is available from ORI/institutional misconduct inquiries, journal expressions of concern or retraction notices on the papers cited in the application, and image-integrity screening of figures in the cited publications and the PI's dissertation.
48.features_to_create: Nearest applicable control is a pre-award and continuation integrity screen: automatically resolve every publication cited in an application or progress report to retraction/correction/expression-of-concern feeds and to open institutional or ORI misconduct records for the named PI/key personnel, and hold award or the next-year disbursement pending certification review when a hit appears. Add image-duplication/manipulation screening of figures in cited works and require affirmative attestation of any pending misconduct proceeding.

49.ways_to_identify: Peripheral vascular intervention volume per physician, and repeat interventions on the same limb within short intervals, stand far above same-specialty peers and are traceable prepay via procedure codes plus the absence of documented failed conservative therapy or objective vascular testing. The kickback leg shows as payments styled as rent: referring practices concentrated in the referral graph, with lease/rent relationships disclosed or discoverable at credentialing, and referral share from those practices out of proportion to geography.
49.features_to_create: Build a provider-month feature counting peripheral vascular interventions per unique patient, repeat-intervention intervals per limb, and the ratio of interventions to prior diagnostic vascular studies; fire a prepay documentation request (ABI/duplex results, conservative-care history, symptom documentation) and a prior-authorisation edit when above calibrated percentiles. Add a referral-concentration graph flagging clinics where a small set of referrers supply most interventional volume and where a financial relationship (rent/lease/space sharing) exists, routing to Stark/AKS review before payment.

50.ways_to_identify: Prepay signals: explosive enrolment growth at a small number of centres, members travelling implausible distances to attend, attendance rosters with identical sign-in patterns, and heavy overlap between the day-care centre's enrollees and the affiliated fiscal intermediary's home-care members - shared ownership makes that overlap visible from enrolment ownership data. Beneficiary-side, kickback recruitment shows as members with attendance billed on days they have conflicting inpatient/other-provider claims, plus complaint and interview evidence from member outreach surveys.
50.features_to_create: Build a centre-day attendance verification edit: compare billed attendance units against biometric/electronic sign-in records and deny or pend units with no matching check-in, and flag centres whose per-member monthly units, enrolment growth rate or member travel distance exceed calibrated percentiles. Add an ownership-graph feature computing member overlap between commonly owned day-care centres and fiscal intermediaries, and place payment suspension plus member-verification interviews on centres above threshold.

51.ways_to_identify: No payer claims are involved - this is direct-to-consumer sale of counterfeit drugs from offshore sellers paid by wire and cash. Detection sits with import screening, payment processors and manufacturer serialisation: parcels from unregistered foreign shippers, online pharmacy sites without VIPPS/state licensure, and DSCSA serial numbers on Keytruda vials that do not resolve to a legitimate distribution record.
51.features_to_create: Nearest applicable controls: a serialisation/pedigree verification service that flags vials whose DSCSA serial numbers are unissued, duplicated or outside the authorised distribution chain, and payment-processor rules blocking merchant accounts tied to unlicensed online pharmacy domains. For payers, add a pharmacy-claim edit rejecting high-cost biologics dispensed by pharmacies not in the manufacturer's authorised distributor/specialty network.

52.ways_to_identify: Claim-volume velocity for a brand-new lab with no prior claim history, no CLIA capacity commensurate with 126,000 tests, and no matching specimen-collection or ordering-provider records is visible before payment. Identity misuse is caught by batch-matching claimed patients against the Death Master File, incarcerated-population files, and duplicate-address clusters (shelters, non-residential addresses such as substations), plus repeated members with no other claim history anywhere.
52.features_to_create: Build an enrolment-plus-velocity gate for uninsured-programme labs: cap and pend payment when a provider's weekly claim count exceeds the throughput implied by its CLIA certificate and reported instrumentation, requiring attestation and site verification. Add prepay identity edits that deny claims whose patient matches the Death Master File after the service date, matches a state incarceration roster on the service date, or belongs to an address cluster with anomalous patient counts, and require ordering-provider NPI plus specimen-collection evidence on every claim.

53.ways_to_identify: EVV telemetry itself carries the fraud: caller ID/GPS shows visits attested from the same device or phone number for many different clients, from the owner's/manager's own line, or from locations distant from the client's home, and multiple simultaneous or overlapping visits by one caregiver. Cross-matching the attesting caregiver ID against payroll and against the agency's owner/manager roster exposes principals logging clinical visits at scale.
53.features_to_create: Build an EVV-to-claim reconciliation edit that denies units without a matching check-in/check-out pair and pends visits whose GPS/caller ID is outside a tolerance of the client's registered address or duplicates another concurrent visit by the same caregiver. Add a caregiver-level feature flagging attestation from a single device/number across many clients and from IDs matching owners/managers, triggering payment suspension and client-contact verification for the agency.

54.ways_to_identify: Trip-level data allows matching each billed ride to a clinic encounter claim on the same date - rides with no corresponding methadone/clinic visit are phantom. Group rides are exposed by comparing pickup/drop times, GPS or vehicle assignment across claims: multiple single-passenger claims for the same vehicle and overlapping time window on the same route should have been billed as a shared trip.
54.features_to_create: Build a prepay edit that requires a same-date service encounter for the destination provider before paying an NEMT trip leg, and denies legs with no matching encounter. Add a vehicle/driver/time-window clustering feature that groups claims sharing vehicle, driver, date and route window and repriced them to group-ride rates, firing a documentation request (signed trip logs, GPS telematics) and prepay review when a provider's single-passenger share exceeds same-market peers.

55.ways_to_identify: This is internal embezzlement by a claims adjuster, detectable inside the insurer's own payment system: over a thousand claims all priced just below the handler's $2,000 no-approval authority, claimant portal registrations using email domains/patterns controlled by one user, and payment bank accounts repeated across unrelated claimants and matching an employee's own account. Duplicate payee bank details and no supporting provider claim or employer first-report-of-injury are the strongest prepay signals.
55.features_to_create: Build a payee-account dedup and employee-match control that blocks disbursement when the payee bank account, address, phone or email matches another claimant or any employee HR record, and require dual approval for any payment to a repeated account. Add an authority-threshold-clustering monitor per handler (share of approvals in the band just below their limit, count of self-created claimants, claims with no employer FROI or provider bill on file), auto-suspending the handler's payment authority for investigation when above the calibrated percentile.

56.ways_to_identify: The EIDL and PUA legs are loan/benefit programmes with no payer adjudication, caught by cross-programme identity and entity screening (shell entities with recent registration dates, no payroll tax filings, shared addresses/IPs/bank accounts across many applications). The Medicaid leg is catchable at enrolment: newly formed entities whose owners, addresses, phones and EFT accounts cluster with other applicants and with the loan-fraud shells, and whose billing begins at high velocity with no verifiable site.
56.features_to_create: Build an enrolment entity-resolution screen linking applicant owners, addresses, phones, IP/device fingerprints and EFT accounts into clusters; auto-hold enrolment and prepay all claims when an applicant shares identifiers with other recent applicants or with known shell-entity registries, pending site visit. Add a new-provider payment ceiling with velocity monitoring that suspends payment when first-90-day claim volume or dollars exceed peer norms for the specialty.

57.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic as the companion case: SBA EIDL and PUA fraud have no claim-adjudication touchpoint, so the control is identity/entity screening at application - shell companies with recent formation, no payroll history, and shared bank accounts, addresses and devices across applications. For the Medicaid leg, the pre-payment signal is a newly enrolled provider or member whose identifiers cluster with those shells and whose billing has no verifiable service footprint.
57.features_to_create: Implement a shared identity-graph screen across provider enrolment and member enrolment (owner SSN/EIN, address, phone, email, IP/device, EFT account), blocking enrolment and pending claims when clusters exceed the calibrated linkage threshold and requiring in-person or site verification. Add new-entity payment throttles with velocity-based suspension, and route entities linked to laundering typologies (rapid pass-through of receipts to personal accounts) to prepay review.

58.ways_to_identify: The steering shows up in claims as an abrupt, near-total shift in catheter brand/HCPCS supplier mix among a set of urology practices, with prescriptions from those practices concentrating on one manufacturer's affiliated DME supplier. Free-goods and discount inducements are visible from manufacturer transparency/Open Payments and rebate reporting, and from practices receiving in-office supplies at values inconsistent with their purchase records.
58.features_to_create: Build a referral-steering feature at the ordering-practice/quarter level computing the share of intermittent-catheter prescriptions routed to a single manufacturer-affiliated supplier, and flag step-changes and shares above same-specialty peers for AKS review before continued payment. Cross-join Open Payments/free-sample and discount data to those practices, firing an investigative hold and documentation request on the affiliated supplier's claims where financial-relationship value and steering share co-occur.

59.ways_to_identify: Add-on psychotherapy codes 90833/90836 billed with nearly every E/M visit is a mechanical outlier: compute the ratio of add-on psychotherapy to E/M visits per rendering provider against same-specialty peers, and check whether the E/M level's documented time plus the add-on's required minutes fit the provider's billed day. Providers whose add-on attachment rate approaches 100% and whose implied daily minutes are infeasible should be pended for records before payment.
59.features_to_create: Build a rendering-provider/month attachment-rate feature (share of E/M visits carrying 90833/90836/90838) plus a per-day implied-minutes sum across all timed codes; fire a prepay documentation request for session notes with start/stop times and separate psychotherapy content when the attachment rate or daily minutes exceed the calibrated peer percentile. Add a claim-level edit denying the add-on where the paired E/M's time already consumes the encounter, and escalate persistent outliers to prepay review of all behavioural claims.

60.ways_to_identify: This is a product-misbranding/procurement fraud rather than a claim-adjudication fraud, so the payer-side hook is the supply chain and any respirator/PPE pass-through billing: verify the claimed NIOSH approval number and manufacturer on the FDA/NIOSH Certified Equipment List and the CDC counterfeit-respirator list before purchase order or before reimbursing PPE add-on codes, and check whether the seller is a listed FDA device establishment. Signals available pre-payment include a distributor with no device establishment registration, a NIOSH approval number that does not match the manufacturer of record, unit prices far above pre-pandemic baselines, and brand-new supplier entity registered weeks before the sale. Otherwise this is caught post-payment via lab testing and recall/False Claims recovery.
60.features_to_create: Build a supplier/product validation service keyed on (NDC/UDI or catalog number, manufacturer, NIOSH approval number) that cross-references the NIOSH Certified Equipment List, FDA establishment registration and recall/counterfeit feeds; any PPE purchase order or PPE-related claim line whose approval number is absent, mismatched, or on a counterfeit alert is hard-stopped pending certificate-of-conformance documentation. Add a price-outlier monitor on PPE line items comparing unit price to the pre-emergency rolling median and to same-product peers, flagging above-calibrated-percentile prices for manual procurement/claims review and price-gouging referral.

61.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic as the companion case: a manufacturer/distributor pair sold non-conforming respirators as NIOSH-approved N95s, which is visible at procurement/credentialing time rather than at adjudication. A payer or hospital could match the asserted NIOSH approval number and manufacturer against the NIOSH Certified Equipment List and FDA device establishment registrations, and note that neither entity had a history of respirator approvals before spring 2020. Definitive proof requires lab filtration testing, so the residual route is post-payment recovery plus sample testing of high-volume PPE lots.
61.features_to_create: Implement a pre-purchase/pre-pay device-conformance edit: for any respirator or regulated device line, require a resolvable NIOSH approval number plus FDA registration for the named manufacturer, and suspend payment when the seller is not the approval holder or an authorized distributor of record. Layer an entity-age and product-history rule that routes first-time PPE suppliers formed within the recent lookback window to documentation request (certificate of conformance, lot test reports) before any payment or reimbursement of PPE pass-through.

62.ways_to_identify: The pre-pay signals are structural: CGX panels billed for beneficiaries with no cancer diagnosis history, no treating-physician relationship, ordering providers geographically remote from the beneficiary, and kits mailed after telemarketing contact rather than an office visit. Concentration analysis on the ordering NPI (one physician ordering high-cost hereditary cancer panels across many states with no prior claims for those patients) and on beneficiary clustering by marketing lead source is visible at adjudication. The offshore sham marketing contract and per-test kickbacks are only provable post-payment via financial records and interviews.
62.features_to_create: Build a prepay edit on hereditary cancer panel codes requiring, in the claim history window, an evaluation-and-management encounter with the ordering NPI and a cancer or family-history diagnosis supporting the panel; claims failing both conditions are pended for medical-record and order documentation. Add ordering-provider surveillance computing distinct-beneficiary count, state dispersion, and share of CGX orders with no prior relationship versus same-specialty peers, plus lab-level detection of beneficiary cohorts arriving in bursts from the same mailing/lead source, triggering prepay review or payment suspension of the lab.

63.ways_to_identify: Enrolment-time signals dominate: four newly enrolled hospices with nominee owners who are foreign nationals not physically in the country, addresses/leases and phone numbers sharing landlords, IP addresses or registered agents, and bank accounts opened by third parties. At adjudication, hospice election claims appear for beneficiaries with no supporting terminal-diagnosis history, no prior hospitalization or physician contact, and often concurrent claims from other providers inconsistent with hospice election. Rapid post-enrolment billing ramp for a brand-new hospice is a strong prepay flag.
63.features_to_create: At enrolment, run identity and presence verification on owners (SSA/DHS travel or death/exit data, credit-header residency) and cluster new applications by address, phone, IP, bank routing, registered agent and lease landlord; matched clusters go to site visit and application hold. At claims, apply a new-provider prepay review regime on hospice elections for the first period of billing, firing when the beneficiary lacks a terminal-illness diagnosis trail or the certifying physician has no prior claims for that beneficiary, and suspend payments when a cluster fires.

64.ways_to_identify: Identical mechanic to the companion case: sham hospices enrolled under identities of foreign nationals who had left the country, billing for beneficiaries never terminally ill and never seen. Pre-pay detectable via owner identity/presence verification at enrolment, shared-infrastructure clustering across the four entities, and beneficiary-level checks that hospice elections lack any terminal diagnosis, prior hospitalization, or certifying-physician relationship. Money laundering through shell corporations is a post-payment financial-analysis route (bank subpoenas, asset tracing).
64.features_to_create: Build an enrolment identity control that verifies owner presence and identity against immigration/exit and death data and holds applications whose owners cannot be verified as physically present; combine with a graph clustering job on addresses, phones, bank accounts and registered agents linking multiple hospice applications. Pair with a prepay hospice-election edit requiring documented terminal diagnosis and a prior claims relationship with the certifying physician, escalating to suspension and credible-allegation-of-fraud referral when a linked cluster bills concurrently.

65.ways_to_identify: Two hard prepay signals exist here: certifying physician NPIs belonging to deceased or non-participating doctors, and hospice/home-health certifications from physicians with no other claim history for that beneficiary. Both are checkable at adjudication against the provider enrolment file, SSA/NPPES death and deactivation data, and the beneficiary's claim history. Nominee foreign-national ownership and shared leases/bank accounts across the entities are catchable at enrolment through identity verification and cluster analysis.
65.features_to_create: Implement a hard prepay edit rejecting any hospice election or home-health certification where the attending/certifying NPI is deceased, deactivated, or has no active enrolment on the service date, and pend where the certifier has zero prior encounters with that beneficiary. Add a physician-identity misuse monitor that alerts the physician of record when certification volume spikes or when certifications originate from an agency the physician has never billed with, and suspend the agency's payments pending signature and record validation.

66.ways_to_identify: No health-care claim component: this is PPP loan eligibility fraud resolved under the False Claims Act. The signal was available at loan underwriting and forgiveness review by comparing the borrower's certified employee count against payroll tax filings (941s), state wage records, and affiliate rosters, which would have exposed a headcount above the eligibility cap. No payer-side claims control applies.
66.features_to_create: For the loan program administrator, build an eligibility cross-check that joins the applicant EIN to IRS payroll filings and state unemployment wage data plus common-ownership affiliate mapping, computing total employees across affiliates and firing when the certified figure understates the computed figure; hold forgiveness pending reconciliation. Nearest payer-side analogue: reconcile provider-reported staffing/FTE data on cost reports and relief-fund attestations against payroll data before disbursement.

67.ways_to_identify: Prepay signals: orthotic brace claims (L-codes for ankle, wrist, knee, back braces) where the ordering physician has no prior or contemporaneous encounter with the beneficiary, beneficiaries clustered nationwide around one supplier, and multiple braces per beneficiary in short windows. Ordering-NPI concentration - a handful of physicians signing orders across many states for a single supplier - is visible in the claims graph at adjudication, as is a new supplier's steep post-enrolment ramp in a single L-code family. Telemarketing payments themselves are post-payment financial evidence.
67.features_to_create: Build a prepay edit on orthotic L-codes requiring a face-to-face or telehealth E/M claim with the ordering NPI within the required lookback and a supporting musculoskeletal diagnosis; failures pend for medical records and signed order review. Add supplier-level analytics computing share of claims tied to a small set of ordering NPIs, beneficiary geographic dispersion, and braces-per-beneficiary versus same-specialty DME peers, firing prepay review or suspension above the calibrated percentile.

68.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic: telemarketer-sourced orthotic brace orders bearing physician signatures where no encounter occurred. Detectable prepay by joining each DME claim's ordering NPI to that beneficiary's encounter history (no E/M with the ordering physician), by high concentration of one supplier's volume in a few ordering NPIs, and by beneficiaries spread far from both the supplier and the ordering physician. Multiple distinct braces per beneficiary within a short window is an additional adjudication-time flag.
68.features_to_create: Deploy a claim-line edit denying/pending orthotic brace codes lacking a qualifying encounter with the ordering provider and a supporting diagnosis, with a documentation request for the signed order and clinical notes. Complement with a supplier scorecard (ordering-NPI concentration index, cross-state beneficiary dispersion, brace-per-beneficiary rate, post-enrolment growth slope) that moves outliers onto prepay review and, on physician attestation of forged signatures, payment suspension.

69.ways_to_identify: Identical brace-mill mechanic: signed orders from physicians who never treated the beneficiary, generated by paid telemarketing leads. The payer can see at adjudication that the ordering NPI has no claim history with the beneficiary, that the supplier's orders funnel through a tiny set of signing physicians, and that beneficiaries are geographically scattered relative to the supplier. Physician outreach/attestation campaigns on top-signing NPIs confirm the forgery before further payment.
69.features_to_create: Build the ordering-relationship prepay edit (no E/M with ordering NPI within lookback, or diagnosis not supporting the brace) with automatic documentation request; add an automated physician-verification workflow that mails/portals attestation requests to NPIs whose brace-order volume exceeds their peer-specialty norm. Suspend the supplier's payments when attestation is denied or unreturned, and register the involved NPIs on a prepay watchlist across all suppliers.

70.ways_to_identify: Even without a payer bill, the controllable data is prescribing: a PDMP/pharmacy view shows a single clinic address (unlicensed, no physical site) generating high-volume oxycodone prescriptions from rotating short-tenure prescribers, all patients cash-pay, no accompanying E/M or urine drug screen claims, and long-distance patient travel to fill. State licensure/facility registration files would show no licensed pain clinic at the address. These signals are visible to plans, PBMs and PDMP administrators before dispensing.
70.features_to_create: Build a clinic-address-level controlled-substance monitor joining PDMP/pharmacy claims to prescriber licensure and facility registration, computing MED per patient, prescriber-turnover rate at the address, share of opioid prescriptions with no companion E/M or toxicology claim, and patient-to-pharmacy distance; fire when the address has no licensed facility registration or exceeds peer thresholds. Action: prescriber/pharmacy alert plus prior-authorization or pharmacy-lock edit on opioid claims from that address pending verification of a legitimate practice site and examination records.

71.ways_to_identify: There is no billing scheme here, so no prepay claims edit would have caught it; the abuse was detected by home video and reported. Payer-adjacent signals that can be systematized are workforce screening at hire (state abuse registry, exclusion list, criminal history, prior MFCU findings) and complaint/EVV pattern review, plus incident and injury reporting from the member's other claims (ED visits or injury diagnoses during an aide-covered shift). The realistic route is post-service: complaint intake and MFCU referral.
71.features_to_create: Build a caregiver-level screening service that re-runs exclusion list, state abuse/neglect registry and licensure checks on a recurring cadence and blocks claims naming a disqualified aide as the service provider. Add a member-safety trigger that correlates EVV-attributed shifts with new injury/ED claims or complaint records for the same member and opens an urgent quality-of-care investigation and MFCU referral rather than a payment edit.

72.ways_to_identify: No claims-payment mechanic: this is PPP eligibility fraud under SBA affiliation rules, resolved via FCA settlement. It was detectable at underwriting/forgiveness by aggregating employee counts across commonly controlled affiliates using the health system's ownership disclosures, Medicare cost report related-organization schedules, IRS payroll filings and system-wide W-2 counts. No payer-side prepay claims control applies.
72.features_to_create: For the loan administrator, implement affiliation-aware size testing: resolve applicant EIN to a corporate family via ownership registries and Medicare/Medicaid ownership disclosures, sum affiliate employees from payroll tax and state wage data, and block disbursement or forgiveness when the aggregate exceeds the program cap. Payer-side analogue: reconcile provider-submitted ownership/control disclosures with cost report related-party schedules and flag inconsistencies for enrolment review.

73.ways_to_identify: This Stark/kickback arrangement is visible in the payer's own data as referral concentration: non-employee physicians holding administrative-services contracts with a hospital whose lab, imaging and supply referrals to that hospital exceed same-specialty peer patterns, especially where the physician's paid administrative hours are implausible relative to their clinical claim volume. Ownership/compensation relationships are reportable (Open Payments, hospital financial-relationship disclosures) and can be joined to referral flows at adjudication. Fair-market-value and commercial-reasonableness findings generally require post-payment audit and were surfaced by a whistleblower.
