73.features_to_create: Build a referral-relationship graph linking each referring NPI to hospital/lab/DME billing entities and to disclosed compensation arrangements (Open Payments, contract registry), computing the physician's share of referrals to the paying entity versus same-specialty peers and the ratio of administrative compensation to documented clinical time. Fire above the calibrated percentile into a Stark/AKS documentation request for the written arrangement, time logs and FMV opinion, and hold claims for designated health services from flagged physician-entity pairs pending review.

74.ways_to_identify: This is a cost-report fraud, so the control lives in cost-report intake rather than claim adjudication: related-organization schedules (Worksheet A-8-2) for 44 commonly owned SNFs can be cross-checked against ownership/control disclosures, secretary-of-state and PECOS ownership data, and vendor names appearing in each other's filings to detect undisclosed related parties and costs booked above the lower of cost or market. Comparing per-diem management, therapy, staffing-agency and rent costs across commonly owned facilities and against non-affiliated peers exposes inflated related-party charges before settlement.
74.features_to_create: Build a cost-report edit that resolves every vendor on each SNF's cost report against a common-ownership graph (PECOS ownership, state corporate filings, shared officers/addresses) and fires when a material vendor is related but not disclosed on the related-organization schedule, or when related-party unit costs exceed market benchmarks and peer commonly owned facilities. Action: hold interim-rate settlement and issue a documentation request for related-party cost buildups; escalate systematically filed chains to audit.

75.ways_to_identify: Several signals are visible at adjudication: claims with service dates preceding kit shipment/delivery dates, repeated COVID antigen and PCR claims for the same beneficiary across many dates from a single lab, one ordering physician NPI attached to essentially all claims with no treating relationship, and antigen codes billed as professionally observed by an entity with no clinical site or staff. Beneficiary cohorts arriving from a single website lead source, and beneficiaries who never requested tests (complaint and Explanation-of-Benefits feedback), corroborate. Lab enrolment data would show no CLIA capacity matching the PCR volume billed.
75.features_to_create: Build prepay edits for COVID testing: deny/pend claims where the same lab bills repeat antigen or PCR tests for a beneficiary above the calibrated frequency, where the service date precedes the shipment/delivery date on the lab's own supply data, and where the observed-administration modifier is used by a supplier with no site-of-service or staffing on file. Add ordering-NPI concentration and CLIA-capacity-versus-volume checks that trigger payment suspension and beneficiary verification outreach for labs above the calibrated percentile.

76.ways_to_identify: All four abuse patterns are detectable prepay from claims data alone: exact duplicate claims (same veteran, date, hours), billed hours exceeding EVV-verified caregiver clock-in/out, dates of service after the veteran's date of death, and aggregate caregiver hours exceeding feasible hours per day. Cross-referencing the administrator's authorization records and the enrolment/death file at adjudication would have stopped the majority of the roughly 10,000 claims. Repayment evasion and offshore transfers are post-payment recovery issues.
76.features_to_create: Implement four prepay edits keyed on (veteran, date, caregiver): exact/near-duplicate detection, date-of-death check against the eligibility and death file, EVV reconciliation denying billed hours in excess of verified visit minutes, and a caregiver-day-hours cap that flags impossible aggregate hours across veterans. Combine failures into an agency-level score that triggers payment suspension and prepay review of all claims for single-owner agencies with rapid volume growth.

77.ways_to_identify: Prepay signals: a single order-generation platform's fingerprint across thousands of claims - the same small set of telemedicine physician NPIs signing orders for beneficiaries nationwide, no E/M encounter or only a brief telehealth code with no follow-up, and identical L-code brace and compounded pain-cream combinations across unrelated suppliers and pharmacies. Beneficiary recruitment via mailers and offshore call centers shows up as geographic dispersion and bursty enrollment cohorts shared by multiple suppliers. Kickback payments themselves surface post-payment through financial records.
77.features_to_create: Build a cross-supplier ordering-provider graph: for each signing NPI compute distinct suppliers/pharmacies served, distinct states, orders per active practice day, and share of orders with no prior beneficiary relationship; above the calibrated percentile, place the NPI on a prepay hold list so every downstream brace/pain-cream claim citing that NPI pends for documentation. Add an edit requiring a qualifying encounter and supporting diagnosis for L-codes and compounded topical analgesics, and suspend suppliers whose volume is concentrated in flagged NPIs.

78.ways_to_identify: The platform's output is statistically distinctive at adjudication: bulk orders signed by a few telemedicine physicians for beneficiaries they never examined, distributed to many unaffiliated DME suppliers and pharmacies that share the same signing NPIs and the same product mix. No prior beneficiary-physician claim history, minimal or absent telehealth E/M, and cross-state dispersion are all observable before payment. Physician attestation campaigns on the top signing NPIs confirm no examination occurred.
78.features_to_create: Create a signing-provider risk engine that scores each ordering NPI on orders-per-day, downstream-supplier breadth, no-prior-relationship rate and product concentration, and auto-pends all claims naming high-scoring NPIs pending signed order and clinical documentation. Add a supplier/pharmacy-side edit: when a payee's claims share the same flagged NPI cohort above the calibrated share, trigger prepay review and payment suspension pending kickback/marketing-contract disclosure.

79.ways_to_identify: Same DMERx mechanic across multiple payers, so the strongest signal is cross-payer/cross-supplier reuse of a small set of signing physician NPIs paired with mailer- and call-center-sourced beneficiaries in bursts. At adjudication one can see absent or token telehealth encounters, no prior beneficiary-physician relationship, formulaic brace-plus-pain-cream bundles, and identical order templates across unrelated suppliers. Kickbacks between the platform, telemedicine firms and suppliers are post-payment financial findings.
79.features_to_create: Implement a shared prepay watchlist of ordering NPIs derived from graph metrics (suppliers served, states, daily order volume, share without prior relationship) that pends brace and compounded-cream claims for documentation, and share the list across Medicare, TRICARE and VA community-care adjudication. Add a beneficiary-cohort burst detector that flags groups of beneficiaries first appearing on multiple suppliers' claims within the same short window via the same ordering NPI, escalating to supplier payment suspension and beneficiary verification calls.

80.ways_to_identify: This is employment-tax and bankruptcy fraud with no claims-payment component, so no payer adjudication control would have caught it; the detection route is IRS matching of W-2 withholding reported by the employer against Form 941 filings and trust-fund deposits, plus bankruptcy schedules cross-checked against property records and bank data. A payer-side analogue is enrolment screening: a contracted staffing/provider entity with unpaid federal tax liens or unfiled payroll returns is a financial-instability and diversion risk.
80.features_to_create: Build an enrolment/revalidation screen that runs the entity and its owners against federal/state tax lien, judgment and bankruptcy filing feeds and flags mismatches between W-2 aggregate withholding and 941 filings where the data is available; fire a credentialing review and require a corporate financial attestation. Otherwise state plainly no claims-payment control applies to this case.

81.ways_to_identify: The signal is a manufacturer-to-surgeon payment stream reported to Open Payments as 'consulting' with no deliverable, sitting alongside the same surgeons' implant utilization; a payer can join Open Payments general/consulting payments by physician NPI to its own claims for that manufacturer's implant codes and see that payment recipients drive disproportionate device volume. Pre-payment, the credentialing and prior-authorization files for high-cost spine implants can be checked for undisclosed vendor financial relationships.
81.features_to_create: Build a physician-level monthly join of Open Payments payments (by paying manufacturer, nature-of-payment) to implant/spine surgery claims; compute the share of a surgeon's implant volume tied to manufacturers paying them and flag surgeons above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers for prepay review of medical necessity. Additionally flag manufacturers whose consulting payments cluster in small round amounts across many surgeons with no reported research output, and route to SIU/AKS referral.

82.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic as the SpineFrontier consulting-fee case: sham 'consulting' payments disclosed under the Sunshine Act to disguise referral inducements to implanting surgeons. Payers can detect it by linking Open Payments records to their own device and surgery claims to find surgeons whose implant selection tracks the paying manufacturer, and by requiring disclosure of vendor financial ties at credentialing and for implant prior authorization.
82.features_to_create: Implement a surgeon-manufacturer influence score: per NPI, compute payment dollars/counts by manufacturer from Open Payments and the concentration of that manufacturer's devices in the surgeon's implant claims; fire prepay medical-necessity documentation requests on implant claims where concentration and payment both exceed calibrated percentiles. Flag manufacturers with many small uniform 'consulting' payments lacking documented work product for AKS referral and possible network termination.

83.ways_to_identify: This is a personnel announcement, not a fraud case; there is no scheme, no claims and nothing for a payer to detect. No pre-payment or post-payment signal exists.
83.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. If ingesting DOJ press releases into an intelligence pipeline, add a classifier that drops non-case items (appointments, awards, annual round-ups) before they generate provider risk flags.

84.ways_to_identify: The scheme is visible arithmetically at adjudication: a single physician NPI billing over 100 one-hour in-home visit units in one calendar day exceeds the hours in a day, and cumulative 30,000 hours far exceeds any plausible provider-day capacity. Time-based home-visit codes also permit overlap checks (two visits at different addresses at the same time) and travel-feasibility checks between patient addresses.
84.features_to_create: Build a provider-day time-accumulator: for each rendering NPI and date of service, sum the time implied by all time-based E/M and home-visit codes plus the units billed, and hard-deny or pend claims that push the day above a calibrated maximum billable-hours threshold. Add an overlap edit for same-NPI concurrent home visits at distinct patient addresses and a travel-time feasibility check; repeated firing triggers payment suspension and a records request.

85.ways_to_identify: Two independently checkable signals: credentialing data (the surgeon's federal felony convictions, prior termination for unnecessary surgery, NPDB and exclusion/licensure adverse-action reports) should have blocked privileging and facility claims tied to him; and claims patterns showing hysterectomy, sterilization and pre-39-week induction/C-section rates far above same-specialty peers, with sterilization claims lacking valid Medicaid consent forms and inpatient-only procedures billed as outpatient. Consent-form and gestational-age documentation are requestable pre-payment on these specific code families.
85.features_to_create: Run continuous NPDB/OIG-LEIE/state licensure/criminal-record monitoring on all privileged and rendering NPIs and auto-pend facility and professional claims where the operating physician has an unresolved adverse action. Add prepay edits: sterilization claims require an attached valid consent form dated within the required window; early elective induction/C-section claims require documented gestational age and medical indication; and Medicare inpatient-only procedure codes billed as outpatient are denied. Layer a per-surgeon hysterectomy/C-section rate outlier model versus same-specialty peers driving prepay medical-necessity review.

86.ways_to_identify: Pure employment-tax fraud (withholding W-2 amounts, never filing 941s, diverting funds personally) with no billed claims at issue, so it is not detectable at claim adjudication; the detection route is IRS matching of aggregate W-2 withholding to filed 941s and deposits. A payer sees only indirect signals such as tax liens against the sleep-center entity and owner-level commingling.
86.features_to_create: Add tax-lien, judgment and bankruptcy feeds plus owner-level financial screening to provider enrolment and revalidation, flagging entities with liens or unfiled payroll returns for credentialing review and enhanced payment monitoring. Otherwise no claims-payment control applies to this mechanic.

87.ways_to_identify: Referral-concentration data shows the tell: nearly all of one lab's urine drug-testing volume originating from a handful of clinics, with standing-order-like panel uniformity and testing billed for chiropractic patients where UDT has no plausible role. The pre-signed prescription scheme is visible as a single prescriber issuing controlled-substance scripts clustered on one weekday, with no corresponding office-visit claim for the patient near the fill date, and per-prescriber opioid MME volume far above peers.
87.features_to_create: Build referral-concentration monitoring: per lab TIN, compute the share of definitive/presumptive UDT revenue from each ordering NPI and flag pairs above the calibrated percentile, cross-checked against common ownership/employment and payroll links between ordering and lab entities; pend those lab claims for prepay review. Separately, per prescriber, compute day-of-week concentration of controlled-substance fills, fills without a preceding E/M encounter claim, and MME per patient versus peers; fire prepay pharmacy edits requiring encounter linkage and refer to the state PDMP/licensing board.

88.ways_to_identify: This is HUD housing-voucher eligibility fraud plus a state COVID business-grant fraud, with no health care claims, so there is no payer adjudication control; detection sits with the housing authority and grant administrator matching self-certified income against IRS/state wage, business-license and merchant-deposit data, and testing grant spending against business bank records. Post-award, bank-statement review shows grant funds moving to household expenses.
88.features_to_create: For benefit-eligibility programs, build an automated income-verification match at each recertification against state wage records, business registration/sales-tax filings and 1099-K merchant data, flagging any undisclosed business entity tied to the applicant's SSN. For relief grants, require and automatically parse business bank statements to test that disbursed funds were spent on business expenses, holding tranches until verified. No health-payer claim edit applies.

89.ways_to_identify: Two hard, pre-payment verifiable facts: the rendering provider's license was suspended on many dates of service, and he was outside the country on others. License status is available from state board feeds at adjudication; absence can be surfaced by impossible-day patterns (high volume with no gaps) and, once suspected, by travel/immigration or credit-card data in investigation.
89.features_to_create: Build a license-status edit that validates each claim's date of service against the rendering provider's licensure and sanction effective/end dates from state board and LEIE feeds, auto-denying services rendered during suspension and suspending payment on the TIN when hits recur. Add a solo-provider capacity model per NPI-day (visits, implied minutes, patients per hour) versus same-specialty peers, pending claims above the calibrated percentile for attendance documentation such as signed encounter logs.

90.ways_to_identify: Volume and quality signals are visible before payment: claim counts per accessioned specimen and per instrument/testing capacity for the lab's CLIA certificate, negative-result rates and turnaround times far outside peer distributions, and a positivity rate implausibly low for the community prevalence. Under the HRSA uninsured program, patient attestation and specimen-collection records were required and could have been sampled pre-payment; reagent dilution itself is only provable via proficiency testing and lab records post-payment.
90.features_to_create: Build a lab capacity/plausibility engine: per CLIA-certified lab per day, compare billed test volume against certificated test menu, staffing and instrument throughput, and compute positivity and inconclusive rates versus regional peers; pend claims above the calibrated volume percentile or with anomalous positivity for prepay documentation of accession logs and result reports. Add duplicate-detection on patient/date/test triples and require unique specimen identifiers on claims, with payment suspension on repeated failure and a referral for CLIA proficiency-testing review.

91.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic as the companion count: a single lab billing an emergency uninsured-testing program for enormous test volumes that exceed its CLIA-certified instrument and staffing capacity, with implausibly uniform negative results and no verifiable specimen accession trail. Pre-payment, HRSA-style programs can sample-verify patient attestations and accession numbers; the reagent dilution is provable only post-payment through lab records and proficiency testing.
91.features_to_create: Implement per-lab throughput ceilings derived from CLIA certificate, instrument inventory and reported staffing, auto-pending any day's claims above the ceiling; require a unique specimen accession ID per claim line and deny duplicates or reused IDs. Add peer-relative positivity/inconclusive-rate outlier scoring that triggers prepay documentation requests and, on repeat, payment suspension pending an on-site or records audit.

92.ways_to_identify: The reincarnation pattern is the key pre-payment signal: after suspension, new DME PTANs enrolled under nominee owners while sharing addresses, phone numbers, bank accounts, billing agents and beneficiary populations with the suspended entities. Also visible is orthotic brace billing driven by a few marketing-sourced prescribers with no prior treating relationship, brace volume per prescriber far above peers, and identical code combinations across thousands of beneficiaries.
92.features_to_create: Build an entity-resolution graph across enrolment records (address, phone, bank account, EFT, billing agent, authorized officials, prior PTANs) and auto-hold enrolment and payments for any new DME applicant linked to a suspended, revoked or excluded entity. Add a prepay orthotic-brace edit requiring a documented treating relationship (prior E/M with the ordering NPI) and flag prescriber-supplier pairs and per-prescriber brace volumes above calibrated percentiles for prepay review; monitor for common beneficiary overlap between the suspended and new suppliers.

93.ways_to_identify: Pharmacy-level dispensing data shows the pattern before payment: an outsized share of revenue in opioids/benzodiazepines, high rates of the classic dangerous combination therapy, long-distance patients travelling past nearer pharmacies, cash-equivalent inducements reflected in zero copay collection, and duplicate-therapy claims paid without intervention. Copay waiver and 'Monkey Bucks' inducements are inferable from systematically zero patient responsibility and from patient interviews at audit.
93.features_to_create: Build a pharmacy risk score per NPI: controlled-substance share of scripts, opioid+benzo+muscle-relaxant concurrency rate per patient, mean patient-to-pharmacy distance, prescriber concentration, and share of claims with zero collected copay; fire prepay edits denying dangerous-combination claims absent documented justification and pend high-scoring pharmacies for audit or payment suspension. Add a prescriber-side edit requiring an examination/E/M encounter linked to controlled-substance scripts and flag prescribers whose scripts cluster on a single weekday.

94.ways_to_identify: Two deterministic pre-payment checks would have stopped this: dates of service after the rendering clinician's employment/roster end date and license reassignment (and, more simply, after they were no longer affiliated or credentialed), and dates of service after the beneficiary's date of death from the eligibility/master death file. Volume per clinician also exceeded feasible psychotherapy hours per day.
94.features_to_create: Add a hard prepay edit denying any claim whose date of service follows the beneficiary's recorded date of death, and a roster-affiliation edit validating that the rendering NPI is actively credentialed and affiliated with the billing TIN on the date of service, with an attestation-refresh workflow when clinicians depart. Layer a per-clinician daily therapy-minutes accumulator that pends claims exceeding calibrated maximum billable hours and triggers payment suspension on repeat hits.

95.ways_to_identify: Order-level metadata is the giveaway: one physician certifying thousands of portal orders with review times measured in seconds, no prior or concurrent E/M claim with the beneficiary, patients spread nationwide with no geographic relationship to the prescriber, orders for deceased beneficiaries, and knee/ankle braces for amputees. Beneficiary-complaint feeds about cold calls and requests for Medicare numbers provide an early independent signal.
95.features_to_create: Build a telehealth-ordering integrity model per ordering NPI: count of orders, orders per active day, share with no antecedent E/M encounter, beneficiary geographic dispersion, and share flowing to a small set of labs/DME suppliers; auto-pend downstream genetic-test and brace claims from prescribers above the calibrated percentile pending documentation of the patient encounter. Add hard edits for date-of-service-after-death and clinical-impossibility pairs (laterality/amputation status versus braced limb, prior amputation history in claims), and cluster suppliers sharing the same prescriber pool for coordinated prepay review.

96.ways_to_identify: The distribution of E/M levels is the signal: essentially every COVID collection encounter billed as level 2-5 E/M by a single rendering NPI across hundreds of thousands of claims, with no site-of-service or staffing consistent with physician evaluation, and specimen-collection codes almost never used. A second E/M billed for result notification produces same-patient duplicate E/M pairs days apart with no separately identifiable service, and the single-provider volume vastly exceeds feasible daily encounters.
96.features_to_create: Build a rendering-NPI E/M profile that computes level distribution and daily encounter counts versus same-specialty peers and against a feasible-encounters-per-day ceiling; auto-downcode or pend claims when a provider's COVID-test-site E/M claims exceed the ceiling or when level distribution sits above the calibrated percentile with no supporting diagnosis complexity. Add edits requiring specimen-collection codes for test-site encounters, denying a second E/M for result communication on the same episode, and flagging any NPI listed as sole rendering provider across multiple physical sites on the same day for payment suspension and records request.

97.ways_to_identify: This is an assault-on-a-federal-officer prosecution with no claims, provider or payer involvement, so there is nothing detectable pre-payment.
97.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. In intelligence intake, filter non-health-care-fraud prosecutions so they do not generate provider risk scores.

98.ways_to_identify: Detectable pre-payment from order metadata and claim linkage: a single physician signing thousands of cancer/pharmacogenomic and brace orders with no telehealth or office-visit claim for those beneficiaries, patients drawn from nationwide marketing lists rather than a local panel, and the resulting claims concentrated in a handful of labs and suppliers. Per-order payment to the signer is not on the claim, but the volume-without-encounter pattern and supplier-prescriber concentration are.
98.features_to_create: Implement a prepay edit that denies or pends high-cost genetic testing and orthotic brace claims when no E/M or telehealth encounter claim exists between the ordering NPI and the beneficiary within a defined lookback, requiring documentation of medical necessity and patient contact. Add prescriber-level scoring on order volume, distinct downstream billers, and beneficiary geographic dispersion versus peers, plus a supplier-side check flagging billers whose orders concentrate on a few prolific out-of-area prescribers for coordinated review and payment suspension.

99.ways_to_identify: Coding-mix data shows near-exclusive use of the highest-reimbursing crisis-intervention code, which by definition should be episodic, plus per-counselor daily service volumes exceeding feasible hours and services billed for beneficiaries the counselor never met. Cloned documentation is detectable on prepay records review as byte-identical progress notes across patients, and patient-recruitment payments surface via beneficiary interviews and clusters of new members enrolled from the same recruiter address.
99.features_to_create: Build a provider-level code-mix monitor for behavioral health: share of billing in crisis-intervention/highest-intensity codes versus same-specialty peers, and repeat crisis claims per beneficiary per period; pend claims above the calibrated percentile for prepay records review. Add a per-counselor daily minutes accumulator with hard denial above feasible hours, and an automated note-similarity check (text-hash/near-duplicate scoring) on submitted documentation that triggers payment suspension and beneficiary verification calls when clone rates are high.

100.ways_to_identify: This is a loan-program eligibility fraud, not a claims-payment scheme: the observable signal is the affiliation/size certification on the PPP application versus corporate ownership data. SBA could have run the applicant EINs and addresses against Dun & Bradstreet/corporate-family trees, SAM.gov parent-entity registrations, and IRS/state UI wage filings to detect that five loans traced to subsidiaries of one foreign-owned parent whose combined headcount exceeded size limits.
100.features_to_create: Build a pre-disbursement affiliation-graph check: cluster loan applications by shared parent EIN, common officers/registered agents, address and bank-account overlap, and sum affiliate employee counts from UI wage data before approving any loan or forgiveness; fire a hold and manual size-standard review when the cluster's aggregate headcount/revenue exceeds the program limit. Apply the same clustering again at forgiveness stage, since forgiveness is a second payment event, and hold lender processing fees pending resolution.

101.ways_to_identify: Every element was visible on the claim: prescriber DEA number validity, prescriber specialty, prescriber-to-pharmacy geographic distance, and drug/patient-sex incompatibility. A payer or PDMP could flag hydrocodone/carisoprodol fills written by OB/GYNs for male patients, prescribers hundreds of miles away, and DEA registrations that are invalid, expired or not authorized for the schedule dispensed.
101.features_to_create: Prepay pharmacy edits: (1) validate prescriber DEA/NPI against the active DEA registration file including schedule authority and reject on invalid/expired; (2) compute prescriber-patient-pharmacy distance and specialty-plausibility (e.g., OB/GYN prescribing scheduled opioids to male members) and deny or pend for documentation; (3) pharmacy-level scorecard on share of controlled fills from out-of-area or specialty-mismatched prescribers and 'trinity' combinations, triggering payment suspension and an on-site CSA records audit above the calibrated percentile.

102.ways_to_identify: Attendance-driven gift-card inducements show up as implausibly perfect per-patient attendance and near-maximum billable days per member, plus a cost-report/bank trail of large gift-card purchases funded by Medicaid deposits. The paired lab arrangement is visible as a single drug-testing lab receiving essentially all of this program's specimens with definitive testing on nearly every visit.
102.features_to_create: Provider-month analytics: compute distribution of billed service days per member and flag programs whose members cluster at the maximum allowable days with abnormally low no-show variance versus same-specialty peers; flag single-lab referral concentration from one SUD program. Fire prepay review/documentation request for attendance sign-in sheets, and cross-check the provider's disclosed expenditures and bank records for stored-value/gift-card purchases during audit; auditor-statement inconsistencies should trigger payment suspension.

103.ways_to_identify: The underlying kickback scheme was a compounding-pharmacy referral arrangement detectable prepay through marketer-sourced prescriptions, formulaic high-cost compound combinations and one-to-few prescriber concentration. The supervised-release/restitution-evasion conduct has no payer-side claims signal; it is caught post-payment by monitoring exclusion status and by tracing new bank accounts and successor entities the debtor controls.
103.features_to_create: Prepay: flag compound claims whose ingredients match high-reimbursement templates and whose prescribers concentrate in a small marketer-linked set; require dispensing documentation and patient attestation before payment. Post-payment: run a recurring screen matching convicted/excluded individuals to new NPIs, EINs, bank routing/account numbers and family-member owners on enrolment files, and auto-deny enrolment plus refer for restitution offset when a match hits.

104.ways_to_identify: Per-patient recruiting fees produce a distinctive pattern: sudden influx of new Medicaid members from outside the practice's normal service radius, and a very high conversion rate from a prophy/exam visit to billable restorative or surgical care because payment only triggered on services beyond prevention. Enrolment-time disclosure of marketing contracts and the practice's paid-vendor ledger would show the per-head fee structure.
104.features_to_create: Practice-quarter model: compute new-member share, mean travel distance, and ratio of members receiving beyond-preventive treatment to members seen, compared to same-specialty Medicaid peers; fire a prepay documentation/medical-necessity review and a marketing-contract disclosure request when multiple indicators exceed the calibrated percentile. Add an attestation edit requiring disclosure of any per-patient marketing compensation and cluster practices sharing the same recruiting vendor's address, phone or payments.

105.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic as the paired case: per-patient referral compensation banned by the CTDHP provider manual, visible as bursts of new Medicaid patients arriving from a common recruiter's catchment, shared transport/appointment-scheduling patterns across unrelated practices, and high treatment-conversion rates. The recruiter link is confirmable by finding the same vendor paid by multiple practices in AP records obtained at credentialing or audit.
105.features_to_create: Build a shared-recruiter graph: link practices by common referral vendor identifiers, patient-cohort overlap and same-day multi-practice patient batches; combine with new-patient surge and out-of-radius member share to fire prepay review. Require an annual signed disclosure of all patient-marketing arrangements as a condition of claim payment, and treat undisclosed per-patient fee contracts as grounds for payment suspension and AKS referral.

106.ways_to_identify: Both mechanics are fully visible on claims: presumptive screen and definitive confirmation codes for the same member on the same date with no intervening practitioner order, and specimens whose ordering entity is a sober home / residential monitoring program rather than a treating clinician of a covered service. Reflex-testing patterns show as near-100% confirmation rates and standing panels of the same analytes for every member regardless of history.
106.features_to_create: Prepay edit: deny definitive UDT billed same-date-of-service as presumptive from the same lab unless a documented practitioner reflex order is attached; require the ordering NPI to be an enrolled treating clinician and deny where the order originates from a residential/monitoring facility with no covered service. Lab-month analytics on confirmation-to-screen ratio, analytes per specimen and member test frequency versus peers, with prepay review above the calibrated percentile.

107.ways_to_identify: The signature is a small set of ordering physicians generating brace orders for members spread nationwide with no prior or subsequent clinical relationship, and no telehealth or office E/M claim from that physician for the same member. Multiple DME suppliers billing off the same physicians' orders, sharing addresses, owners or billing agents, is visible in enrolment and claims data at adjudication.
107.features_to_create: Prepay edit on orthotic/brace HCPCS: require a paid qualifying encounter by the ordering NPI within a lookback window and reject orders where ordering-physician-to-beneficiary distance and state count exceed plausible practice patterns. Ordering-physician velocity model (braces ordered per day, distinct suppliers served, share of members with no other claims from that NPI) triggering prepay suspension of all downstream supplier claims and revocation review; cluster suppliers by shared billing agent/telemarketing lead source.

108.ways_to_identify: Modifier 25 misuse is measurable at adjudication: the share of E/M claims carrying modifier 25 when billed same-day with a procedure, per provider versus same-specialty peers. Critically, this payer had already notified the provider and assessed an overpayment in 2019, so its own audit-outcome data should have driven a prepay control rather than allowing four more years of identical billing.
108.features_to_create: Provider-quarter metric: proportion of pain-injection encounters with a same-day modifier-25 E/M, benchmarked to same-specialty peers; above the calibrated percentile place the provider on prepay documentation review requiring the separate E/M note before payment. Add a rule that any provider with a prior education letter or assessed overpayment on a specific code/modifier is auto-enrolled in prepay review for that code for a defined period, with continued aberrance escalating to suspension.

109.ways_to_identify: This is contractor labor-rate mischarging, not clinical claims: the signal is invoiced labor category versus each named employee's actual degree and years of experience, which the payer holds in resumes/key-personnel submissions. Reconciling monthly invoice line items to the contract's labor-category qualification matrix and to the approved personnel roster would have surfaced the mismatch before payment.
109.features_to_create: Build an invoice-to-roster edit for services contracts: for each billed labor hour, match employee ID to the approved qualification file and compute whether the billed category's education/experience floor is met; suspend payment on non-conforming lines and request substantiating credentials. Add periodic sampling audits of subcontractor personnel, since substitutions after award are the common failure point.

110.ways_to_identify: Rendering-provider identity misuse is detectable prepay: physicians listed as treating provider on claims from clinics they have no reassignment or employment link to, no corresponding presence in the clinic's location/schedule, and volumes exceeding feasible hours per day per NPI. Payment routing to accounts with rapid outbound foreign wires and a beneficiary population with no local footprint are additional pre-payment enrolment signals.
110.features_to_create: Prepay edit: reject claims where the rendering NPI has no active reassignment/affiliation to the billing TIN, and pend where the rendering NPI's aggregate same-day billed time across all sites exceeds feasible service minutes. Cross-payer/commercial-plan sharing of the same rendering NPI appearing at unrelated TINs, plus bank-account velocity screening at enrolment, should trigger payment suspension and provider-attestation outreach directly to the named physicians rather than to the clinic.

111.ways_to_identify: Diversion of operating funds is visible in cost reports and financial filings before further payment: owner distributions and guaranteed payments rising while accounts payable, insurance premiums and payroll-tax deposits go unpaid. External signals available prepay include vendor liens/judgments, lapsed employee benefit filings (Form 5500/401(k) delinquency), IRS trust-fund tax delinquency notices, and staffing-level and complaint data from state survey agencies.
111.features_to_create: Chain-level financial monitoring: for each commonly owned SNF group, compute related-party distributions as a share of Medicare/Medicaid revenue, days payable outstanding, and payroll-tax/benefit-remittance delinquency flags from cross-agency feeds; fire enhanced oversight, escrow or payment suspension when distributions rise while payables and staffing deteriorate. Require related-party transaction disclosure as a condition of continued enrolment and re-verify at each ownership change.

112.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic as the companion case and detectable from the same data: CMS funds certified for resident care while owner distributions surge and vendors, employee health premiums, 401(k) withholdings, resident trust accounts and withheld employment taxes go unpaid. Resident personal-fund account shortfalls and unpaid-premium complaints reach state survey and DOL/IRS systems well before the loss reached $146 million.
112.features_to_create: Build a cross-agency solvency/diversion dashboard keyed to the owning chain: inputs are cost-report related-party distributions, Form 5500 and trust-fund tax delinquency, vendor judgment filings, resident trust-fund audit exceptions and staffing hours per resident day; firing thresholds set on deterioration versus the chain's own baseline and peer chains. Action is heightened enrolment review, periodic payment escrow or suspension pending an independent monitor, plus mandatory attestation that CMS funds were applied to operations.

113.ways_to_identify: This is workers' compensation benefit fraud detectable prepay through inconsistency between the claimed injury and objective evidence: the employer's use-of-force reports, incident video, body-worn/facility camera footage and witness statements versus the claimant's narrative to the Board, treating physicians and IMEs. Continued cash-benefit payments over years with unchanged subjective complaints, no objective imaging findings, and outside activity (secondary employment, social media, surveillance) are the ongoing signals.
113.features_to_create: Claim-level intake edit: require the employer's incident report and available video to be attached and cross-read against the claimant's stated mechanism of injury before the first indemnity payment, flagging narrative conflicts for investigation. Build a long-duration-claim review queue keyed on duration of total disability beyond expected recovery for the diagnosis, IMEs whose findings conflict with treating notes, and cross-match to payroll/UI wage data for concurrent earnings; fire suspension of cash benefits pending examination.

114.ways_to_identify: This is eligibility/identity fraud at enrolment rather than a provider billing scheme: the signal is one SSN/identity document supporting two distinct biometric or photo identities and conflicting DMV, SSA and immigration records. Cross-matching the Medi-Cal applicant's SSN and name against SSA Numident, DMV photo/facial-recognition duplicates and border-crossing records would show the same SSN tied to two faces and to an individual whose sibling is the true owner.
114.features_to_create: Enrolment identity-proofing edit: run applicant SSN/name/DOB through SSA verification and a DMV photo-duplicate/facial-match service; fire a hold and in-person documentation request when one identifier maps to multiple photos, when the applicant's asserted identity is also actively enrolled or filing elsewhere, or when address/household data conflicts. Add periodic re-verification sweeps of active enrollees against SSA death/mismatch and duplicate-photo results.

115.ways_to_identify: Pure investment fraud with no health-plan claims component, so no payer adjudication control applies; the deceit lived in fabricated bank statements, supply contracts and distributor agreements shown to private investors. Detection routes are investor/escrow-side: independent confirmation of bank balances directly with the institution, verification of the Chinese manufacturer and Texas plant's existence and capacity, FDA/EPA registration checks for an antiviral aerosol claim, and SEC/state securities filing review.
115.features_to_create: No payer-side claims edit applies. Nearest applicable control is a procurement/grant vetting check for PPE and COVID-product buyers: verify supplier registration, manufacturing capacity and FDA/EPA product registration, confirm bank documents directly with issuing institutions rather than accepting borrower-supplied PDFs, and require escrowed milestone payment against verified delivery.

116.ways_to_identify: Not a fraud case: this is a personnel announcement press release with no defendants, claims or payer loss described, so there is nothing to detect prepay.
116.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. If a control must be named, the nearest is ordinary large-dollar Medicare claim analytics on the unrelated $100 million scheme alluded to in passing, which cannot be specified from this document.

117.ways_to_identify: Classic phantom-DME billing on stolen identities, visible at adjudication: ordering NPIs who deny/never order such equipment, beneficiaries geographically remote from the supplier with no related clinical claims, no qualifying face-to-face encounter, and abrupt post-enrolment claim volume from a new supplier. Enrolment-side signals include a virtual or non-conforming business location, a shared third-party biller, and payments routing to a single individual-controlled account.
117.features_to_create: Prepay edits for new/recently enrolled DME suppliers: cap payment pending site verification, require an ordering-NPI qualifying encounter within the lookback window, and reject claims where the ordering physician's specialty/location makes the order implausible or where the beneficiary has no other claims in the state. Add velocity triggers (claims per day, distinct beneficiaries per ordering NPI, submitted dollars in first 90 days) that auto-suspend payment and initiate beneficiary and physician verification letters.

118.ways_to_identify: Licensure and contract scope were checkable before any payment: the facility billed residential and partial-hospitalization levels of care for which it held no state license and no VA Community Care contract authorization. Staffing credential rosters versus the program's required clinician mix, and specialty 'veteran program' codes billed with services identical to standard care, are further prepay signals.
118.features_to_create: Build a service-to-licensure edit: for each billed level-of-care code, verify against the state licensing file that the facility's license category and bed authorization cover that service on the date of service, and against the network contract that the level of care is authorized; hard-deny non-covered scope. Add a staffing-credential attestation cross-check (licensed clinician FTEs per census pulled from credentialing data) and prepay documentation review of treatment plans for programs billing specialty/enhanced rates.

119.ways_to_identify: Medi-Cal's Code 1 rules make this adjudicable: payment requires an approved diagnosis on file or an approved treatment authorization request, so claims lacking a documented approved indication should never have paid. The signal is Code 1 drug claims with no diagnosis submitted or with a member diagnosis history inconsistent with the approved indication and no corresponding TAR.
119.features_to_create: Prepay edit for Code 1 formulary drugs: require a diagnosis code on the pharmacy claim and validate it against the approved-indication table, cross-referencing the member's medical-claim diagnosis history; deny when neither an approved diagnosis nor an approved authorization request exists. Add a chain/store-level metric on share of Code 1 fills paid without diagnosis substantiation to target audits and recoupment where legacy claims already paid.

120.ways_to_identify: At enrolment the consumer-directed program has both the member's address and the attendant's address plus the family relationship attestation; an attendant whose residence is hundreds of miles from the member and who is the spouse/legally responsible relative is a hard eligibility and feasibility conflict visible before the first timesheet is paid. At adjudication, the same person being both the employer-of-record approving timesheets and the beneficiary receiving care, plus implausible hour volumes (near-continuous coverage, hours exceeding the authorized plan of care), are all in the fiscal-agent timesheet data. No EVV geolocation records would exist matching the attendant to the member's home.
120.features_to_create: Build an enrolment-time edit in the fiscal-employer-agent system that geocodes attendant and member addresses and flags pairs beyond a calibrated commute distance, plus a relationship/self-approval edit that blocks a case where the approver, member and payee resolve to the same household or the attendant is a spouse barred from payment; hold claims pending manual review. Add a per-member per-period hour accumulator that suspends payment when billed hours exceed the authorized service plan or overlap the attendant's other employment/claims, and require EVV check-in/out geocoordinates within a radius of the member's residence as a condition of payment.

121.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic: the consumer-directed enrolment file contains the attendant's address, SSN and relationship to the member, so a spouse living hundreds of miles away being paid as attendant is detectable at enrolment rather than after 9,819 hours were billed. Timesheet data shows the member self-approving her own attendant's hours and cumulative hours far above the authorized plan of care and above same-program peers. Absence of any EVV location or telephony call originating at the member's home corroborates non-delivery pre-payment.
121.features_to_create: Implement enrolment screening that geocodes member/attendant address pairs and blocks or pends payment beyond a calibrated distance, and a conflict-of-interest edit where employer-of-record, beneficiary and payee are the same person or spouses. Layer a cumulative-hours edit per member per authorization period that suspends payment and triggers a documentation/EVV-record request when billed hours exceed authorized units or exceed the same-program peer percentile.

122.ways_to_identify: Newly enrolled Housing Stabilization Services providers with no service history, shared addresses/bank accounts/phone numbers and rapid revenue ramp to millions within months are visible in enrolment and claims-volume data before payment. Referral concentration is another signal: large blocks of members whose claims trace to a handful of addiction treatment centers or shelters, many of whom also have claims from other HSS providers for the same dates, and members lacking any documented needs assessment or housing-focused plan authorizing the service. Duplicate/templated service notes only surface on documentation request, so pair the volume trigger with prepay records review.
122.features_to_create: Build a new-provider ramp monitor for HSS: per-NPI monthly paid amount and distinct-member count with a velocity trigger that routes the provider to prepay documentation review (assessment, person-centered plan, dated service notes) once billing accelerates above the calibrated new-enroller percentile. Add prepay edits for member-level duplicate transition/sustaining units across providers on the same date, missing authorization/assessment on file, and units-per-consultant-day exceeding what one staffer could deliver; plus enrolment link analysis on shared address, bank account, phone and owner identity to cluster and suspend affiliated shells together.

123.ways_to_identify: This is government procurement (defense contract) fraud, not health care claims - the false statement is a certification that headsets met military specification testing. The payer-side analogue is invoice-payment certification: the contracting officer could require and match test reports/certificates of conformance to each lot before paying, and flag invoices where no test artifact exists for the serial/lot numbers delivered. Detection otherwise depends on self-disclosure or acceptance testing.
123.features_to_create: Nearest applicable control: an accounts-payable edit that will not release payment on a spec-critical line item until a matching lot/serial-level test report or certificate of conformance has been uploaded and the testing lab is on an approved list. Add a periodic sampling program that pulls delivered units for independent spec testing and suspends further payments to the vendor on any failure.

124.ways_to_identify: No health care claims component - this is SBA PPP/EIDL loan fraud. The lender/SBA could have caught it pre-disbursement by verifying submitted bank statements and tax returns directly against IRS transcripts and bank-provided data, and by flagging clusters of applications sharing the same preparer, IP address, email domain, phone or bank account across otherwise unrelated shell companies with no payroll filings.
124.features_to_create: Build a pre-disbursement application-linkage engine keyed on preparer identity, IP/device, contact details, bank routing/account and business address, which pends any application belonging to a cluster above the calibrated size. Require automated IRS transcript and bank-account verification of claimed payroll/revenue, with disbursement blocked where the submitted documents do not reconcile.

125.ways_to_identify: This is an annual enforcement round-up rather than a single scheme, so there is no specific pre-payment signal to reconstruct. The generalizable payer-side hooks are: linking survey/staffing/quality data (deficiency citations, staffing hours per resident day, ownership changes) to facility payment, and screening for the identity-theft-driven billing patterns typical of elder-targeted schemes such as claims for beneficiaries with no prior relationship to the biller.
125.features_to_create: Nearest applicable control: a facility-level quality-and-staffing feed that pends or flags nursing-home claims for review when reported staffing hours cannot support the billed census or when immediate-jeopardy/substandard-care citations are open. Additionally, a beneficiary-level alert when a new provider bills for a member outside the member's historical geographic and provider network, routing to prepay verification and beneficiary contact.

126.ways_to_identify: No scheme mechanics, defendants, or billed amounts are described - this is an announcement of investigative subpoenas, so there is nothing to catch pre-payment from this record. If specific allegations were that services were billed under codes not matching the procedure performed or with false diagnosis attestation, the payer route would be diagnosis-to-procedure consistency and prior-authorization documentation matching.
126.features_to_create: Nearest applicable control: a prepay code-to-diagnosis and age consistency edit for procedures with coverage criteria tied to documented clinical findings, pending claims that lack a matching authorization or diagnosis. Otherwise no payer-side control can be derived from this case.

127.ways_to_identify: No health care claims payment component - this concerns customs/tariff evasion by importers and is enforced through Tariff Act collection and FCA suits. The analogous pre-payment control sits with CBP entry data (declared value, country of origin, HTS classification) rather than any insurer.
127.features_to_create: No payer-side health care control applies. The nearest analogue is an entry-level import screening rule comparing declared unit values and origin against comparable-commodity distributions and transshipment patterns, holding release/liquidation for review on outliers.

128.ways_to_identify: Upcoding of repair type after Mohs is visible in claims: the ratio of flap-repair codes to simple/linear closure codes per Mohs surgeon, and the distribution of repair sizes (larger flap tiers) versus same-specialty peers, are computable before payment. Defect-size codes billed can also be checked against the number of Mohs stages/blocks billed on the same date - large flap tiers reported with single-stage, small-lesion Mohs are internally inconsistent. Confirmation requires the operative note, so a prepay documentation request on outliers closes it.
128.features_to_create: Build a per-NPI, per-facility monthly metric of flap/graft closure codes as a share of all post-Mohs repairs and mean billed repair size, with a trigger at the calibrated same-specialty percentile that puts the provider on prepay operative-note review for those code pairs. Add a claim-line edit flagging repair-size tier inconsistent with the Mohs stage/lesion codes billed on the same date and same anatomic site, pending the claim for documentation.

129.ways_to_identify: The stacking pattern is directly visible in claims: the same specimen date and same facility population showing a COVID-19 test plus a large respiratory pathogen panel for essentially every resident, with no symptom-bearing diagnosis codes and no variation by clinical presentation, is detectable at adjudication. Facility-level saturation (RPP billed for nearly 100% of residents at a long-term care site) and reimbursement per specimen far above peers are strong prepay flags. The sham per-facility marketing fee is found in the lab's contracts and ledgers, so pair claims flags with a credentialing/AKS attestation review and post-pay contract audit.
129.features_to_create: Build a specimen-level reflex-testing edit: when a high-cost multiplex respiratory panel is billed on the same date/specimen as a COVID-19 test, require a symptomatic diagnosis and treating-clinician order, and deny or pend absent both. Add a facility-cohort saturation metric (share of residents at a single congregate site receiving RPP from one lab per month) that suspends the lab's RPP payments and triggers a medical-necessity documentation request and AKS review of any per-facility marketing agreements.

130.ways_to_identify: Same detectable pattern: one lab billing thousands of respiratory pathogen panels concentrated at a defined set of long-term care facilities, with near-universal panel use per resident, no symptomatic diagnoses, and in some cases RPP billed with no corresponding COVID-19 test despite the swabbing pretext. Volume-based 1099 commission arrangements and flat per-facility 'marketing' fees are visible in credentialing disclosures and financial records, so a targeted contract request during enrolment revalidation adds confirmation.
130.features_to_create: Implement a prepay medical-necessity edit requiring symptomatic diagnosis plus a documented ordering clinician for multiplex respiratory panels, with automatic denial when the panel appears without any corresponding COVID test or clinician order for congregate-care specimens. Add a lab-level facility-concentration and per-resident panel-rate monitor that triggers payment suspension and a request for marketing/sales-rep compensation agreements when panel rates at referring facilities exceed the calibrated peer percentile.

131.ways_to_identify: Pharmacy claims data shows the signal before payment: a small set of prescribers generating extreme volumes of Schedule II stimulant prescriptions to geographically dispersed, mostly young adult patients with no prior treatment history, no covered E/M or telehealth encounter on file, and standardized dose/quantity patterns. The absence of any billed evaluation encounter preceding a controlled-substance fill, and PDMP data showing new-patient stimulant starts far above peers, are both available at adjudication. Re-emergence of the same prescriber roster under a new corporate entity (MMW) after pharmacies blocked the original is detectable by linking prescriber NPIs across billing entities.
131.features_to_create: Build a prescriber-level controlled-substance monitor computing monthly stimulant prescriptions, distinct patients, new-start rate, patient geographic spread and share of fills with no antecedent billed encounter; firing above the calibrated peer percentile places the prescriber's stimulant claims on prepay review or prior authorization. Add a pharmacy-benefit edit requiring a documented, billed telehealth or in-person evaluation within a defined lookback before paying an initial stimulant fill, and an entity-linkage rule that carries an existing block/flag to any new billing entity sharing prescriber NPIs, ownership or platform identifiers.

132.ways_to_identify: Coverage can be tied to device clearance: a payer can maintain the FDA-cleared indication for the specific device model used and deny ERG codes when the only device in the practice is cleared for VEP only, using the manufacturer/model reported on the claim or captured at credentialing. Claims-side signals include ERG billed for nearly every patient visit, ERG on patients without a covered retinal-disease diagnosis, and abrupt adoption clusters across many unrelated small practices seeded by one vendor's sales program. The FDA-submission failure itself is regulatory and only fully verifiable outside claims.
132.features_to_create: Build a device-to-code coverage table keyed to FDA clearance and require the device make/model on ERG claim lines; deny or pend lines where the reported device lacks clearance for the billed test. Add a per-provider ERG-per-patient-visit rate and diagnosis-eligibility edit that pends claims lacking a qualifying retinal diagnosis, plus a vendor-cluster alert that flags simultaneous ERG billing onset across practices sharing a single equipment supplier for coordinated prepay review.

133.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic as the related settlement: the payer can compare the billed ERG code against the FDA-cleared indication of the device model actually in use, information obtainable at credentialing or by requiring device identification on the claim. High-yield claims signals are ERG performed on a near-universal share of visits, absence of qualifying retinal pathology diagnoses, and synchronized billing onset across unrelated practices following one manufacturer's placement campaign.
133.features_to_create: Implement a prepay edit that denies ERG codes when the reported device model/UDI is not cleared for that test, and requires a qualifying diagnosis and prior imaging/exam findings for coverage. Add manufacturer-cluster analytics that group practices by equipment vendor and trigger prepay medical-necessity documentation review when ERG-per-visit rates exceed the calibrated peer percentile within a cluster.

134.ways_to_identify: Ordering-physician concentration is visible pre-payment: a mobile diagnostics company whose transcranial doppler volume traces to a small number of high-volume ordering physicians, each ordering TCD for an outsized share of their panel and without stroke/cerebrovascular indications, is an outlier pattern in claims. Space-rental and administrative-services agreements between the testing company and its referrers are disclosable at credentialing and revalidation; rent paid to the same physicians who order the tests, scaling with order volume, is the tell. Financial confirmation of the kickback requires records review, so combine claims flags with an agreement request.
134.features_to_create: Build an ordering-physician/testing-entity dyad metric: TCD studies per ordering NPI per month, share of that physician's patients tested, and share of the testing entity's volume from its top referrers, firing above the calibrated peer percentile to place the entity's TCD claims on prepay medical-necessity review. Add a credentialing rule requiring disclosure of any lease or administrative-services payments to referral sources, with automated cross-check flagging referrers who also receive payments and referring those dyads for AKS investigation and payment suspension.

135.ways_to_identify: Enrolment analytics would have surfaced 41 behavioral-health clinics credentialed and billed by a single offshore billing/credentialing agent sharing addresses, phones, bank accounts and NPI-application IP addresses - a cluster that could be pended before any high-dollar payment. Claims signals include implausible therapy hours per clinician per day, a beneficiary population concentrated among homeless and tribal members recruited through sober homes with duplicate billing across clinics for the same dates, and, for the wound-graft arm, extreme per-patient amniotic allograft units billed by nurse practitioners on hospice/elderly patients with square-centimeter amounts exceeding plausible wound size. Both arms show explosive new-provider revenue ramps detectable within the first billing cycles.
135.features_to_create: Build enrolment link analysis clustering applications by billing agent, address, phone, bank account and submission IP, with automatic prepay review or payment suspension for high-dollar behavioral-health claims from any cluster above the calibrated size; combine with a new-provider revenue-velocity trigger. Add prepay edits for provider-level therapy units exceeding staffed clinician capacity per day, cross-provider duplicate service dates per member, and skin-substitute claims where billed square centimeters, application frequency, or concurrent hospice election are inconsistent - pending payment for wound measurements, photographs and treating-physician orders.

136.ways_to_identify: Certifying-physician concentration is visible before payment: one physician certifying an outsized share of a single hospice's admissions, with certified patients whose diagnoses and prior claims history show no terminal decline, and with unusually long lengths of stay or live discharges. Financial relationships between the hospice and the certifying physician (medical-director or consulting payments not proportionate to work) are disclosable at enrolment and in the hospice's cost report. The kickback itself needs records review, so pair the certification-pattern flag with a documentation and agreement request before paying.
136.features_to_create: Build a certifying-physician/hospice dyad metric computing share of the hospice's certifications from each physician, beneficiary six-month-prognosis plausibility from prior diagnosis/utilization history, long-stay and live-discharge rates; above the calibrated peer percentile, place new admissions on prepay review requiring the certification narrative and clinical records. Add an enrolment cross-check flagging hospices whose certifying physicians also receive medical-director or other payments, routing to AKS review and, where certifications are unsupported, suspension of election-period payments.

137.ways_to_identify: Both mechanics are pure claims-data patterns: a COVID-testing entity billing an E/M service on nearly every specimen - often with no qualified clinician attached and identical code levels - and billing two to four COVID test codes for a single collection date on the same patient are detectable at adjudication. Unit-per-specimen and E/M-attachment rates versus other testing sites are computable per NPI per week. The auto-generated records defeat retrospective document review, so the control must be prepay volume/edit-based rather than reliance on requested charts.
137.features_to_create: Build a prepay edit limiting COVID-19 test codes to one payable unit per patient per collection date and denying duplicate/overlapping methodology codes on the same specimen; and a second edit denying E/M billed by a testing-only entity absent an identified rendering clinician and documented separate evaluation. Add an NPI-level ratio monitor (E/M claims per test claim, test units per patient-day) that triggers payment suspension when it exceeds the calibrated peer percentile, and treat identical templated notes across patients as a fraud indicator rather than substantiation.

138.ways_to_identify: Prescription and claims data show one physician's DEA number attached to Schedule II volumes and to Suboxone prescriptions written on dates and locations where he had no billed encounter, and to patients with no E/M claim from him at all - a prescriber-to-encounter mismatch computable at adjudication. Also visible: signatures/attestations on records for patients whose visits were billed by a different NPI, and clinic-level opioid prescribing per patient far above pain-management peers. PDMP-to-claims linkage flags prescriptions issued while the prescriber was demonstrably not practicing.
138.features_to_create: Build a prescriber-encounter linkage edit that pends or denies controlled-substance pharmacy claims where no encounter by that prescriber exists for the patient within a defined lookback, and flags a single DEA number used across multiple mid-level or unauthorized providers/locations. Add clinic-level opioid MME-per-patient and Schedule II scripts-per-prescriber-day monitors that trigger prepay review of the practice's professional claims plus a records request comparing rendering-provider attestation to the billed NPI, escalating to prescriber payment suspension and DEA referral.

139.ways_to_identify: The ordering physician's claims show hereditary cancer panels, other lab tests and orthotic braces ordered for large numbers of beneficiaries with no prior or concurrent treating relationship, many clustered by assisted-living/adult-day-care addresses and by event dates, alongside high-level office visit codes billed at volumes exceeding available clinic hours. Genetic-panel orders without a cancer diagnosis or documented family history, and multiple braces per beneficiary from a single supplier, are all prepay-detectable. Supplier/lab-to-orderer concentration (one physician driving most of two labs' and one DME company's volume) is likewise computable before payment.
139.features_to_create: Build an ordering-physician edit that denies or pends high-cost genetic panels and orthotic braces when the ordering NPI has no prior qualifying encounter with the beneficiary and the claim lacks a supporting diagnosis/family-history indicator, and caps braces per beneficiary per period across suppliers. Add a physician time-plausibility check (billed E/M minutes plus test-order volume per day versus feasible hours) and an orderer-concentration metric per lab/DME supplier; exceeding the calibrated percentile triggers payment suspension for that dyad and a records/medical-necessity request, plus AKS referral.

140.ways_to_identify: The impossible-day signals were all visible prepay: claim dates while the beneficiary was incarcerated (CMS inmate/Prisoner file), while the beneficiary or the billing/rendering provider was outside the country (CBP/passport travel data, or provider absence inferred from zero-claim gaps at other sites), and dates when the clinic was closed (weekends/holidays, posted hours, utility or badge data). Botox volume per NPI versus same-specialty peers and per-beneficiary injection frequency far above the calibrated percentile is also a prepay screen. Falsified records surfaced only after subpoena, but a pre-payment documentation request on the outlier population would have forced early production.
140.features_to_create: Build a claim-line eligibility/impossible-day edit that denies or pends any date of service where the beneficiary appears on the incarceration or deceased file, or where the rendering NPI has documented out-of-country travel, plus a service-date-versus-practice-calendar edit flagging dates the practice reports as closed. Add a provider-level Botox/J-code utilization outlier model (units per beneficiary per year, share of panel receiving injections versus same-specialty peers) that triggers prepay review and a medical-records request, escalating to payment suspension on credible fraud.[detect]

141.ways_to_identify: No claims-payment component: this is unauthorized PHI access and false statements to a licensing board, with no billing or payer loss. The detectable signal lives in EHR audit logs — record access by a clinician with no encounter, order, or care-team relationship to the patient — and in state-board disciplinary and NPDB feeds at credentialing time.
141.features_to_create: Nearest applicable control: an EHR access-audit rule that joins each record-view event to the patient's active encounters, orders and care-team assignments and fires a privacy investigation when a user views records with no treatment relationship, weighted for same-sex/age-pattern browsing. At credentialing, automate NPDB/state-board query refresh so board findings and false-statement adjudications block or flag network participation.[detect]

142.ways_to_identify: Wholly visible prepay: one ordering NPI appears as certifier on braces and hereditary cancer panels for thousands of beneficiaries spread across many states with no companion E/M claim from that NPI and no prior treating relationship in claims history. Telemedicine-only or absent encounter, distance between ordering provider and beneficiary, and concentration of the same ordering NPI across a handful of DME suppliers and labs are all computable at adjudication. The undercover-agent beneficiaries would themselves have flagged as members with no clinical history matching the order.
142.features_to_create: Build an ordering-provider linkage edit: for DME braces (L-codes) and hereditary cancer panels, require a paid E/M or covered telehealth encounter with the ordering NPI within a lookback window; if absent, deny prepay pending records. Add a certifier-network model computing per-ordering-NPI counts of unique beneficiaries, distinct states, distinct billing suppliers/labs, and share of orders with no prior relationship versus same-specialty peers, firing prepay review of all downstream supplier/lab claims tied to that NPI and referral for revocation.[detect]

143.ways_to_identify: The signature is reflexive definitive UDT at every visit from an in-office lab: near-1.0 ratio of definitive drug-test claims to office visits, and use of the highest-tier definitive code (largest analyte class count) for essentially the entire panel, versus same-specialty peers. Self-referral to a commonly owned lab is visible from shared address, TIN, and ownership data on the CMS-855 enrollment. Pair with the prescriber's controlled-substance volume and MME per patient from Part D/state PDMP.
143.features_to_create: Build a prescriber-level edit computing definitive UDT claims per patient encounter and the share billed at the top analyte tier; when both exceed the calibrated percentile against same-specialty peers, deny or pend the definitive test lines and allow only presumptive testing pending documentation of individualized medical necessity. Add a linkage rule flagging labs sharing address/TIN/ownership with the ordering practice and route their claims to prepay review, plus a PDMP-linked high-MME prescriber flag.[detect]

144.ways_to_identify: Detectable prepay through clustering: many beneficiaries residing at the same assisted living/adult day/retirement addresses receive identical high-cost cancer panels ordered by a single physician on the same or adjacent dates, alongside COVID test claims, with no prior treating relationship. The same physician also bills top-level prolonged E/M for those beneficiaries — implausible time-in-day totals per rendering NPI per date. Kickbacks themselves need post-payment proof, but the referral concentration between the physician, two labs and one DME supplier is computable at adjudication.
144.features_to_create: Build a cohort-clustering detector keyed on beneficiary residence address plus ordering NPI plus test code, firing when a single orderer generates same-code high-cost genetic panels for many co-resident beneficiaries within a short window; pend the lab and DME lines and request the ordering record. Add a per-rendering-NPI daily time-accumulation edit that denies E/M levels whose summed typical minutes exceed a plausible workday, and a referral-concentration score (share of a lab's or supplier's volume from one orderer) triggering prepay review and suspension.[detect]

145.ways_to_identify: Not a specific fraud case — it is an enforcement-priority announcement with no claims, provider or loss mechanics to detect. No case-level payer detection applies.
145.features_to_create: Nearest applicable control: maintain a mapped portfolio of prepay and post-pay analytics covering the named priority areas — MA risk-adjustment diagnosis validation (chart-unsupported HCCs), drug/device price-and-rebate reporting reconciliation, network-adequacy access audits, referral-concentration kickback scoring, and EHR-driven upcoding/cloned-note detection — each with an owner and a fire-to-action path.[detect]

146.ways_to_identify: Catchable at enrollment: nominee-owner structures show up as new DME suppliers sharing addresses, phone numbers, bank accounts, billing agents, surety bonds and IP/submitter IDs with each other and with a previously excluded or convicted individual; the hidden owner appears in corporate registry, UCC and bank signatory records not matching the CMS-855S disclosure. Post-enrollment, the five suppliers billing identical L-code mixes with overlapping beneficiaries and recruiter-sourced referrals is a prepay signal.
146.features_to_create: Build an enrollment-time entity-resolution graph linking applicants by address, phone, bank routing/account, EFT payee, submitter ID, registered agent and owner identity, and auto-refer any applicant linked to an excluded/convicted person or to a common nominee for site visit and denial; screen all disclosed and inferred owners against LEIE, GSA and criminal-history sources continuously. Layer a new-supplier prepay hold with escalating documentation requests when claim ramp rate, beneficiary overlap across linked suppliers, and single-recruiter beneficiary concentration exceed calibrated percentiles.[detect]

147.ways_to_identify: No payer-side claims component: this is SBA PPP/EIDL loan fraud, not health care billing. The detectable signals sat with the lenders and SBA — applicant entities with no payroll filings, tax transcripts that do not match IRS records, duplicate applications for related entities across multiple banks, and shared addresses/owners/bank accounts.
147.features_to_create: No payer claims control applies. Nearest equivalent: at the funding agency, an application-time edit that reconciles claimed wages and employee counts against IRS transcript and state wage-report data, plus cross-lender entity resolution on EIN, owner SSN, address and bank account to flag multiple applications by one controller; mismatch or duplication holds disbursement pending verification.[detect]

148.ways_to_identify: This is an annual collections round-up covering two unrelated defendants with no billing mechanics described, so nothing case-specific is detectable. The generally applicable prepay signals for the hospice component are long-stay non-terminal patients, high continuous/general-inpatient day share, and physician certifications without supporting decline documentation; the misbranded-injectable component is caught through drug pedigree/NDC and licensure checks rather than claim analytics.
148.features_to_create: Nearest applicable controls: a hospice provider-level model on median length of stay, share of beneficiaries exceeding long-stay thresholds, live-discharge rate and GIP/continuous-care day share versus peers, firing prepay medical-record review and payment suspension on credible allegation. For drugs, an NDC-validity and licensed-supplier edit denying claims for products not in the approved drug file or dispensed by unlicensed/unauthorized entities.[detect]

149.ways_to_identify: No health care claims component: EIDL and Pandemic Unemployment Assistance fraud using stolen identities. Detectable at application by the benefit agencies through identity-proofing failures, SSNs and names that do not match SSA/state wage records, and many applications routing to a common set of bank accounts, IP addresses, devices and phone numbers.
149.features_to_create: No payer claims control applies. Nearest equivalent for any benefit payer: application-time identity verification against authoritative sources plus a payment-routing graph that counts distinct applicant identities sharing a bank account, debit card, device fingerprint or IP; exceeding the calibrated threshold holds disbursement and triggers manual identity proofing.[detect]

150.ways_to_identify: Prepay signal is extreme referral concentration: a single pain clinic prescriber accounts for an outsized share of one pharmacy's high-cost compounded drug claims, with per-claim amounts and refill counts far above peers and a narrow set of expensive compound formulas. The kickback conduit — the prescriber's son on the pharmacy's payroll as a 'marketer' — is discoverable from ownership/employee disclosures, corporate filings and shared surname/address matching against the prescriber's identity.
150.features_to_create: Build a prescriber-pharmacy dyad model computing each pharmacy's claim-dollar share from a single prescriber, average compound claim cost and formula concentration, firing prepay review and prior authorization on compounded claims when the dyad exceeds the calibrated percentile.
