Add a relationship-screening rule matching pharmacy owners, employees and marketing contractors against high-volume prescribers' names, addresses and family links, routing matches to kickback investigation.[detect]

151.ways_to_identify: Not a fraud case — a personnel announcement. Nothing to detect and no payer data involved.

152.ways_to_identify: Not a health care fraud case and no claims were submitted; there is no payer-side signal. If the defendant were an enrolled provider, the only payer-relevant hook would be criminal-history and licensure monitoring.
152.features_to_create: No payer claims control applies. Nearest equivalent: continuous criminal-conviction, exclusion-list and licensure monitoring of enrolled providers and their employees, auto-terminating participation on a disqualifying conviction.[detect]

153.ways_to_identify: Prepay-visible: services billed under a physician NPI on dates when the practice's only clinicians present were NPs/PAs — testable against the practice's rostered staff, licensure files and the volume-per-physician-day implied by claims. Billing implanted neurostimulator codes from a chiropractic-owned office with no facility, anesthesia, or operative claim on the same date is an internally inconsistent claim combination. Allergy-injection and neurostimulator claims with no corresponding drug/device NDC or HCPCS supply line, and no supplier invoice, are also checkable prepay.
153.features_to_create: Build a rendering-provider plausibility edit comparing billed rendering NPIs against the practice's credentialed staff roster and per-provider daily service totals, denying or pending physician-rate claims that exceed plausible physician presence and requiring incident-to documentation. Add code-consistency edits: deny neurostimulator implantation codes billed by non-surgical specialties or without a same-date facility/anesthesia/device-supply claim, and deny injection administration codes lacking a paired drug/device line.[detect]

154.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic as the related case and equally visible prepay: claims billed at physician rates while the actual renderers were mid-levels, detectable by reconciling rendering NPIs against the practice's credentialed roster, licensure type, and implied physician service-hours per day. Neurostimulator implant codes billed by a chiropractic practice with no operative, facility or device-supply line is a code-eligibility contradiction; allergy injections with no drug supply line or purchase volume to support them is another.
154.features_to_create: Implement a rendering-identity/scope edit that cross-checks each claim's rendering NPI against taxonomy, state scope of practice and the practice's roster, pending physician-rate payment when the service could not have been personally performed. Add specialty-eligibility edits denying implanted neurostimulator and allergy-immunotherapy administration codes absent same-date device/drug supply lines and a facility claim, and reconcile billed injection units against distributor purchase data on audit.[detect]

155.ways_to_identify: Prepay signals of body-brokering: clusters of newly enrolled, out-of-state members with recently purchased individual policies all admitting to the same facility/sober-home pair, often with premiums paid by a third party, plus repeat admissions of the same members cycling between facilities. Facility claim patterns show high-cost UDT and residential day billing per admission and a small number of referral sources supplying most admissions.
155.features_to_create: Build an admission-cohort model per facility computing share of admissions from out-of-area members, days from policy effective date to admission, third-party premium payment flags, and readmission cycling across affiliated facilities; exceeding the calibrated percentile triggers prepay review, verification of the member's residence and referral source, and documentation requests. Add a referral-source concentration score and flag any facility payments to individuals who are not licensed clinicians for kickback investigation.[detect]

156.ways_to_identify: Not detectable in a single claim: the device was FDA-cleared and the implant claims looked normal. The route is post-payment device-outcome surveillance — linking implanted device identifiers (UDI/lot on the operative claim or hospital implant log) to subsequent revision-surgery claims to compute time-to-revision by device model versus comparators, plus monitoring MAUDE complaint volumes and manufacturer internal knowledge surfaced by qui tam.
156.features_to_create: Build a device-registry analytic that joins UDI/device model captured at implant to downstream revision/removal claims for the same beneficiary and joint, computing model-level revision hazard rates versus peer devices; when a model exceeds the calibrated benchmark, open a manufacturer FCA/recovery referral and flag the model for prior authorization. Require UDI capture on implant claims as a prepay data-completeness edit so the linkage is possible.[detect]

157.ways_to_identify: No claims-payment fraud: this is employment-tax theft by a home-care employer, with the loss to IRS and employees, not to the payer. Detectable by tax authorities from a filer that shows wage withholding on W-2s issued to employees but no filed W-2/W-3 or Form 941 deposits, and by the payer only indirectly through payroll-tax noncompliance signals during provider financial screening.
157.features_to_create: No direct payer claims control; nearest payer-side check is an enrollment/revalidation financial-integrity screen that verifies the provider's employment-tax filing status and any federal tax liens for Medicaid/Medicare home-care participation, flagging nonfilers for corrective action. At the tax agency, an automated edit comparing employee-reported withholding on returns against employer 941/W-2 filings, firing when withholding is claimed with no matching employer remittance.[detect]

158.ways_to_identify: Fully checkable at enrollment: applications reporting income implausibly clustered just above the subsidy-eligibility floor, with income attestations that fail IRS/SSA and Equifax data-matching, mismatched or shelter/PO-box addresses, and SSN-name mismatches. Broker-level clustering — one NPN or brokerage submitting many such applications, repeatedly switching enrollees' plans or agents of record — is visible before subsidies are paid.
158.features_to_create: Build an application-time edit that scores each enrollment on income-attestation deviation from IRS/SSA data, proximity of attested income to the eligibility threshold, address reuse across unrelated applicants, and SSN/name mismatch; failures require documentary income verification before advance premium tax credits begin. Add a broker/agent-level anomaly model on volume, data-match failure rate, threshold-clustering and unauthorized agent-of-record changes, suspending the broker's marketplace access and withholding commissions pending review.[detect]

159.ways_to_identify: Pure claim-edit issue, visible at adjudication: E/M billed on the same date of service as bilateral intravitreal injections for the same beneficiary and provider, without a valid modifier or documented separately identifiable service, contrary to NCCI/global-period rules. Provider-level rate of same-day E/M-plus-injection pairs versus same-specialty peers identifies the systematic biller.
159.features_to_create: Implement an NCCI/global-surgery bundling edit that automatically denies same-date E/M lines paired with eye injection procedure codes for the same beneficiary/provider unless a supported modifier is present, and validate modifier use by sampling records. Add a provider scorecard on the share of injection encounters carrying a separately billed E/M and modifier-override frequency, referring outliers above the calibrated percentile for prepay documentation review and overpayment recovery.[detect]

160.ways_to_identify: This is an annual DOJ round-up rather than a single case, so there is no one mechanic to edit against; the recurring signals across its components are, however, all payer-observable: opioid dispensing volumes and MME/day per prescriber and pharmacy, therapy minutes clustered at the top RUG/quota threshold, inpatient behavioral length-of-stay and admission-criteria documentation, dispensed-but-never-picked-up prescriptions still billed, and physician compensation above fair market value or in excess of collections in credentialing/Stark disclosures. Retained-overpayment components are only detectable post-payment via credit-balance and self-audit reporting timelines.
160.features_to_create: Build a provider-level composite risk board that scores each enrolled entity on peer-relative dispensing MME, therapy-minute clustering at reimbursement thresholds, inpatient behavioral readmission/LOS outliers, and Part D reversal-without-return reconciliation, firing prepay review when multiple domains exceed calibrated percentiles. Add a Stark/AKS attestation feed at credentialing that compares physician compensation to collections and to same-specialty FMV bands, and a 60-day overpayment clock that flags unreturned identified credit balances for demand letters.

161.ways_to_identify: Amniotic membrane insertion (e.g., CPT 65778/65779 plus the Q-code product) is a low-frequency procedure; a single optometrist accounting for hundreds of such claims is a stark volume and specialty-scope outlier visible at adjudication. Payers can also reconcile billed membrane units against the provider's purchase invoices from the tissue supplier, and check scope-of-practice rules for optometrists performing the procedure. The audit-interference conduct is only reachable post-payment, but the audit itself should have been protected from external inquiry by logging contacts.
161.features_to_create: Prepay edit: cap and manually review amniotic membrane/tissue-graft claims when a provider's per-beneficiary or monthly volume exceeds the calibrated same-specialty percentile, and require the tissue product invoice/lot number on the claim, denying when lot data are absent or duplicated across patients. Add a scope-of-practice edit blocking the procedure code for non-authorized taxonomies, and an audit-integrity control that logs and escalates any third-party or political inquiry into an open provider audit.

162.ways_to_identify: Multi-state Medicaid claims can be screened against eligibility, death-master and correctional-custody files to catch billing for deceased or incarcerated beneficiaries, and against NPI-to-employer consistency to catch NPIs rented or harvested through fake job applications. Rendering-provider NPIs appearing suddenly at unrelated new entities, and high-complexity urine drug testing paired with every psychotherapy visit, are both visible pre-payment. Investigator-created fictitious beneficiary IDs surfacing on claims is itself a decisive detection signal if the sentinel IDs are wired into adjudication.
162.features_to_create: Build prepay eligibility edits denying claims whose service dates fall inside a date-of-death or incarceration window, plus a sentinel-ID tripwire that suspends and refers any provider billing a decoy beneficiary. Add an NPI-affiliation monitor that flags rendering NPIs newly linked to a group with no prior claim history or with implausible geography, and a definitive-UDT frequency edit requiring documentation when presumptive/definitive test rates exceed same-specialty percentiles; new behavioral-health enrollees go on prepay review with service-note sampling.

163.ways_to_identify: Single-use device reuse is visible as a mismatch between the count of procedures billed and the provider's documented device purchases or the absence of any billed/supplied disposable per encounter, which a payer can test by requesting purchase invoices. The medical-necessity side shows as an outlier rate of the same gynecologic procedure per patient and repeat procedures at short intervals versus same-specialty peers. Sanitary-condition and adulteration facts come from site visits and FDA/board referrals rather than claims.
163.features_to_create: Prepay edit: for procedures requiring a single-use disposable, compare the provider's monthly procedure volume against supplier purchase records or billed device units and suspend payment with a documentation request when procedures exceed devices acquired. Add a per-beneficiary repeat-procedure frequency edit for gynecologic procedures with automatic records review above the calibrated percentile, and route sanitation/reuse allegations to a site-visit and licensing-board referral queue.

164.ways_to_identify: The decisive signals are all in the claim data: the same rendering clinician billed by two or more employers for different recipients at overlapping times, and service dates that fall while he was abroad, which can be tested against impossible-day totals and, where available, EVV geolocation. Cumulative billed hours per clinician per day exceeding a feasible workday is computable pre-payment across all payers of the same Medicaid program.
164.features_to_create: Build a rendering-clinician daily-hours aggregator across all billing entities that denies or suspends claims when summed units exceed a feasible workday or when two encounters overlap in time for different recipients. Require EVV check-in/out with geolocation for skill-building services and auto-deny units lacking a matching visit record; flag clinicians whose billed days form continuous blocks with no gaps for documentation request.

165.ways_to_identify: Inducement schemes show up as explosive enrollee growth at one small care-coordination provider concentrated in a narrow geography and referral source, with claims for every enrollee at the maximum allowed units and little or no downstream prenatal care claims from OB providers. Beneficiary outreach or verification letters asking whether coordination visits occurred is a cheap pre-payment test for new providers.
165.features_to_create: Place newly enrolled prenatal care-coordination providers on prepay review with a documented-visit note and beneficiary attestation required for payment. Build a provider-level monitor computing new-member growth rate, share of members billed at maximum units, and absence of corroborating prenatal claims from a distinct OB provider, firing suspension and a beneficiary-verification mailing when several exceed calibrated thresholds; screen marketing/gift expenditures at enrollment as an AKS attestation.

166.ways_to_identify: The backdating is directly detectable: service dates precede the client's enrollment/assignment date with that provider, and often precede the pregnancy episode itself, all checkable at adjudication. Cash enrollment bonuses show as clustered same-day sign-ups from one recruiter and a member roster far larger than the provider's staffed capacity.
166.features_to_create: Prepay edit denying any care-coordination claim whose date of service precedes the member's enrollment/assignment effective date with the billing provider or falls outside the documented pregnancy/postpartum window. Add a capacity check comparing billed coordination hours to credentialed staff FTEs and a same-day mass-enrollment detector, both triggering payment suspension and beneficiary verification letters.

167.ways_to_identify: This is a general office-activity press release with no defendant, payer, service line, or scheme mechanics described, so no case-specific pre-payment signal can be derived; the only route is the post-payment qui tam/settlement channel that produced it.
167.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies to this item as written. The nearest applicable control is a standing intake process that converts FCA/AKS settlement terms into concrete prepay edits and provider watchlist entries once the underlying mechanics are published.

168.ways_to_identify: At enrolment the ownership disclosure could have been cross-matched to the state exclusion list, which would have exposed the concealed excluded co-owner. In claims, one provider having nearly every child qualified by a single QSP assessor and billed at the maximum authorized ABA hours, with technician hours exceeding credentialed staff capacity and technicians who are minors/relatives, is all computable pre-payment; forged QSP and provider signatures on authorizations can be tested by signature/credential verification. Parent cash kickbacks surface through beneficiary interviews and shared-address clustering.
168.features_to_create: Build an enrolment control that resolves all disclosed and inferred owners/managers (address, phone, bank account, tax ID overlap) against exclusion lists and denies or revokes on match. Add an EIDBI/ABA analytic firing when a provider's share of members billed at maximum authorized units, single-assessor qualification concentration, or billed technician hours per staff FTE exceed calibrated percentiles, with automatic prepay suspension, signature verification on authorizations, and cross-program linkage to child-nutrition site rosters at the same address.

169.ways_to_identify: Enrolment identity-proofing is the common failure: companies were enrolled using a stolen physician's and a stolen optometrist's identities, which contact-verification calls to the licensee of record, bank-account/address matching and license-board cross-checks would expose before any claim paid. In claims, brace and office-visit volumes implausible for the staff and location, telehealth-ordered DME where no encounter exists between the ordering physician and the beneficiary, and duplicate billing of the same visits to Medicare, Medi-Cal and the HRSA uninsured program are all pre-payment signals. Drug diversion by the nurse is caught by dispensing-cabinet/waste reconciliation, not claims.
169.features_to_create: Implement enrolment identity verification that calls the licensee at their board-registered contact, matches EFT account ownership to the disclosed owner, and holds first payments pending verification; auto-deny COVID/uninsured-program claims duplicating a claim for the same beneficiary-date already paid by Medicare or Medicaid. Add a DME prepay edit requiring an ordering-provider encounter with the beneficiary within a lookback window and flagging ordering NPIs whose orders concentrate at one telemedicine entity or exceed same-specialty percentiles; refer controlled-substance waste discrepancies from facility ADC logs to investigators.

170.ways_to_identify: Billed drug quantities can be reconciled against wholesaler acquisition data (ARCOS/837-independent purchase reporting or supplier invoices requested from the pharmacy) - a pharmacy cannot dispense more units than it bought. Pre-payment flags include NDC-level billed units exceeding plausible inventory, high-cost drug concentration, and dispensing without corresponding prescriber e-prescribing records.
170.features_to_create: Build an invoice-versus-claims reconciliation engine at pharmacy-NDC-month granularity: cumulative billed units minus documented purchases; when the gap exceeds a calibrated tolerance, suspend payment and issue a purchase-invoice documentation request. Add prepay edits for missing/unmatched prescriber e-prescription records and for beneficiaries with no other claim activity in the pharmacy's service area.

171.ways_to_identify: CGX claims arriving for beneficiaries who have no cancer diagnosis, no treating-oncologist relationship, and whose ordering physician is a distant telemarketing-linked provider are visible at adjudication; geographic dispersion between beneficiary, ordering provider and lab is a strong pre-payment marker. Payer complaint lines and beneficiary reports of unsolicited test kits give early warning; per-test 'marketing' payments appear only in post-payment financial review.
171.features_to_create: Prepay edit for hereditary-cancer panels requiring a cancer or documented family-history diagnosis plus an ordering provider with a prior E/M relationship with the beneficiary within a lookback window; deny or pend for records otherwise. Add a lab-level analytic on ordering-provider concentration, beneficiary-to-lab distance and unsolicited-kit complaint counts, triggering prepay review and an AKS marketing-contract audit when above calibrated percentiles.

172.ways_to_identify: Brace claims from multiple DME suppliers routed through one billing company, sharing ordering physicians, addresses and bank accounts, and with sibling/common ownership, are linkable at enrolment and adjudication. Ordering physicians whose brace-order volume dwarfs their peers, or who order for beneficiaries in states they never practice in, indicate purchased or forged orders; signature verification against the prescriber's on-file exemplar and prescriber outreach are cheap pre-payment tests.
172.features_to_create: Build a supplier-affiliation graph keyed on billing agent, owner identity, address, phone and EFT account that pools brace billing across related suppliers and applies aggregate prepay review when pooled volume or ordering-provider overlap exceeds calibrated percentiles. Add an ordering-provider validation service that pends orthotic claims for prescriber confirmation when the ordering NPI's brace-order rate is an outlier or when beneficiary-prescriber distance is implausible.

173.ways_to_identify: An excluded individual concealing ownership is catchable at enrolment by resolving indirect owners, managers, authorized officials, addresses, phones and bank accounts against the exclusion database and prior revoked-provider records, and by site visits confirming who actually controls the business. In claims, brace volumes generated by out-of-state call centers show as ordering-provider concentration and beneficiary-supplier geographic dispersion before payment.
173.features_to_create: Enrolment control: fuzzy-match all disclosed and inferred owners/officers/agents (name, SSN, DOB, address, phone, EFT) against exclusion and prior-revocation lists, plus adverse-media/affiliate linkage, and deny enrolment or revoke with payment suspension on match. Layer a new-supplier prepay hold on orthotic claims until a site visit and first-claim audit clear, and flag suppliers whose orders trace to a small set of call-center-linked ordering NPIs.

174.ways_to_identify: This is an off-the-books payroll, tax and workers'-compensation premium fraud with no health care claims submitted, so there is no pre-payment claims signal for a health payer; detection sits with IRS wage-reporting mismatches, check-cashing/CTR patterns at the check casher, and comparison of insurer-reported payroll to contract volumes and certified payrolls.
174.features_to_create: No payer-side claims control applies. The nearest control is a workers'-compensation carrier premium-audit rule comparing declared payroll to state wage filings, subcontractor payment records and job-site headcounts, firing an audit when declared payroll per contract dollar falls below industry benchmarks.

175.ways_to_identify: Compounded topical creams, 'foot soaks' and similar high-cost non-formulary items concentrated at a few pharmacies, with prescribers who never had an in-person or documented telehealth encounter with the beneficiary and who prescribe across many distant states, are visible at Part D adjudication. Beneficiary complaints about telemarketing calls and identical prescription templates (same drug mix, same quantities, same refills) across unrelated patients are strong pre-payment markers.
175.features_to_create: Prepay edit requiring prior authorization for high-cost compounded topicals with a documented prescriber-beneficiary encounter within a lookback window and denial where the prescriber's state/geography does not match the beneficiary. Add pharmacy- and prescriber-level analytics on compound-claim concentration, template-identical formulations and prescriber-pharmacy pairing exclusivity, triggering payment suspension and an AKS contract/financial-flow audit above calibrated percentiles.

176.ways_to_identify: Claims for COVID test kits mailed to beneficiaries who never requested them show as unsolicited-item patterns: no ordering-provider relationship, no prior claims from the beneficiary in that region, bulk identical claims across purchased beneficiary IDs, and duplicate kit claims for the same member within short windows. Beneficiary MSN complaints and the ineligibility of the billed item under the benefit are both checkable before payment.
176.features_to_create: Prepay edit denying test-kit/OTC claims for codes not covered under the benefit and rejecting duplicates beyond the allowed per-member frequency. Add a provider-level analytic on share of beneficiaries with no prior claim relationship, geographic dispersion and same-day claim bursts across sequential beneficiary IDs, firing payment suspension plus beneficiary verification mailing; cross-check enrolled entity owners against known ID-purchase networks.

177.ways_to_identify: The tell is that the lead-generator/order-signer is also a part owner of the supplier receiving the claims - detectable by matching supplier ownership disclosures against the entities receiving 'marketing' payments and against the NPIs appearing as ordering or referral sources. In claims, a supplier whose brace orders trace overwhelmingly to one lead source, with flat per-order payments disguised as hourly marketing invoices, is reviewable pre-payment.
177.features_to_create: Build an ownership-versus-referral-source conflict check: flag and pend claims where the ordering provider, marketer or lead vendor shares ownership, address or bank account with the billing supplier, requiring an AKS safe-harbor attestation and contract production. Add a referral-concentration metric per supplier (share of orders from a single source) that triggers prepay review above the calibrated percentile.

178.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic as the other brace mills: orthotic claims for beneficiaries with no ordering-provider encounter, orders sourced from kickback-paid lead vendors, and a supplier whose investor/owner set overlaps with other suppliers already under investigation. Once co-conspirators were arrested, ongoing payments to affiliated entities and post-arrest transfers of proceeds should have triggered an affiliate-based payment suspension rather than continued payment.
178.features_to_create: Maintain an affiliation graph linking suppliers by owners, investors, addresses, EFT accounts and billing agents, and automatically extend payment suspension to all affiliated TINs when any node is indicted or has payments suspended. Keep the standing orthotic prepay edit requiring a documented ordering-provider encounter and beneficiary confirmation of medical need before payment.

179.ways_to_identify: Prescriptions manufactured by a call center appear as ordering NPIs signing brace orders in volumes and geographies inconsistent with their practice, beneficiaries with no encounter history with the signer, and identical order templates across many patients; the same billing company submitting for multiple related suppliers links the network at enrolment. Beneficiary complaints about cold calls and MSN entries for braces never wanted give early, pre-payment warning when routed into the edit logic.
179.features_to_create: Prepay edit: pend orthotic claims where no encounter exists between the ordering provider and beneficiary in the lookback window, where the ordering NPI's order volume or out-of-state share exceeds calibrated percentiles, or where the order signature/authorization fails prescriber confirmation. Add cross-payer sharing so Medicare Advantage plans and FFS pool supplier/billing-agent affiliation and complaint signals, and suspend all suppliers sharing a billing agent once one is flagged.

180.ways_to_identify: At enrolment, the sham suppliers share addresses, bank accounts, phone numbers, mail drops and a nominee/beneficial owner network with previously revoked DME PTANs, and the owner concealed ownership on the 855S — resolvable by cross-matching 855S disclosable parties against corporate registries, licensing records and prior revocation lists. At adjudication the pattern is unmistakable: L-code orthotic braces billed nationwide to beneficiaries with no geographic or care relationship to the supplier, ordered by a tiny set of telemedicine prescribers who each 'order' braces for hundreds of beneficiaries with no prior or subsequent visit, often multiple braces per beneficiary and duplicate HICNs across sibling suppliers. Beneficiary complaint intake ('I never ordered this') and identity-theft flags on the beneficiary IDs add corroboration prepay.
180.features_to_create: Build an enrolment graph-linkage screen keyed on address/phone/bank/registered-agent/owner identity that scores new DME applicants for shared identifiers with revoked or high-risk suppliers, holding the PTAN for site visit and beneficial-ownership verification. At claim level, build a prepay edit on orthotic brace HCPCS that computes, per ordering NPI, the share of orders with no evaluation/management encounter with that beneficiary in the prior and following look-back window, the beneficiary-state-to-supplier-state distance distribution, and the count of distinct suppliers sharing that prescriber; claims from prescribers above the calibrated percentile suspend for documentation of a bona fide clinical encounter, and suppliers with beneficiary-ID overlap to other flagged suppliers go to payment suspension.

181.ways_to_identify: No health-care claims-payment component: this is embezzlement from a special-needs trust administrator, detectable through fiduciary audit, not claim adjudication. The observable route is post-hoc: annual independent reconciliation of pooled-trust bank/custodial balances to per-beneficiary statement balances, and trustee bonding/audit filings required by state courts and Medicaid third-party-trust rules. Bank-side signals (transfers from trust accounts to owner-controlled LLCs, real estate and aircraft purchases) would be caught by AML monitoring.
181.features_to_create: Nearest payer-side control: for Medicaid agencies that approve (d)(4)(A)/(d)(4)(C) pooled trusts, require and automatically track annual third-party attestation reconciling custodial cash to sum of beneficiary sub-account balances, firing a review when the reconciliation is missing, late, or shows an unexplained delta. Add a rule flagging trust-administrator disbursements to entities sharing officers with the administrator; no claim-level edit applies.

182.ways_to_identify: At adjudication the tell is diagnosis-result decoupling: essentially every trans-cranial doppler claim from this practice carries the same qualifying cerebral occlusion/stenosis ICD-10 code, at a positivity rate far above same-specialty and same-test peers, and the diagnosis appears on the ordering claim before any interpretive report exists. Also visible: an ophthalmology practice ordering high-volume vascular ultrasound at a rate far above optometry/ophthalmology peers, a single third-party mobile TCD entity appearing under many practices, and concentration of downstream radiology referrals into one group (a Stark/AKS financial-relationship signal available from the practice's own disclosures and from referral-concentration analytics).
182.features_to_create: Build a per-provider diagnosis-positivity monitor: unit of observation = ordering NPI × TCD/vascular-ultrasound CPT, computing the fraction of tests carrying the coverage-qualifying diagnosis and the practice's test-per-1,000-patient rate versus same-specialty peers; above the calibrated percentile, apply a prepay documentation request for the interpretive report supporting the diagnosis. Add a referral-concentration edit that fires when >a calibrated share of a practice's imaging referrals route to one entity that also supplies staff/equipment to the practice, routing to Stark/AKS review and, for repeat offenders, prepay review of all TCD claims.

183.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic as the companion case: near-100% attachment of the coverage-qualifying cerebral occlusion/stenosis diagnosis to every trans-cranial doppler claim, with the diagnosis assigned before results existed — detectable prepay by comparing per-provider diagnosis-positivity rates against same-specialty peers and by requesting the interpretive report. Secondary signals: an eye practice ordering vascular ultrasound volumes far above peers, one mobile TCD vendor recurring across many ordering practices, and referral concentration to a single radiology group indicating a volume-based financial relationship.
183.features_to_create: Implement an ordering-NPI × test-code positivity and utilization outlier model (share of tests billed with the qualifying diagnosis; tests per 1,000 attributed patients versus peers) that triggers prepay documentation requests for the signed interpretation and medical-necessity note. Pair it with a vendor-linkage rule flagging practices whose imaging/diagnostic services are performed by a third party that is also the source of the referrals or is compensated per test, routing to AKS/Stark investigation and suspension of the affected test codes.

184.ways_to_identify: Prior-authorization metadata is the carrier: PA forms for the high-cost naloxone auto-injector arrive from the dispensing pharmacy's fax/portal account or IP rather than the prescriber's, are submitted in bursts, and reuse identical step-therapy language ('failed Narcan') across unrelated patients. That claimed prior trial is falsifiable prepay against the plan's own Part D claim history — most patients have no prior naloxone/Narcan fill. Also visible: one pharmacy accounting for an extreme share of national Evzio volume with the same handful of prescribers.
184.features_to_create: Build a PA-integrity check: unit = PA request, computing submitter identity/channel versus the attesting prescriber's registered contact, template-similarity of free-text across requests, and whether the asserted prior therapy is corroborated by pharmacy claim history for that member; mismatch on submitter or absent corroborating prior fill auto-denies or pends the PA pending prescriber attestation. Add a pharmacy-level monitor for concentration in a single high-cost brand NDC and PA-approval volume versus peers, triggering prepay review of all claims for that NDC.

185.ways_to_identify: Identical mechanic: the pharmacy authored and signed prescriber PA forms for Evzio, so the PA's submission channel, fax header and IP trace to the pharmacy, not the physician's office, and the 'tried and failed Narcan/naloxone' assertion contradicts the member's own Part D fill history. Extreme concentration of a single very-high-cost NDC in one pharmacy, with repeated identical PA narratives, is visible before payment.
185.features_to_create: Automate PA provenance validation (submitter identity/fax/IP vs prescriber of record; prescriber callback or e-signature verification for high-cost NDCs) and step-therapy auto-verification against internal pharmacy claim history, denying or pending PAs whose asserted prior therapy has no corroborating fill. Layer a pharmacy outlier report on share-of-revenue from one NDC and PA-approval rate versus peers, escalating to prepay review and payment suspension.

186.ways_to_identify: No payer, no claims: embezzlement of customer cash deposits at a car dealership concealed by false journal entries — detectable only by employer-side controls (segregation of duties between cash receipt and ledger posting, daily deposit-to-DMS reconciliation, surprise audit of voided/adjusting entries by the accountant who books them). Nothing is visible at claim adjudication.
186.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. The nearest analogous control, if any payer wanted it, is an internal-accounting rule that flags journal entries created and approved by the same user against customer deposit accounts and any cash receipt lacking a matching bank deposit within one business day.

187.ways_to_identify: Enrolment screening is the choke point: the 855S listed a nominee owner while the true owners were concealed, so identity/ownership verification (credit-header and corporate-registry match on the applicant, prior involvement of the same address, phone, bank account or accountant with other DME PTANs) plus an unannounced site visit to the claimed New Hampshire location would have exposed a shell. Post-enrolment, first-90-day billing behavior — immediate high-volume orthotic brace claims to out-of-state beneficiaries from a handful of telemedicine prescribers, with no local referral base — is visible before payment.
187.features_to_create: Build a nominee-owner risk score at enrolment combining applicant age/credit-history thinness, absence of prior health-care industry footprint, shared identifiers with other applicants, and site-visit outcome; high scores require verified beneficial-ownership documentation before PTAN activation. Add a new-supplier ramp edit: for DME PTANs within their first billing months, cap payment and auto-suspend when brace-code volume, out-of-state beneficiary share, or prescriber concentration exceeds calibrated percentiles for new suppliers, with prepay documentation review and beneficiary contact.

188.ways_to_identify: The signal is diagnosis substitution inside prior-authorization packets submitted by a third-party PA-services vendor on behalf of compounding pharmacies: the diagnosis asserted on the PA does not appear anywhere in the patient's medical or claims history from the named prescriber. Comparing PA-stated diagnoses to the member's historical diagnosis profile, and tracing PA submitter identity to a vendor rather than the prescriber's office, is doable prepay. Vendor fingerprinting — one fax number/portal account submitting PAs across many unrelated pharmacies and prescribers with unusually high approval rates — is another prepay flag.
188.features_to_create: Implement a PA diagnosis-corroboration edit: for each PA on compounded or high-cost drugs, check whether the asserted qualifying diagnosis appears in the member's prior claims history from the attesting prescriber or any provider; absent corroboration, pend for medical records rather than auto-approve. Add submitter-entity analytics that cluster PAs by fax/IP/agent account and flag third-party submitters whose diagnosis-change rate or approval rate exceeds the calibrated percentile, suspending auto-approval for that channel.

189.ways_to_identify: Beneficiary-identifier misuse is detectable prepay: the same beneficiary IDs, harvested and sold in bulk, appear across a cluster of DME suppliers in short windows, with the supplier located far from the beneficiary and no ordering physician with any prior encounter history for that patient. Brace claims for beneficiaries who have no matching diagnosis, no prior musculoskeletal care, and often multiple braces on the same date are also visible. Beneficiary complaints and 'services I never received' hotline reports corroborate that nothing was delivered; proof-of-delivery is absent on request.
189.features_to_create: Build a beneficiary-ID compromise monitor: unit = beneficiary ID, counting distinct DME suppliers, distinct states, and brace HCPCS billed within a rolling window; when counts exceed the calibrated percentile, tag the ID and route all further DME claims to prepay review with proof-of-delivery and signed-order requests. Add a supplier-level edit that suspends payment when a supplier's share of claims on tagged/compromised IDs, or its share of beneficiaries with no prior encounter with the ordering NPI, exceeds peer-calibrated thresholds.

190.ways_to_identify: PDMP and pharmacy-claim data show the pattern prepay: a single prescriber writing high-MME Schedule II opioids plus concurrent benzodiazepines to a large panel, with short intervals, high cash/out-of-area patient share, and no corresponding office-visit or exam claims. Failed or inconsistent urine drug screens on file alongside continued escalating prescribing is a documented red flag visible in the practice's own lab claims. Missing E/M encounters paired with active prescriptions is a direct claims-level contradiction.
190.features_to_create: Build a prescriber-level controlled-substance risk monitor joining PDMP dispensing to medical claims: compute per-prescriber average daily MME, opioid+benzodiazepine co-prescribing rate, share of prescriptions with no E/M encounter in the look-back window, and patient travel distance, versus same-specialty peers. Above calibrated percentiles, trigger prescriber education/audit, prior authorization on further opioid claims for that prescriber's patients, and referral to DEA/licensure; pend pharmacy claims tied to prescribers under active review.

191.ways_to_identify: Pure employment-tax and personal income-tax fraud with no health-care claim — not detectable by a payer. IRS-side detection is automatic: W-2/W-3 wage totals reported to SSA versus Form 941 filings and EFTPS deposits for the same EIN, plus non-filer scoring for a person with reported six-figure W-2 wages and no 1040.
191.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. The applicable government control is an automated 941-to-W-2 reconciliation per EIN that opens a trust-fund-recovery case when withheld amounts reported on W-2s exceed deposits, plus non-filer flags where third-party wage reports exist without a filed return.

192.ways_to_identify: Same as the companion entry: no claims, no payer — payroll trust-fund diversion and non-filing. Visible only to the tax authority via mismatch between W-2/W-3 reported withholding for the EIN and actual 941 filings/EFTPS deposits, and via non-filer scoring against third-party wage reports.
192.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Build (at IRS) an EIN-level automated deposit-versus-reported-withholding variance monitor that escalates persistent multi-quarter shortfalls to responsible-person assessment, and a non-filer trigger for individuals with substantial reported wages and no return.

193.ways_to_identify: This is misappropriation from a self-funded plan's trust account by the plan sponsor's CFO, not a false claim, so no adjudication edit sees it; it surfaces through bank-level and plan-accounting controls — checks drawn on the benefit trust payable to the CFO, her creditors, or an unrelated long-term-care insurer, and disbursements not matching any TPA-adjudicated claim funding request. Reconciling trust disbursements to the TPA's paid-claims register plus admin fees leaves an unexplained residual.
193.features_to_create: Build a benefit-trust disbursement reconciliation control: unit = each disbursement from the plan's trust account, matched to a TPA claim-funding wire, stop-loss premium, or approved admin invoice; any payee not on an approved-payee whitelist, or any month where disbursements exceed adjudicated paid claims plus fees beyond tolerance, fires an alert to the plan fiduciary and auditor. Require dual signature/approval separated from the person who reconciles the account.

194.ways_to_identify: No claim-adjudication signal: the CFO wrote checks directly from a self-funded health benefit trust partly funded by federal grants. Detection routes are the annual Single Audit / OMB grant audit, bank monitoring for trust-account checks payable to insiders or their personal creditors, and monthly reconciliation of trust outflows to the TPA's paid-claims and premium records.
194.features_to_create: Implement automated payee screening on benefit-trust and grant-funded accounts that flags any disbursement to an employee, employee's spouse, or an employee's known creditor, and any check lacking a matching claim-funding or invoice record; flags block release pending second-signature approval. Add a monthly variance monitor of trust outflow versus adjudicated claims plus fees, with unexplained residuals reported to the audit committee and grantor agency.

195.ways_to_identify: Two prepay-visible contradictions: buprenorphine/Suboxone prescriptions written under a physician's DEA number for patients with no corresponding encounter claim from that physician (and often on dates the physician had no claims at the clinic at all), and a rigid urine-drug-testing profile where nearly every patient receives the same large definitive multi-drug panel at every visit regardless of history. Lay ownership and non-clinical control of prescribing shows up in enrolment/ownership disclosures for a clinic owned by a non-licensed person, and in prescriber-to-clinic volume ratios that are physically implausible per provider-day. UDT units per patient-year versus same-specialty peers is a direct outlier metric.
195.features_to_create: Build a prescription-to-encounter linkage edit for controlled substances and MAT: for each prescription attributed to a DEA/NPI, require a same-patient encounter by that prescriber within the look-back window; unmatched prescriptions pend and the prescriber's volume-per-workday is scored against a plausibility ceiling. Add a UDT profile edit computing, per clinic, definitive-panel frequency and analyte count per patient-year and the share of patients receiving the identical panel, above calibrated percentiles requiring prepay documentation of individualized testing rationale; flag clinics whose disclosed owners hold no clinical license for enhanced review.

196.ways_to_identify: Encounter-level time arithmetic exposes it prepay: the worker's billed community-support units per day exceed feasible working hours, include overlapping or back-to-back sessions at geographically incompatible locations, and cluster on identical durations (uniform 60-minute notes). Notes submitted in batches long after the service date, and beneficiaries with no other service history who suddenly receive daily CSW hours, are further flags; beneficiary verification letters and GPS/EVV data confirm no visit occurred.
196.features_to_create: Build a rendering-staff daily-capacity edit: unit = staff NPI/employee ID × date, summing billed CSW units and flagging totals above a feasible-hours ceiling, overlapping time spans, and travel-time-infeasible location pairs; violations deny or pend prepay. Add electronic visit verification for community-based behavioral health so claims without a matching time-and-location check-in are not payable, plus a per-worker note-uniformity metric (identical duration/text similarity) that triggers documentation audit and beneficiary confirmation.

197.ways_to_identify: Not a health-care claim scheme: this is SBA PPP/EIDL loan fraud. Pre-disbursement detection is available from data the lender/SBA already holds — applicant EIN and payroll figures verifiable against IRS 941/W-2 transcripts and state UI wage filings, business existence verifiable against state registration and formation date, and duplicate-applicant detection across 23 applications sharing one SSN, bank account, address, phone or IP.
197.features_to_create: Build a pre-disbursement verification pipeline: for each application, auto-match claimed payroll/revenue to IRS transcript and state UI wage data and reject or manually review on material variance; block applications for entities formed after the eligibility date or absent from state registries. Add cross-application entity resolution on SSN/EIN/bank account/address/device-IP that holds funding when one identity appears across multiple applications or when the same bank account receives multiple program disbursements.

198.ways_to_identify: Order provenance is measurable: the NP signed pre-populated orders in seconds via a telemedicine platform, so platform audit logs (time-open-to-signature, orders signed per session/day) plus claims data showing no E/M encounter by that NP with the beneficiary before or after the order reveal the absence of a treating relationship. Volume implausibility — hundreds of genetic-test and DME orders from one mid-level provider for out-of-state beneficiaries, concentrated into a few labs/suppliers — is visible before payment. Cancer-panel/PGx testing with no oncology or supporting diagnosis history for the beneficiary is an additional prepay flag.
198.features_to_create: Build a treating-relationship edit for high-risk order-driven services (hereditary cancer/PGx panels, orthotic braces): deny or pend when the ordering NPI has no E/M or telehealth encounter claim with that beneficiary in the look-back window, and when the ordering NPI's daily order count or lab/supplier concentration exceeds calibrated peer percentiles. Require submission of the signed order with authorship/timestamp metadata for flagged prescribers, and place labs/suppliers whose orders come predominantly from such prescribers on prepay review.

199.ways_to_identify: No claims-payment component: this is destruction of government records and obstruction arising from a health-care fraud prosecution, not billing conduct. Detection lies with agency device management and e-discovery — mobile-device management backup and retention policies that preserve texts on government phones, litigation-hold enforcement, and audit logs showing deletion after a preservation order.
199.features_to_create: No payer-side claim control applies. The applicable control is enforced server-side archiving of all government-issued device communications with immutable retention and automated alerts when messages are deleted on a device subject to an active litigation hold.

200.ways_to_identify: The DOT certification side is not a claims-payment scheme, but the pre-signed pad is visible in PDMP and pharmacy claims data: controlled-substance prescriptions written under one prescriber's DEA number where the patient is an employee at the same practice address, or dispensed to the prescriber herself or immediate family, and prescriptions issued on dates with no corresponding office visit claim for that patient. Also detectable at credentialing time by cross-checking DOT National Registry certification submissions against the examiner's exam volume. Enrolment-time route: state medical board and DOT National Registry status feeds.
200.features_to_create: Build a prescriber-level PDMP/pharmacy-claims edit that flags controlled-substance fills where patient address/phone/employer matches the prescribing practice, where prescriber and patient share surname or the prescriber is the patient, or where no E/M encounter exists for that patient within a calibrated lookback window; fire a prepay pharmacy edit plus a documentation request for the chart note. Add a self/family-prescribing counter per DEA number that triggers referral above the same-specialty peer percentile.

201.ways_to_identify: This is embezzlement from a nonprofit plus payroll-tax and personal income-tax fraud, not a claims-payment scheme, so no prepay claim edit would have caught it. The detectable route is IRS matching of Form 941 withholding against W-2 wage reports and against deposits, and grantor/payer oversight of the nonprofit's Form 990 and audited financials showing officer withdrawals and accrued unpaid payroll taxes.
201.features_to_create: For payers or grantors that fund nonprofit entities, build an entity-level financial-integrity monitor that compares reported payroll withholding to remittance records and flags accrued tax liabilities, single-signatory disbursements to the executive director, and missing independent audits; action is a payment hold on further grant draws and a documentation request. Otherwise state that this is a tax/IRS control, not a payer claim edit.

202.ways_to_identify: The claim is a self-attested need for full-time personal assistance while the beneficiary was concurrently a full-time federal employee, which is visible by matching the caregiver-program applicant against federal payroll and wage-reporting data at eligibility determination and at each annual reassessment. A second signal is the mismatch between claimed total dependence in ADLs and the veteran's own encounter record, which shows no corresponding functional-status documentation or care utilization.
202.features_to_create: At enrolment and reassessment, run an automated wage/employment match (federal payroll, state new-hire and quarterly wage files) for both the veteran and the paid caregiver, and fire a hold when a beneficiary certified at the highest assistance tier shows concurrent full-time employment earnings. Add a consistency edit comparing certified ADL dependency tier against clinical encounter and DME/home-care utilization, requiring an in-person functional assessment before the tier is renewed.

203.ways_to_identify: Every home visit claim carries a rendering-provider NPI; the payer can match each rendering NPI against state licensure files and, where a supervising-physician arrangement is claimed, verify the supervisor's own claim volume for the same day. Red flags include a single billing physician's NPI attached to visit volumes physically impossible in a day, visits at dispersed addresses within implausible travel times, and rendering clinicians with no active state license or with foreign-credential-only status.
203.features_to_create: Build a prepay edit that rejects home-visit claims whose rendering NPI lacks an active in-state license on the date of service, and a per-billing-NPI daily capacity/geo-feasibility check (visits per day and drive-time between successive service addresses) that suspends payment above the calibrated feasibility bound. Add a credentialing check requiring the roster of all clinicians performing visits, with supervision attestations reverified periodically.

204.ways_to_identify: The signature is a tight closed referral cluster: a defined cohort of beneficiaries (here elderly, same language group, recruited via one nonprofit) whose claims across many unrelated specialties all trace back to the same small set of providers, with near-identical service bundles and shared addresses, phone numbers or billing agents. Beneficiary-level network analysis at adjudication shows implausibly high provider-sharing concordance, and repeat use of the same marketer-linked entities. Kickback payments themselves surface only post-payment via financial records.
204.features_to_create: Build a beneficiary-cohort graph feature: cluster beneficiaries by shared provider sets, and compute for each provider group the share of its patients that also appear at the other members of the cluster versus geographic base rates; fire prepay review and a documentation request on all providers in clusters above the calibrated percentile. Layer an entity-linkage check (shared address/phone/bank account/billing agent across referring and rendering NPIs) that suspends payment pending ownership disclosure.

205.ways_to_identify: Dispensing volume is the signal: a single-location pharmacy dispensing hundreds of thousands of oxycodone dosage units a year, far above same-size peers, with a high share of cash-pay high-dose immediate-release oxycodone, patients travelling long distances, and heavy concentration on a few prescribers. PDMP and ARCOS/wholesaler purchase data compared to dispensed quantities exposes both the diversion and the record manipulation (purchases exceeding reported dispensing).
205.features_to_create: Build a pharmacy-level monthly monitor computing controlled-substance dosage units per prescription and per pharmacy, share of oxycodone in total volume, cash-pay share, prescriber concentration, and mean patient-to-pharmacy distance versus same-size peers; fire network suspension/prepay review above the calibrated percentile. Add a reconciliation edit comparing wholesaler purchase quantities to PDMP-reported dispensing, flagging unexplained gaps for on-site inventory audit.

206.ways_to_identify: This is pure pandemic loan fraud with no health-care claims component, so no payer claim edit applies. Prepayment detection sits with the lender/SBA: cross-check applicant payroll figures against IRS Form 941/W-2 filings and state wage records, and detect one applicant filing multiple applications across several entities using shared addresses, bank accounts, IP addresses and EINs.
206.features_to_create: Nearest applicable control is a loan-underwriting duplicate-and-verification engine: key each application on principal SSN, EIN, bank account, address and device/IP, block funding where the same controlling person appears on multiple applications or where reported payroll exceeds IRS-verified wage filings, and require tax-transcript match before disbursement. No payer-side claim control applies.

207.ways_to_identify: Transcranial doppler is a low-volume test; a mobile diagnostics company billing ~$1M concentrated among a handful of referring internists, with each referrer ordering hundreds of scans, is visible at adjudication. Supporting signals: the diagnosis codes used to justify the scan appear only on the ordering claim and nowhere else in the patient's history, no neurology consult or follow-up imaging, and no change in treatment after the scan.
207.features_to_create: Build an ordering-physician-level rate feature for TCD/mobile diagnostic CPT codes (tests per 100 patients, share of panel receiving the test, referral concentration into one supplier NPI) and fire prepay review with medical-record request above the same-specialty peer percentile. Add a diagnosis-corroboration edit that denies pending documentation when the justifying diagnosis appears on no other claim in the member's history and no downstream neurologic care follows.

208.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic as its co-defendant case: a mobile diagnostics supplier with nearly all volume funneled from a small ring of internists ordering hundreds of transcranial doppler scans each, using boilerplate justifying diagnoses absent from the rest of the patient record. At adjudication the payer sees per-referrer test rates far above same-specialty peers and no neurologic workup or follow-up around the scan.
208.features_to_create: Implement a supplier-referrer concentration metric (share of a mobile diagnostics supplier's claims from top referrers, and each referrer's TCD tests per attributed patient) with prepay suspension and records request above the calibrated percentile. Pair with an edit requiring documented symptoms/prior neurologic evaluation coded elsewhere in the member's history before TCD is payable.

209.ways_to_identify: The orders are visible as one nurse practitioner signing hundreds of brace orders for beneficiaries scattered across a state with whom she has no prior or subsequent relationship, tied to telehealth encounters of extremely short duration and to a small set of DME suppliers. Prepay signals: no established-patient history, no prior visit for the affected joint, out-of-area beneficiary geography, and repeated identical order text across patients.
209.features_to_create: Build an ordering-clinician monitor for orthotic/brace HCPCS: count distinct beneficiaries ordered per month, share with no prior encounter with that clinician, telehealth encounter length where available, and geographic dispersion; suspend DME claims linked to clinicians above the calibrated percentile and require the signed clinical note. Add a prepay edit denying brace claims where the ordering NPI has no evaluation claim for that member within a lookback window, and a supplier-side check on referral concentration into a single telemarketing-linked clinician pool.

210.ways_to_identify: Units-per-claim are absurd on their face: 1,000 units of a B-12 injection, and later billed amounts of $15 million per injection, are catchable by a units-versus-MUE/charge-plausibility edit before a dollar moves. Backdating is visible by comparing dates of service to the license-suspension date in the state board feed and to the claim submission date; the DEA-number misuse is visible by verifying that the prescriber NPI on controlled-substance claims owns the DEA number presented.
210.features_to_create: Build a prepay units and charge sanity edit per procedure code (units above the medically unlikely maximum, or billed charge above a calibrated multiple of the allowed amount) that hard-denies and routes to review. Add an eligibility-date edit that denies claims whose date of service precedes suspension but is submitted after it unless documentation is supplied, and an NPI-to-DEA ownership match on controlled-substance prescriptions that rejects mismatches.

211.ways_to_identify: This is employment-tax fraud by a facility chain, not claim fraud, so prepay claim edits do not reach it; the IRS route is matching Form 941 withholding and W-2 filings against actual deposits per EIN, and the DOL route is missing Form 5500 filings. A payer can still see the correlated risk: a multi-state chain with unpaid trust-fund taxes, missing 5500s, wage garnishment/lien filings and staffing-cost anomalies in cost reports.
211.features_to_create: Build a chain-level financial-viability monitor for institutional providers using cost-report payroll versus reported withholding, federal/state tax lien filings, missing Form 5500 filings and payroll-service termination signals; fire enhanced oversight, escrow of payments, or a change-of-ownership review rather than a claim denial. Primary enforcement remains an IRS deposit-versus-withholding match.

212.ways_to_identify: The mechanic is reflex, per-visit definitive urine drug testing for every chronic opioid patient routed to a clinic-owned in-house lab, which shows at adjudication as a near-100% testing rate per office visit, identical large test panels for every patient regardless of risk, and lab claims billed under an NPI sharing address and ownership with the referring pain clinic. Also checkable: the practice's self-referral/ownership disclosure, and retention of COVID provider-relief funds after the practice ceased billing.
212.features_to_create: Build a per-provider UDT intensity feature (definitive drug tests per patient per year, tests per E/M visit, distinct analytes per panel, share of panels identical across patients) with prepay review and a records request above the same-specialty peer percentile, plus a hard edit on multiple definitive panels per encounter. Add an ownership-linkage flag when referring practice and lab share address, TIN or owners, and a relief-fund reconciliation that recoups when a recipient TIN stops submitting claims.

213.ways_to_identify: No claims-payment component: this is obstruction of justice by a management consultant and opioid-marketing conduct by a manufacturer, so no payer prepay edit would have caught it. The nearest payer-visible signal is manufacturer-driven prescribing patterns — high-value-prescriber targeting shows up as concentrated growth in high-dose long-acting opioid prescribing among a small set of prescribers with heavy manufacturer sales/payment contact.
213.features_to_create: Nearest applicable control: a prescriber-level opioid monitor joining pharmacy claims MME per patient per day, share of long-acting opioids, and Open Payments manufacturer payment/detailing intensity, firing prior authorization and prescriber outreach above the calibrated percentile. No payer control addresses the obstruction conduct itself.

214.ways_to_identify: Same as the companion case: obstruction and consulting-driven opioid promotion, with no claim submitted to a payer, so nothing was catchable at adjudication. Payers could only observe the downstream effect — abnormal growth in OxyContin and high-MME prescribing concentrated in prescribers identified as high-value targets.
214.features_to_create: Build a prescriber trend feature on brand-specific long-acting opioid volume and MME growth versus same-specialty peers, joined to manufacturer payment data, triggering prior authorization, formulary step edits and prescriber audit. State plainly that the obstruction offense has no payer-side control.

215.ways_to_identify: The claimed relationship is contradicted by records already held: the veteran's file showed the spouse had been removed on divorce, and a state vital-records marriage/divorce match would show no marriage subsisting at death. A surname change filed shortly before or after the claim, and a prior dependency record showing termination for divorce, are both visible at eligibility adjudication before survivor benefits or CHAMPVA cards issue.
215.features_to_create: Build an eligibility edit for survivor/dependent benefit applications that compares the claimed marital status against prior dependency-termination reason codes in the beneficiary's own file and against state vital-records divorce/marriage data, holding payment when a prior 'divorce' termination exists without a documented remarriage. Add a name-change alert (surname adopted within a short window of the claim) and require certified marriage certificate and death-linked documentation before CHAMPVA enrolment activates.

216.ways_to_identify: A pediatrician writing opioid, benzodiazepine and stimulant prescriptions to adult women is a specialty/age mismatch visible in PDMP and pharmacy claims at point of adjudication, together with no corresponding office-visit claims for those patients. The identity misuse is visible as prescriptions dispensed under a member's ID for a drug regimen inconsistent with that member's other claims, and as several members at different addresses sharing one prescriber and identical regimens.
216.features_to_create: Build a prescriber-specialty/patient-age plausibility edit that flags controlled-substance claims where the prescriber's specialty and the patient's age band are incompatible (pediatrician to adults) and where no E/M encounter exists for that patient-prescriber pair in a lookback window; deny pending documentation. Add an identity-consistency check comparing dispensed controlled-substance regimen to the member's own diagnosis/encounter history and flagging clusters of members sharing one prescriber, one pharmacy and identical regimens.

217.ways_to_identify: Two separable problems: the underlying overbilling was detectable at adjudication (exam and testing volumes per provider-day above peers, services with no supporting record, repeat visual-field/imaging testing per patient), and the bribery was detectable in audit-governance data — an open audit closed or settled after external political intervention, with settlement authority exercised outside normal delegation. The bribe payments themselves surface only post-payment via bank records and the fiance's practice checks.
217.features_to_create: Build a provider-level utilization monitor for optometry (encounters per provider-day, tests per patient per year, share of claims with no distinct documentation) with prepay review above the calibrated percentile. Separately harden audit workflow controls: log every external contact and settlement-authority override on an open audit, require dual independent sign-off and an integrity-office review for any audit cancellation or discounted settlement, and auto-alert on cases closed after non-program contacts.

218.ways_to_identify: The billing itself was catchable prepay: eye exam and diagnostic-testing volumes per provider-day and repeat testing frequency per patient far above same-specialty Medicaid peers, and claims for services with no corresponding chart entry. The bribery is only visible post-payment/administratively — an audit cancelled and settled at a steep discount following contact from outside the agency, plus practice checks reimbursing personal payments to an official.
218.features_to_create: Implement optometry-specific prepay edits: cap payable diagnostic tests per member per period without documented medical necessity, and flag providers above the calibrated percentile on encounters per day and tests per encounter for prepay record review. Add an audit-integrity control that requires independent approval and audit-committee review for any cancellation or below-extrapolation settlement of an open provider audit, with automated alerts when external officials contact case staff and when provider-linked disbursements match official payees.

219.ways_to_identify: The products were unapproved herbal drugs marketed as FDA-approved COVID treatments and sold direct to consumers, so there may be no payer claim at all; where reimbursement was sought, the signal is a claim carrying an NDC or compound description that is absent from the FDA approved-drug/NDC directory or flagged in FDA warning-letter and import-alert feeds. Marketing claims of FDA approval for an unlisted product are detectable at formulary/coverage-file load, before any payment.
219.features_to_create: Build a prepay pharmacy/medical-benefit edit that validates every submitted NDC or product identifier against the FDA NDC directory and approved-drug and unapproved-drug lists, hard-denying products with no approval basis and auto-blocking any NDC appearing in FDA warning letters or import alerts. Add a coverage-file gate that requires FDA approval status and an evidence review before any COVID-treatment product is added, plus member-alert referral for cash-market unapproved-cure marketing.

220.ways_to_identify: No claims-payment component: this is employment tax fraud against the IRS, detectable from the payer side by reconciling W-2/Form 941 filings - employer issued W-2s showing withholding while no matching 941 returns or EFTPS deposits exist for the same quarters. The signal is a non-filer/underdeposit gap on the employer's EIN across consecutive quarters, visible at return-processing time rather than in any claim.
220.features_to_create: Build an EIN-level quarterly reconciliation job that joins W-2/W-3 wage-and-withholding totals to filed Form 941 liabilities and deposited funds, and fires when withholding is reported at the annual level but quarterly returns or deposits are missing for two or more consecutive quarters. Action: automatic non-filer notice and referral to a trust-fund recovery examination before further refunds or credits are allowed. No payer-side medical claim control applies.

221.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic as the companion case and again not a health-claims scheme: withheld trust-fund taxes were never remitted and 941s were never filed while the company continued to run payroll and make large discretionary disbursements. IRS-side signals are the W-2-to-941 mismatch on the EIN plus continued payroll activity with zero deposits; the luxury spending is only visible post-payment through bank records.
221.features_to_create: Implement an EIN trust-fund monitor computing, per quarter, expected withholding from payroll/W-2 data minus actual EFTPS deposits, flagging repeat-quarter gaps and escalating where the same responsible officer appears on multiple delinquent EINs. Action: automated non-filer assessment, responsible-person identification, and freeze on any related-entity refunds pending examination.

222.ways_to_identify: This is internal embezzlement of resident trust funds rather than false claims, but a payer/regulator can see it: patient trust fund reconciliations show hundreds of cash disbursement checks signed with one countersignature, resident ledger debits with no resident receipt, and continued premium/insurance deductions for a cancelled policy. Facility cost reports and the required resident-funds surety/quarterly accounting are the data carriers; also EIP deposits to resident accounts followed immediately by cash withdrawals.
222.features_to_create: Build a resident-trust-account audit routine per facility: count and value checks payable to cash or to a single employee per month, test signature/countersignature pairs against authorised signer files, and compare ledger debits to signed resident receipts and bank statements. Fire when cash-check volume or per-employee disbursement share exceeds the calibrated percentile versus peer facilities, or when a resident's federal benefit deposit is withdrawn as cash within days - action: documentation request for the trust-fund reconciliation and referral to state survey/MFCU.

223.ways_to_identify: The underlying scheme was alteration of compounded-drug prescription forms, which a PBM can see prepay: the same faxed prescription template with modified drug/ingredient lines, high-reimbursement compound NDC combinations, and fax origination numbers not associated with the prescriber's registered practice location. Compare the prescriber's NPI/DEA address of record and normal prescribing mix to the compound claims being submitted.
223.features_to_create: At adjudication, edit compound claims on prescriber-plus-pharmacy pairs where the compound ingredient mix or reimbursement per script exceeds the same-specialty peer percentile, or where the originating fax/e-script source does not match the prescriber's enrolled practice location. Fire a prepay documentation request for the original signed prescription and prescriber attestation, and suspend payment on the pharmacy's compound claims while the prescriber is contacted directly.

224.ways_to_identify: Not a health-claims case: SBA loan fraud. Detectable at underwriting by cross-checking applicant-stated employee counts, payroll and gross revenue against IRS Form 941/W-2 transcripts and filed returns, and by de-duplicating applications across shared EIN, address, bank account, phone and principal identities - eleven EIDLs plus eight PPP loans to one couple should have collided in an entity/identity graph.
224.features_to_create: Build a pre-disbursement rules engine: (1) require IRS transcript match of payroll to stated average monthly payroll with tolerance, flagging mismatch; (2) an identity/entity graph keyed on SSN, EIN, address, bank routing/account, device and phone that fires when the same principal or bank account appears on multiple loan applications. Action: hold disbursement pending documentation, and post-disbursement trace of proceeds to asset purchases for clawback.

225.ways_to_identify: No payer adjudication occurred - the defendants were the fake payer selling sham 401(k), workers' comp and ACA-exemption products. Detection sits with regulators and with providers/employers verifying coverage: certificates of insurance naming national carriers can be validated against the named carrier's policy system, retirement contributions can be reconciled to trustee/custodian statements and Form 5500 filings, and ACA hardship exemptions exist only in the federal exemption registry.
225.features_to_create: Build a coverage-verification API check for any presented certificate of insurance or exemption number: query the named carrier's policy master and the federal exemption registry, and flag any certificate whose policy number is absent or whose issuing entity is not a licensed carrier in the state. Additionally reconcile withheld retirement contributions to custodian deposit records and fire when withholding occurs with no matching trust deposit; action: regulator referral and suspension of the entity's ability to be accepted as a coverage source.

226.ways_to_identify: Prepay signals are dense: prior-authorization requests from one telehealth group asserting identical DSM-5 workups, urine drug screens and prior non-stimulant failures with no corresponding UDS lab claims or prior non-stimulant pharmacy fills in the member's own history; stimulant scripts written by a handful of NPs at volumes far above same-specialty peers; visit durations billed below the minimum for the psychiatric evaluation code; and refills continuing past the member's date of death. Cross-checking PA attestations against the plan's own claims history for that member is the single strongest catch.
226.features_to_create: Build an auto-verification layer on stimulant PAs: for each request, look up member claim history for a UDS claim and a prior non-stimulant trial fill and for an E/M encounter of adequate duration; deny or route to clinical review when attested elements are absent from the payer's own data. Add prescriber-level monitors for controlled-substance scripts per NP per month, share of new starts with no follow-up visit within the expected interval, and any fill dated after a date-of-death match - action: prepay suspension of the group's stimulant claims and PA privileges pending records.

227.ways_to_identify: Mostly a consumer-deception and trust-fund-tax case, not claims submission - the product sold was a limited-benefit discount plan, so there are no provider claims to edit. Payer-adjacent detection: state DOI licensure files show unlicensed sellers writing business, carrier commission systems show churning (same consumer replaced repeatedly within short intervals) and duplicate monthly draws on the same cardholder, and the marketing scripts claim carrier affiliations that carriers can disprove. The withheld payroll taxes are caught by the W-2-to-941 reconciliation.
227.features_to_create: For entities that pay commissions or process member drafts, build a producer-level monitor: verify every writing agent's ID against state licensure feeds prepay of commission, and compute per-consumer replacement/cancel-rebuy counts and duplicate-draft rates per agency, firing above the calibrated percentile. Action: withhold commissions and refer to state DOI; separately run the EIN W-2-versus-941 withholding gap check for the trust-fund tax exposure.

228.ways_to_identify: Enrolment-time signals dominate: four new hospices with owners who are recent foreign-national identities holding no clinical or industry history, shared addresses, sequential bank accounts and leases signed by the same agent, and no verifiable medical director. Post-enrolment, claims show hospice election periods with no visit-level activity, no attending physician relationship, and beneficiaries who simultaneously have unrelated Part A/B utilisation inconsistent with terminal care.
228.features_to_create: At enrolment, build an owner/identity graph across new hospice applications keyed on SSN/ITIN, address, phone, bank account and notary/agent, and require in-person site verification plus identity-proofing when a listed owner is newly created or appears on multiple applications; hold billing privileges until cleared. For newly enrolled hospices, apply a prepay review flag on all claims for an initial period and fire when election periods lack any documented visit encounters or when beneficiaries show concurrent curative-intent utilisation - action: payment suspension and revocation referral.

229.ways_to_identify: Prepay claim-graph signals: brace claims where the ordering physician is in a different state from the beneficiary and has no prior or subsequent E/M relationship with that beneficiary, one telemedicine physician ordering across hundreds of unrelated beneficiaries, and identical brace code sets (multiple joints per beneficiary) repeating verbatim. Splitting volume across three DME storefronts is itself detectable by linking the storefronts on shared owners, addresses, bank accounts and the same ordering-physician pool.
229.features_to_create: Build a beneficiary-ordering-physician relationship edit that denies or pends orthotic DME claims where no covered E/M encounter with the ordering NPI exists in a defined lookback and the geographic distance exceeds a calibrated threshold. Add a supplier-cluster detector that links DME NPIs by shared ownership, address, bank account and overlapping ordering-physician set and aggregates their volume for outlier scoring; action: prepay review of the whole cluster, plus documentation request for the order and beneficiary contact attestation.
