230.ways_to_identify: Each strand has a prepay tell: DOL-OWCP therapy hours overlapping a facility surgery claim for the same claimant on the same date; COVID test claims tied to beneficiaries whose date of death precedes the service date and to beneficiary lists funnelled from one recruiter; genetic testing billed under physician identifiers with no ordering encounter and volumes wildly off the physician's specialty norm; and EEG billing concentrated on referrers receiving 'loan', directorship or consulting payments disclosable in ownership/financial-relationship data.
230.features_to_create: Build (1) a same-claimant temporal conflict edit that denies therapy/office services overlapping an inpatient/operative claim window; (2) a date-of-death and beneficiary-ID-reuse edit on test claims, plus a recruiter-linkage graph over beneficiary lists shared across billing NPIs; (3) an ordering-physician validation edit requiring a documented ordering encounter and firing when a physician's genetic-test order volume exceeds the same-specialty peer percentile, with fraud-hold on the lab. Action: prepay suspension of the billing NPI and revocation review, with referral where identifiers appear stolen.

231.ways_to_identify: PDMP-plus-claims joins show it prepay: two prescribers issuing Schedule II opioid dosage units far above same-specialty peers, a high share of patients travelling long distances or sharing a single recruiter's address, cash-heavy visits with cookie-cutter same-day E/M codes, and pharmacy concentration where a handful of pharmacies fill nearly all scripts. Diagnosis support for chronic opioid therapy is absent from the member's other claims.
231.features_to_create: Build a prescriber-level controlled-substance surveillance job computing MME per patient per month, share of patients on high-dose opioids, patient-address clustering and pharmacy concentration, and fire above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers. On fire, apply prepay pend on the practice's E/M and the linked pharmacy's opioid claims with a documentation request for treatment plans and PDMP reconciliation; refer for DEA/MFCU action and consider prescriber payment suspension.

232.ways_to_identify: Prepay signals: hospice census dominated by beneficiaries referred from a small set of group homes and one hospital discharge coordinator, one physician certifying and re-certifying terminal illness for an outsized share of the census, live-discharge and long-length-of-stay rates far above peers, and beneficiaries with no prior hospice-consistent diagnosis trajectory. After the search warrant, the reopening under straw owners is catchable at enrolment by ownership-graph matching to the sanctioned entity's addresses, staff, medical director and bank accounts.
232.features_to_create: Build a hospice certification-concentration monitor (share of certs by one physician, referral-source concentration, beneficiaries alive past the calibrated percentile of expected stay) that triggers prepay medical-record review of certifications and payment suspension. Separately, at enrolment run a successor-entity detector linking new applications to prior investigated/revoked providers on address, phone, bank account, medical director, employees and managing-employee identity, and deny or hold billing privileges pending on-site verification.

233.ways_to_identify: Payer/PBM-side prepay: script volume attributed to two physicians' DEA numbers spikes far above their historical and peer baselines, with fills for individuals who have no encounter history with that practice and often no coverage relationship at all. Cash-pay fills bypass claims, so the PDMP is the primary data carrier - prescriber-level dispensing counts reported there can be pushed back to the prescriber for confirmation.
233.features_to_create: Build a prescriber-identity integrity monitor that compares controlled-substance fill volume per DEA/NPI against that prescriber's own historical baseline and specialty peers, and fires on step-change increases or on fills for patients with no prior encounter with that prescriber's TIN. On fire, pend the pharmacy claims, send an automated prescriber-verification request ('did you write these?'), and notify PDMP/DEA; add an alert for prescriptions whose patient identity cannot be resolved to a real member record.

234.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic as the companion case: forged scripts under two physicians' DEA numbers dispensed to non-patients and fictitious names. Observable prepay at the pharmacy/PBM layer are repeated fills for patients with no encounter history with the prescriber, multiple different patients picking up at the same pharmacy on the same days by the same individuals, identical directions and quantities across scripts, and fictitious patient identities that fail eligibility/identity resolution.
234.features_to_create: Implement (1) a prescriber-baseline step-change edit on controlled-substance volume per DEA number with automated prescriber verification before payment; (2) an identity-resolution edit rejecting fills where patient demographics do not resolve to a verified member/person record; (3) a pharmacy-level pickup-clustering report over shared payer/pickup identifiers. Action: prepay pend on the affected DEA number's scripts and referral to DEA and the state board.

235.ways_to_identify: Non-dispensing is detectable prepay through inventory-versus-billing logic: aggregate NDC units billed by each pharmacy far exceed wholesaler acquisition data (ARCOS/834-type purchase records) for the same NDCs, and refill patterns are too regular (exact 30-day cadence, no gaps, no partial fills). Also visible are beneficiaries with no corresponding prescriber encounter or who live implausibly far from the pharmacy, and five pharmacies under common ownership showing the same signature pattern.
235.features_to_create: Build a monthly per-pharmacy, per-NDC billed-units-versus-purchased-units reconciliation using wholesaler purchase data, firing when billed units exceed purchases beyond tolerance, and aggregate across commonly owned NPIs. Combine with a refill-regularity and beneficiary-distance score; on fire, place the pharmacy on prepay review with documentation requests for signature logs and acquisition invoices, and suspend payment where the inventory gap persists.

236.ways_to_identify: Compound kickback schemes show prepay as extreme reimbursement-per-claim, a narrow set of high-margin compound formulations, and referral concentration - a small number of prescribers accounting for nearly all of one pharmacy's compound volume, often out-of-state and outside the therapeutic specialty, with marketer-driven patient cohorts appearing in bursts. Cross-payer view (DOL-OWCP, TRICARE, Medicare) is important because the pharmacy shifted the same formulations across programs.
236.features_to_create: Build a compound-claim outlier engine at pharmacy level: average paid per compound claim, share of revenue from the top compound formulations, and Herfindahl-style prescriber concentration versus peers; fire above the calibrated percentile. On fire, apply prepay documentation review requiring proof of patient-specific medical necessity and prescriber attestation of no financial relationship, and check prescriber-to-pharmacy financial ties; suspend payment and refer for kickback investigation where marketer payments are found.

237.ways_to_identify: Several distinct prepay tells: claims billed with brand NDCs while acquisition records show only generic purchases (brand/generic NDC-versus-inventory mismatch); scripts billed under a prescriber NPI who has no relationship to the member and can be verified by outreach; billed units exceeding purchased units for the diverted opioids; and a reported robbery used to explain inventory loss that should trigger reconciliation rather than close it.
237.features_to_create: Build per-pharmacy NDC-level reconciliation of billed brand versus purchased brand units (fires on any material brand-billed/generic-purchased gap and on billed-exceeds-purchased for controlled substances), plus a prescriber-validation edit rejecting claims whose prescriber NPI has no encounter/relationship history with the member. Action: prepay pend and automated prescriber verification; on inventory loss reports, auto-open an audit that reconciles ARCOS purchases, dispensing records and claims.

238.ways_to_identify: No claims payment - this is credential fraud, and the payer-relevant control is at credentialing/enrolment: licences issued to candidates whose diploma and clinical hours come from a small set of schools with implausible graduate volume, transcripts that cannot be confirmed by primary-source verification, and NCLEX candidates whose program attendance dates conflict with employment history in another state. Nurse-compact and board databases plus school-level graduate counts carry the signal.
238.features_to_create: Make primary-source verification mandatory and automated in credentialing: verify diploma and clinical-hour transcripts directly with the institution's registrar API, and flag any applicant whose program is on a high-risk school list built from graduate-volume-per-faculty and NCLEX pass-rate anomalies. Fire a hold on network participation/billing privileges until verification returns, and run a retroactive sweep of already-credentialed staff from flagged schools with claims-payment suspension for services rendered by unverified licensees.

239.ways_to_identify: Not a medical-claims case: pandemic unemployment insurance fraud. Detectable pre-payment by cross-matching claimant-reported employer and wages against state quarterly wage records (no wage record for the claimed employer), and by de-duplicating on the filer's IP/device, bank account or debit-card routing, mailing address and phone across 65+ claims filed by one person. Supporting documents can be checked against employer verification responses before first payment.
239.features_to_create: Build a pre-payment UI adjudication rules set: (1) require wage-record match for the claimed employer and hold claims with no match pending employer verification; (2) an identity/payment-instrument graph that fires when more than a small number of distinct claimants share a bank account, address, phone, device fingerprint or IP. Action: suspend first payment and route to identity verification and document authentication before release.

240.ways_to_identify: Every claim named a specific treating physical therapist (rendering NPI) on dates when that therapist was physically outside the country - detectable by cross-checking rendering-provider claim volume against absence evidence, and more cheaply by the pattern signal: continuous same-therapist billing with no gaps, including on dates where the same NPI appears as sole renderer for implausibly long service-minute totals. Timed-unit PT codes billed under one NPI can be summed per day and compared to a feasible workday. CBP/travel data is not payer data, but sudden identical-daily-pattern billing and later beneficiary/therapist interviews close it post-pay.
240.features_to_create: Build a rendering-NPI per-day capacity edit: sum billed timed PT units plus untimed procedures per rendering NPI per date of service across all TINs, convert to minutes, and pend claims exceeding a calibrated feasible-day threshold or where one NPI is the sole renderer for an entire clinic's panel every business day. Add a 'renderer identity attestation' documentation request (signed treatment notes with therapist credentials and time in/out) when a solo-renderer clinic shows zero absence days over long periods versus same-specialty peers.

241.ways_to_identify: This is a Stark/AKS relationship case, visible not in claim lines but in the financial-relationship data the hospital must disclose: EHR-subsidy agreements, office equipment provided to referring physicians' private practices, and 'clinical integration' bonus payments. A payer can require and analyze physician financial-relationship disclosures at hospital enrollment/revalidation and correlate each subsidized physician's referral share into the sponsoring system before paying designated health services. Qui tam and expense-ledger review (a custom lounge cost center) are post-payment routes.
241.features_to_create: Create a financial-relationship registry keyed to (hospital TIN, referring physician NPI) populated from mandatory Stark/EHR-donation and physician-compensation disclosures, then compute for each disclosed physician the share and volume of designated health services referred into the donor system, trended pre/post agreement date. Fire a review flag and a DHS claim hold when referral share jumps above the calibrated percentile after an agreement start or where compensation varies with referral volume; require attestation of fair market value and non-volume-based compensation at revalidation.

242.ways_to_identify: Skin-substitute graft applications billed under one podiatrist's NPI at volumes and product spend far above same-specialty peers, with graft product units purchased from a single distributor and applications occurring at times/places where the billing podiatrist is simultaneously billing elsewhere. Q-code product spend per beneficiary and per rendering NPI per day, plus 'incident to' supervision rules, are all adjudication-visible. Sales-rep involvement surfaces on records review showing no physician signature or an unlicensed applicator's handwriting.
242.features_to_create: Build a rendering-NPI daily capacity and place-of-service concurrency edit for CPT 15271-15278 with paired Q-code units: pend when one NPI's graft applications per day, or graft product dollars per beneficiary, exceed the calibrated same-specialty percentile, or when the same NPI bills applications at two locations in overlapping windows. Trigger a prepay documentation request for wound measurements, product lot/invoice, and the credentialed applicator's identity; suspend on evidence of application by unlicensed personnel.

243.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic: claims assert the podiatrist personally performed skin-graft applications actually done by an unlicensed sales rep, so the payer sees outlier graft volume and product spend concentrated on one NPI with a single graft supplier, and geographic/time impossibility across service sites. Supervision and licensure requirements for skin-substitute application are checkable at adjudication against state licensure files for anyone documented as applying. Confirmation requires records review or beneficiary interviews (patients knew the applicator as 'Dr. Gabe').
243.features_to_create: Implement a graft-application integrity edit: per rendering NPI per date, count 15271-15278 applications and sum associated Q-code allowed amounts, flag above calibrated same-specialty percentile or where per-beneficiary graft spend is an extreme outlier; also flag overlapping service times across POS. Route flagged claims to prepay documentation request requiring the applicator's name and license number, and validate that name against state licensure and payer credentialing files before payment.

244.ways_to_identify: Prescriber-side signal: hundreds of thousands of oxycodone/hydrocodone units dispensed by one pharmacy under prescriptions attributed to 10+ prescribers whose own PDMP/claims histories show little or no opioid prescribing, out-of-area prescriber-patient distances, cash-pay or uniform high-quantity/high-MME prescriptions, and duplicate prescriber signature images. A payer or PDMP analytic can compare each pharmacy's opioid share and prescriber mix against peers and verify prescriptions with the named prescribers before paying.
244.features_to_create: Build a pharmacy-prescriber concordance check: for each dispensing NPI, compute opioid share of scripts, average MME per script, patient-prescriber distance, and the fraction of opioid volume attributed to prescribers whose specialty/claim history is inconsistent with that prescribing; fire when multiple metrics exceed calibrated peer percentiles. Action is prepay suspension of opioid claims plus mandatory prescriber verification (call-back/e-prescribe-only requirement), and referral of the pharmacist to licensure/DEA.

245.ways_to_identify: One certifying physician's NPI appears on plans of care for many unrelated home health agencies with no corresponding face-to-face evaluation claim in her own claim history, and her certification-signing claims cluster in batches. Pre-signed blank forms show as certifications with dates that precede or do not match any documented encounter, and as identical clinical findings across patients. All of this is visible at adjudication by joining HHA claim certifying-physician fields to physician E/M claim history.
245.features_to_create: Build a certification-linkage edit: for each home health episode, require a matching face-to-face encounter claim by the certifying NPI within the required window; deny or pend when absent. Add a certifying-physician monitor computing distinct HHAs served, episodes certified per month, and share of certifications lacking an encounter versus peers, firing prepay review of all episodes tied to that NPI and a documentation request for signed, dated F2F notes.

246.ways_to_identify: This is a DEA recordkeeping/diversion civil penalty rather than a claims-payment fraud, so there is no claim edit that catches it directly; the payer-side analogue is monitoring the pharmacy's controlled-substance dispensing profile and reconciling purchased inventory (ARCOS/wholesaler data) to dispensed claims. Large unexplained gaps between acquisitions of oxycodone/alprazolam and billed dispensing, plus one staff pharmacist accounting for the bulk of controlled fills, are the observable signals.
246.features_to_create: Build an inventory-to-claims reconciliation for pharmacy network participants: per NDC per quarter, compare wholesaler/ARCOS acquisition units to units dispensed on adjudicated claims and flag unexplained shrinkage above a calibrated tolerance. Also compute controlled-fill concentration by individual pharmacist ID on the claim; fire network audit, corrective action plan, and prepay review of controlled-substance claims when either metric breaches.

247.ways_to_identify: Claims show CGx/PGx panels ordered by a small set of telehealth physicians for beneficiaries hundreds of miles away, with no prior treating relationship, no oncology/cancer diagnosis history, and no follow-up care or treatment change after the result. Specimen-collection venues (malls, churches, nursing facilities) show up as clustered service dates and addresses and as bursts of identical panels billed by the same lab. Marketing-company kickbacks per swab are detectable pre-pay through these ordering-pattern signals and lab-marketer contract disclosure at enrollment.
247.features_to_create: Build an order-legitimacy edit for CGx/PGx codes: deny or pend when the ordering NPI has no prior E/M with the beneficiary in a lookback window, when ordering is via a telehealth-only NPI outside the beneficiary's region, or when the beneficiary lacks a supporting diagnosis history. Add lab-level monitors for same-day clustered collections at one geography and share of volume from a single marketing entity, firing prepay suspension and a request for the signed order, medical record, and marketer compensation arrangement.

248.ways_to_identify: Recruiter-driven volume shows as many labs billing high-dollar genetic panels for the same cohort of beneficiaries, orders concentrated in a few physicians who never treated them, and repeat/duplicate panels on the same beneficiary across labs. The sham 'hourly' invoices are post-payment evidence, but per-referral economics are inferable pre-pay from the tight correlation between one intermediary's beneficiary list and multiple labs' claims. Payment-to-billed ratios and lack of any follow-on clinical care are adjudication-visible.
248.features_to_create: Implement a beneficiary-level duplicate-panel and orphan-order edit: deny repeat CGx/PGx panels on the same beneficiary within the clinically implausible window regardless of billing lab, and pend panels whose ordering NPI has no treating-relationship claim. Add a network-graph monitor linking beneficiaries shared across otherwise unrelated labs to common ordering NPIs; when a cluster exceeds the calibrated threshold, place involved labs on prepay review with documentation requests and payment suspension.

249.ways_to_identify: Two catchable points: enrollment, where undisclosed ownership by an individual with disqualifying criminal history is detectable by requiring full owner/managing-employee disclosure and running background/exclusion and address/phone-linkage checks against known bad actors; and adjudication, where a new agency bills millions in counseling units for a narrow member population (American Indian Health Plan) with rendering-clinician hours exceeding feasible workdays and members whose eligibility records were manipulated. Member outreach/EOB verification confirms services never occurred.
249.features_to_create: At enrollment/revalidation, require and verify all 5%+ owners and managing employees against criminal-history, exclusion and prior-adverse-action files plus shared-identifier linkage (address, phone, bank account, EIN) to previously denied entities; deny or place a payment hold on mismatch. At adjudication, monitor new behavioral-health providers for units per rendering clinician per day, member-eligibility-record recency, and month-over-month billing ramp; fire prepay review, session-note documentation requests, and payment suspension for credible fraud allegation.

250.ways_to_identify: An excluded individual's control was hidden behind family-member owners - catchable at enrollment by requiring disclosure of all owners, managing employees and their family relationships, and by linkage checks (shared addresses, phones, bank accounts, prior CHOW history) against the exclusion list. At adjudication, hospice claims show long lengths of stay with no decline, live discharges, non-terminal diagnoses, and marketer-driven admission clusters; certifications lack valid face-to-face visits. The fabricated charts submitted on ADR are detectable by internal inconsistency and identical templated narratives.
250.features_to_create: Build an ownership-integrity screen: match all disclosed owners/managers plus their linked identifiers and immediate relatives against exclusion and prior-fraud files, and hold payments for any hospice whose ownership shares identifiers with an excluded party. Add hospice claim edits for missing/invalid F2F certification, cap-relevant long-stay and live-discharge rates above the calibrated percentile, and admission clustering by referral source; fire prepay ADR with authenticity checks (metadata, duplicate-narrative detection) and suspension on findings.

251.ways_to_identify: No health-care claims-payment component: this is a federal procurement False Claims Act matter about self-dealing subcontracts and unauthorized workers on Navy contracts. The catchable signals sit in contract administration - undisclosed conflicts of interest where a company officer owns subcontractors, and unverified employment eligibility of subcontractor labor - visible from mandatory organizational-conflict-of-interest disclosures, subcontractor ownership data, and E-Verify status.
251.features_to_create: For contract-paying agencies (analogue for payers: vendor/subcontractor integrity), build a conflict-of-interest screen matching officers/employees of the prime against ownership records of all subcontractors and flagging any match before invoice approval, plus a subcontractor-level requirement for E-Verify attestation. Fire invoice hold and contracting-officer review on any owner-identifier match or missing eligibility attestation; no direct claims edit applies.

252.ways_to_identify: The lab's Medicaid/Medicare urine drug testing volume is concentrated in patients from a single SUD clinic and billed under a physician's NPI that the lab was not authorized to use - detectable by measuring referral concentration per ordering NPI and by verifying with the named ordering physician (who had objected). Payments flowing from the lab to the referring clinic owner are visible only on audit, but the one-source referral pattern, uniform high-complexity definitive panels, and standing-order uniformity are prepay signals.
252.features_to_create: Build a lab referral-concentration and order-authenticity check: per lab NPI, compute the share of UDT claims attributable to a single ordering NPI or clinic TIN and flag above the calibrated percentile; require an ordering-provider verification (e-signature or portal attestation) before paying definitive UDT for high-concentration pairs. Provide an ordering-physician dispute channel that immediately suspends payment on claims using that NPI and triggers investigation of lab-clinic financial arrangements.

253.ways_to_identify: Every patient receiving the highest-tier definitive drug-testing code regardless of clinical presentation is a distribution anomaly: near-100% use of the top-paying UDT code, uniform large analyte counts, and testing frequency identical across a whole panel of patients, all visible on claim lines at adjudication. Peer comparison of code-tier mix among labs serving SUD clinics isolates it before payment; medical necessity is confirmed by requesting the ordering rationale and prior test results.
253.features_to_create: Build a UDT code-tier distribution edit: per lab (and per ordering clinic), compute the share of definitive testing billed at the highest analyte-count tier and tests per patient per month, and pend claims when both exceed the calibrated same-peer percentile or when top-tier billing is not preceded by a presumptive screen or documented individualized order. Action: prepay downcode/deny to the supported tier pending documentation request for patient-specific medical necessity.

254.ways_to_identify: Claims for urine drug tests and office visits with no plausible encounter trail: no ordering provider with a treating relationship, beneficiaries geographically remote from the company, and repeat high-frequency testing (97 claims on one member) that no clinical pathway supports. Beneficiary verification letters/EOB response and specimen-tracking (no collection site, no chain of custody) would have exposed it before payment; the two commonly-owned entities billing the same members is another adjudication-visible link.
254.features_to_create: Build per-beneficiary UDT frequency and encounter-linkage edits: cap and pend UDT claims exceeding a calibrated per-member-per-month frequency, deny when no ordering provider encounter exists in a lookback window, and flag when the same members are billed by multiple commonly-owned TINs. Add automated beneficiary verification mailings/portal confirmation for new labs with steep billing ramps, with payment suspension when verifications come back negative.

255.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic as the companion case: phantom UDT screens and office visits from a newly enrolled owner-operated lab with explosive billing growth, no ordering-provider treating relationship, extreme per-member claim counts, and members who deny any contact. Ownership linkage between the two Winston-Salem entities (shared owner, address, bank account) shows a single scheme split across TINs to dilute outlier detection.
255.features_to_create: Implement a common-ownership aggregation rule so outlier and frequency edits are computed across all TINs sharing owner/address/bank identifiers, not per TIN. Combine with per-member UDT frequency caps, an orphan-order denial (no ordering-provider encounter), and a new-provider ramp monitor; when triggered, place the provider group on prepay review with beneficiary-verification letters and suspend payment on negative or non-responsive verification.

256.ways_to_identify: No health-care claim payment involved: this is PPP loan eligibility fraud where five affiliated companies each certified fewer than 500 employees while their affiliate group exceeded the cap. The catchable signal is affiliation - common ownership, shared addresses, shared officers and shared payroll agents across the five applications - plus payroll-tax filings that reconcile group headcount, all available at underwriting.
256.features_to_create: For loan/grant programs, build an affiliation-aggregation screen at application: cluster applicants by owner TIN/SSN, officers, address, bank account and payroll provider, sum reported employees and payroll across the cluster, and reject or refer for manual underwriting when the aggregated headcount exceeds the size standard or when multiple near-identical loan amounts appear in one cluster. Verify headcount against IRS 941/state UI wage records before forgiveness. No payer claims control applies.

257.ways_to_identify: Consumer-directed timesheets were created and approved by the same actor using recipients' and attendants' stolen identities, so the payer can see one device/IP/email/phone submitting and approving timesheets across many unrelated recipients, attendants billing overlapping or impossible hours across multiple members, and attendant identities with no independent contact history. EVV location/time data and duplicate bank-account routing for attendant pay are the strongest prepay signals; the parallel UI claims filed on the same identities show as cross-program identifier reuse.
257.features_to_create: Build an identity/self-approval control for consumer-directed programs: flag and hold any timesheet where submitter and approver share a device fingerprint, IP, phone, email or bank account, or where one identifier appears across recipients in unrelated households. Add attendant-hour aggregation across all members to deny overlapping or beyond-feasible-day hours, require EVV geolocation match to the member's residence, and refer identifier clusters to cross-program (Medicaid/UI) matching.

258.ways_to_identify: Extreme dollars-per-beneficiary: ~$14M across only 37 beneficiaries, with one beneficiary at $736K from the same expensive wheelchair parts replaced hundreds of times. Repeat-replacement counts per HCPCS per beneficiary, replacement intervals far shorter than the part's expected life, and repair billing without a base-equipment history are all computable at adjudication before payment.
258.features_to_create: Build a DME repair/replacement frequency edit: per beneficiary per HCPCS, count lifetime replacements and compare to expected useful life and calibrated peer replacement rates; deny or pend when counts or per-beneficiary annual allowed dollars exceed thresholds, and when repairs are billed without a documented base wheelchair or with no corresponding delivery. Add a supplier-level metric of allowed dollars per unique beneficiary versus peers, triggering prepay review, delivery-proof/serial-number documentation requests, and payment suspension.

259.ways_to_identify: Claim-side signals: visits billed for dates with no EVV check-in, aide hours exceeding feasible schedules, billed units above authorized plan-of-care amounts, and services for members who were hospitalized or otherwise unavailable. Peer comparison of units per member per month and certification/plan-of-care completeness for a small agency with fast revenue growth flags it prepay; the bank-statement and paycheck falsification is a lender-side matter, though the same fabricated payroll would fail a payroll-to-claims reconciliation on audit.
259.features_to_create: Implement an EVV-to-claim reconciliation that denies home health visit lines lacking a matching verified visit record, plus edits capping billed units at the authorized plan-of-care and rejecting service dates overlapping inpatient stays. Add an agency-level payroll-to-billed-hours reconciliation at audit (state UI wage data versus billed aide hours) and place agencies with unexplained gaps or outlier units-per-member on prepay documentation review.

260.ways_to_identify: Epps was already payment-suspended, so the signal is a suspended/excluded individual's fingerprints appearing behind other NPIs: shared billing IP address and portal credentials, shared practice address/phone/bank routing with the suspended provider, and a step-change in Tomczak's and Tyson's psychotherapy volume beginning the month after Epps's suspension. Session-level impossibilities are also visible prepay - psychotherapy units on federal/state holidays, and rendering-hour totals per counselor exceeding a plausible workday. The 25% revenue split is only visible post-pay via bank records, but the suspension-adjacent billing surge is prepay-detectable.
260.features_to_create: Build a suspended/excluded-affiliate linkage engine: for every excluded, suspended or credibly-alleged provider, hash their address, phone, TIN, bank account, portal login ID and submitter IP, and match against all incoming claim submissions; a hit triggers prepay suspension of the linked NPI and a records request. Add a rendering-provider capacity edit that sums timed psychotherapy units per NPI per calendar day and denies/pends when total minutes exceed a calibrated workday ceiling or fall on dates the provider had no active roster, plus a holiday/date-of-service reasonableness flag, and a change-of-behavior monitor firing on volume jumps versus the provider's own 12-month baseline and same-specialty peers.

261.ways_to_identify: This is a Medicare Advantage marketing-kickback scheme, so the payer-side signals are enrolment-pattern rather than claim-line: enrolment applications for a given plan concentrated among a handful of source practices, high shares of enrolees whose 'permission to contact' leads trace to the same clinic staff, and paired financial records showing lump 'coordination of care' advances to physicians who then generate enrolments. CMS can see beneficiary-to-referring-practice concentration and agent/broker attribution in enrolment files before capitation flows.
261.features_to_create: Build an enrolment-source concentration monitor: unit of observation is plan-month by originating practice/TIN, computing share of new enrolees whose lead source, PCP-of-record or agent maps to that practice, firing when concentration exceeds the calibrated percentile versus peer plans in the same market. Pair it with a vendor-payment screen that reconciles plan general-ledger payments to physicians/practices (rent, 'coordination of care', advances) against enrolment counts from those same practices, and pend capitation for review plus require a written fair-market-value/personal-services agreement when correlation is high.

262.ways_to_identify: Detectable prepay from referral-concentration and ordering-pattern data: a single lab receives an outsized share of one physician's orders, and the ordering physicians' toxicology/definitive-drug-test panel volumes and panel breadth jump versus same-specialty peers with no diagnosis support. The disguised remuneration (rent, phlebotomy, toxicology fees) is visible at credentialing/disclosure time as lab-to-referrer payment relationships and as lab lease agreements at referrer addresses; the cash-to-clinic and volume-based marketer commissions surface post-pay in bank and 1099 records.
262.features_to_create: Build a lab-referrer concentration edit: per ordering NPI per quarter, compute Herfindahl concentration of lab referrals and the ratio of high-value toxicology/definitive panels to peer median, flagging pairs above the calibrated percentile for prepay documentation request (medical necessity, treatment plan). Add a relationship screen that joins lab ownership, lease and service-agreement disclosures, shared addresses and lab-issued 1099/commission payments to referring NPIs, and suspend payment on claim streams where the lab pays the referrer, and where marketer compensation is per-test rather than fixed.

263.ways_to_identify: No clinical claim is at issue - the false statement is an annual cybersecurity compliance certification by a TRICARE contractor, so it is caught at contract administration rather than claim adjudication. The observable signals are the contractor's own vulnerability-scan cadence and remediation logs, unresolved third-party and internal audit findings, and configuration evidence for access control, firewall, patching and password policy, which contradict the attestation on file.
263.features_to_create: Build an attestation-versus-evidence reconciliation control for contractor payments: unit of observation is contractor-year, ingesting scan frequency, mean time to remediate critical vulnerabilities, and open audit findings from required artifact submissions, and firing when self-certified compliance is asserted while artifacts are missing, stale, or show unremediated findings. Action is to withhold the compliance-linked portion of the administrative fee and require independent third-party validation before release.

264.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic as the companion case: the lab's payments to referring physicians are dressed up as rent, phlebotomy and toxicology fees, while a marketer earns per-test commissions and pays a clinic cash for orders. Prepay signals are extreme referral concentration from a few practices into one out-of-area lab, toxicology panel volume and breadth far above same-specialty peers, and disclosed or discoverable lease/service arrangements between the lab and its referrers; the cash payments appear post-pay in financial records and 1099s.
264.features_to_create: Implement an ordering-physician/lab dyad analytic: compute per-dyad referral share, distance from patient population, and toxicology panel intensity versus specialty peers, and pend claims above the calibrated percentile pending medical-necessity documentation. Layer a financial-relationship rule that flags any lab claim where the lab has a lease, phlebotomy, service or commission payment relationship with the ordering NPI or its marketing intermediary, requiring fair-market-value and non-volume-based compensation attestation before payment resumes.

265.ways_to_identify: The overlapping shifts are fully visible prepay because both employers bill Medicaid with the same aide/community-support worker identity: the same rendering staff member appears on concurrent time-based units for different beneficiaries at different locations on the same date and hour. Aggregate daily hours per worker across all employing agencies also exceed a feasible workday, and EVV timestamps/GPS for the personal care visits conflict with the telephonic behavioral health encounter times.
265.features_to_create: Build a cross-agency caregiver-overlap edit: key time-based personal care and community support claims by rendering-staff identifier (SSN/license/EVV worker ID) and interval, and deny or pend any claim whose service interval overlaps another paid or pending interval for that worker, regardless of billing TIN. Add a daily and weekly hours-per-worker ceiling edit and an EVV-versus-claim reconciliation that requires visit-level GPS/telephony evidence before payment for flagged dates.

266.ways_to_identify: There is no health-plan claim here - unlicensed importation and retail sale of unapproved drug products containing sildenafil/tadalafil to smoke shops and consumers, so the enforcement route is FDA import screening and state wholesale licensure, not claim adjudication. Observable signals are import entries from foreign manufacturers lacking FDA registration, an importer without a wholesale distributor or pharmacy license, and '100% natural' supplement labeling inconsistent with declared ingredients.
266.features_to_create: Nearest payer-side control is a licensure and product-integrity screen: cross-check any entity billing or supplying drug products against state wholesale/pharmacy licensure and FDA establishment registration, and block payment or network participation on mismatch. For non-payer enforcement, build an import-entry rule linking consignee licensure status to product category and flagging supplement-labeled entries whose supplier ships known PDE-5 API for laboratory verification.

267.ways_to_identify: Every element is detectable at adjudication: inpatient E/M professional claims with a place-of-service hospital whose facility CCN was terminated or reported closed on the date of service; dates of service after the beneficiary's date of death in the eligibility/DMF file; professional inpatient visits for beneficiaries with concurrent nursing-facility or long-term-care residency claims; and summed timed/visit units implying more than 24 hours of provider work in one day.
267.features_to_create: Build four prepay edits keyed to claim line: (1) deny when POS/facility identifier maps to a facility with a closure or termination effective date on or before the date of service; (2) deny when date of service is after date of death; (3) pend inpatient professional visits that conflict with an overlapping institutional stay of a different type for the same beneficiary; (4) compute per-rendering-NPI per-day aggregate service time from RVU/time-typical values and suspend payment with a records request when it exceeds a calibrated 24-hour feasibility ceiling.

268.ways_to_identify: No health care payer is involved - this is identity theft, consumer/commercial lending fraud and embezzlement from a business, so no claim-adjudication signal exists. The only payer-adjacent fact is the defendant's prior health care fraud and kickback conviction, which is an exclusion-list and credentialing signal.
268.features_to_create: Applicable control is an ongoing exclusion/conviction rescreen: re-run all owners, officers, managing employees and billing agents of enrolled providers against OIG LEIE, SAM and court/conviction feeds monthly, and auto-suspend billing privileges and payments when a health care fraud conviction or exclusion appears. Otherwise no payer-side control applies to this conduct.

269.ways_to_identify: Prepay signals in the insurer's own data: patients enrolled in rich individual policies shortly before admission (often with premiums paid by a third party), travelling long distances to two commonly-owned Orange County facilities, and repeated admissions cycling through the same facilities. Level-of-care escalation is visible as drug-positive toxicology at admission for patients whose intake history did not support it, plus billing concentrated in the highest-paying residential/detox day rates and frequent definitive urine drug testing. Broker payments themselves surface in the facility's ledgers - obtainable via audit or, post-pay, financial records.
269.features_to_create: Build an admission-provenance model at the facility level: compute share of admissions with policies effective within a short window before admission, third-party premium payment, out-of-state/long-distance residence, and readmission cycling, firing at the calibrated percentile to trigger prepay review and pre-authorization requirements. Add a level-of-care justification edit requiring ASAM criteria documentation and admission toxicology consistency before paying residential/detox day rates, and a marketing-expense audit rule requiring fixed, FMV, non-volume-based referral-source contracts as a condition of network payment.

270.ways_to_identify: Prepay-detectable through certification and workforce integrity: home health episodes certified by a physician with little or no documented face-to-face encounter claim for the beneficiary, and nursing/therapy visits attributed to a clinician whose license or agency employment/roster ended before the dates of service. In the documentation response, forged records show as identical reused signature images, mismatched fonts/paper artifacts and signature dates inconsistent with the signer's employment period - detectable by image-hash comparison during the records review rather than only after payment.
270.features_to_create: Build a certifying-physician linkage edit that requires a matching face-to-face encounter claim from the certifying NPI within the allowed window and denies episodes lacking it, plus a referral-concentration flag when one physician certifies an outsized share of a single agency's episodes. Add a clinician-eligibility edit checking rendering license status and agency roster/termination dates against dates of service, and in medical-review workflows run perceptual-hash comparison of signature blocks across submitted documents, escalating duplicate-signature-image hits to payment suspension.

271.ways_to_identify: All three mechanics are adjudication-visible: claims for beneficiaries whose eligibility segment is closed or whose date of death precedes the service date; RN-rate procedure codes billed on dates when only LPN staff were on the agency's roster or where the rendering clinician's license is LPN not RN; and aide-hour totals per beneficiary per day/week far above the authorized plan-of-care units and peer distributions. Billing all performed remotely by an out-of-state owner also shows as a single submitter IP/credential across three separate agency TINs.
271.features_to_create: Deploy prepay edits: (1) eligibility/date-of-death gate on every date of service; (2) credential-to-code consistency check joining the rendering clinician's licence type to the skilled-nursing rate code, denying RN-rate lines rendered by LPNs; (3) authorized-units cap comparing billed aide hours to the approved service authorization and pending overages. Add a common-control detector clustering agencies by shared owner, submitter credential and IP, and applying a combined prepay review and records request to the cluster.

272.ways_to_identify: The distinguishing fact is staff qualification: G0156 home health aide services under a plan of care require trained aides supervised under a skilled plan, so the payer can compare the rendering staff's training/certification records and the presence of a skilled discipline on the plan of care against the code billed. Prepay signals are G0156 volume with no concurrent skilled nursing/therapy visits and an agency whose payroll roster shows uncertified staff, with the code mix shifted almost entirely to the higher-paying aide code versus peers.
272.features_to_create: Build a code-versus-qualification edit: for each G0156 line, require an active certified/trained aide identifier on the agency roster and a concurrent skilled discipline visit within the episode, otherwise reprice to the non-skilled personal care rate or pend for documentation. Add an agency-level code-mix monitor computing the share of aide services billed at the skilled-plan rate versus same-state peers and triggering a training-records request when above the calibrated percentile.

273.ways_to_identify: Fully visible in claims: hospital outpatient imaging billed under the hospital's NPI/CCN for beneficiaries with no other encounter at that hospital, and with service-facility addresses (or the equipment/technician location) that are the independent imaging center's, not the hospital's. Also detectable are professional/technical component pairs where the interpreting physician is affiliated only with the imaging company, geographic implausibility between beneficiary residence and the hospital, and a step-change in the hospital's outpatient imaging volume after the arrangement began. The 17% fee split appears post-pay in financial records.
273.features_to_create: Build a place-of-service/service-facility validation edit: deny or pend hospital outpatient (facility-rate) imaging claims whose service-facility address, NPI-registered practice location, or rendering technician/equipment registration is not an enrolled location of that CCN. Add a beneficiary-linkage rule requiring at least one other encounter or registration record at the billing hospital within a defined window, and a hospital-level outpatient-imaging volume change monitor that triggers site-of-service audit and payment suspension for outlier facilities.

274.ways_to_identify: Prepay-detectable via site-of-service and code-context mismatch: surgical neurostimulator electrode implantation codes billed with an office place of service, no operating room or facility claim, no anesthesia claim, and no corresponding implantable-device invoice or HCPCS device code. Volume per physician per day for a supposedly invasive procedure also far exceeds same-specialty peers, and repeat 'implantations' on the same beneficiary within short intervals are inconsistent with a permanent implant.
274.features_to_create: Build a prepay edit that denies neurostimulator implantation CPT codes when place of service is office/clinic and no paired facility, anesthesia, or implantable-device claim/invoice exists, routing them to the correct acupuncture/electro-acupuncture device coding. Add a per-provider frequency and repeat-implant analytic across Medicare and workers' compensation claim feeds, suspending payment and requesting operative reports and device serial-number invoices for providers above the calibrated percentile.

275.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic: high-paying surgical implantation codes submitted for a non-incisional, clinic-applied ear device. Adjudication-visible signals are office place of service, absence of any facility or anesthesia claim, absence of an implantable device HCPCS line or purchase invoice, and implausible per-day volumes and repeat implantations on the same beneficiary versus same-specialty peers.
275.features_to_create: Implement a site-of-service and device-evidence edit that denies neurostimulator electrode implantation codes billed in office POS without paired facility/anesthesia claims and a documented implantable device with invoice/serial number. Add a provider-level outlier and repeat-procedure monitor on these codes, firing above the calibrated percentile to pend claims and issue an operative-report and device-purchase documentation request before payment.

276.ways_to_identify: Diversion at a 'ghosting pharmacy' shows as a purchase-versus-dispense mismatch: ARCOS/wholesaler purchase data show massive hydrocodone/oxycodone acquisition while the pharmacy reports essentially zero dispensing to the state PMP and submits few or no third-party claims for those NDCs. Prescriber-level support is absent entirely, and banking behavior shows structured cash deposits - a post-pay/financial signal, but the purchase-to-dispense gap is available prospectively from wholesaler and PMP feeds.
276.features_to_create: Build a controlled-substance reconciliation engine at pharmacy-NDC-month level: compare wholesaler/ARCOS purchase quantities to PMP-reported dispensations plus billed claims, and flag any pharmacy whose unaccounted-for volume exceeds a calibrated tolerance for immediate on-site audit, DEA referral, and suspension of network participation and payment. Add a zero-or-near-zero PMP reporting flag for pharmacies with active controlled-substance purchases, and a cash-only/no-claims dispensing ratio outlier check.

277.ways_to_identify: Pure employment-tax embezzlement and non-filing; no health care claim, provider enrolment or payer payment is implicated, so no claim-adjudication signal exists. Detection sits with IRS matching of W-2 withholding reported by employees against Form 941 deposits and missing-return indicators.
277.features_to_create: No payer-side claims control applies. The nearest applicable control is a provider-enrolment financial-integrity screen that checks enrolling or revalidating entities and their owners against federal/state tax-lien, unfiled-return and trust-fund-penalty indicators, requiring resolution or a payment plan as a condition of continued billing privileges.

278.ways_to_identify: No health care payer is involved - this is internal embezzlement from a private construction company via self-directed payments, card misuse and duplicate payroll checks. It would be caught by employer-side controls (segregation of duties, bank-account whitelisting, payroll change review), not by any claim edit.
278.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies to the fraud itself; the transferable control for payers and providers is an internal-disbursement monitor that flags payments to bank/card accounts matching an employee's own account, duplicate payroll runs for the same employee-period, and self-approved payroll or bonus changes, routing them to dual approval before release.

279.ways_to_identify: Detectable at eligibility determination rather than claim adjudication: the identity used did not match SSA records for the claimed citizen, and cross-checks of SSN issuance data, immigration/SAVE status, and biometric/photo or wage-history consistency would show the applicant's earnings and residency history diverging from the identity claimed. Continued dual SSA-disability and Medicaid payments over years also present a long-running eligibility redetermination gap.
279.features_to_create: Build an eligibility identity-verification control: at application and each redetermination, match applicant SSN, name, date of birth and citizenship attestation against SSA Enumeration/Numident and DHS SAVE, and suspend benefit and Medicaid capitation/claim payment on any mismatch pending in-person documentary verification. Add a duplicate-identity detector clustering applications by SSN, address, phone and bank account across SSA and Medicaid files, flagging cases where the same SSN shows conflicting demographic or wage history.

280.ways_to_identify: This is a payroll-tax and workers'-comp premium fraud with no health claims component; the payer-side analogue is the workers' compensation carrier and state wage/UI data. The carrier could have caught it by comparing the policy's declared payroll ($169,400) against the volume and dollar value of certificates of insurance issued to unrelated contractors and against checks deposited to the insured's account, and by noting that a single small construction insured was named on dozens of unrelated jobsites. IRS/state cross-match of Form 941/W-2 filings against the ~$8 million of 1099/check payments received by the shell entity would also have flagged the missing withholding pre-audit.
280.features_to_create: Build a carrier-side certificate-of-insurance monitor: unit of observation is the policy; compute count of distinct certificate holders/jobsites and estimated exposed payroll implied by those jobs versus declared payroll, and fire a mid-term premium audit or policy suspension when the ratio exceeds the calibrated percentile for same-class construction policies. Add a data-match rule that flags any insured whose deposited receipts or 1099-reported income greatly exceeds reported payroll with no 941 filings, routing to audit before renewal.

281.ways_to_identify: The Medicare component is fully detectable prepay: home-visit E/M claims (99341-99350) with dates of service after the beneficiary's date of death in the Medicare enrollment/EDB file, or overlapping an active Part A inpatient or SNF stay, are contradictions inside Medicare's own data. The tax evasion piece is not payer-detectable and belongs to IRS asset/offer-in-compromise verification.
281.features_to_create: Prepay edits on the claim line: deny any home/domiciliary visit whose DOS is after the beneficiary date of death, and deny or suspend home-visit claims whose DOS falls inside an inpatient/SNF/hospice institutional claim span. Add a provider-level counter of such conflicts and trigger prepay documentation review of all home-visit claims for providers above the calibrated peer percentile.

282.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic as the companion case: home-visit claims billed for deceased beneficiaries and for beneficiaries who were inpatients on the service date, both verifiable against the enrollment date-of-death field and concurrent Part A institutional claims at adjudication. The falsified records only surface on documentation request, but the date conflicts alone justify prepay review.
282.features_to_create: Implement date-of-death and institutional-overlap edits for place-of-service 12/13/14 E/M codes, denying conflicting lines outright. Track per-NPI rates of home-visit claims per beneficiary-day and share of visits conflicting with institutional stays; providers above the peer percentile go on prepay medical-record review.

283.ways_to_identify: Orthotic brace claims (L-codes for ankle, wrist, knee, back) clustered on a small set of ordering NPIs with no prior treatment relationship to the beneficiary are visible prepay: check whether the ordering physician has any evaluation/management claim history for that beneficiary, and whether ordering physicians are geographically remote from the beneficiary. Critically, the re-enrollment of a new DME entity by a principal whose prior supplier was payment-suspended is catchable at enrollment via ownership/officer, address, phone, and bank-account matching.
283.features_to_create: Prepay edit: suspend brace L-code claims where the ordering NPI has no prior office/telehealth encounter with the beneficiary within a lookback window, or where multi-brace 'combo' orders exceed the peer percentile per ordering NPI. Enrollment control: graph-match new DME applications on owner/officer SSN, address, phone, bank account and billing agent against suspended or revoked suppliers and deny/hold pending review.

284.ways_to_identify: Rapid ramp-up of COVID test billing volume with no corresponding ordering-provider footprint, specimen collection sites, or beneficiary encounter history is visible prepay, as is billing volume implausible for the lab's staffing, CLIA certificate scope and site capacity. Straw ownership is detectable at enrollment by matching listed owners against the true controlling parties through shared addresses, bank accounts, and cross-lab billing-agent and claim-pattern identity across the four labs.
284.features_to_create: Build a lab capacity model: per CLIA/NPI compute daily test volume, distinct beneficiary states, and tests per FTE/analyzer against the certificate scope, and auto-suspend payment when volume exceeds the calibrated capacity or growth percentile. Add an entity-linkage feature clustering labs on shared bank accounts, addresses, billing agents and overlapping beneficiary rosters and place linked clusters on prepay review with documentation requests for requisitions and result reports.

285.ways_to_identify: This is internal drug diversion by a facility administrator, not billed claims, so it is not visible at adjudication; the detection route is facility controlled-substance inventory reconciliation and PDMP/dispensing-to-administration matching after the fact. Signals include emergency-kit and cart counts that do not reconcile to MAR administrations, repeated 'wastage' or missing patches, and the same employee present across multiple facilities with discrepancies.
285.features_to_create: Require and ingest per-facility controlled-substance reconciliation feeds: unit of observation is drug-facility-shift; compute dispensed/kit-stocked units minus MAR-documented administrations plus witnessed waste, and fire an alert when unexplained variance exceeds the calibrated threshold. Add a cross-facility employee-linkage rule that aggregates variance by staff member on duty and refers repeat outliers to the MFCU and licensing board.

286.ways_to_identify: Fully prepay-detectable: claim lines carrying a referring-physician NPI that is deceased or has no other claim relationship with the beneficiary, and service dates after the beneficiary's date of death, are contradictions in Medicare's own enrollment and PECOS data. Also check that the lab's CLIA/test-site license is active and in scope on the date of service, and monitor rapid draw-down of payments by a foreign-resident owner.
286.features_to_create: Prepay edits: reject lab claims where ordering NPI date of death precedes DOS, where beneficiary date of death precedes DOS, or where the ordering NPI has zero encounter claims with that beneficiary in the lookback window. Add an active-CLIA/license-on-DOS edit and auto-suspend payments to any lab exceeding the calibrated percentile for share of claims tied to a single or unverified ordering NPI, with a requisition documentation request.

287.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic: deceased referring physicians and deceased beneficiaries on service dates, plus continued billing after the test-site license expired, all verifiable at adjudication from PECOS, enrollment date-of-death and CLIA status files. Physician complaints of unauthorized NPI use and absent requisitions provide corroboration on documentation request.
287.features_to_create: Implement a license-validity edit that denies lab claims with DOS outside the CLIA/test-site effective period, and date-of-death edits on both beneficiary and ordering NPI. Add an ordering-NPI concentration and 'no prior relationship' feature that triggers prepay suspension and requisition/result documentation requests before any further payment release.

288.ways_to_identify: Prepay signals: respiratory pathogen panel claims billed in bulk for long-term-care residents from a handful of facilities, RPPs billed without a paired COVID test or diagnosis supporting panel-level testing, and near-identical panel utilization per resident regardless of symptoms. The kickback structure (flat-fee marketing agreement plus per-referral 1099 commissions) is only visible in the lab's contracts and payment ledgers, so that is a post-payment/audit or whistleblower route, but the utilization pattern alone supports prepay review.
288.features_to_create: Build an RPP medical-necessity edit: unit of observation is beneficiary-DOS; require a documented symptom/diagnosis code and flag RPPs billed without a same-episode COVID or targeted test, denying or pending lines that fail. Add a facility-cluster feature computing share of a lab's RPP volume from a small set of LTC facilities and per-resident RPP frequency versus peers, triggering prepay review plus a request for the lab's marketing and sales-compensation agreements.

289.ways_to_identify: Detectable at eligibility determination, not claim adjudication: the asset workup showed a $186,000 transfer out and a claimed $194,000 vehicle under the one-automobile exclusion, a valuation wildly inconsistent with a 1961 vehicle's condition and with any independent valuation guide or title/registration record. The same attorney appearing as representative across many LTC eligibility applications with unusual exclusion claims is a second, list-level signal.
289.features_to_create: Build an eligibility-application edit: when a claimed excluded asset's declared value exceeds the calibrated percentile of book value for that make/model/year, or when a large cash transfer within the lookback window is offset by an asset acquisition of similar value, auto-require independent appraisal and title/inspection documents before approval. Add a representative-level analytic aggregating applications by preparer attorney/agent and flagging preparers with outlier rates of high-value exclusion claims for audit.

290.ways_to_identify: Detectable at dispensing and in PDMP data: Schedule II prescriptions written under a hospital's institutional DEA number but signed by a prescriber name with no matching state medical license or individual DEA registration, and 177 scripts to only nine patients at high dosage units. Pharmacies could have validated prescriber license/DEA at fill; PDMP could flag an institutional DEA number generating outpatient oxycodone scripts for a narrow patient set.
290.features_to_create: Prepay/point-of-sale edit: validate the prescriber's individual DEA registration and active state license against the name on the script and reject controlled-substance claims where the DEA number is institutional or the prescriber identity does not resolve. Add a PDMP monitor computing per-DEA-number outpatient CII volume, patient count, and dosage units, alerting the registrant hospital and DEA when an institutional number exceeds the calibrated pattern.

291.ways_to_identify: No health-insurance claims are involved; this is vendor-invoice embezzlement inside a hospital foundation, so no payer adjudication control applies. Detection sits with the organization's accounts-payable controls: new vendors added and approved by the same executive who approves payment, invoices lacking purchase orders or receiving evidence, vendor addresses/bank accounts matching an employee, and consumer-retail purchases run through vendor accounts.
291.features_to_create: Implement AP anomaly controls at the paying organization: unit of observation is invoice; fire when the requester and approver are the same person, when a vendor is new within a short window and receives outsized payments, or when vendor bank/address data matches employee records, holding disbursement pending independent verification. Add merchant-category screening on card and vendor payments to route luxury-retail purchases to internal audit.

292.ways_to_identify: Not a fraud case — it is a personnel announcement about a U.S. Attorney being sworn in, with no claims, provider or payment component. There is nothing for a payer to detect.
292.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies; do not create any feature from this item. If ingested into a case corpus, tag it as non-case so it is excluded from control design and model training.

293.ways_to_identify: Prepay signals: brace L-code claims where the ordering physician's only contact was a brief telehealth encounter from a telemarketing-sourced call center, orders concentrated on a few telemedicine NPIs, and beneficiaries geographically dispersed far from the supplier. Straw ownership is catchable at enrollment by matching listed owners against the true controller through shared addresses, phones, bank accounts and prior enrollment history and by verifying disclosure filings.
293.features_to_create: Prepay edit: pend brace claims whose ordering NPI is a telehealth-only prescriber with no in-person or longitudinal encounter history with the beneficiary, and cap/deny multi-brace bundles above the peer percentile per ordering NPI. Enrollment control: run identity/ownership graph checks on DME applications (owner, officer, address, bank, billing agent) and require site visits plus payment holds for suppliers whose brace-to-total-billing mix and telehealth ordering share exceed calibrated thresholds.

294.ways_to_identify: Prepay detectable through targeted documentation review: a new or low-volume HHA billing episodes with a single certifying physician, and a documentation response containing cut-and-pasted, photocopied or misaligned signatures and notes signed by a nurse no longer employed on the date of service. Cross-check certifying physician face-to-face encounter claims and nurse license/employment dates against visit notes.
294.features_to_create: Build a prepay documentation-request workflow for HHAs above the peer percentile on episodes per certifying physician and on new-provider billing ramp; require submission of orders, F2F encounter notes and visit logs before payment. Add automated authenticity checks on submitted records: signature-image hashing to detect reuse of identical signature bitmaps across documents and validation that each signer's license and employment period covers the documented visit date, with clinician-attribution mismatches triggering payment suspension.

295.ways_to_identify: Visible in PDMP and pharmacy claims before further fills: one internal-medicine NPI issuing oxycodone and promethazine-with-codeine to patients drawn from dozens of states, cash-pay visits with no corresponding E/M claims, high units per prescription, and multiple patients sharing addresses or presenting inconsistent identities. Backdated records only appear on audit, so records authenticity is a post-hoc route.
295.features_to_create: Build a prescriber controlled-substance profile: per NPI compute share of CII/cough-syrup scripts, MME per patient, patient count outside the practice's home state/radius, and absence of paired office-visit claims, firing an alert and pharmacy point-of-sale hold when multiple indicators exceed calibrated peer percentiles. Add a patient-identity dedup check across scripts (shared address/phone, mismatched demographics) and refer flagged prescribers to licensing board and DEA.

296.ways_to_identify: Not a specific fraud case — it is an announcement of a strike-force expansion and an annual recovery total, with no identifiable scheme mechanic, provider or claim set. No pre-payment signal exists to detect.
296.features_to_create: No case-specific control applies; the nearest applicable payer action is to align referral pipelines and data-sharing with the strike force's geography (e.g., routing regional outlier provider lists from existing prepay analytics to that office). Tag the item as a non-case press release and exclude from feature derivation.

297.ways_to_identify: All the red flags cited are present in pharmacy claims data at adjudication: excessive daily MME, early refills before the prior day's-supply is exhausted, concurrent opioid+benzodiazepine+muscle relaxant 'trinity' fills, long travel distances between patient, prescriber and pharmacy, and cash-then-bill patterns. A payer can also see store-level and prescriber-level concentration of these patterns and the absence of documented resolution of red flags.
297.features_to_create: Prepay POS edits: reject or require prior authorization for fills exceeding the calibrated MME threshold, refills before the calibrated percent of days supply elapsed, and trinity combinations without an override reason code documenting the pharmacist's red-flag resolution. Add store- and chain-level scorecards on rate of red-flag fills and per-prescriber concentration, with network-level corrective action, payment suspension, or exclusion referral for outliers.

298.ways_to_identify: Prepay detectable: every paid claim rested on prescriptions from a single ordering provider, an extreme ordering-NPI concentration measurable at adjudication, coupled with high per-beneficiary equipment volume, beneficiaries far from the supplier, and no prior treatment relationship between the ordering provider and the beneficiaries. Delivery-proof and medical-necessity failures surface on documentation request before payment release.
298.features_to_create: Compute per-supplier Herfindahl-style concentration of ordering NPIs and the share of billed dollars from the top ordering provider; when concentration and growth exceed calibrated percentiles, place the supplier on prepay review requiring proof of delivery and medical-necessity documentation. Add reciprocal ordering-provider monitoring that suspends payment when one NPI's DME order volume exceeds same-specialty peer percentiles or lacks corresponding E/M encounters.

299.ways_to_identify: Prepay signals: clinics with beneficiary rosters that are shared across the owner's multiple clinic NPIs, patients traveling long distances, uniform batteries of diagnostic tests per visit regardless of diagnosis, and beneficiaries appearing at several unrelated clinics on the same day — a marker of paid patient recruitment. Beneficiary interviews and complaint data about cash payments provide confirmation; common ownership across the three clinics is verifiable at enrollment.
299.features_to_create: Build a beneficiary-sharing/recruitment detector: unit of observation is beneficiary-month; flag beneficiaries appearing across multiple commonly-owned clinics and clinics whose share of such shared beneficiaries or same-day test-battery uniformity exceeds calibrated peer percentiles, triggering prepay review and beneficiary verification letters. Link clinics by owner/address/bank at enrollment so suspensions apply to all entities of the same principal.

300.ways_to_identify: The signature signal is beneficiary sharing and travel: the same small pool of Medicare beneficiaries appearing across three commonly-owned Detroit clinics receiving identical diagnostic test batteries, often with beneficiaries residing far from the clinic or clustered by recruiter address. Enrollment data linking the three clinics to one owner plus abnormally high tests-per-beneficiary and high new-patient-to-test conversion is visible at adjudication. Payment of beneficiaries is only provable by interview, but the claim pattern (no treatment following abnormal test results, no continuity of care) is prepay-visible.
300.features_to_create: Build a common-ownership cluster entity (link clinics by owner/officer TIN, address, bank account from PECOS) and compute per-cluster shared-beneficiary rate, diagnostic tests per beneficiary per quarter, and beneficiary-to-clinic distance distribution versus same-specialty peers; fire prepay review when multiple metrics exceed calibrated percentiles. Add a beneficiary-level edit for repeated identical test panels at commonly-owned sites with no follow-up treatment claims, requiring records before payment. On naturalization/exclusion checks, re-screen owners of clustered high-risk clinics at revalidation.

301.ways_to_identify: No payer claims-payment component: this is a DOJ asset forfeiture/remission announcement covering Ponzi, wire, EIDL and tax matters. The only health-care-adjacent element is a business email compromise that redirected a company's insurance premium wire, which is treasury/vendor-payment controls, not claim adjudication.
301.features_to_create: Nearest applicable control is payer-side vendor and payee integrity: verify any change to bank routing details for provider or vendor payments through out-of-band callback to a pre-registered number, hold the first payment after any EFT change for a cooling-off period, and alert when multiple providers point to one newly added bank account. No claims edit applies.

302.ways_to_identify: The ordering physician's NPI appears as ordering provider on thousands of DME, compounded pain cream and genetic test claims with no corresponding evaluation or management claim by him or anyone in his group, and with beneficiaries scattered nationwide across many states. Order volume per day per ordering NPI and the ratio of orders to billed patient encounters are both computable at adjudication before the supplier claim is paid.
302.features_to_create: For each ordering NPI, compute per-day and per-month counts of DME/genetic/compound orders, the share of ordered items with no prior E/M or telehealth visit by that NPI within a look-back window, count of distinct billing suppliers relying on that NPI, and geographic spread of beneficiaries; fire a prepay edit denying or pending supplier claims whose ordering NPI exceeds calibrated peer percentiles on order-without-visit share. Escalate ordering NPIs used by three or more unrelated suppliers to payment suspension and records request.

303.ways_to_identify: This is internal drug diversion, not a claim-payment scheme, so it is invisible in claims; the detectable data is the automated dispensing cabinet audit trail — high hydromorphone withdrawal counts per nurse-shift, frequent cancel/null transactions, withdrawals under patients not assigned to that nurse, and mismatch between cabinet dispenses and eMAR administrations/wastage witnessing. Pharmacy inventory reconciliation and patient pain-score non-response provide corroboration post hoc.
303.features_to_create: Build a nurse-shift level diversion model joining ADC transaction logs, staffing/assignment rosters and eMAR: compute controlled-substance withdrawals per shift, cancelled/nulled transaction rate, unwitnessed waste rate, and dispenses for non-assigned patients, all normalized to unit peers; fire an alert and pharmacy audit plus cabinet access review above calibrated percentiles. Payer-side, no prepay claim edit applies; add post-pay review of 340B/inventory reconciliation for units with anomalies.

304.ways_to_identify: Pure employment tax fraud by a remodeling and fence business with no claims submitted to any health plan; nothing in claims adjudication would surface it. Detection route is IRS matching of W-2 withholding reported to Social Security against Form 941 deposits.
304.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. If any payer relationship existed, the nearest analogue is enrollment-time and revalidation screening of an owner's tax-lien/unremitted-payroll-tax status as a financial-risk factor feeding elevated review category.

305.ways_to_identify: Risk-adjustment abuse shows as a sudden, group-wide spike in the prevalence of two narrow, high-RAF spinal codes (spinal enthesopathy, sacroiliitis) among one provider group's MA members, far above same-region same-specialty peers, and codes appearing only on chart-review/addenda rather than on treatment-bearing encounters. Absence of corroborating claims (no imaging at the time, no spine-directed therapy or specialist care) and retro-dated radiology reports supplied only after a plan query are strong prepay/pre-submission signals inside the plan's encounter pipeline.
305.features_to_create: At the provider-group level, compute prevalence and year-over-year delta for each high-RAF diagnosis versus peers, plus the share of those diagnoses lacking any supporting service claim (imaging, injection, PT, specialist visit) within a look-back/look-forward window; suppress unsupported codes from RAF submission and open targeted chart validation above calibrated percentiles. Flag radiology reports whose creation/interpretation date postdates the plan's diagnosis inquiry, and audit addendum-only diagnoses from vendors.

306.ways_to_identify: The lab's mix is skewed to the highest-reimbursing definitive UDT panels with near-uniform panel size per beneficiary regardless of clinical context, and referrals concentrate in a handful of practices whose staff — not the physician — generated orders. Payer can see reflex-to-definitive without presumptive testing, identical panels across unrelated diagnoses, and ordering NPIs whose UDT volume is wildly out of line with their own visit volume; percentage-of-collections marketing paid through shell entities is visible in enrollment/ownership disclosures and post-pay financial audit.
306.features_to_create: Per billing lab, compute distribution of UDT panel tiers, mean analytes per specimen, share of definitive tests without a preceding presumptive test or documented medical necessity diagnosis, and Herfindahl concentration of ordering NPIs; fire prepay pend and documentation request on high-tier panels above calibrated peer percentiles. Add an ordering-NPI edit comparing UDT orders to that NPI's own E/M encounters, and cross-reference lab-disclosed contractor addresses/officers against the lab's own owners to detect self-controlled marketing entities at enrollment.

307.ways_to_identify: Cancer/hereditary panel claims billed at very high unit values for beneficiaries with no oncologist, no family-history workup and no treating relationship, all funneled through a handful of telemedicine ordering NPIs signing hundreds of orders per day across many states. Recruitment shows up as tight geographic clusters of beneficiaries (same neighborhoods, senior centers) sharing an ordering NPI and specimen collection date; kickbacks to marketers are visible only in post-pay financial records.
