307.features_to_create: Build an ordering-NPI daily order counter and an order-without-encounter ratio for molecular/genetic CPT codes, plus a beneficiary-cluster detector keying on collection date, ZIP cluster and shared ordering NPI; auto-pend high-dollar genetic claims failing the treating-relationship test and demand the physician's evaluation record before payment. Cap and prepay-review new labs whose genetic billing per beneficiary exceeds calibrated peer percentiles, and place payment suspension on labs whose top ordering NPIs are shared with other flagged labs.

308.ways_to_identify: The 14-Day Rule violation is arithmetically visible: compare the lab claim's date of service and specimen collection date to the beneficiary's inpatient discharge date on the hospital claim, and look for order/claim dates clustering just past day 14. Systematic clustering of specimen-collection-to-billing intervals at 15-16 days post-discharge for one lab, plus cancelled-and-resubmitted claim histories for the same specimen, is detectable at adjudication once inpatient stay data is joined.
308.features_to_create: Build a claim-level edit joining outpatient reference-lab claims to the beneficiary's recent inpatient/outpatient discharge record: if specimen collection occurred during or within 14 days of the stay, deny the lab's direct bill and route to the hospital as bundled. Add a lab-level monitor for the distribution of days-from-discharge-to-DOS spiking immediately after day 14, and a duplicate/void-and-rebill detector on the same specimen ID or accession, both triggering audit.

309.ways_to_identify: Kickbacks dressed as MSO investment distributions leave two traces: physician-owners appearing in ownership disclosures of management entities whose only economic activity tracks their referral volume, and referral volume to the specific labs rising in lockstep with distributions. At adjudication the payer can see abrupt shifts of a physician's entire lab book to one out-of-state lab, high-dollar cardiovascular/panel testing per patient, and zero patient cost-share collection (copay/deductible waiver) on those claims.
309.features_to_create: Correlate, per referring NPI, monthly test volume/allowed dollars to each lab and flag step changes plus single-lab concentration above calibrated peer percentiles; cross-match physician ownership disclosures and MSO/officer names against lab owners and marketer entities at enrollment to build a relationship graph and pend claims where a referral crosses a financial-interest edge. Add a routine-waiver detector comparing billed patient responsibility to amounts actually collected (remittance/EOB data or lab's own zero-balance pattern), triggering documentation request and referral to SIU.

310.ways_to_identify: Shared rides billed as individual trips are detectable by overlapping trip records: two or more beneficiaries with the same vehicle/driver, same pickup or drop-off address and overlapping time windows, each billed the solo per-trip rate. Trip logs, GPS/telematics and driver IDs submitted with NEMT claims carry the signal at adjudication.
310.features_to_create: At the trip level, cluster claims by driver ID, vehicle, date and time window with pickup/dropoff geocoding; when two or more beneficiaries fall in the same vehicle-time cluster, auto-reprice to the shared-ride rate and deny the excess. Add a provider-level monitor for share of trips billed solo versus peers serving the same facilities, firing prepay review and a request for GPS/manifest records.

311.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic as the companion case: solo-rate billing for rides physically shared. Payer can detect it prepay by joining trip manifests, driver/vehicle identifiers and GPS timestamps and finding multiple beneficiaries transported in one vehicle over the same interval to the same destination facility.
311.features_to_create: Implement a vehicle-time clustering edit on NEMT claims (driver+vehicle+date+overlapping time+matching origin/destination) that automatically downcodes to the shared-ride rate; hold claims lacking driver/vehicle/GPS fields pending manifest submission. Track provider-level solo-trip percentage against peers and open audit above the calibrated percentile.

312.ways_to_identify: Implanted neurostimulator electrode codes billed with an office place of service by a practice with no surgical suite, no anesthesia claim, no facility claim and no implantable device invoice is a self-contradictory claim pattern visible at adjudication. Repetition of the same high-value implant code for the same beneficiary at short intervals (impossible for a true implant) further confirms the P-Stim substitution.
312.features_to_create: Build a prepay edit: deny surgically-implanted neurostimulator/electrode codes when place of service is office, when no companion anesthesia/facility claim exists, or when the same code repeats for the same beneficiary inside a clinically implausible interval; require device invoice/serial number documentation for payment. Add a provider-level counter of implant codes per practice with no ASC affiliation, firing SIU review and prepayment review status.

313.ways_to_identify: Two independent prepay signals: rendering-provider identifiers that do not match any active state license for the billed behavioral health service, and a newly enrolled entity whose president/address/phone/bank account link to an already-excluded or terminated provider. Service volume implausible for the staff roster (units per counselor per day) and identical session notes across recruited beneficiaries round it out.
313.features_to_create: At enrollment, graph-match new applicants' officers, addresses, phones, bank accounts and email domains against the exclusion/termination list and deny or flag for site visit on any match to a barred individual. At adjudication, validate every rendering NPI against the state licensure file for the billed behavioral health code set and deny unlicensed renderers; add a per-rendering-provider daily service-units cap versus calibrated peers that pends claims and requests attendance documentation.

314.ways_to_identify: For the resident diversion, claims show nothing; the signal is in ADC/anesthesia records — controlled substance withdrawals per case versus peer anesthesiologists, waste without witness, and cases where documented administration is less than dispensed. For the amniotic fluid injections, the payer can see an unclassified/experimental biologic billed under a miscellaneous or unlisted code with no FDA approval or covered indication, at high dollars, concentrated in one practice.
314.features_to_create: Build a provider-level controlled-substance reconciliation model (dispensed vs administered vs wasted per case, normalized to same-specialty clinicians) generating pharmacy audit alerts, since no prepay claim edit exists. Separately, maintain a coverage table for amniotic/placental and other investigational biologics: hard-deny unlisted/miscellaneous J-codes for non-approved products, require product name, NDC and invoice on the claim, and pend high-dollar unlisted-code claims from any single practice above calibrated volume.

315.ways_to_identify: The mechanic is billing an add-on psychotherapy code alongside E/M medication management without separate, timed psychotherapy documentation, so it appears as a practice whose psychotherapy-with-E/M pairing rate and average units-per-prescriber-day far exceed same-specialty peers, sometimes exceeding available clinical minutes in a day. Time-in-session math (sum of timed code minutes per clinician per day versus scheduled hours) is computable prepay from claims alone; internal whistleblower complaints indicate the payer should also weight prior compliance history.
315.features_to_create: At clinician-day level, sum minutes implied by all timed codes plus E/M and flag days exceeding plausible working minutes; at practice level compute the share of med-management visits carrying an add-on psychotherapy code versus peers. Above calibrated percentiles, place the practice on prepayment review requiring timed psychotherapy notes (start/stop times, distinct treatment plan) before paying the add-on.

316.ways_to_identify: One APRN-owned clinic billing across three unrelated service lines — orthotic braces, PT and psychosocial rehab — for the same elderly beneficiaries is a scope/mix anomaly visible at adjudication, as is service volume exceeding the licensed staff's possible hours. Templated documentation is detectable when records are pulled: identical patient quotes and repeated typos across many charts, i.e., near-duplicate note text; multi-payer coordination would show the same beneficiaries billed identically to Medicare, MA, Medicaid and commercial plans.
316.features_to_create: Build a provider service-mix breadth check (distinct unrelated benefit categories billed under one enrollment) and a clinician-day capacity check on timed units versus licensed staff FTE; exceeding calibrated peer percentiles triggers prepayment review with mandatory records. On received documentation, run text-similarity/shingle hashing across the provider's notes and fire on high near-duplicate rates; add a beneficiary-kickback signal (same beneficiaries repeatedly appearing with braces plus behavioral health at one address) and move the provider to payment suspension pending investigation.

317.ways_to_identify: Same scheme as the companion case: implausible cross-benefit billing (braces, PT, psychosocial rehab) from a single small clinic, with billed units per clinician per day beyond physical capacity and beneficiaries who never received the devices. Rapid ramp in monthly allowed dollars for a newly high-volume APRN-owned enrollment, plus overlap of the same beneficiary rosters across payers, is visible before payment.
317.features_to_create: Deploy a new-provider velocity monitor (monthly allowed dollars and distinct HCPCS families versus peers with the same specialty and enrollment age) that auto-pends claims on step-change growth; couple it with a clinician-capacity edit on timed units. Add prepay verification for orthotic HCPCS from non-DME-accredited billers, and refer to SIU with payment suspension when device delivery documentation and proof-of-delivery signatures cannot be produced.

318.ways_to_identify: Billing for pre-scheduled appointments that never occurred shows as perfectly regular, calendar-like claim series per beneficiary continuing without interruption for months, including on holidays or after the beneficiary moved or deployed; beneficiary attestation surveys and explanation-of-benefits confirmations would break it. The NPI misuse is detectable at adjudication by checking whether the rendering provider is still affiliated with the billing entity and whether that NPI's total daily units are physically possible.
318.features_to_create: Build a per-beneficiary regularity/periodicity score on repetitive therapy claims (fixed-interval, fixed-unit series with zero gaps and no discharge) that pends the series and triggers a beneficiary verification letter above the calibrated threshold. Validate rendering NPI-to-billing-TIN affiliation and license status on every claim, denying claims for renderers with terminated affiliation, and cap rendering-NPI daily units at a physically possible maximum with prepay pend on breach.

319.ways_to_identify: The scheme rents licensed acupuncturists'/therapists' enrollments across three boroughs, so the signal is one NPI billing implausible daily volumes at multiple locations, shared billing addresses/bank accounts/billing agents across nominally separate practices, and beneficiaries whose only claims are these services with no referring physician. Patient-recruitment kickbacks surface via beneficiary verification letters showing members who never visited; the bribed insurer employees are an internal-controls matter detectable by reviewing which adjudicators repeatedly overrode edits for these providers.
319.features_to_create: Build a rendering-NPI multi-site capacity edit (sum of timed units and locations per NPI per day) plus an ownership/payment graph linking practices by address, phone, bank account and billing agent, pending claims from clusters exceeding calibrated peer percentiles. Add automated beneficiary verification sampling for high-frequency acupuncture/PT series, and an internal audit rule flagging adjudicators/staff with anomalous override or pend-release rates for specific providers.

320.ways_to_identify: The signal is a single ordering NPI whose orders fan out across unrelated DME suppliers, pharmacies and labs in many states with no prior treating relationship — visible at adjudication by joining the ordering NPI on DME/lab/pharmacy claims to that NPI's own E/M history for the same beneficiary. Telehealth E/M claims billed the same day as high-value braces, topical creams or cancer panels, with the telehealth visit and the item ordered from different geographies, plus beneficiaries clustering to a handful of marketing-linked suppliers, are all pre-pay observable. Forged/'doctor-chased' orders also surface as beneficiary and physician complaints and as orders signed by physicians whose claim history shows no telehealth activity at all.
320.features_to_create: Build an ordering-physician fan-out edit: per ordering NPI per month, count distinct billing suppliers, distinct states of beneficiary residence, and share of ordered items with no prior face-to-face E/M by that NPI or their group; suspend payment and request the order plus visit documentation when the composite exceeds the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers. Add a claim-level pairing edit that flags DME/lab/pharmacy claims whose only supporting encounter is a telehealth E/M under the calibrated minimum duration or billed by a telemedicine entity with no other care for that beneficiary. Feed physician/beneficiary complaint intake into the same score so complaint volume triggers prepay review of all downstream suppliers sharing that ordering NPI.

321.ways_to_identify: Social adult day care billing is attendance-driven, so the payer can compare billed attendance days per site against licensed capacity, staffing rosters and building hours — sustained billing above physical capacity is a pre-pay arithmetic check. Rapid enrollment surges of members recruited by marketers, high geographic dispersion of members relative to the center, and overlap of the same members with a related fiscal intermediary or home health entity under common ownership/address are visible in enrollment and claim data. Kickbacks to members are best confirmed post-pay via member interviews and cash-flow tracing, but the shell-entity common-ownership link is detectable at enrolment.
321.features_to_create: Build a site-day capacity edit: for each center and service date, sum billed attendance units and compare to licensed capacity times operating hours; deny or pend the excess and require sign-in sheets. Add an enrollment-velocity monitor per center (new members per month, share recruited within a short window, travel distance) that triggers prepay documentation review and member verification calls above the calibrated percentile, and a common-ownership graph linking the center, fiscal intermediaries and shell entities by owner, EIN, address, phone and bank account to force consolidated review.

322.ways_to_identify: This is eligibility/identity fraud rather than provider billing: the catchable signal is at enrolment, where the applicant's SSN, name and date of birth do not match the SSA/Death Master and credit-header records, or the same SSN is already active in another state or under another name. Duplicate-identity detection across Medicaid and SNAP eligibility files, and address/phone reuse across cases, are pre-payment checks. Confirmation typically requires identity verification with the true holder.
322.features_to_create: Build an eligibility-side identity proofing check that scores every new or renewing application against SSA verification, cross-state duplicate SSN/DOB matches, and reuse of address, phone or bank account across unrelated cases; hold benefit issuance and require in-person identity documents when any hard mismatch or duplicate fires. Add a periodic sweep of active cases against updated death and cross-state enrollment files to suspend issuance mid-cycle.

323.ways_to_identify: No fraud and no claims-payment component — this is a personnel announcement naming an Acting U.S. Attorney, so no payer-side detection signal exists.
323.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. If desired, exclude such press releases from fraud-intelligence ingestion by a source classifier so they do not generate spurious provider risk scores.

324.ways_to_identify: All the tells are arithmetic on the claim line: summed timed psychotherapy units per rendering NPI per day exceeding a plausible workday, service dates after the beneficiary's date of death, and repeated 60-minute sessions for patients whose only other history with that provider is a single pre-surgical evaluation. Provider travel is inferable from a gap between service-date claims and any location/geolocation data, but the impossible-day and post-death checks alone are pre-pay deniable using the eligibility death file and time-unit accumulation.
324.features_to_create: Build a rendering-provider daily time accumulator that sums all timed-code minutes across payers-in-network per NPI per date and denies or pends lines once the total exceeds a plausible workday, plus a hard prepay edit denying any service date on or after the eligibility death date. Add a longitudinal profile edit: when a beneficiary's psychotherapy series follows a single evaluation code with no interval progress-note documentation on file, pend and issue a records request, and route providers whose submitted records show identical templated text to investigation.

325.ways_to_identify: Remote patient monitoring claims concentrated on beneficiaries all sourced from one marketing vendor show up as an abrupt enrollment surge with near-identical diagnosis coding and near-universal billing of the maximum monthly RPM management minutes. At credentialing, ask for and screen marketing agreements for per-referral or per-enrolled-patient compensation; flat 'per lead' terms are the kickback signal. Kickback payments themselves are usually post-pay findings via vendor invoices and bank records.
325.features_to_create: Build an RPM utilization profile per supplier: share of beneficiaries billed the maximum treatment-management tier, monthly enrollment growth, and concentration of referring NPIs or beneficiary acquisition channels; above the calibrated percentile versus peers, pend claims and request the patient consent, device-transmission logs and any marketing contract. At enrolment/revalidation, require disclosure of marketing arrangements and flag per-referral or per-enrollee compensation structures for review before claims are paid.

326.ways_to_identify: Billing new-equipment HCPCS codes requires a serial number and acquisition trail; the payer can require serial numbers on PAP claims and match them against manufacturer recall and prior-billing registries — a serial already billed to another beneficiary or listed on an FDA recall is a prepay denial. Supplier purchase invoices showing acquisition from online resellers rather than authorized distributors, and margins far above peer acquisition cost, are auditable at revalidation. Physical refurbishment is only provable on site inspection, the post-pay route.
326.features_to_create: Build a serial-number edit for capped-rental and purchased DME: require the device serial on the claim, deny when the serial is absent, previously billed to a different beneficiary, or appears on an active FDA recall list, and flag new-vs-used modifier mismatches. Add a supplier-level check comparing invoiced acquisition sources against authorized-distributor lists at revalidation, triggering prepay review and site inspection when secondary-market purchases are detected.

327.ways_to_identify: No health-plan claims were paid — this is theft and diversion of donor-funded commodities plus fraudulent distributor authorization, so the controls are grant/supply-chain, not claim adjudication. The observable signals are inventory reconciliation gaps between shipped and received quantities at the recipient authority, and unverified 'Letter of Authority' documents presented in sole-source procurement.
327.features_to_create: Nearest applicable control: a commodity reconciliation feature that matches donor shipment manifests to recipient warehouse receipts and downstream dispensing counts by lot/serial, firing on unexplained variance, plus an authenticity check that verifies claimed distributor authorization letters directly with the named manufacturer before any sole-source award. No claim-level payer edit applies.

328.ways_to_identify: Service dates while the provider was incarcerated or out of the country are catchable by cross-checking billed dates against public incarceration records and against the provider's own absence of any other activity, and by an impossible-volume check on daily patient counts per solo practitioner. Mass enrollment of new members recruited at schools and events shows as a spike of first-time patients with identical code sets and no cost sharing collected. Fabricated audit records surface post-pay, but records with uniform handwriting/templates and no contemporaneous scheduling data are a review trigger.
328.features_to_create: Build a rendering-provider daily-capacity edit (distinct beneficiaries and total timed units per NPI per date) that pends claims above the calibrated percentile for solo chiropractic peers, and a provider-availability edit that denies dates matching incarceration, license lapse or verified absence records. Add a new-patient surge monitor plus beneficiary verification letters ("were you seen on these dates?") issued prepay when a practice's new-patient share and per-patient visit counts both exceed peer percentiles.

329.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic: billed dates when the provider was in Aruba or incarcerated, plus volumes exceeding a solo practitioner's day, are both computable prepay; and non-covered massage delivered by massage therapists is detectable when the rendering credential on file is not eligible for the billed chiropractic manipulation code. Free-service recruitment shows as zero patient responsibility with high visit counts per newly enrolled member. Record rewriting is a post-pay audit finding.
329.features_to_create: Build a credential-to-code edit that denies manipulative/therapy codes when the rendering provider's licensed scope does not permit them and when supervision requirements are unmet, and a provider-availability edit denying dates matching incarceration or verified absence. Layer a daily-capacity accumulator and a beneficiary attestation mailing triggered prepay for practices with outlier visits-per-member and outlier new-patient acquisition rates.

330.ways_to_identify: Pharmacy claims carry the prescriber NPI, so the payer can test whether the prescriber has any billed E/M encounter with that member near the fill date — controlled-substance fills with no supporting visit history are the core prepay signal. Sequential prescription numbers, identical quantities and dates spread across many patients indicate pre-signed pads, and the prescriber's own claims showing full-time employment elsewhere (or no clinic claims at all) contradicts an active cash clinic. Aggregate MME per prescriber versus specialty peers is visible at adjudication.
330.features_to_create: Build a prescriber-integrity edit on Schedule II fills: require an E/M encounter by the prescriber or their group within the lookback window, and pend fills lacking one; compute per-prescriber monthly MME, patient count, distance travelled by patients and share of cash-clinic patients, suspending payment above calibrated peer percentiles pending chart review. Add a pre-signing detector that flags prescriptions from one prescriber sharing identical drug/quantity/directions across many members with clustered written dates, and cross-check the prescriber's asserted practice location against PDMP and claim-based activity.

331.ways_to_identify: Complaint intake is the loudest signal here: hundreds of physician and beneficiary complaints about orders they never authorized should have suspended payment before further claims were paid. At adjudication, the supplier's orders concentrate on a few ordering NPIs with no treating relationship to the beneficiary, and braces are ordered for beneficiaries with no relevant diagnosis or prior conservative care. Payment for orders is proven post-pay via bank records and marketing invoices.
331.features_to_create: Build a complaint-linked suspension rule: when verified 'order not mine' complaints against a supplier or ordering NPI exceed a calibrated rate per thousand claims, place the supplier on prepay review or payment suspension automatically. Add a supplier-level ordering-concentration and clinical-support edit (share of items from top ordering NPIs, share with no prior E/M or supporting diagnosis) that pends claims and demands the signed order plus the medical record before payment.

332.ways_to_identify: Diagnosis-to-sex and diagnosis-to-code coherence is a hard prepay edit — cervical cancer diagnoses on male beneficiaries, or hereditary cancer panels with no personal/family history codes, can be denied at adjudication. The ordering NP's telehealth claims, if billed at all, show durations and volumes incompatible with real assessments, and hundreds of panel orders from one mid-level with no oncology or genetics practice pattern is a peer outlier. Kickbacks from the telehealth entity are traced post-pay.
332.features_to_create: Build a clinical-plausibility edit for high-cost genetic panels: deny/pend when diagnosis conflicts with beneficiary sex or age, when no qualifying personal or family history diagnosis is present, or when no counseling/E/M encounter by the ordering provider exists. Add an ordering-provider concentration score (panel orders per month, share to a single lab, share with sub-minute or absent encounters) that triggers payment suspension for the lab's claims from that NPI and a documentation request for the order and chart.

333.ways_to_identify: A single nurse practitioner contracted to telehealth companies generating over a thousand brace orders across many states and suppliers is a fan-out outlier computable at adjudication from the ordering NPI on DME claims. Supporting signals: no E/M claim by that NPI for the beneficiary, orders for multiple braces per beneficiary on one date, and beneficiaries geographically remote from the certifying provider. Kickback flows are post-pay bank-record work.
333.features_to_create: Build an ordering-NPI velocity and geography edit for orthotics: per NPI per month compute distinct beneficiaries, distinct states, distinct billing suppliers, braces per beneficiary, and share with no prior face-to-face or documented telehealth encounter; pend all downstream DME claims above the calibrated percentile and require the certification plus encounter record. Add a per-beneficiary duplicate-brace edit denying multiple same-anatomy orthotics within the reasonable-useful-lifetime window.

334.ways_to_identify: The signal is billing under the physician NPI on dates and times when the rendering work was done by NPs — detectable by comparing the physician's claimed daily service volume to a plausible personal workday, and by the absence of any claims under the employed NPs' own NPIs despite payroll/credentialing showing them active. Missing supervision/incident-to modifiers combined with services on dates the physician was not on site is checkable prepay if a provider roster and modifier are required.
334.features_to_create: Build an incident-to/supervision edit: require the rendering provider identifier and, where a physician NPI is billed, verify the practice's credentialed NP/PA roster and physician presence, pending claims where the physician's aggregate daily volume exceeds plausible capacity or where employed mid-levels submit no claims of their own. Compute a practice-level ratio of physician-rate lines to physician availability and refer above-percentile practices for prepay documentation of who performed each service.

335.ways_to_identify: Orthotic braces sourced from one marketer show as extreme concentration of ordering NPIs and near-identical code combinations per beneficiary; eligibility problems (items within reuse windows, deceased or hospice/inpatient beneficiaries) are prepay deniable. Critically, the reincarnation under a nominee owner is catchable at enrolment by matching the new applicant's address, phone, bank account, billing agent, employees and item mix to the entity already under investigation.
335.features_to_create: Build an enrolment identity-linkage graph that blocks or places on prepay review any new DME application sharing address, phone, bank account, billing service, NPI staff, or ownership relations with a supplier under investigation or previously revoked, including nominee-owner patterns. Add a supplier-level brace profile edit (top-referrer concentration, braces per beneficiary, reuse-window and inpatient/hospice overlap) that suspends payment above calibrated peer percentiles pending records, and share both signals with Medicare Advantage plans.

336.ways_to_identify: The arrangement is visible in the correlation between a medical director's stipend and his referral volume — payer-side, the proxy is that a small number of certifying/attending physicians account for most of the hospice's admissions and that those physicians are also the hospice's paid contractors, disclosable at enrolment/revalidation. Rising admission counts tracking new director contracts, plus long lengths of stay and low live-discharge rates, are prepay profileable; the compensation-to-volume link itself usually requires contract and payroll review.
336.features_to_create: Build a certifying-physician concentration monitor per hospice: share of admissions from physicians with a financial relationship disclosed to the payer, month-over-month admission growth per such physician, and comparison to peer hospices; above the calibrated percentile, pend claims and request the medical-director agreements and time logs. Require disclosure of medical-director compensation terms at enrolment and flag agreements whose payment varies with patient census for review before claims are paid.

337.ways_to_identify: Provider-enrolment screening is where this dies: nominee owners are foreign nationals with stolen identities, so SSA/passport identity verification, in-person interview and site visits would fail, and the entities share addresses, leases, bank accounts and billing patterns. At adjudication, hospice election claims certified by physicians who have no other treating relationship with the beneficiary — or whose NPI is being used across several unrelated hospices — plus beneficiaries with no terminal diagnosis history and no prior hospital/oncology utilization, are prepay flags.
337.features_to_create: Build an enrolment control that identity-proofs every disclosed owner against SSA/immigration and death files, requires a verified site visit, and blocks applications sharing address, bank account, phone or billing agent with existing or revoked hospice/home-health entities. At adjudication, add a certifying-physician edit that suspends hospice election claims when the certifying NPI has no prior claims for the beneficiary or certifies for multiple unrelated new hospices, and a clinical-history edit pending payment when no terminal-illness diagnosis or supporting utilization exists; notify physicians of certifications filed in their name.

338.ways_to_identify: Ownership misrepresentation is detectable at enrolment: verify the purchase agreement, source of funds, and continuing control by the prior owner via bank signatory, lease, phone and management-company links, and screen the true controller against exclusion/revocation lists. Post-enrolment, a new-owner DME supplier ramping to nine-figure billing in a short period, with beneficiaries scattered nationwide, no prior treating relationships, and large cash withdrawals from the receiving account, is a payment-suspension case well before $33 million is paid.
338.features_to_create: Build a billing-velocity autopilot for newly enrolled or newly transferred DME suppliers: model claims and paid dollars per week against the supplier's tenure and peer distribution and auto-place on prepay review or suspension when growth exceeds the calibrated percentile, releasing only after proof-of-delivery and beneficiary verification sampling. At enrolment, require and verify ownership-change documentation (funding source, bank signatories, lease, management contracts) and link-analyze applicants to prior owners and known bad actors before granting billing privileges.

339.ways_to_identify: No payer or claim is involved — this is unlawful international distribution of a controlled substance direct to consumers, so there is no adjudication signal. Detection routes are customs/parcel interdiction of mislabeled shipments, payment-processor and marketplace monitoring of the seller's accounts, and DEA import controls.
339.features_to_create: No payer-side claim edit applies. The nearest analogous control is a pharmacy-network/PBM check that flags dispensing or purchase of veterinary-labeled controlled substances by non-veterinary entities and reconciles licensed distributors' pentobarbital acquisition against ARCOS-type reporting; otherwise this is a law-enforcement and customs control.

340.ways_to_identify: The NPI application itself carried the signal: a claimed physician/ARNP taxonomy with no matching active state license number in the state board licensure file, and a credential attestation that never verified against primary-source licensure data. At the pharmacy end, e-prescriptions for a Schedule III arrived under an NPI whose taxonomy/DEA registration did not support controlled-substance prescribing, and one prescription named a real doctor as prescriber while routing from a different NPI/e-prescribing account.
340.features_to_create: At enrolment, auto-verify every NPI/PECOS application's claimed prescriber taxonomy against primary-source state licensure and DEA registration files; mismatch or no-hit puts the NPI in a non-prescribing status and blocks pharmacy claim adjudication. At claim time, deny (prepay edit) any controlled-substance pharmacy claim where the prescriber NPI has no active DEA registration/schedule authority or where the prescriber NPI on the claim differs from the account credential that transmitted the SCRIPT message, and alert the named physician.

341.ways_to_identify: Claims data shows high-volume CGx/PGx panels for beneficiaries with no treating-physician relationship: the ordering NPI is a telemedicine physician with no prior or subsequent E/M claim for that beneficiary, geographically remote, and ordering across many unrelated labs. Beneficiary clustering by recruitment site (many enrollees sharing a marketer's ZIP/date-of-service cluster) and absence of any oncology/hereditary-risk diagnosis history are visible before payment.
341.features_to_create: Build an ordering-physician concentration model: per ordering NPI per month, compute count of high-cost genetic panels, share with no E/M encounter by the orderer within a lookback window, and beneficiary-state dispersion; above the calibrated percentile, suspend payment and issue a documentation request for the order and medical record. Add a prepay edit denying CGx panels lacking a qualifying diagnosis plus a treating-relationship encounter, and flag labs whose referral volume is concentrated in a few marketer-linked ordering NPIs for kickback review.

342.ways_to_identify: The kickback is disguised as MSO investment returns, so the payer signal is the referral pattern: ordering physicians whose lab-test ordering volume and test mix (expensive panels) jump abruptly and route almost exclusively to one out-of-state lab, versus same-specialty peers. Ownership/investment disclosures at enrolment and out-of-state lab claims for in-state patients are visible prepay; the actual MSO payments generally surface only post-payment via bank records, whistleblowers, or Open Payments/tax-record review.
342.features_to_create: Per ordering NPI, compute monthly lab-referral concentration (share to a single lab TIN), out-of-state lab share, cost per patient for lab panels, and change-point detection versus that NPI's own baseline and specialty peers; firing cases go to prepay review with a documentation request for medical necessity and a financial-relationship attestation. Maintain a lab-marketer/MSO entity graph from enrolment ownership disclosures and deny or suspend claims where an ordering provider has an undisclosed financial link to the billing lab.

343.ways_to_identify: This is drug diversion inside a facility; the payer sees little directly, but the hospital's dispensing/ADC (Pyxis) records versus the eMAR expose the nurse: overrides, withdrawals not matched to an administration, and wastage without witness, concentrated on one clinician. Payer-side, charge lines for administered controlled substances that exceed documented administration on the record are detectable in a post-payment record audit.
343.features_to_create: Require facilities to run per-nurse-per-shift reconciliation of ADC withdrawals to eMAR administrations and documented waste, firing on override rate, unwitnessed waste, and withdrawal-without-administration counts above peer percentile on the same unit; positive cases trigger internal referral and payer notification. For the payer, add a post-payment audit sampling controlled-substance charge lines against MAR entries at facilities with reported diversion events, with recoupment where administration is undocumented.

344.ways_to_identify: Same diversion mechanic with a direct billing effect: drugs charged as administered were never given, so line-level pharmacy charges exist with no clinically coherent context (opioid administrations to ED patients whose diagnoses/vitals/orders do not support them, repeated across one nurse's shifts). Prepay, the payer can only see anomalous controlled-substance charge intensity per encounter; confirmation requires MAR/ADC records, so the practical route is a targeted post-payment audit triggered by that signal.
344.features_to_create: Build an encounter-level edit computing opioid administration units per ED visit against diagnosis-adjusted peer norms, and a facility-level metric of controlled-substance charge intensity per ED encounter by administering clinician ID where captured; outliers trigger a documentation request for the MAR and ADC dispensing log with prepay suspension for that facility's flagged claims. Recoup lines where administration cannot be evidenced and refer for diversion investigation.

345.ways_to_identify: Even with a cash-only practice, the prescriptions land in PDMP and pharmacy claims: one prescriber writing Schedule II opioids to essentially 100% of patients, with high MME per day, long-distance patient travel (patient ZIP far from prescriber ZIP), and cash-pay dispensing clusters. Pharmacy claims paid by the plan for prescriptions from that NPI, plus PDMP dispensing counts versus same-specialty peers, are visible before further payment.
345.features_to_create: Per prescriber NPI per month, compute share of patients receiving Schedule II opioids, average daily MME, mean patient-to-prescriber distance, count of distinct dispensing pharmacies, and share of patients traveling over the calibrated distance percentile; above threshold, place the prescriber on prepay review and refer to PDMP/board and DEA. Add a pharmacy-side edit requiring pharmacist attestation/denial for opioid claims from prescribers on the high-risk list.

346.ways_to_identify: The fingerprint is identity hijack of prescribers: new e-prescribing accounts enrolled under existing NPIs with changed phone numbers, emails, and addresses just before a burst of oxycodone and promethazine-codeine prescriptions dispensed at pharmacies far from the prescriber's practice and outside the prescriber's specialty pattern. Pharmacy claims show one prescriber NPI suddenly appearing at many distant pharmacies with cash or unusual payment patterns.
346.features_to_create: Monitor e-prescribing/EHR account provisioning events against the provider master file: fire on demographic change (phone, email, address, MFA device) followed within a short window by controlled-substance prescribing volume above the prescriber's own baseline, and require out-of-band re-verification with the licensed provider before scripts transmit. At adjudication, add a prepay edit suspending controlled-substance claims when prescriber-pharmacy distance and pharmacy-count-per-prescriber exceed calibrated percentiles, and notify the prescriber of record.

347.ways_to_identify: Phantom community-support encounters show up as impossible service-day arithmetic for one worker: billed units per day exceeding a feasible workday, overlapping encounter times across beneficiaries, and services billed on days the worker had no location evidence. Higher-level codes billed uniformly (no variation in duration) against the same beneficiary panel is another prepay-visible pattern.
347.features_to_create: Per rendering-staff identifier per date, sum billed service units/time across all beneficiaries and flag totals above a feasible-day threshold or with time overlaps; auto-deny overlapping units and suspend the remainder pending encounter notes. Add a distribution check on billed duration/level per worker versus agency and program peers, firing on near-constant maximum-unit billing, with a documentation request for progress notes and a supervisory attestation.

348.ways_to_identify: Private duty nursing and personal care billed in excess of hours actually delivered is visible as aide/nurse schedule impossibilities, hours billed exceeding authorized plan-of-care hours, and billing while the beneficiary had an inpatient or ED claim on the same dates. Pre-signed blank notes yield tell-tale documentation: identical signatures/dates across many visits and notes with uniform vitals, detectable via a targeted record request before payment for flagged agencies.
348.features_to_create: Build prepay edits: (1) deny hours exceeding the authorized service plan or overlapping with facility claims for the same beneficiary; (2) per caregiver ID per day, sum hours across beneficiaries and flag over a feasible-day maximum with time overlap detection using EVV timestamps; (3) flag agencies where EVV records are missing or where visit check-in/out geolocation does not match the beneficiary address. Firing agencies go to prepay documentation review and payment suspension pending nursing-note audit.

349.ways_to_identify: One physician signing orders for thousands of beneficiaries she never contacted is measurable prepay: no E/M or telehealth claim from that NPI for the beneficiaries she ordered for, ordering volume orders of magnitude above same-specialty peers, and orders spread across multiple unrelated labs and states. Labs' claims share a single ordering NPI at extreme concentration, and the certification of treating relationship is contradicted by the claim history.
349.features_to_create: Per ordering NPI per month, compute count of genetic-test orders, percentage with no accompanying qualifying encounter claim by that NPI within the lookback window, distinct billing labs, and beneficiary state dispersion; when the no-encounter share and volume exceed calibrated percentiles, suspend payment on all downstream lab claims citing that NPI and request the signed order plus records. Also apply a claim-level prepay edit requiring an encounter link and cancer/hereditary-risk diagnosis for high-cost panels.

350.ways_to_identify: Largely a cash-pay med-spa/FDA misbranding case with no payer claims, so prepay claim edits are not the primary route; the observable signals are an unlicensed owner performing injections and product sourced outside the legitimate US supply chain. A payer or state could catch it via credentialing/licensure checks on any enrolled entity and via product-serialization/wholesaler purchase records, plus adverse-event (botulism) clusters reported to public health.
350.features_to_create: For any enrolled or credentialed injectable-service entity, require primary-source license verification for every individual who administers drugs and verify botulinum-toxin purchases against authorized US distributor records; unverifiable supply or unlicensed administrator blocks enrolment and denies claims. Add a public-health/payer feed linking adverse-event or ED-diagnosis clusters (botulism, injection complications) back to the facility for investigation referral; note that for pure cash practices only licensure/enforcement controls apply.

351.ways_to_identify: Facility claims data exposed the pattern: one surgeon's hysterectomy, sterilization, and elective-induction volume per patient panel far above same-specialty peers at the same hospital, high rates of inductions coded before 39 weeks without a qualifying maternal/fetal indication, and repeat surgeries on the same patients. For Medicaid sterilizations, the required consent form with a 30-day waiting period is a checkable claim attachment — claims paid without a valid, timely signed consent were payable-in-error prepay.
351.features_to_create: Prepay edit: deny Medicaid sterilization claims unless a validated consent form is on file with a signature date at least the required interval before the procedure date, matching patient and procedure. Build a surgeon-level outlier monitor per facility for hysterectomy/sterilization/early-induction rates and diagnosis-support ratios versus same-specialty peers, firing a prepay medical-necessity documentation review on that surgeon's and the facility's related claims, and escalate to the facility's governing body.

352.ways_to_identify: Several checkable signals: wholesale controlled-substance orders placed under prescriber licenses by a non-clinical biller (DEA ARCOS/wholesaler ship-to inconsistent with the registrant's practice address), prescriptions written to a self-related patient identity, and TMS services billed with a rendering provider whose license cannot be primary-source verified. The pain-pump implant claim rests on a cancer history absent from the insurer's own longitudinal claims (no oncology encounters, imaging, or chemotherapy claims).
352.features_to_create: Add prepay edits: deny/suspend claims where the rendering or supervising NPI's license is not verified active for that service (TMS requires licensed clinician), and deny prescriber-written prescriptions where prescriber and patient identity match or share address/SSN. Build a clinical-coherence edit for high-cost implants (intrathecal pump) requiring corroborating diagnosis history in prior claims; absence triggers documentation request and record authentication, plus a feed comparing wholesaler shipments per DEA registrant to that registrant's own prescribing/practice location.

353.ways_to_identify: A third-party biller submitting for two practices produced detectable artifacts: claims where the patient is the biller himself or a household member, upward drift in E/M level distribution after the billing agent took over, and services billed on dates with no corresponding scheduling/encounter record. Cross-payer, the same billing TIN's claim mix shifted versus specialty peers.
353.features_to_create: Flag claims where the subscriber/patient identity matches the submitting billing agent's principals or their dependents (identity match on name, SSN, address) and route to prepay review. Monitor E/M level distribution per practice NPI with change-point detection against its own pre-period and specialty peers, and per billing-agent submitter ID across all client practices; firing submitters get prepay documentation requests on sampled claims.

354.ways_to_identify: This is manufacturer-caused false claims for defective implants; payers can see it in device-level revision-surgery outcomes: linking implant UDI/catalog numbers on hospital claims to subsequent revision-knee claims yields premature-failure rates per device model versus comparators. Signals also include FDA MAUDE complaint density and internal manufacturer knowledge, which the payer learns post-payment via qui tam or recall notices.
354.features_to_create: Build a device-outcome surveillance pipeline: require UDI/device identifiers on implant claims, compute per-model time-to-revision survival curves versus same-category peers, and fire when the revision hazard exceeds the calibrated percentile, triggering a coverage review and FCA referral. Add a prepay edit denying claims for devices under recall or on a non-covered-device list from the recall/FDA feed, with post-payment recovery against the manufacturer for pre-flag claims.

355.ways_to_identify: Reuse of single-use sensors/catheters shows up as a supply-to-service mismatch: a practice bills far more anorectal manometry and pelvic-rehab sessions than its documented purchases of single-use catheters/probes could support, and the manufacturer's shipment volumes are low relative to procedure counts billed by its customers. Prepay, high per-patient session counts for pelvic muscle rehabilitation versus peers is visible; the reuse instruction itself surfaced via a whistleblower, i.e., post-payment.
355.features_to_create: Build a consumable-reconciliation audit: for procedures requiring a single-use device, compare each provider's billed procedure counts to purchase/shipment records obtained from manufacturers or distributors and fire when procedures exceed devices purchased; positive cases get a documentation/attestation request and prepay hold. Complement with a provider-level outlier check on pelvic-muscle-rehab and manometry units per patient versus same-specialty peers, and open manufacturer-level FCA inquiry when multiple customers of one manufacturer fire.

356.ways_to_identify: Classic brace-mill pattern visible prepay: newly enrolled DME suppliers under common ownership billing multi-brace combinations (back, knee, shoulder) to beneficiaries spread nationally, with ordering physicians who have no prior treatment relationship and often no orthopedic diagnosis history. Duplicate braces per beneficiary across the related companies and telemarketing-sourced beneficiary clusters are detectable before payment.
356.features_to_create: Per supplier, compute braces per beneficiary, share of beneficiaries with no prior musculoskeletal diagnosis or orderer encounter, beneficiary geographic dispersion, and ownership links to other suppliers; new suppliers exceeding calibrated growth/percentile thresholds go on prepay review with mandatory order and medical-record submission. Add claim-level edits: deny multi-brace same-day combinations without a supporting diagnosis and orderer encounter, and deny where the same beneficiary already received the same HCPCS within its reasonable-useful-lifetime window, plus beneficiary confirmation letters.

357.ways_to_identify: Same unwanted-and-unordered DME mechanic across two commonly owned companies: rapid billing ramp from newly enrolled suppliers, ordering NPIs with no encounter claim for the beneficiary, beneficiaries far from the supplier, and near-identical HCPCS mixes across both TINs sharing an owner, address, or bank account. Money-laundering transfers are post-payment (bank data), but the claim pattern and the shared-identity enrolment links are prepay signals.
357.features_to_create: At enrolment, graph suppliers on owner, address, phone, bank account, and billing-agent identifiers and inherit risk across the cluster; a flagged cluster puts all member TINs on prepay review. At adjudication, edit for orders lacking a documented treating-provider encounter and for supplier ramp rate above the calibrated percentile, with payment suspension plus beneficiary verification letters before release of funds.

358.ways_to_identify: No health-care claims component — this is PPP loan and forgiveness fraud against SBA. It was catchable at underwriting and forgiveness by cross-checking the applicant's claimed employee count and payroll against IRS Form 941/W-2 filings and state unemployment-insurance wage records for the same quarters; the 500-versus-under-100 discrepancy would appear immediately.
358.features_to_create: For loan/forgiveness programs, build an automated third-party payroll verification: match applicant EIN to IRS 941 and state UI wage-base employee counts and total wages per quarter, and hold disbursement or forgiveness when the application overstates employees or eligible payroll beyond a tolerance. No payer claims control applies; the nearest payer-side analogue is verifying provider-reported staffing/cost-report headcount against payroll tax filings.

359.ways_to_identify: Payer-visible signal is a surge in screening breast MRIs ordered for average-risk women at specific sites: high-risk-justified MRI claims whose beneficiaries lack qualifying genetic, family-history, or prior-cancer indicators in claims history, clustered at providers using one vendor's risk-calculator software. The software defect itself is only knowable post-payment (qui tam/vendor disclosure), but the ordering-pattern anomaly is detectable prepay.
359.features_to_create: Prepay edit for breast MRI: require a documented qualifying high-risk indication (diagnosis code, genetic result, or prior malignancy) present in claim history or attached risk score with the calculation method; absent that, deny or request documentation. Add a facility-level monitor of screening-MRI rate per mammography volume versus peers, with drill-down on the risk-assessment software/version so vendor-linked clusters trigger recovery and referral against the software supplier.

360.ways_to_identify: Risk-adjustment diagnoses that appear only on provider-generated encounter data and never recur in any other setting are visible in the MA encounter feed: cluster the plan's chart-review/EDPS submissions by submitting provider and HCC and look for a single group contributing a spike in spinal enthesopathy (M46.0x) and sacroiliitis codes far above same-specialty peers, with no matching imaging, procedure, DME or specialist follow-on claims for the same members. The retro-dated radiology reports are catchable by comparing report creation/authoring metadata and imaging claim dates to the date the plan first queried the diagnosis. Payment inflation flows through the risk score, so the primary route is a prepay encounter-data edit plus a pre-submission audit before the risk-score run.
360.features_to_create: Build a provider-HCC concentration monitor: unit = (submitting TIN, HCC, sweep period); compute the share of the plan's members receiving that HCC solely from this TIN and the fraction with no corroborating clinical claim (imaging, injection, PT, rheumatology visit) within a trailing window; fire above the calibrated percentile to hold those diagnoses out of the risk-score submission and open a medical-record request. Add a second edit that flags any imaging report supplied as diagnosis support whose service date postdates the plan's query or whose report authoring date is after the encounter's original submission, routing to SIU.

361.ways_to_identify: ESRD monthly capitation/visit codes (MCP tiers) are countable per physician per patient-month, and phantom visits show up as impossible service volume: count distinct dialysis patients billed at the highest visit tier per month per NPI and divide by plausible clinic hours, and cross-check the dialysis facility's own treatment records/place-of-service dates against the physician's claimed visit dates. Also look for MCP billed for months where the patient had no dialysis treatment claims, was hospitalized, or was concurrently billed by another nephrologist.
361.features_to_create: Unit = (nephrologist NPI, beneficiary, month): fire a prepay edit when the MCP tier billed implies more face-to-face visits than the facility's dialysis session records support, when the same beneficiary-month is billed by two physicians, or when the patient was inpatient/absent for the claimed visit dates. Add an NPI-level capacity feature (total MCP patient-months and implied visit hours per day versus same-specialty peers) that triggers prepay documentation review of visit notes.

362.ways_to_identify: Billing 24 hours/day of custodial care per member per day is detectable at adjudication by summing all attendant-hour units per beneficiary per date and comparing to the authorized hours on the plan's own service authorization; the paid authorization said 8 or 12 hours. Cross-check aide-level totals too: the same caregiver IDs cannot cover 24-hour shifts across multiple members. The PPP/EIDL side is not a payer matter, but the SBA loan data (employee counts, payroll) can be compared to the payer's own remitted volumes as a corroboration signal.
362.features_to_create: Prepay edit: unit = (member, date of service); sum personal-care/home-health hour units across all lines and reject or pend anything exceeding the authorized daily hours on the active authorization, with a hard cap edit at 24 hours and a caregiver-level constraint that no single aide ID exceeds plausible daily hours across all members. Add a provider-level monitor on average billed hours per member-day trending upward versus authorization to trigger a records/timesheet request.

363.ways_to_identify: This is an enrolment/credentialing control, not a claims edit: the accrediting inspector and the applicant were related. Screen accreditation records for inspector-to-supplier relationships (shared surnames, addresses, phone numbers, registered-agent or corporate-officer overlap in Secretary of State filings) and for inspectors whose approval rate, inspection duration and time-to-accreditation are outliers versus peer inspectors. Also flag newly accredited suppliers that change ownership shortly after enrolment - the sell-on of enrolled shells.
363.features_to_create: Build an accreditation-integrity model: unit = (inspector, accredited supplier); compute conflict-of-interest matches across name/address/phone/officer data, inspector approval rate and median days-to-accreditation versus peers, and fire to withhold billing privileges pending re-inspection by an independent surveyor. Second control: unit = supplier PTAN; flag change-of-ownership or authorized-official change within a short window of initial accreditation and place a prepay review/payment hold until revalidation.

364.ways_to_identify: The signature volume is the signal: one ordering NPI attached to thousands of orthotic brace claims across thousands of beneficiaries nationwide, with no prior or subsequent E/M relationship with any of them and beneficiary residences far outside the prescriber's service area. At adjudication, brace claims (L-code back/knee/wrist braces) can be tested for an ordering provider whose only claim history with the member is a brief telehealth encounter or none at all, and for multiple braces per beneficiary in a short window.
364.features_to_create: Prepay edit: unit = (orthotic brace claim); deny/pend when the ordering NPI has no in-person or substantive E/M claim for that beneficiary within the lookback window, or when beneficiary-to-prescriber distance and the prescriber's cross-state beneficiary count exceed calibrated percentiles. Add a prescriber-level velocity feature (distinct DMEPOS orders per day and per beneficiary, share of same-HCPCS orders, share tied to a single telemedicine entity) that suspends payment on all downstream suppliers using that NPI and triggers documentation requests for the telehealth encounter record.

365.ways_to_identify: Dispensing without inventory is provable pre-payment by reconciling billed NDC units against wholesaler acquisition data (ARCOS/wholesaler invoices) for the same NDC and period; a pharmacy billing high-cost anticoagulants and inhalers far in excess of purchases cannot have dispensed them. Also visible: the pharmacy's dispensing mix concentrated in a few high-reimbursement NDCs versus peer pharmacies of similar size, refills at implausibly perfect intervals, and no beneficiary cost-share collection evidence.
365.features_to_create: Build an inventory-reconciliation feature: unit = (pharmacy NPI, NDC, month); compute billed units minus wholesaler-purchased units and fire a prepay suspension plus invoice request when billed materially exceeds purchases. Add a high-cost-drug concentration score (share of revenue from top NDCs, growth rate, beneficiaries per prescriber) versus same-size peers, escalating to prepay review of dispensing logs and signature records.

366.ways_to_identify: This is an annual round-up of separate resolutions, so no single control applies; each component has its own prepay signal. Walgreens' never-picked-up prescriptions are catchable by reconciling adjudicated claims against dispensing/return-to-stock events and auto-reversing claims not picked up within the return-to-stock window. Bluestone-style ALF visits are catchable by per-facility, per-day E/M level and visit-frequency profiling; Hurt's genomic tests by telemarketer-sourced orders with no treating relationship; Moffitt by clinical-trial enrolment flags (modifier/condition codes and NCT identifiers) that should route the item to the sponsor; Insys speaker fees are visible in Open Payments matched to Subsys prescribing volume.
366.features_to_create: Build a suite: (a) pharmacy claim-reversal monitor - unit = (Rx claim); auto-recoup when no pickup/dispense confirmation within the return-to-stock window; (b) ALF panel edit - unit = (prescriber, facility, month); flag monthly high-level E/M for nearly all residents versus peers and request notes; (c) genetic-test edit requiring an ordering provider with a treating-relationship claim; (d) research-billing edit requiring trial modifier/NCT reconciliation against sponsor-funded item lists; (e) Open Payments-to-prescribing correlation score triggering prepay review of the drug's claims.

367.ways_to_identify: No payer or health-care claims component exists - this is an investment/wire fraud against private investors, detectable only by banks and securities regulators (funds routed to a personal account rather than an escrow or trade account, altered bank statements). There is no adjudication-time signal for a health payer.
367.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. The nearest analogue is a payment-integrity control on payee banking: verify that remittance accounts are titled to the enrolled legal entity and flag payments routed to personal or newly opened accounts, plus manual review of any submitted bank documentation for alteration.

368.ways_to_identify: Same matter as the companion case: pure wire fraud on private investors with no claims submitted to any health plan, so nothing was catchable at adjudication. Detection sits with financial institutions (personal-account receipt of pooled investor funds, altered statements) and with securities/commodities regulators.
368.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. If a control must be mapped, enforce entity-name-to-bank-account matching and alteration screening on any financial documents submitted during provider enrolment or payment setup.

369.ways_to_identify: Several signals were visible pre-payment: the rendering/supervising individual was unlicensed and operating under a pseudonym, so identity and license verification against the state licensing board and BCBA registry at enrolment would have failed, and the principal had a prior state Medicaid fraud conviction that exclusion/adverse-action screening should have surfaced. At adjudication, BCBA supervision codes billed with no corresponding technician direct-service code on the same date, and ABA services on dates when the child had an inpatient hospital claim, are hard edits. Payroll-versus-claims reconciliation (no employee paid for billed hours) is a records-request test.
369.features_to_create: Enrolment control: unit = (provider, owner, rendering NPI); run identity proofing plus license/certification and OIG-LEIE/state-exclusion and criminal-conviction matching, including pseudonym/alias and incarceration-record checks, and deny or revoke on hit. Prepay edits: reject ABA supervision codes lacking a paired technician service line for the same beneficiary-date; reject any outpatient behavioral service overlapping an inpatient stay; and add a rendering-staff capacity check comparing billed service hours to credentialed staff on file, escalating to a payroll/timesheet documentation request.

370.ways_to_identify: A brand-new supplier at a shared/virtual office space billing orthotics for hundreds of beneficiaries scattered nationwide within months of enrolment is an enrolment-plus-velocity signal: the practice address maps to a mail-drop/coworking suite shared by other billing entities, there is no ordering-provider relationship, and beneficiaries are far outside any plausible service radius. Site verification and beneficiary-geography dispersion are both available before payment; outbound wires to foreign banks are a bank-side signal that arrives after payment.
370.features_to_create: Enrolment control: unit = supplier location; match the practice address against coworking/virtual-office and mail-drop registries and against other enrolled suppliers at the same suite, and require an unannounced site visit before releasing billing privileges. Prepay control: unit = (new supplier, first 6 months); compute claim velocity, distinct-state beneficiary count, median beneficiary-to-supplier distance and share of orders from prescribers with no other relationship to the supplier's members, and place a payment hold with proof-of-delivery and beneficiary-verification requests when above calibrated percentiles.

371.ways_to_identify: This is contractor procurement corruption, not claims fraud: a vendor paying a federal employee for favorable treatment on contract awards. The detectable signals sit in procurement and financial data - a single contracting official repeatedly steering awards to one vendor, sole-source or unusually narrow solicitations, and payments from the vendor to a government employee visible in financial-disclosure filings and bank records. Nothing surfaces at claim adjudication.
371.features_to_create: Build a procurement-integrity analytic rather than a claims edit: unit = (contracting official, vendor); compute award concentration, sole-source rate, and modification/price-growth versus peer officials, and cross-match vendor disbursements against employee financial-disclosure and payroll identities to trigger suspension of award actions pending IG review. Nearest payer-side analogue: conflict-of-interest attestation and vendor-to-employee payment matching before contract award or provider network approval.

372.ways_to_identify: Neurofeedback billed under inapplicable codes with mutually exclusive combinations and inflated time units is entirely visible at adjudication: NCCI procedure-to-procedure and MUE edits catch the impossible pairs and unit counts, and time-based code reconciliation catches billed minutes exceeding the provider's total available clinic minutes per day. Crucially, the payer, an auditor and CMS had already warned this provider - prior audit findings and warning letters should have driven the provider onto prepay review instead of continuing auto-adjudication.
372.features_to_create: Turn on and log NCCI PTP/MUE and time-unit edits for neurofeedback/biofeedback and psych testing codes: unit = (claim, rendering NPI, date); deny lines whose summed timed units exceed the provider's plausible daily minutes or that pair non-billable code combinations. Add a recidivism control: unit = provider; when a provider has prior audit findings or education letters on the same code family and continues billing the same pattern, automatically place the provider on prepay documentation review or payment suspension rather than sending another letter.

373.ways_to_identify: The victims here are franchise buyers, not a payer, so the core fraud has no claim component; however the relabeled devices and the cure claims for Alzheimer's/autism are catchable if any franchise clinic sought reimbursement - unregistered device labeling, missing FDA clearance for the claimed indication, and unlisted/miscellaneous HCPCS codes with unsupported indications. Watch for new clinics from a single franchisor billing an identical unusual code set with identical narratives.
373.features_to_create: Prepay edit: unit = (device/HCPCS, indication); deny electro-stimulation device or therapy claims billed for indications with no FDA-cleared or covered use, and require manufacturer, model and serial number on the claim, rejecting relabeled or unverifiable device identifiers against the FDA/GUDID registry. Add a franchisor-cluster feature grouping providers by shared corporate parent, billing template and address lineage, routing new clusters to prepay review; otherwise this scheme is a consumer-protection matter, not a payer one.

374.ways_to_identify: Common-control across seven supplier PTANs behind straw owners is visible at enrolment through shared addresses, phone numbers, bank accounts, billing agents, authorized officials and Secretary-of-State officers; the same orders and prescribers appearing across all seven confirms the ring. At adjudication, the brace claims share a small set of ordering NPIs with no treating relationship, beneficiaries did not request the items, and per-beneficiary duplicate braces across sibling suppliers are detectable.
374.features_to_create: Build a supplier-affiliation graph: nodes = PTANs, owners, addresses, phones, bank/EFT accounts, billing agents; fire when a cluster exceeds the calibrated size or when a new supplier links to an entity already under review, and apply the payment hold or revocation across the whole cluster. Prepay edits: deny orthotic claims where the ordering NPI has no treating-relationship claim, cap same-anatomic-site braces per beneficiary across all affiliated suppliers, and require proof of delivery plus beneficiary contact verification on flagged clusters.

375.ways_to_identify: This is beneficiary eligibility fraud, catchable at application/renewal rather than in claims: applicants declared low earned income while being owners or officers of retail businesses. Eligibility determination can be run against state wage/quarterly UI records, tax filings, Secretary-of-State officer/owner registries and business license data, plus federal income data hub sources, to detect self-employment income omitted from the application.
375.features_to_create: Build an eligibility verification rule: unit = (application/renewal, household member); cross-match declared income against UI wage records, state tax data and business-registry officer/ownership records, and fire when the applicant is a registered owner/officer of an active business with no reported self-employment income, pending manual verification before approval. Add periodic re-verification that re-runs the match mid-certification and triggers a redetermination and recovery referral on new hits.

376.ways_to_identify: Two checkable things: the rendering provider's credentials (claimed degree/BCBA status) were false, verifiable at credentialing through primary-source degree and certification verification with the awarding institution and the BACB registry; and he billed more than 24 hours of service in a day, an arithmetic impossibility detectable by summing timed ABA units per rendering NPI per date. Assessment and treatment-plan codes billed by a provider whose credential type is not eligible for those codes is also a prepay edit.
376.features_to_create: Credentialing control: unit = rendering individual; require primary-source verification of degree and certification (institution and BACB/state board) before adding to the provider file, with automatic re-verification and claim rejection when credentials lapse or fail verification. Prepay edits: reject when summed timed units per rendering NPI per date exceed available hours, and reject ABA assessment/plan-of-care codes billed under a credential type not authorized for them, routing the provider to documentation review.

377.ways_to_identify: Prepay signals: hereditary-cancer and cardiac panel claims where the ordering NPI has no treating-relationship claim for the beneficiary, orders concentrated from a handful of telemedicine NPIs, beneficiaries spread nationwide with no local clinical footprint, and no follow-up genetic counseling or treatment change after a result. Ownership concealment is catchable at enrolment via identity/family-relationship and address/phone matching plus prior-lab lineage, and billing-shifting across sibling labs is visible when the same order-source prescribers and beneficiaries move between related TINs after a review begins.
377.features_to_create: Prepay edit: unit = (genetic test claim); pend or deny CPT 81xxx/PLA panels when the ordering NPI lacks a qualifying treating encounter with the beneficiary in the lookback window, when the ordering NPI's cross-state ordering volume and per-day order count exceed calibrated percentiles, or when the same panel is duplicated for the beneficiary. Build a lab-affiliation graph on owners, family names, addresses, bank accounts and billing agents that transfers review status and payment suspension across sibling labs, and monitor abrupt migration of a prescriber cohort's volume from one TIN to an affiliated TIN as a suspension trigger.

378.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic: telemarketer-sourced genetic panels signed by telemedicine prescribers with no treating relationship, disguised kickbacks via sham marketing/consulting contracts, and hidden ownership via family nominees. All three are observable pre-payment - the missing treating-encounter claim for the ordering NPI, extreme per-prescriber order velocity and beneficiary geographic dispersion, and enrolment-time ownership matching against relatives and prior sanctioned labs.
378.features_to_create: Implement a treating-relationship prepay edit on high-cost molecular panels (deny/pend absent a qualifying E/M by the ordering NPI) plus an ordering-provider velocity and dispersion score that suspends payment on all labs fed by that NPI. Add enrolment screening that resolves beneficial ownership through family/address/phone/bank linkage to previously sanctioned or reviewed labs, and require disclosure of marketing contracts with per-order or percentage-of-revenue compensation as a condition of billing.

379.ways_to_identify: Identical scheme profile: call-center-generated orders, telemedicine signatures without any patient consultation, kickbacks papered as contracts, and nominee owners. Pre-payment the payer can see genetic panel claims whose ordering NPI has no encounter history with the beneficiary, a tiny set of prescribers driving nearly all of a lab's volume, nationwide beneficiary spread relative to the lab's location, and rapid ramp-up of a newly enrolled lab's high-cost panel billing.
379.features_to_create: Build a lab-level prepay scorecard: unit = (lab TIN, month); features include share of claims from top-5 ordering NPIs, share of orders lacking a treating encounter, beneficiary state dispersion, revenue concentration in a few panel codes, and month-over-month growth; above the calibrated percentile, place the lab on prepay documentation review or payment suspension. Pair with a claim-level edit denying panels without a documented treating relationship and with an enrolment beneficial-ownership graph that blocks re-entry through family-named entities.

380.ways_to_identify: No health-claims component: this is a PPP loan and forgiveness fraud. The catchable signals sit with the SBA/lender at application - ownership listed as the wives while the operating control and signatures trace to a paroled felon (a disqualifier), and forgiveness certifications contradicted by payroll tax filings (941s) and the fact that employee health insurance was cancelled while $660,000 in owner draws left the account. A second loan to the same EIN/affiliated entity should have tripped a duplicate-borrower check.
380.features_to_create: Build a loan-underwriting entity-resolution check: match applicant officers, address, phone, bank account and IP against criminal-history/debarment attestations and against other applications, firing when a declared owner's spouse or associate is a disqualified person or when the same EIN/bank account appears on more than one loan. At forgiveness, reconcile claimed payroll to IRS 941/state wage data and to bank outflows, holding forgiveness for documentation where owner draws or non-payroll transfers exceed reported payroll.

381.ways_to_identify: Pure individual income tax fraud with no payer claim component; the detection route is IRS-side, comparing reported taxable income to third-party reporting (1099s, insurer/payer remittance totals, merchant card receipts) for the practice. A payer contributes only by making its annual paid-claims totals per TIN available for such matching.
381.features_to_create: No payer-side prepay control applies. Nearest applicable control: an annual reconciliation feed of paid amounts per provider TIN/NPI to tax authorities, plus a credentialing flag when a provider is convicted of a tax or fraud offence so the exclusion/revalidation workflow starts.

382.ways_to_identify: No health claims: PPP eligibility fraud by a foreign-government-owned tour operator. The observable signals at application were the ownership chain (owned by the government of Ireland, so ineligible) and affiliated-entity headcount exceeding size limits, both testable against corporate registry/affiliation data and payroll filings rather than the borrower's self-certification.
382.features_to_create: Add an eligibility-screen at loan application that resolves ultimate beneficial ownership against foreign-state-ownership and affiliate registries, and aggregates employee counts across all commonly-controlled EINs from wage-reporting data; fire a manual review hold before disbursement and again before forgiveness when either test fails self-certification.

383.ways_to_identify: Diversion is visible in PDMP and pharmacy claim data before payment: two individuals obtaining high-dose oxycodone from several unconnected prescribers with overlapping fill dates, cash or short-interval refills, and travel distance between patient home, prescriber and pharmacy. Multi-provider 'doctor shopping' counts and MME per day per beneficiary are computable at point of adjudication.
383.features_to_create: Build a beneficiary-level prepay edit computing distinct prescribers and pharmacies for schedule II opioids in a rolling window plus cumulative daily MME; fire a pharmacy-level reject/prior-authorisation requirement above the calibrated percentile versus peers and route the prescriber cluster to investigation. Add a prescriber-level report of patients shared with other high-MME prescribers.
