384.ways_to_identify: Attendance-driven gift-card inducements show up as implausibly perfect attendance: the same cohort of beneficiaries billed the maximum days per week for long unbroken stretches, high units per patient-day, and patients travelling far to a single clinic. The lab kickback shows as near-100% of the clinic's definitive drug tests routed to one lab with high panel-size per test; the DME arm shows one-to-many physician signing of prefilled brace/compression orders and copay waivers.
384.features_to_create: Build a facility-level intensity model on attendance/units per enrolled beneficiary per week and the share of beneficiaries at maximum billable frequency, plus a referral-concentration ratio from clinic to single laboratory TIN; fire prepay review and documentation requests (sign-in sheets, treatment plans) above the calibrated peer percentile. For DME, edit on ordering-physician order volume per day and on braces ordered for beneficiaries with no prior treating relationship, suspending payment pending signed medical-necessity records; flag copay-waiver patterns from zero patient-responsibility remittances.

385.ways_to_identify: No payer claims involved - off-books cash payroll and workers' compensation premium evasion. The signals are financial: millions in check-cashing-business negotiations by a contractor whose 941 wage reports are tiny relative to contract revenue, and workers' comp payroll audits inconsistent with the general contractors' 1099 payments.
385.features_to_create: No health-payer prepay control applies. Nearest control for a workers' comp carrier: build a premium-audit rule comparing insured-reported payroll to third-party revenue and wage data plus check-cashing/currency-transaction patterns, firing an audit hold and premium recalculation when the revenue-to-payroll ratio is an outlier versus same-trade peers.

386.ways_to_identify: The pill-mill leg is visible prepay in prescriber/pharmacy analytics: a small clinic generating extreme oxycodone/Norco volumes, a single pharmacy filling a dominant share of one prescriber's controlled scripts, cash-paid patients travelling long distances, and 'patients' with no other medical claim history. The nursing-home substandard-care leg is best caught by joining survey/staffing data (PBJ hours, immediate-jeopardy citations) to per-diem billing; the never-dispensed drugs leg is caught by comparing dispensed NDC volumes to wholesaler acquisition data (invoice-vs-billed reconciliation), largely post-pay.
386.features_to_create: Build prescriber-pharmacy dyad edits: share of a prescriber's schedule II volume filled by one pharmacy, patients with no non-pharmacy encounter claims, and beneficiary-prescriber distance - firing prepay suspension and DEA referral. Build a pharmacy invoice-reconciliation audit that flags billed units exceeding purchased units per NDC, and a nursing-home payment-integrity flag joining staffing hours per resident day and serious deficiency citations to trigger medical review of per-diem claims.

387.ways_to_identify: Straw-owner enrolment is detectable at credentialing: shared addresses, phones, bank accounts and IPs across dozens of newly enrolled supplier NPIs, foreign-resident owners, recently purchased dormant entities, and no local physical inspection. At adjudication, the billing pattern is unmistakable - catheter and DME volumes per beneficiary far above peers, beneficiaries spread across states with no treating-physician relationship, ordering NPIs whose own claim history shows no such patients, and identical 'consent' recordings reused across beneficiaries.
387.features_to_create: Build an enrolment link-analysis engine clustering applicant NPIs on address, phone, bank, EIN, owner identity and login IP, auto-placing new-supplier clusters on prepay review or payment hold pending site visit. Add adjudication edits on units per beneficiary per period, share of beneficiaries with no prior claim from the ordering physician, and geographic dispersion of a supplier's beneficiaries; add audio-fingerprint/duplicate-hash detection on submitted consent recordings and a beneficiary-verification outreach sample before release of payment.

388.ways_to_identify: Kickback-driven genetic testing shows as orders concentrated from a handful of telemedicine prescribers who have no other treating relationship with the beneficiary, identical prepopulated diagnosis codes across thousands of requisitions, and cancer-panel volumes far above peer labs. The sham pass-through to another lab appears as reference-lab billing where the performing site differs from the billing TIN; the OTC COVID-test leg appears as high test-kit counts per beneficiary with no beneficiary request and fabricated consent recordings.
388.features_to_create: Build a lab-level ordering-concentration and diagnosis-homogeneity check: distinct ordering NPIs, share of claims from telehealth-only orderers, and entropy of ICD codes on requisitions; fire prepay medical review requiring the signed order and the treating-encounter note. Add per-beneficiary frequency caps and duplicate-supplier detection for OTC test kits, plus duplicate-hash checks on consent audio and a place-of-service/performing-lab mismatch edit for pass-through billing.

389.ways_to_identify: All five schemes are visible prepay in claim metadata: stolen beneficiary IDs surface as claims for beneficiaries far from the supplier with no ordering-physician relationship and reused AI 'consent' files; the HRSA Uninsured Program billings surface as a physician submitting hundreds of thousands of specimens through Texas labs with no facility activity, no matching patient encounters, and patient lists identical to a former employer's roster; the never-provided COVID tests surface as billed test volumes exceeding lab capacity/purchased reagent quantities.
389.features_to_create: Build a lab/supplier capacity-plausibility edit: daily tests billed per accession versus staffed capacity and reagent purchases, and claims per rendering NPI per day, holding payment above plausible limits. Add a duplicate-patient-roster detector (overlap of a new biller's patient set with another entity's historical panel), beneficiary-supplier distance and no-prior-relationship edits, consent-audio duplicate hashing, and pre-disbursement bank-account/ownership link clustering for programs that pay uninsured claims without beneficiary cost-sharing.

390.ways_to_identify: Per-test payments to ordering doctors show up as an extreme ordering-volume concentration: a mobile diagnostics TIN whose TCD ultrasound claims come from a small set of physicians whose ordering volume tracks linearly with payments received, with TCDs ordered for patients lacking any neurologic diagnosis or follow-up. Sham 'rental/administrative services' agreements are visible at contract review and in Open Payments/vendor payment records; the medical-necessity failure is visible from diagnosis codes and absence of any resulting treatment change.
390.features_to_create: Build an ordering-physician profile per test code: TCD studies ordered per physician versus same-specialty peers, share of a supplier's volume from top orderers, and the proportion of studies with no supporting neurologic diagnosis or downstream care - firing prepay medical-necessity review and documentation requests. Add a financial-relationship cross-check that flags claims where the ordering physician receives payments from the billing supplier (lease/services agreements) for anti-kickback review before payment.

391.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic as the companion case: per-scan cash/check payments to ordering physicians disguised as fair-market-value rent and admin agreements. Prepay signals are the supplier's TCD volume concentrated in a handful of high-ordering physicians, no neurologic indication on the claim diagnosis, no prior neurology workup, and repeat scans on the same beneficiaries at short intervals.
391.features_to_create: Implement supplier-orderer dyad analytics on TCD/mobile diagnostic codes: orders per physician versus specialty peers, dyad share of supplier revenue, and repeat-scan interval per beneficiary; fire prepay review requiring the order, indication and interpreting-physician report. Cross-reference vendor payment/lease records and Open Payments against ordering physicians and route matches to an anti-kickback review queue with payment suspension.

392.ways_to_identify: Each leg has a prepay signature: hospice enrollees drawn disproportionately from a few group homes and one psychiatric hospital discharge coordinator, with long lengths of stay, live discharges and no decline in status, certified by a single physician; skin-substitute claims with huge product units per patient and no qualifying chronic-wound diagnosis or debridement history; a lab billing kickback-driven genetic panels via shell TINs with a tiny set of orderers; COVID Uninsured Program consultations billed with no supporting encounter data; and opioid prescribers/pharmacies with extreme MME and cash-pay patients.
392.features_to_create: Build hospice admission-source concentration and certification-physician concentration metrics plus long-stay/live-discharge rates, firing prepay medical review of the terminal-illness certification. Add a skin-substitute edit on units/sq cm per wound and required qualifying wound diagnosis with prior conservative-care claims; add lab shell-entity link clustering on address/bank/owner; add prescriber MME and single-pharmacy-share edits with payment suspension and DEA referral.

393.ways_to_identify: Amniotic allograft overuse is visible at adjudication: very high units/square centimetres of skin-substitute product per beneficiary, applications repeated at short intervals, patients with no qualifying chronic non-healing wound diagnosis or prior debridement/offloading claims, and a single mid-level practitioner accounting for extreme product spend versus peers. Kickback-sourced patients appear as beneficiaries with no prior relationship to the practice and clustered referral sources.
393.features_to_create: Build a practitioner-level skin-substitute check computing product units per beneficiary and per wound area, application frequency, and share of applications lacking a qualifying wound diagnosis with documented failed conservative care; fire a prepay documentation request (wound measurements, photos, treatment history) and place outlier NPIs on prepay review. Add a referral-source concentration flag where a high share of beneficiaries arrive from a single marketer or entity.

394.ways_to_identify: Cash-only buprenorphine dosing is detectable through PDMP and pharmacy data even where the visit was not billed: a clinic network whose patients receive high-dose buprenorphine with dose changes that track payment rather than clinical course, no corresponding office-visit claims to any payer, and no counselling or toxicology claims. Prescriber-level dose distribution far above buprenorphine peers plus long patient travel distances are computable prepay at the pharmacy claim.
394.features_to_create: Build a prescriber-level buprenorphine profile: mean daily dose distribution versus peers, share of patients above high-dose thresholds, absence of associated evaluation/counselling or toxicology claims, and patient travel distance; fire prior authorisation on high-dose fills requiring the treatment plan and visit note. Flag clinics whose prescription volume greatly exceeds their billed encounter volume for state licensing/DEA referral.

395.ways_to_identify: Prepay pharmacy claim data shows the mismatch: opioid prescriptions issued with no contemporaneous office-visit claim, the patient residing far outside the prescriber's state, dispensing at a distant pharmacy after nearby pharmacies refused, and a prescriber address that is a residence. Pharmacy refusal patterns and PDMP records carry these signals.
395.features_to_create: Build an edit at pharmacy adjudication requiring a recent evaluation/management encounter from the prescriber for continued schedule II fills, and computing prescriber-patient-pharmacy geographic distance and the number of distinct pharmacies used after prior rejections; fire a reject with prior-authorisation requirement and open a prescriber review. Flag prescribers whose practice location resolves to a residential address with high controlled-substance volume.

396.ways_to_identify: The 'holy trinity' and excessive benzodiazepine pattern is directly computable at pharmacy adjudication - concurrent opioid, benzodiazepine and carisoprodol/muscle-relaxant fills for the same beneficiary from one prescriber, high daily doses, and one pharmacy filling most of that prescriber's controlled scripts. The paired unnecessary office visits show as E/M claims that occur only on prescription-refill dates with thin, templated documentation.
396.features_to_create: Build a concurrency edit at claim level firing on overlapping opioid + benzodiazepine (+ muscle relaxant) days supply per beneficiary-prescriber, with prescriber-level rate versus same-specialty peers, resulting in prior authorisation and a records request. Add a linked-billing check comparing a prescriber's E/M claim dates to fill dates and templated-note indicators (identical durations/no vitals), routing high-rate prescribers to prepay review and exclusion referral.

397.ways_to_identify: The straw-ownership network is detectable at enrolment: twenty-plus DME suppliers sharing addresses, phones, bank accounts, billing agents and beneficiary overlap, with nominee owners of little means and rapid open-close cycles timed to audits. At adjudication, brace claims arrive for beneficiaries with no prior orthopaedic care, from a few high-volume signing physicians who never treated them, and marketer payments booked as 'business process outsourcing' are visible on contract/financial review.
397.features_to_create: Build enrolment link-analysis clustering supplier applications on address, phone, bank account, EIN, authorised official and billing-agent identity, plus a successor-entity rule flagging new NPIs sharing identifiers with recently closed or audited suppliers - action: payment hold and site visit before first payment. Add prepay brace edits on ordering-physician volume per day, ordering-physician-beneficiary prior-relationship absence, and beneficiary-supplier distance, escalating to prepay review and suspension for cluster members.

398.ways_to_identify: Pill-mill signals available prepay: tens of thousands of oxycodone and promethazine-codeine prescriptions from one solo office, extreme MME per patient, cash-pay and long-distance patients, and cross-checks that catch impossible encounters - a prescription or billed visit for a beneficiary who is incarcerated or otherwise institutionalised on that date. Billed in-person visits and counselling with no corresponding pharmacy, lab or vitals data, and identical boilerplate notes, are visible on records request.
398.features_to_create: Build a prescriber controlled-substance volume/MME outlier model with a hard eligibility-status cross-check (incarceration, institutional, deceased files) that rejects claims and fills for dates when the beneficiary could not have been seen. Add an E/M-frequency edit for patients whose only claims are refill-day visits and require submission of progress notes; fire prepay suspension and licensing/DEA referral for prescribers above the calibrated percentile.

399.ways_to_identify: Detectable in PDMP/pharmacy claim data: stimulant and benzodiazepine prescriptions issued to patients with no evaluation encounter, no diagnosis supporting ADHD or anxiety treatment, short intervals between fills, and patients travelling from outside the practice's normal catchment. Prescriber-level Adderall plus Xanax co-prescribing rates versus same-specialty peers are computable before payment.
399.features_to_create: Build a prescriber profile for schedule II stimulants and benzodiazepines: patients per month, co-prescribing rate, absence of a supporting diagnosis or prior evaluation claim, and patient distance - firing prior authorisation on the fill and a documentation request for the initial assessment. Escalate prescribers above the calibrated peer percentile to prepay review and state medical-board/DEA referral.

400.ways_to_identify: This is investor fraud with no claims-payment component - no payer adjudicated anything, so no prepay claim edit applies. The nearest analogue is verifying regulator-issued authorizations directly with the source agency rather than accepting provider-supplied PDFs; an FDA marketing-authorization or licence number given by an applicant should be matched to the agency's public database. Detection here is post-hoc, via bank-flow and investor complaint channels.
400.features_to_create: Where a payer or program accepts any regulator credential (FDA authorization, DEA registration, state licence) as part of enrolment, build an automated source-of-truth verification: parse the claimed identifier and match it against the issuing agency's electronic registry, and hold enrolment when there is no match or the document is submitted as an image without a verifiable number. Flag submitted credential images whose seal/letterhead hashes do not match known agency templates for manual review.},{"index":401,"service_groups":["Pharmacy"],"ways_to_identify":"Street diversion of legitimately dispensed oxycodone is not visible as a false claim, but the upstream supply is: PDMP and pharmacy claims show one beneficiary receiving repeated high-MME oxycodone fills that are then resold. Payer-side signals are early refills, cash-vs-benefit mixing, single-prescriber/single-pharmacy loyalty, and quantities far above same-diagnosis peers. Distribution itself is only reachable post-payment via law-enforcement referral.","features_to_create":"Build a member-level controlled-substance profile joining PDMP and pharmacy claims that computes daily MME, refill-interval compression, prescriber/pharmacy concentration and cumulative days supply, firing a prepay edit requiring prior authorization when a member exceeds the calibrated percentile for their therapy cohort. Add a prescriber-level companion metric (share of panel on chronic high-MME opioids versus same-specialty peers) that triggers a documentation request and referral.

401.ways_to_identify: This is street-level diversion and resale of legitimately dispensed oxycodone plus witness tampering, so the payer-side footprint is limited to the source prescriptions filled for the relative. A payer could see it in pharmacy claims data as a member with repeated early refills of short-acting oxycodone at high MME, cash/no-diagnosis support, or multiple prescriber/pharmacy pairs — visible at point-of-sale adjudication via PDMP and refill-history data. The distribution itself is only detectable through law enforcement, not claims.
401.features_to_create: Build a point-of-sale edit at the member-drug level that computes cumulative daily MME, days-supply overlap, early-refill percentage, and distinct prescriber and pharmacy counts over a rolling window for Schedule II opioids, firing a prepay reject with prescriber-attestation/documentation request when overlap plus multi-prescriber criteria exceed the calibrated percentile for same-drug peers. Pair it with a lock-in program referral and a PDMP cross-check at fill time; add prescriber-level surveillance for opioid volume versus same-specialty peers to find the upstream supply.

402.ways_to_identify: The billing physician's NPI appears as rendering provider on dates he was out of the country, which is testable against travel/absence evidence and, more practically, against internal inconsistencies: incident-to and direct-supervision codes billed on days when no other claim, no facility log, and no supervising presence exists. A payer can also compare the practice's mix of mid-level-performed services to claims submitted under the physician NPI with no NPP claims at all.
402.features_to_create: Build a rendering-provider presence check: per NPI per date of service, count supervision-required or E/M codes and cross-check for the same NPI billing simultaneously at other locations or for gaps consistent with absence; also compute the ratio of physician-NPI claims to employed-NPP claims at the practice TIN. Fire a prepay documentation request for supervision attestation and daily schedules when supervision-required volume under one NPI is implausible or when the practice bills no NPP-rendered lines despite an NPP roster.

403.ways_to_identify: Phantom dispensing is detectable prepay by reconciling billed NDC units against wholesaler acquisition data (ARCOS, 340B/wholesaler purchase feeds, or pharmacy-supplied invoices) - a pharmacy cannot dispense more units of an NDC than it bought. Additional signals: dispensing volume out of line with store size and foot traffic, and high-cost NDCs with no purchase history at all.
403.features_to_create: Build a pharmacy-NDC inventory reconciliation engine: per pharmacy per NDC per rolling period, sum billed units and compare with purchased units from wholesaler/acquisition data, computing a dispensed-to-purchased ratio. Fire a prepay suspension and invoice-production request when the ratio exceeds unity beyond tolerance or when a high-cost NDC is billed with zero recorded purchases.

404.ways_to_identify: A single independent pharmacy billing hundreds of Dificid claims at >$4,000 each is a glaring high-cost-NDC concentration outlier versus same-region peers, and none of it is backed by wholesaler purchases. The listed prescribers can also be canvassed cheaply: prescriber NPIs appearing on the pharmacy's claims with no corresponding office-visit or C. difficile diagnosis history for those beneficiaries.
404.features_to_create: Build two prepay edits: (1) high-cost-NDC concentration - per pharmacy, the share of paid dollars from a single expensive NDC and its z-score versus peer pharmacies, with automatic prepay review above the calibrated percentile; (2) prescription-provenance linkage - require, for flagged high-cost NDCs, a matching diagnosis and recent encounter for the same beneficiary from the listed prescriber, and suspend payment plus send prescriber-verification letters when absent.

405.ways_to_identify: Not a fraud case - this is a personnel announcement with no scheme, defendant, payer or loss. No payer-side detection question arises.
405.features_to_create: No payer control applies; exclude such documents from case-derived control mining via a source-type classifier so they do not dilute analytics.

406.ways_to_identify: Claims carried the credentials of pharmacists who did not work there, which is checkable against state board licensure files and the pharmacy's reported staff roster, and against those pharmacists' concurrent employment elsewhere (same licence appearing as dispensing pharmacist at two pharmacies on the same day/hours). Volume per credentialed pharmacist-hour also exceeds any physically possible dispensing rate.
406.features_to_create: Build a dispensing-pharmacist integrity check: per pharmacy per date, count claims per pharmacist licence, detect the same licence attributed at multiple pharmacies simultaneously, and compare claims-per-pharmacist-shift with the calibrated peer distribution. Fire a prepay edit and require the pharmacy's payroll/roster attestation; suspend payment where the licence holder is not on the reported roster.

407.ways_to_identify: Two signals were available prepay: orders sourced from a marketing entity rather than a treating relationship (orthotic braces with no prior office visit, no musculoskeletal diagnosis, and one physician ordering for beneficiaries scattered nationwide), and continuity of billing after enrolment revocation through successor/related supplier NPIs sharing address, bank account, principals or phone. Signed-order anomalies (identical signature images, unsigned or altered orders) are visible on documentation review.
407.features_to_create: Build (1) a common-ownership/successor-entity graph over enrolment data (address, phone, bank routing, owners, licensees) that blocks payment to any new supplier NPI linked to a revoked entity; (2) an ordering-physician-to-supplier concentration edit for orthotic HCPCS - per ordering NPI, count distinct suppliers, geographic dispersion of beneficiaries, and absence of a prior in-person encounter or supporting diagnosis - firing prepay documentation requests and payment suspension above calibrated thresholds.

408.ways_to_identify: This is lender fraud using a stolen identity, not a claims scheme, so no adjudication edit catches it; the applicable checks sit with the lender (identity verification against SSA/credit-file data, borrower-vs-beneficial-owner mismatch, disbursement to an account not in the applicant's name). A payer's adjacent control is enrolment-side: the pharmacy's disclosed owners versus the person actually receiving financing proceeds.
408.features_to_create: For payer enrolment, build an ownership-disclosure verification that matches disclosed owners/managing employees against identity and corporate-registry data and flags mismatches between listed owners and bank-account signatories, holding enrolment pending resolution. Note in the model that loan-application identity fraud is a lender KYC control, not a payer prepay edit.

409.ways_to_identify: A mobile diagnostics company generating $70M of transcranial doppler claims shows extreme single-CPT concentration, TCDs ordered by a tight cluster of physicians who each order at rates far above same-specialty peers, and TCD volume per beneficiary with no stroke/cerebrovascular diagnosis or follow-up care. The sham rental/administrative agreements are visible in cost/contract review and in the correlation between payments to a physician and that physician's ordering volume - a post-payment analytic that also supports prepay review of the flagged orderers.
409.features_to_create: Build an ordering-concentration and medical-necessity edit for high-volume diagnostic CPTs: per ordering NPI, compute tests per 1,000 panel patients, share of tests lacking a qualifying diagnosis, and share of a single supplier's revenue attributable to that NPI; fire prepay documentation requests above the calibrated percentile. Add a kickback-correlation analytic linking supplier vendor-payment records or disclosed financial relationships to referral volume, escalating to payment suspension when correlation is strong.

410.ways_to_identify: Charitable donation and grant fraud with no insurance claims - nothing for a payer to adjudicate. The applicable control belongs to grantmakers: verify claimed military decorations and DD-214 discharge documents with the service branch/VA rather than accepting applicant-supplied copies, and verify that a claimed housing program has real addresses and residents before disbursing.
410.features_to_create: For any program that grants status or funds on veteran/disability documentation, build automated source verification of the claimed record against the issuing authority and a document-tamper check (metadata, template/seal mismatch, altered fields), holding disbursement on failure. State plainly that no claims-payment prepay edit applies to this case.

411.ways_to_identify: Everything needed was on the claims themselves: time-based psychotherapy units summing to 12-24+ hours in a single day for one solo NPI, service dates on holidays and weekends, and dates falling inside travel windows, plus claims for members who were inpatient on the same date. Cross-payer/cross-employer overlap (billing solo while W-2 employed full-time elsewhere) and claims for members with no other treatment history complete the picture.
411.features_to_create: Build a rendering-provider daily-capacity edit: per NPI per date, convert time-based codes to minutes, and deny or pend any day exceeding a physically plausible workday, with escalation when the pattern repeats. Add conflict edits that pend claims when the same date has (a) an inpatient/institutional claim for the member, (b) concurrent claims for the same NPI under another employer's TIN, or (c) geolocation conflicts, and auto-suspend payments plus request session notes when a provider trips the capacity edit repeatedly.

412.ways_to_identify: One physician NPI signing thousands of DME brace and hereditary-cancer-panel orders for beneficiaries in many states, with no corresponding telehealth E/M claim, no prior relationship, and no cancer or musculoskeletal diagnosis, is visible before the DME/lab claims pay. Batch signing patterns (hundreds of orders same day, identical digital signature) and the ordering NPI's total absence of professional-claim volume relative to order volume are strong prepay markers.
412.features_to_create: Build an ordering-provider integrity score for DME HCPCS and genetic-testing CPTs: per ordering NPI, compute order volume, distinct beneficiary states, ratio of orders to billed telehealth/office encounters for the same beneficiary within a lookback window, and diagnosis support; auto-pend claims from ordering NPIs above the calibrated percentile. Require a matching paid E/M encounter with the ordering NPI as a prepay condition for these HCPCS, with documentation request or denial when absent.

413.ways_to_identify: Kickbacks to patient-recruiting firms are not on the claim, but their footprint is: sudden step-changes in new Medicaid patient volume at a practice, clusters of new patients sharing addresses or arriving in same-day cohorts from outside the normal service radius, and transportation/recruiter links. Practice general-ledger and vendor payments labelled marketing or per-patient fees surface on audit; this is largely a post-payment/credentialing-attestation route with prepay review of the volume spike.
413.features_to_create: Build a new-patient-acquisition anomaly detector: per practice per month, compute new Medicaid patients, their geographic dispersion versus the practice's historical catchment, and same-day cohort clustering, flagging step-changes above the calibrated percentile for prepay review and a vendor-contract/marketing-payment documentation request. Pair with an enrolment-time attestation and audit trigger requiring disclosure of any per-patient marketing arrangement, with recovery under the false-certification theory.

414.ways_to_identify: Drug diversion by clinical staff is caught in facility dispensing-cabinet and EHR data, not payer claims: ADC transactions showing waste discrepancies, overrides, and withdrawals attributed to one CRNA far above peers, plus administrations documented in the chart with no matching pain-score or patient response, and record accesses for patients not on the clinician's assignment. Payer-visible only indirectly, e.g. anesthesia records inconsistent with documented drug use - essentially a post-payment/facility-control matter.
414.features_to_create: Build a clinician-level controlled-substance reconciliation over automated dispensing-cabinet logs and the MAR: per clinician per shift, compute withdrawn-minus-documented-administered-minus-witnessed-waste, override rate, and per-case fentanyl quantity versus same-role peers, auto-escalating outliers to compliance for immediate practice suspension and testing. Add an EHR access-audit rule firing on record access outside assigned patient panel.

415.ways_to_identify: A single NP signing 1,000+ DME orders with no billed evaluation for those beneficiaries, spread across states, is detectable prepay; so is clinical impossibility - a left knee brace for a beneficiary with claims history of left-leg amputation, or bilateral braces for members with no orthopedic diagnosis. Concentration of one ordering NPI across a handful of supplier NPIs indicates a paid-order pipeline.
415.features_to_create: Build (1) a clinical-conflict edit that denies DME laterality/anatomy claims contradicted by the member's history (amputation, prior surgery, prosthesis) using diagnosis and procedure lookbacks; (2) an ordering-NPI volume/geography edit computing orders per month, distinct supplier count, and share of orders lacking any encounter by that NPI, pending payment and requesting the telehealth encounter record above calibrated thresholds.

416.ways_to_identify: The provider billed New York services from Florida: address-of-record versus place-of-service mismatch, no in-state footprint, and psychotherapy/E/M units on dates with no plausible presence are all visible at adjudication. The Adderall prescriptions run to a person with no encounter claims since 2016 - a prescriber-to-patient relationship gap testable against PDMP plus claims. Provider Relief Fund misuse is detected through post-payment attestation audit and revenue-loss reconciliation.
416.features_to_create: Build a prescriber-relationship edit for controlled substances: pend or deny stimulant fills where PDMP/claims show no qualifying encounter with the prescriber within the lookback window. Add a residency/place-of-service consistency edit comparing provider practice address, licensure state, and POS on time-based behavioral claims, pending claims with no in-state encounter footprint; route COVID relief attestations to a post-payment revenue-reconciliation audit.

417.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic as the companion case: psychotherapy and E/M billed for a New York practice location while the provider resided and operated in Florida, with claim volume and daily time units unsupported by any real schedule, and stimulant prescriptions issued to a person with no encounter since 2016. Both are visible prepay from claim-level POS/address inconsistency and PDMP-to-claims linkage; PRF misuse is post-payment audit.
417.features_to_create: Implement a provider-location consistency check (practice address, licence state, POS code, beneficiary residence) that pends time-based behavioral claims lacking any in-state care footprint, plus a daily-minutes capacity edit per rendering NPI. Add a prepay pharmacy edit requiring a documented encounter with the prescriber within a lookback window before adjudicating amphetamine fills.

418.ways_to_identify: Two distinct prepay-visible signals: overlapping/duplicated billable units for the same patient and same clock time (IOP session units billed twice or unbundled into separate codes on one date) and free housing or other value given to Medicaid patients contingent on entering reimbursable treatment, which surfaces in enrolment/marketing materials, patient cohorts sharing sober-home addresses, and rapid re-admission cycling. Address clustering of members across affiliated housing plus census-versus-billed-hours mismatch is computable from claims.
418.features_to_create: Build a same-day time-overlap edit for IOP/group codes: per member per date, sum billable minutes across all codes and providers and deny units exceeding the program's authorized daily maximum or overlapping in wall-clock time. Add a patient-inducement analytic clustering members by residential address and affiliation to the treatment entity, computing share of the provider's census living in affiliated housing and readmission cycling, firing documentation requests and prepay review above the calibrated percentile.

419.ways_to_identify: Members billed for sessions they never attended can be caught prepay by patterns: a solo counselor's panel where many members have no other claims history with the provider, no referral, and no cost-share activity, plus daily time units exceeding a plausible workday. Post-adjudication EOB verification letters to a sample of the counselor's members is the direct confirmation route, and member complaints about services never received are a high-value trigger.
419.features_to_create: Build a solo-provider anomaly bundle: per NPI, compute daily billed minutes, share of panel members with only this provider's claims and no other utilization, and new-member spike rate; pend payment above the calibrated percentile and auto-issue member verification letters with a response window. Escalate to prepay suspension when any member denies receiving services or when the same member's session dates conflict with other providers' claims.

420.ways_to_identify: Worthless-services quality failures are visible pre-payment by joining claim streams to survey/enforcement data and MDS/staffing feeds: PBJ-derived nurse hours per resident day far below same-state peers, repeat immediate-jeopardy or infection-control citations, and MDS records lacking required comprehensive assessments/care plans for residents whose per-diems are being billed. Pharmacy claim data for the same residents showing chain-wide antipsychotic, benzodiazepine, hypnotic and antibiotic prescribing rates above the calibrated percentile is a second observable signal available at adjudication.
420.features_to_create: Build a facility-month quality composite (PBJ staffing hours per resident day, survey deficiency severity history, share of residents with no current MDS assessment or care plan, and psychotropic/antibiotic prescribing rates versus same-state peers) keyed on the facility CCN, and flag facilities in the adverse tail. Firing routes the facility's RUG/PDPM per-diem claims to prepay medical review requiring the care plan and assessment for each billed resident, and triggers a chain-level rollup review across all commonly owned CCNs.  Persistent failure supports payment suspension pending a quality CIA.

421.ways_to_identify: The tell is site-of-service and code-set mismatch: implanted-neurostimulator surgical CPT codes billed with POS office, no anesthesia, no facility claim, no implantable device HCPCS on the same or nearby claim, and often no operative report. Volume of these surgical codes per rendering NPI per day is physically implausible for true implant procedures, and CMS has published guidance that P-Stim/auricular electro-acupuncture devices are not billable as implanted neurostimulators.
421.features_to_create: Prepay edit at claim line level: deny or pend implanted peripheral-nerve/neurostimulator implantation CPTs when POS is office/home, no companion anesthesia claim or facility claim exists for the same beneficiary-date, and no implantable device code is present. Add a provider-month counter of such codes per rendering NPI; above the calibrated peer percentile, place the NPI on prepay documentation review demanding the operative note and device invoice/serial number.

422.ways_to_identify: Look at the ordering physician as the unit: a single NPI signing orthotic/DME orders for geographically dispersed beneficiaries with no corresponding evaluation claim (no office or telehealth E/M in a lookback window) and no prior treating relationship. Cluster the DME claims by ordering NPI and observe the fan-out to many unrelated suppliers plus concentration of a narrow brace HCPCS set arriving in bursts after lead-buying campaigns.
422.features_to_create: Prepay edit: pend brace/orthotic HCPCS when the ordering NPI has no paid E/M or telehealth encounter for that beneficiary within the lookback, or when the beneficiary's residence is beyond the calibrated distance from the ordering NPI's practice. Add an ordering-NPI monthly scorecard (distinct beneficiaries, distinct supplier NPIs, share of orders lacking any encounter) and auto-suspend new orders from NPIs above the calibrated percentile pending records showing the exam and tests certified.

423.ways_to_identify: This is income-tax evasion on lawfully earned Medicaid revenue, so there is no claims-payment control that detects it; the route is a data-match between state Medicaid paid-amount totals per provider TIN and IRS/state receipts reported, which is post-payment and inter-agency. A payer-side proxy is owner-level financial screening at revalidation (personal expenditures funded from the provider account, commingled business/personal banking).
423.features_to_create: Build an annual reconciliation extract of paid dollars per provider TIN/owner SSN shared with tax authorities under an existing data-sharing agreement, flagging providers whose reported receipts differ materially from payer-paid amounts. On the payer side, require enrolled agency provider owners to attest to and reconcile revenue at revalidation and flag failure-to-file indicators for enhanced screening rather than payment action.

424.ways_to_identify: No payer claims component: this is SBA PPP loan fraud. It was detectable at underwriting by cross-matching the applicant EIN against IRS payroll filings (Form 941, W-2/W-3) and state unemployment wage records - the entities had no payroll history at all - and by detecting one owner submitting multiple applications across related entities.
424.features_to_create: For the grant/loan program: an application-level verification service that requires an IRS transcript or state wage-record match for claimed payroll before disbursement, and a common-owner/common-bank-account dedupe across applications. No health-payer control applies; the nearest analogue is owner-level cross-entity linkage at provider enrolment.

425.ways_to_identify: This is a Controlled Substances Act recordkeeping case rather than a false-claim case, but it is observable from data payers and regulators already hold: DEA ARCOS purchase volumes for the registrant compared to dispensing/administration records and to claims showing office-administered controlled substances. A gap between quantities purchased and quantities documented as dispensed is the signal.
425.features_to_create: Build a registrant-level reconciliation comparing controlled-substance acquisition (ARCOS/wholesaler data) with dispensed/administered quantities evidenced in claims and PDMP records; flag unexplained variance for an on-site records audit. For the payer, add a credentialing check that the practice holds current DEA registration and passes recordkeeping audit before paying for in-office controlled-substance administration.

426.ways_to_identify: Face-to-face SNF visit codes are checkable against independent facility data before payment: the beneficiary must be a resident on the service date (matching SNF per-diem/MDS records), and the rendering physician's daily visit count and total implied minutes must be feasible. Concentration of a single NPI billing high-level subsequent-visit codes across many facilities on the same day, and visits on dates the beneficiary was hospitalized or discharged, are the observable flags.
426.features_to_create: Prepay edits: (a) deny SNF visit codes where no overlapping SNF stay exists for the beneficiary on the date of service or an inpatient/hospice overlap exists; (b) compute per rendering-NPI-day the count of nursing-facility visits and implied service minutes and pend claims above the feasibility ceiling. Providers repeatedly firing go on prepay documentation review requiring signed, dated progress notes with facility sign-in logs.

427.ways_to_identify: Two signals are visible at adjudication: implied service time per rendering provider per day exceeding a feasible workday (summing timed psychotherapy units), and a family/household relationship between the rendering provider and the members treated, detectable via shared surname, address, subscriber/dependent linkage on the same policy. Near-daily 60-minute sessions for the same small set of members every day of the year is also an outlier frequency pattern.
427.features_to_create: Build a rendering-provider-day minute accumulator across all timed psychotherapy codes and hard-deny/pend claims once cumulative minutes exceed a feasible day. Add a relationship edit that flags claims where the rendering provider shares subscriber policy, address or surname with the patient, and pend for self/family-treatment review; combine with a member-year session-frequency outlier flag for documentation request.

428.ways_to_identify: Diversion shows as acquisition-versus-administration imbalance: the practice's purchases of high-cost oncology drugs from wholesalers (837/ASP or wholesaler data, DSCSA transaction records) vastly exceed units billed as administered to patients. Payers can also see the buy-and-bill mix - J-code units billed per infusion-eligible patient panel - and downstream sales appearing from an entity with no dispensing licence.
428.features_to_create: Build a practice-level monthly reconciliation of purchased units (wholesaler/DSCSA feed or invoice submission requirement) against J-code units billed for administration; flag material unexplained surplus for investigation and require invoice submission as a condition of payment for high-cost biologics. Add a licence check that purchasers/resellers in the DSCSA chain hold valid wholesale distributor licences, flagging unlicensed downstream buyers.

429.ways_to_identify: The scheme's fingerprint is a single mobile diagnostics company billing one narrow test (TCD) at enormous volume concentrated among a small set of ordering physicians, with the same physicians simultaneously receiving space-rental/administrative payments that track test counts. Ordering-volume-per-physician outliers, absence of neurologic indications in the diagnosis history, and lack of any follow-up treatment for abnormal findings are all visible in claims before payment.
429.features_to_create: Build an ordering-physician/testing-entity dyad model: tests per ordering NPI per month, share of the entity's revenue from the top few orderers, and share of scans with no supporting neurologic diagnosis or subsequent related care; fire prepay review above the calibrated percentile. Require the mobile diagnostic entity to disclose all financial arrangements with ordering physicians at enrolment and run per-test-correlation analysis on rental payments; unresolved concentration triggers payment suspension.

430.ways_to_identify: Massive, fast revenue ramp at one agency plus visit-level implausibility: EVV records absent or mismatched to billed visits, aides billed while beneficiary was inpatient, aides who are the patient's own household members, and aide NPIs/employee IDs with billed hours exceeding a feasible workday. Nursing notes that are byte-identical across visits and patients are detectable by text-similarity scoring on submitted documentation, and aide certification can be verified against state registries at enrolment.
430.features_to_create: Prepay edits: deny visits with no matching EVV check-in/out geolocated at the member's address, deny overlapping-hour claims per caregiver, and flag caregiver-patient household/relationship matches for review. Add an agency-level growth-and-concentration monitor (month-over-month paid growth, referral-source concentration, share of Plans of Care signed by a small set of physicians) and place fast-growing agencies on prepay review with near-duplicate-text detection on nursing notes; aide certification registry match required before hours are payable.

431.ways_to_identify: Brace claims traceable to telemarketing-plus-telemedicine mills share a signature: a small pool of ordering NPIs writing orders for beneficiaries spread across many states and many unrelated supplier NPIs, with no prior treating relationship and often no telehealth encounter claim of adequate duration. Cross-payer view (Medicare plus TRICARE) shows the same orderers and the same lead-source clustering.
431.features_to_create: Prepay edit pending L-code brace claims where the ordering NPI has no qualifying encounter with that beneficiary in the lookback, or where the ordering NPI's distinct-supplier and distinct-state counts exceed the calibrated percentile. Build an orderer-supplier bipartite network score updated nightly; when a supplier's volume is dominated by flagged orderers, suspend payment and demand the order documentation and proof of beneficiary contact.

432.ways_to_identify: When prior authorization is suspended, the compensating control is post-adjudication anomaly monitoring: a single pharmacy NPI capturing an outsized share of statewide spend on a narrow list of non-contracted high-cost generics (including an OTC vitamin) within months, with per-beneficiary quantities and refill frequencies far above peers and prescriptions concentrated among few prescribers. Beneficiary confirmation surveys and prescriber outreach would show drugs never received.
432.features_to_create: Build a pharmacy-NDC-month surveillance feed that computes each pharmacy's share of program spend by NDC, deviation from same-region peer mix, prescriber concentration and per-member days-supply, and auto-imposes a targeted prior-authorization requirement or payment suspension on the flagged pharmacy-NDC pairs even while general PA is waived. Add a rule that non-contracted/OTC NDCs above a spend velocity trigger require proof of dispensing (signature log) before payment.

433.ways_to_identify: No health-claims component: this is workers'-compensation premium fraud and payroll-tax evasion. It was detectable by the carrier and tax authority through mismatch between the policy's declared payroll and the volume of certificates of insurance issued/checks flowing to the shell entity, plus zero 941/state wage filings against millions in check-cashing activity at a check casher.
433.features_to_create: For the comp carrier: an underwriting/audit rule comparing declared payroll to third-party evidence (bank deposits, state wage records, count of certificate-of-insurance requests per policy) and flagging policies with minimum premium but wide certificate distribution for mandatory audit. Cross-agency: flag entities with large check-casher activity and no payroll filings. No payer-side health claim control applies.

434.ways_to_identify: Time-based counseling codes can be tested for feasibility at adjudication: total billed minutes per counselor per day, and per-facility ratio of billed 45-minute units to available staffed clinician hours, will exceed what the roster can deliver when 5-15 minute sessions are upcoded. Separately, the enrolment application was falsifiable-detectable: ownership/managing-employee disclosure screened against federal conviction and exclusion databases would have surfaced the concealed principal's tax conviction and hidden control.
434.features_to_create: Build a rendering-clinician-day and facility-day minute accumulator across timed psychotherapy/counseling codes, comparing billed minutes to licensed-staff hours reported by the facility; pend claims above feasibility and request session start/stop times and notes. At enrolment/revalidation, run automated identity resolution on all owners, officers and managing employees (including prior names, shared addresses, bank signatories) against conviction and exclusion data, and deny or revoke on undisclosed principals.

435.ways_to_identify: Hidden true ownership is detectable at enrolment through identity-resolution: the nominee owner had no industry history, and bank accounts, addresses, phone numbers and prior entity filings link back to the real controller (often already known from prior entities). Payment-flow signals also show it - reimbursements sweeping out of the lab account to entities associated with the undisclosed principal, plus test-mix and per-beneficiary volume outliers typical of a controlled lab.
435.features_to_create: At enrolment/revalidation for labs, require and automatically verify all direct/indirect owners, managing employees and bank-account signatories, scoring nominee risk (owner with no prior claims/tax footprint, shared address/phone/IP with previously sanctioned entities) and holding the billing privilege pending verification. Add a payment-destination control: flag when EFT account holder differs from the enrolled owner or changes shortly after enrolment, and suspend payment pending verification.

436.ways_to_identify: WIC voucher redemption, not health claims: the signal is at the redeeming vendor level - redemption dollars per store far above same-size authorized peers, average voucher redeemed at or near the maximum allowable price, and redemption volume inconsistent with the store's authorized-food purchase invoices from wholesalers. Common ownership across ten stores showing correlated patterns is an additional enrolment-time flag.
436.features_to_create: Build a vendor-month redemption analytics engine: dollars per voucher versus peer price benchmarks, redemption totals versus wholesaler invoice evidence for WIC-eligible stock, and owner-linkage clustering across stores; fire a compliance buy/inventory audit and withhold redemption above the calibrated percentile. Require periodic invoice submission as a condition of continued vendor authorization, with disqualification for unsupported redemptions.

437.ways_to_identify: Same brace-mill signature: supplier claims concentrated in a few L-codes, ordered by NPIs with no encounter history with the beneficiary, beneficiaries far from the ordering practitioner, and some orders using practitioner NPIs whose owners never billed anything else consistent with DME ordering. Practitioner complaints of NPI misuse and beneficiary complaints of unwanted deliveries are additional pre-payment flags in the contractor's complaint data.
437.features_to_create: Prepay edit: pend brace HCPCS where no qualifying face-to-face encounter claim exists for the ordering NPI-beneficiary pair or the beneficiary-orderer distance exceeds the calibrated threshold. Build a supplier scorecard (L-code concentration, orderer fan-in, share of orders from NPIs with no other clinical claims, complaint counts) and auto-suspend payments for new suppliers above the calibrated percentile pending records and beneficiary verification calls.

438.ways_to_identify: Identical mechanic to the companion case: verify at adjudication that the ordering practitioner actually saw the beneficiary (presence of an E/M or qualifying telehealth claim), that the beneficiary lives within plausible distance, and that the ordering NPI's brace-order volume and supplier fan-out are within peer range. Marketing arrangements paying per lead/order are detectable at enrolment by requiring disclosure of marketing contracts and comparing invoices to order counts.
438.features_to_create: Implement the encounter-linkage and distance prepay edit for orthotic L-codes plus an ordering-NPI velocity flag, and a supplier-level new-enrollee payment cap with 100% prepay review during the initial period. Require suppliers to disclose marketing vendor contracts and payment records at enrolment; detected per-order compensation triggers referral and payment suspension.

439.ways_to_identify: HCBS residential claims assert required staffing ratios, which is testable pre-payment: compare billed resident-days per home to submitted staffing rosters/timesheets and EVV or shift-log data, and flag homes where billed days imply more staffed hours than payroll evidences. Licensing inspection findings (unsafe/unsanitary conditions) and complaint records joined to the provider ID are further pre-payment flags, as is the same individual serving as SSA representative payee for residents whose funds she controlled.
439.features_to_create: Build a home-week control comparing billed HCBS resident-days against staff hours evidenced by EVV/payroll for that site and against the ratio required by the waiver; fire a prepay documentation request for staffing records and withhold payment where the ratio cannot be substantiated. Add a provider-level risk trigger from state licensing deficiency and complaint feeds that moves the provider to prepay review, and flag providers who are also representative payees for their own residents for financial-exploitation review.

440.ways_to_identify: Enrollment screening should have matched the owner and any indirect/nominee owners against the LEIE, state Medicaid exclusion list and criminal-history results, and the concealed-ownership pattern would surface by matching Secretary of State officers, tax filings, addresses and bank accounts to the disclosed owner. At adjudication, home-health visit claims overlapping a paid inpatient stay for the same beneficiary are directly visible, as are aide identities that match exclusion or disqualifying-background lists.
440.features_to_create: Build a monthly re-screen job that hashes and matches every disclosed owner, managing employee and billing staff plus corporate address/phone/EIN neighbors against LEIE/state exclusion and background-disqualification files, firing a payment suspension and revalidation on hit. Add a prepay edit that denies HomeHealth/PersonalCare visit lines whose dates of service fall inside an adjudicated inpatient or institutional stay for the same member, and an aide-level edit rejecting lines whose rendering aide ID is on the disqualified-worker roster.

441.ways_to_identify: This is a CSA/CMEA recordkeeping civil case with no claims-payment component, so the payer route is indirect: reconcile the pharmacy's controlled-substance acquisition (ARCOS/wholesaler purchase data, 222/CSOS records) against dispensing claims volume and look for unexplained gaps, and treat DEA inspection findings as a credentialing event. Pseudoephedrine retail logbook/NPLEx certification failures are found on inspection, not in claims.
441.features_to_create: Build a pharmacy-level purchase-to-dispense reconciliation that compares wholesaler controlled-substance acquisition volume by NDC/schedule to paid and cash-reported dispensing, flagging unreconciled variance above the calibrated percentile for audit and documentation request. Add a credentialing feed that ingests DEA administrative actions/inspection findings and triggers network review or on-site record audit of inventory and CMEA logs.

442.ways_to_identify: Rides billed for members with a date of death before service, or with concurrent inpatient/incarceration status, are detectable in eligibility and Vital Statistics/corrections data at adjudication. Mileage/origin-destination anomalies are visible when a member's billed pickup address does not match the eligibility address of record and the destination is a distant NYC clinic while equivalent in-county treatment centers exist, and per-member ride counts and paired billing to a handful of clinics stand out against peer transport providers.
442.features_to_create: Prepay edits: deny transportation lines with DOS after date of death, during a paid inpatient stay, or during a corrections-custody span; deny long-distance/mileage-modifier lines where the billed origin ZIP differs from the member's eligibility address ZIP without an authorized address change. Add a provider-level cluster score (share of trips to a small set of distant destinations, repeat-member concentration, rides per member per week versus same-county peers) that triggers prepay review and trip-log/signature documentation requests.

443.ways_to_identify: Mail-order compounded topical cream billing shows a distinctive prepay signature: a small pharmacy, high-cost compound NDC/HCPCS mix, prescribers geographically distant from the pharmacy and from patients, and referral concentration in a few marketers' prescriber panels. Kickback payments themselves are only provable post-payment, but the referral concentration and prescriber-distance pattern are visible at adjudication.
443.features_to_create: Build a pharmacy-month model computing share of revenue from compounded topical/high-cost ingredient claims, count of distinct prescribers with prescriber-to-pharmacy distance above the calibrated threshold, and Herfindahl concentration of prescribers; fire prepay review with medical-necessity and patient-contact documentation requests. Add an ingredient-cost outlier edit that pends compound claims exceeding same-formulation peer cost percentiles pending pricing substantiation.

444.ways_to_identify: Orthotic brace claims tied to telemedicine orders show a signature payers can see prepay: one ordering NPI signing orders across many states with no prior or subsequent treatment relationship with the patient, extremely short or no telehealth encounter claim, and multiple braces per beneficiary in a short window. Ownership concealment behind nominees is catchable at enrollment by matching addresses, phones, bank accounts and shared management across supplier applications.
444.features_to_create: Prepay edits: deny/pend brace HCPCS lines where the ordering NPI has no qualifying E/M or telehealth encounter with the member in the lookback window, where the ordering NPI's state/patient-distance and beneficiary count exceed calibrated peer percentiles, or where cumulative distinct brace codes per member per period exceed clinical norms. At enrollment, run an entity-resolution graph on supplier addresses/phones/bank accounts/officers to detect nominee networks and place new suppliers with graph links to flagged entities on prepay review or hold.

445.ways_to_identify: No payer-side claims component; this is PPP bank/loan fraud with falsified tax documents and altered bank statements. Detection belongs to the lender/SBA: verify reported payroll against IRS Form 941 transcripts and state wage records, and re-verify bank statements directly with the depository at forgiveness.
445.features_to_create: No payer control applies. Nearest analogue for a health payer is an enrollment-integrity check that verifies a provider's claimed payroll/staffing against state wage and IRS transcript data and cross-checks bank/ownership documents for alteration before granting billing privileges or advance payments.

446.ways_to_identify: Same as the companion case: pure PPP loan and forgiveness fraud with no claims adjudication involved. Lender/SBA controls - IRS 941 transcript matching, state unemployment wage-base matching, and direct bank verification of statements - are the detection path.
446.features_to_create: No payer control applies. If mapped to a payer, implement automated third-party verification of payroll/employee counts and bank documents before any relief, advance or accelerated payment program disbursement, with duplicate-application detection across affiliated EINs and shared owners.

447.ways_to_identify: The claims listed licensed practitioners as rendering providers while unlicensed massage therapists and trainers performed the work; payers can compare the rendering NPI's billed treatment minutes/units per day against the physically possible workday and against staff rosters submitted at credentialing. State licensure boards' data plus site-visit staff rosters reveal that clinic headcount cannot support billed volume across two locations.
447.features_to_create: Build a rendering-provider capacity edit: for each NPI-day, sum timed therapy units across all locations and pend/deny when total treatment minutes exceed the feasible workday or when the same NPI bills concurrently at two service locations. Add a roster-reconciliation check requiring each therapy claim's rendering NPI to appear on the clinic's credentialed licensed-staff roster with an active license on the DOS, and request treatment logs with signatures when clinic units-per-licensed-FTE exceed same-specialty peers.

448.ways_to_identify: A single physician NPI appearing as rendering provider on $20M of rehab claims for an entity he has no affiliation with is visible prepay by comparing the billing entity's TIN to the physician's own historical affiliations, addresses and claim patterns. A sudden new TIN-to-NPI pairing with high volume, plus the physician's own separate practice billing elsewhere at the same times, are strong prepay signals; physician-attestation outreach confirms it.
448.features_to_create: Build a TIN/NPI affiliation-change monitor: when a rendering NPI newly appears under a billing TIN and volume ramps above the calibrated percentile within the first months, pend claims and send an automated attestation notice to the physician's board-of-record address before payment. Add a concurrency edit flagging the same rendering NPI billing at multiple unaffiliated service locations on the same date, and a signature-verification documentation request on pended claims.

449.ways_to_identify: No health care payer involvement: this is employment-tax and state meals-tax evasion by a restaurant. Detection is via IRS/state revenue analytics - comparing reported wages to POS gross receipts and merchant-processor data, and comparing collected meals tax on POS records to remitted amounts.
449.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. The analogous control is a revenue-agency edit comparing third-party payment-processor gross receipts and POS tax-collected totals against filed returns, flagging remittance ratios below the industry-calibrated norm for audit.

450.ways_to_identify: Diverted HIV drugs re-entering the supply chain leave traceable signals: DSCSA pedigree/transaction-history chains that dead-end at unknown small wholesalers, serial numbers already recorded as dispensed to a patient, and pharmacies acquiring high-cost antiretrovirals from non-authorized distributors at below-market cost. Payers can see the downstream side as members with paid ARV fills whose dispensed serialized packages later reappear, and as pharmacies whose ARV purchase sources are not on the manufacturer's authorized distributor list.
450.features_to_create: Build serialization/pedigree verification at the point of claim: require the dispensing pharmacy's supplier to be on an authorized-distributor whitelist for the NDC, and reject or pend claims for high-cost specialty NDCs sourced from unlisted wholesalers. Add a duplicate-serial detector that fires when a package identifier is reported dispensed more than once or reappears after a prior paid claim, plus a member-level 'buyback' signal (repeated full ARV fills with no lab/visit utilization) referred to investigation.

451.ways_to_identify: Billed private-duty nursing and personal-care hours can be reconciled prepay against EVV check-in/out records, nurse licensure status, and per-nurse daily hour totals across all patients; hours billed with no EVV event or exceeding a feasible workday are visible before payment. Pre-signed blank notes show up as documentation whose signature dates cluster or precede service dates, detectable on targeted documentation requests to high-outlier agencies.
451.features_to_create: Prepay edit: deny or pend PDN/personal-care units lacking a matched EVV visit with corroborating start/stop, and deny units where the rendering caregiver's summed hours across members exceed the calibrated daily maximum or overlap in time. Add an agency-level score (hours per member per week vs peers, share of claims without EVV, guardian-paid relationships) that triggers prepay documentation review of nursing notes with signature/date consistency checks.

452.ways_to_identify: The clinic billed acupuncture, therapy and E/M codes for which it had no licensed/qualified provider - a mismatch between the credentialed staff roster's license types and the CPT codes submitted, visible at adjudication. Also visible: high-frequency modality codes (infrared, hot/cold, therapeutic activity, self-care training) billed to every patient on every visit with E/M on the same day, far above same-specialty peer patterns, and non-covered massage delivered but billed as covered services.
452.features_to_create: Build a scope-of-practice/code-to-roster edit: reject claim lines whose CPT requires a license type (acupuncturist, PT, OT) not present on the billing group's credentialed roster on the DOS. Add a per-visit modality-bundle detector flagging providers whose share of visits containing the same fixed set of modality codes plus same-day E/M exceeds the calibrated peer percentile, firing prepay review with treatment-record and patient-attestation requests.

453.ways_to_identify: Definitive/presumptive urine drug testing done at an in-house lab shows prepay signals: uniform high-frequency testing intervals per patient regardless of risk, presumptive and definitive panels on the same specimen, duplicate panels within short windows, and a physician-owned lab receiving essentially all of the practice's referrals. Pre-signed Schedule II prescriptions are detectable by matching prescription/dispense dates to the prescriber's absence - e.g., no billed encounters by that NPI on or around those dates, and PDMP entries while no corresponding visit exists.
453.features_to_create: Prepay edits: limit definitive UDT panels per member per period, deny same-specimen presumptive-plus-definitive and duplicate panels, and pend claims where the ordering physician has a financial interest in the performing lab (self-referral/ownership disclosure match). Build a prescriber-absence check linking PDMP/Part D Schedule II fills to the prescriber's own claim activity, flagging opioid prescriptions issued on dates the prescriber rendered no services for chart review.

454.ways_to_identify: Foreign Medical Program claims are paper/manual and beneficiary-reimbursed, so controls must sit at intake: check for provider concentration (a small set of Panamanian clinics/pharmacies billing most veterans in-country), duplicate or sequential invoice numbering, identical service bundles across unrelated patients, and services/medicines a veteran can be asked to confirm receipt of. Inflated per-visit pricing versus local-market fee benchmarks is visible before payment.
454.features_to_create: Build an FMP prepay analytics layer: normalize foreign invoices to structured codes, compute per-provider price versus country/market benchmark and per-veteran service frequency, and pend claims above the calibrated percentile pending beneficiary confirmation of receipt. Add duplicate-invoice and template-detection (same amounts/line sets across patients) plus a provider watchlist that suspends payment to foreign providers under investigation.

455.ways_to_identify: No health care payer involvement - this is a third-party payroll agent diverting withheld employment taxes. Detection is an IRS control: reconcile aggregate W-2 withholding reported by client employers against 941 filings submitted by the agent, and notify employers directly of amounts reported/paid on their behalf.
455.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest analogue: for entities acting as billing/financial agents on behalf of enrolled providers, require agent registration and send the principal an independent statement of amounts filed/remitted, flagging agents whose reported liabilities diverge from client-level withholding or receipt data.

456.ways_to_identify: Overlapping shifts by one caregiver are fully visible prepay by intersecting time-stamped units across all members, programs and provider TINs for the same worker ID. EVV geolocation showing the worker not at the member's residence at check-in is available before payment and directly contradicts the claim.
456.features_to_create: Build a worker-day timeline engine keyed to caregiver ID/SSN across personal care and behavioral health claim types and across agencies; deny any line whose time interval overlaps another paid or pending line for the same worker. Add an EVV geofence edit that pends units where check-in/out coordinates fall outside the member's service address radius, and suspend a worker with repeated overlap/geofence failures pending investigation.

457.ways_to_identify: Speaker-program kickbacks are visible by joining Open Payments (food/beverage and speaking fees by manufacturer and drug) to Part D prescribing: prescribers with repeat honoraria for the same topic whose Nurtec volume jumps after payments. Prepay-detectable at the prescriber level as rapid new-brand share growth concentrated in paid speakers; the manufacturer-side conduct itself is post-payment/FCA territory.
457.features_to_create: Build a payment-to-prescribing correlation job: for each drug, link Open Payments records to prescriber-level claim volume and compute pre/post-payment prescribing lift, attendee-repeat counts and meal frequency, flagging prescribers above the calibrated percentile for prepay prior-authorization and medical-necessity review. Add a manufacturer-level monitoring report used to open FCA/CIA referrals and to tighten formulary controls on the affected brand.

458.ways_to_identify: Identical mechanic to the companion case: Open Payments speaker-fee and meal records joined to Part D/Medicaid prescribing reveal prescribers whose brand volume rises after honoraria, including repeat same-topic programs and attendees who are the speaker's own colleagues or relatives. Kickback liability is resolved post-payment, but the prescribing-lift signal is available before individual claims pay.
458.features_to_create: Implement the payment-to-prescribing lift model (Open Payments joined to prescriber claim history, per drug) with flags for repeat-program attendance and abnormal new-brand growth, routing flagged prescribers' claims to prior authorization and step-therapy edits. Feed the same output into a manufacturer-level dashboard for referral and into targeted documentation requests on flagged prescriptions.

459.ways_to_identify: TIRF products are indicated only for breakthrough cancer pain, so payers can check prepay whether the member has any cancer diagnosis and a qualifying around-the-clock opioid regimen in claims history; absence of both is a clean denial signal. Prescriber-level signals include concentration of TIRF scripts in a handful of high-volume prescribers who also appear in Open Payments as speakers/advisors for that manufacturer, and manufacturer-funded 'support programs' submitting the prior-authorization paperwork.
459.features_to_create: Prepay prior-authorization edit for TIRF/fentanyl NDCs requiring a cancer diagnosis in the member's claim history plus concurrent long-acting opioid therapy and opioid-tolerance documentation; deny otherwise. Add a prescriber TIRF-concentration monitor cross-joined to Open Payments and PDMP diversion flags that suspends automatic PA approval, forces independent clinical review, and blocks PA submissions originating from manufacturer-sponsored reimbursement-support entities.

460.ways_to_identify: TIRF products are indication-restricted to breakthrough cancer pain, so Part D/TRICARE claims for Lazanda with no cancer diagnosis anywhere in the beneficiary's 12-month diagnostic history and no prior opioid-tolerance evidence are visible at adjudication. Concentration analysis on the prescriber dimension - a handful of NPIs writing the bulk of a manufacturer's TIRF volume - plus cross-matching those NPIs to Open Payments speaker/advisory-board payments from the same manufacturer and to prior-authorization requests submitted with manufacturer hub ('Signature Support') fax numbers or shared contact data, would have surfaced the sponsored-prescriber cluster pre-payment.
460.features_to_create: Build a prepay edit on TIRF NDCs: deny/pend unless the member has a qualifying malignancy diagnosis in claims history and a concurrent long-acting opioid indicating tolerance; route pends to documentation request. Add a prescriber-level monthly scorecard combining TIRF share-of-panel and off-label rate versus same-specialty peers, joined to Open Payments speaking/consulting receipts from the TIRF manufacturer, and to a flag for PA submissions originating from manufacturer-hub contact identifiers; above the calibrated percentile, place the prescriber's TIRF claims on prepay review.

461.ways_to_identify: Dispensing volume can be reconciled against acquisition: pharmacy claims for antipsychotics and inhalers by NDC compared with wholesaler/ARCOS and 340B/distributor purchase records will not balance when drugs were never bought. Also visible pre-payment are refill-too-soon patterns, high-cost NDC concentration versus peer pharmacies of the same size, and beneficiaries who never picked up (no copay collection, out-of-area members, no matching physician office visit).
461.features_to_create: Build a monthly NDC-level inventory reconciliation engine: units billed to all payers minus units purchased from distributors; fire when the unexplained dispensed-over-purchased ratio exceeds the calibrated peer percentile, and place the pharmacy on prepay review or payment suspension for those NDCs. Add a prepay edit flagging high-cost NDC claims where the member has no encounter with the prescriber in the lookback window, and share audit-refusal/inventory-shortfall findings across payers so one auditor's shortfall triggers others' edits.

462.ways_to_identify: Compounded-drug claims are the signal: a single pharmacy billing enormous per-claim amounts for compounded creams/gels, with prescriptions arriving from a geographically dispersed set of prescribers who share no patients with the pharmacy's local area, indicates marketer-brokered referral flow. Kickbacks show up as abnormal marketing/commission spend relative to revenue in cost or ownership disclosures, and as prescriber panels where nearly all compound scripts route to one out-of-state pharmacy.
462.features_to_create: Build a prepay edit on high-dollar compounded claims requiring the prescriber-patient relationship to be evidenced by a paid office visit and requiring the pharmacy to be within a plausible service radius or have documented mail-order status. Add pharmacy-level analytics: compound share of revenue, average allowed per claim, and prescriber-referral concentration (share of scripts from prescribers with no local patient overlap) versus same-specialty peers; above the calibrated percentile, suspend payment on compound claims pending records and screen the pharmacy's marketer contracts for percentage-based compensation.

463.ways_to_identify: Prescriber-identity misuse is detectable at adjudication: claims citing a prescriber NPI whose specialty, historical drug mix, or geography does not fit the drug, or whose NPI appears on scripts filled only at one pharmacy while that prescriber has no patient relationship with the member. Provider outreach/attestation letters to the named prescribers and members are the confirmatory step; state PDMP data will show the prescriptions absent from the prescriber's own records.
463.features_to_create: Build a prescriber-NPI plausibility edit: pend pharmacy claims where the prescriber NPI is inactive, out-of-state, specialty-implausible for the drug class, deceased, or has no encounter with the member in the lookback; require documentation before payment. Add a monitor computing, per pharmacy, the share of claims whose prescriber NPIs appear at that pharmacy only and are absent from PDMP records; above the calibrated percentile, auto-generate prescriber verification letters and suspend payment on affected claims.

464.ways_to_identify: Two independent signals were available pre-payment: acquisition-versus-dispensed reconciliation against wholesaler purchase records for the billed NDCs, and prescriber verification, since the underlying prescriptions were forged and would not exist in the named prescribers' records or the PDMP. Common ownership/staffing across the three pharmacies, and the same forged prescriber NPIs appearing across all three, tie the locations together.
464.features_to_create: Implement NDC-level purchase-to-billed reconciliation per pharmacy with pend/suspend when unexplained dispensing exceeds the calibrated peer percentile. Add a prescriber-verification edit that pends high-cost claims whose prescriber NPI has no other claim relationship with the member and no PDMP entry, and a common-ownership linkage rule that propagates a flag at any one location to all commonly owned NPIs/TINs for prepay review.
