465.ways_to_identify: Extreme unit price is the trigger: a per-box reimbursement in the thousands for medicated scar pads, billed by a single retail pharmacy to a small number of Medicaid members, is a clear outlier against state peer benchmarks. Absence of any surgical, burn, or wound-related diagnosis or procedure in the member's history, and absence of a prior encounter with the ordering prescriber, indicates no medical need; member interviews confirm they never discussed the product.
465.features_to_create: Build a prepay edit on high-cost topical/wound-product NDCs and HCPCS: require a wound/scar-related diagnosis or recent surgical procedure in claims history plus a documented prescriber encounter, else pend for medical records. Add a pharmacy-level outlier monitor on allowed-dollars-per-claim and on newly billed high-unit-cost NDCs never previously dispensed by that pharmacy; above the calibrated percentile, suspend and send beneficiary verification letters.

466.ways_to_identify: The payer itself named the signal: wholesaler inventory records show the pharmacy could not have acquired enough drug to fill what it billed, a reconciliation that can be run pre-payment if purchase data is required as a condition of network participation. Supporting prepay signals include no member cost-share collection, refill-too-soon clusters, and members with no matching prescriber encounter.
466.features_to_create: Require pharmacies to submit periodic wholesaler purchase files and run an automated NDC-level billed-versus-purchased reconciliation; pend or suspend claims for NDCs where billed units exceed purchases beyond a tolerance for returns/transfers. Layer a claim-level edit pending high-cost refills where no pickup/copay signal or prescriber encounter exists, with documentation request as the action.

467.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic as other non-dispensing pharmacies: Part D claims volume by NDC exceeds what the pharmacy ever purchased from wholesalers, provable from distributor data at or before payment if purchase reporting is a network condition. Refills continuing after a member's death, hospitalization, or nursing-home stay, and absence of copay collection, are additional adjudication-time flags.
467.features_to_create: Automate an NDC-level dispensed-versus-acquired ratio per pharmacy per month, firing above the calibrated tolerance into a payment suspension for the implicated NDCs pending purchase-invoice production. Add prepay edits denying refills that overlap inpatient/institutional stays or postdate death, and pending auto-refill patterns with no member contact evidence.

468.ways_to_identify: This was a cash-only diversion operation, so little or nothing flowed through payer claims; the primary detection route is PDMP and DEA/ARCOS dispensing data rather than adjudication - a pharmacy with huge Schedule II volume and near-zero insurance billing, out-of-area cash patients, and prescriber NPIs whose owners deny writing the scripts. The one payer-side hook is the disability benefits application, testable by cross-matching claimed inability to work against business ownership and licensure records.
468.features_to_create: Build a PDMP/ARCOS-fed monitor computing each pharmacy's Schedule II share, cash-pay share, patient travel distance, and prescriber concentration; fire above the calibrated percentile into a referral and, for any payer claims from that pharmacy, prepay review plus prescriber attestation letters. Separately, run a benefit-eligibility cross-match of disability applicants against corporate registry, licensing, and payroll/provider-enrollment data, pending awards on mismatch.

469.ways_to_identify: Specialty drugs are low-volume and high-cost, so billed-versus-acquired reconciliation against wholesaler and specialty-distributor records exposes refills for drugs never stocked. Refill-timing patterns (perfectly regular refills with no gaps, refills for members who had no corresponding specialist visit or lab monitoring for HCV/RA/Crohn's therapy) and forged shipping records that reuse tracking numbers or show impossible delivery patterns are checkable pre-payment via carrier tracking validation. Kickbacks surface as extreme prescriber-referral concentration and as pharmacy employees whose addresses/phones match a prescriber's office.
469.features_to_create: Build a specialty-NDC reconciliation engine (billed units vs. distributor purchases) that suspends payment per NDC on unexplained excess, and a prepay edit requiring, for specialty refills, a documented specialist encounter or monitoring lab within the clinical interval. Add automated shipment-proof validation (carrier API check of tracking numbers for existence, weight, and delivery address matching the member) and a prescriber-concentration/entity-linkage monitor flagging pharmacies where a top prescriber shares phone, address, or payroll ties with the pharmacy; fire into prepay review and audit.

470.ways_to_identify: Brand-for-generic substitution is detectable by reconciling billed brand NDCs against the pharmacy's purchase history - a pharmacy billing brand OxyContin while buying only generic oxycodone cannot support the claims. Reversal-rate analysis catches the return re-billing: returned/undelivered prescriptions that were never reversed appear as duplicate fills of the same drug for the same member within an implausible interval, and as a reversal rate far below same-size peers.
470.features_to_create: Build NDC-level brand-billed-versus-brand-purchased reconciliation per pharmacy, firing above tolerance into suspension of brand claims pending invoices. Add a prepay duplicate/refill-too-soon edit for Schedule II fills and a pharmacy-level monitor of reversal rate and unclaimed-prescription handling versus peers; low reversal rate combined with repeat early fills triggers a documentation request and postpay recovery review.

471.ways_to_identify: The Medicaid piece is catchable at adjudication: a newly enrolled home-health agency with no employed, background-checked, credentialed caregivers on file billing visits, no EVV check-in/check-out records matching the billed units, and members whose other claims show no home-care authorization. Cross-program matching against SBA PPP data (payroll claimed on the loan versus payroll/wage records and the provider's own billed staffing) exposes the inflated-payroll loan; the retail theft has no payer control.
471.features_to_create: Require EVV as a condition of payment and build a prepay edit denying home-health units with no matching EVV visit record or no active authorization, plus an enrolment-time edit blocking billing until at least one credentialed, screened caregiver NPI/employee record is on file. Add a new-provider surge monitor (rapid ramp in billed units per caregiver-hour available) that suspends payment pending records, and a data-share match of provider TINs against PPP/loan payroll certifications versus state wage filings.

472.ways_to_identify: This is benefit-eligibility identity fraud at the application stage, not claim billing: it is caught by identity proofing - SSN-to-name-and-DOB verification against SSA, death-master and duplicate-SSN checks, vital-records validation of the submitted birth certificates, and document-authentication of the driver's licenses whose photo repeats across multiple distinct applicant identities. Repeated use of one mailing address, bank account, phone, or device across supposedly unrelated households is the strongest cross-application signal.
472.features_to_create: Build an application-time identity engine: SSA/SSN validation, state vital-records verification for claimed dependents and spouses, and biometric/photo-hash plus device, phone, address and bank-account clustering across all SNAP/Medicaid applications; hold benefit issuance pending manual identity verification when one identifier links to multiple identities. Add an EBT redemption monitor for card-trafficking patterns (whole-balance transactions at a single retailer, cards used far from the enrollee's address) that suspends the card and reopens the eligibility file.

473.ways_to_identify: No payer-side control applies: this is a cargo-theft/burglary conspiracy against UPS warehouses with no health care claims and no benefit payment involved, prosecuted only incidentally by a health care fraud AUSA. There is nothing observable at claim adjudication, enrolment, or credentialing.
473.features_to_create: No payer control applies. The nearest analogue, if any payer nexus were alleged, would be a supply-chain check validating that DME or drug shipments billed to the plan trace to legitimate distributor invoices and carrier delivery confirmations rather than diverted goods.

474.ways_to_identify: Pure eligibility/identity fraud at intake rather than provider billing: catch it with SSA SSN verification, duplicate-SSN and death-master matching, state vital-records validation of the birth certificates submitted for the fictitious spouse and children, and document/photo authentication that would reveal one photo attached to several distinct identities. Shared addresses, phone numbers, bank accounts and devices across nominally unrelated applications are the clustering signal.
474.features_to_create: Implement an application-time identity-resolution service: validate SSN/name/DOB against SSA, verify each claimed dependent against vital records, hash and compare ID photos, and cluster applications on address, phone, device and account; hold issuance for manual verification whenever one identifier maps to multiple identities. Add EBT-trafficking detection (full-balance swipes at one retailer, geographic mismatch) that suspends the card and triggers eligibility redetermination.

475.ways_to_identify: Time-based E/M and med-check codes can be tested against the calendar: sum billed time-units per rendering NPI per day and flag totals exceeding a plausible workday, and detect overlapping start/end times, including the same provider billing at two service locations in the same window. Distribution analysis showing near-100% use of the higher time-tier code with no shorter-unit claims, versus same-specialty peers, is visible before payment.
475.features_to_create: Build a per-rendering-NPI per-day time accumulator across all sites: deny or pend claims once billed minutes exceed the calibrated daily maximum, and hard-edit any two claims for the same provider with overlapping documented time or impossible travel between locations. Add a code-distribution outlier monitor on time-tiered med-check codes versus same-specialty peers that triggers a records request for start/stop times before payment on subsequent claims.

476.ways_to_identify: This is ransomware extortion, not claims fraud, so there is no adjudication-time signal; detection sits with network security monitoring, threat intelligence, and sanctions/OFAC screening of ransom payments. The only payer-adjacent routes are contractual security attestations at credentialing and watching for post-incident billing anomalies (claim gaps then catch-up surges, or claims submitted from compromised provider credentials).
476.features_to_create: No claims edit prevents the intrusion; build instead a credentialing-time security-attestation requirement and a compromised-credential monitor that flags sudden changes in a provider's submitter ID, EFT bank account, IP geography, or batch volume and holds payment pending out-of-band verification. Pair with an EFT-change hold and callback verification to stop payment diversion following provider network compromise.

477.ways_to_identify: Enrolment screening catches this: the license number on the CMS-855I can be verified in real time against the state medical board's primary source, and the applicant's identity matched against the board's own licensee record - here the same person held only a PA license, so the physician license number would not validate to him. Cross-checking the NPI's taxonomy, NPPES history, education/ECFMG-USMLE verification, and prior PA-level claims history would show a specialty change with no credential basis.
477.features_to_create: Build automated primary-source license verification at enrolment and revalidation: match license number, licensee name, DOB and license type to the state board API, and hard-block enrolment or reassignment when type does not support the claimed specialty or the number is unissued/altered. Add a continuous monitor that flags any NPI whose taxonomy escalates from mid-level to physician without a new verified license, suspending payment on reassigned claims pending credential re-verification.

478.ways_to_identify: Look for the tying pattern at adjudication: members receiving controlled-substance prescriptions from one prescriber who simultaneously and uniformly receive a fixed bundle of other medications dispensed by a pharmacy sharing the prescriber's address/ownership. Self-referral to in-house pharmacies is visible through common TIN/address/ownership between prescriber and pharmacy, and the pre-signed-blank scheme shows as prescriptions dated when the prescriber was absent or as volumes exceeding his own encounter counts, plus interns/unlicensed staff appearing as writers in PDMP data.
478.features_to_create: Build a prescriber-pharmacy affiliation flag (shared TIN, address, phone, ownership from enrolment data) and pend claims where an affiliated pharmacy dispenses a repeating multi-drug bundle to controlled-substance patients with no supporting diagnoses. Add a per-prescriber reconciliation of controlled-substance prescriptions against billed encounters for the same member-date; when prescription counts exceed encounters above the calibrated threshold, suspend payment and request charts and signature logs.

479.ways_to_identify: Genetic-panel claims ordered by telemedicine prescribers with no treating relationship are visible pre-payment: no prior or subsequent encounter with the ordering NPI, one ordering NPI spread across many states and labs, and identical diagnosis-code sets repeating across unrelated beneficiaries - the signature of prepopulated 'dummy proof' order forms. Reflex/pass-through billing shows as the billing lab's claims for tests it did not perform, detectable via referring-lab CLIA mismatch and sudden migration of the same ordering NPIs from one lab TIN to another.
479.features_to_create: Build a prepay edit on high-cost genetic panels requiring a treating-provider encounter with the ordering NPI within a defined lookback and a diagnosis supporting the specific panel; deny or pend for medical necessity documentation otherwise. Add analytics on diagnosis-code entropy per ordering NPI (repeated identical code sets), telehealth-order share, and cross-lab NPI migration/CLIA-versus-performing-site mismatch; above the calibrated percentile, suspend the lab's genetic-testing payments and audit its contracts with marketers and referring labs.

480.ways_to_identify: Claims data shows one prescriber accounting for nearly all prescriptions dispensed at pharmacies he owns (common ownership/address/TIN linkage between prescriber NPI and pharmacy NPI), with each beneficiary receiving an identical multi-drug 'bag' of high-margin topicals/creams plus a concurrent oxycodone fill. PDMP/Part D data would show extreme oxycodone MME per patient from a single prescriber, and prescriptions signed on dates when the prescriber was not present or written by unlicensed interns (signature/DEA number mismatch, pre-signed blank forms) is detectable via state license checks on the writer.
480.features_to_create: Build a prescriber-pharmacy affiliation graph (shared owners, addresses, bank accounts, corporate filings) and prepay-flag pharmacy claims where the referring prescriber is affiliated and represents an outsized share of that pharmacy's revenue. Add a 'kit' detector clustering identical multi-NDC dispense baskets per beneficiary and a rule firing when a beneficiary receives the basket plus a Schedule II opioid from the same prescriber; suspend payment and require dispensing/medical records. Validate that the prescribing practitioner on each controlled-substance claim holds an active license and DEA registration at the fill date.

481.ways_to_identify: Prescriber-level PDMP and pharmacy claims show a single internal medicine office writing oxycodone and promethazine-with-codeine to patients whose home ZIP codes span dozens of states, with no corresponding office-visit claims (cash pay) and no diagnostic or imaging workup. Duplicate or mismatched patient identities (same SSN/DOB tied to different names, or names with no payer eligibility history) and pharmacy shopping across distant pharmacies are visible at fill adjudication.
481.features_to_create: Prescriber panel-geography check: compute the distribution of patient residence distance and state count per prescriber per drug class, and flag Schedule II/promethazine-codeine writers above the calibrated peer percentile for out-of-area patients or for opioid fills unaccompanied by any evaluation claim. Add an identity-integrity edit at the pharmacy that fires on SSN/DOB/name mismatch or reused demographics, and trigger a prepay documentation request plus referral of the prescriber to the licensing board and DEA.

482.ways_to_identify: Presumptive and definitive UDT billed on the same date for essentially every patient of a referring practice, with identical CPT combinations and identical diagnosis codes, is the signature of a blanket standing order rather than individualized necessity. Requisition forms with pre-checked panels, and lab-employed collectors physically embedded in referring offices (shared address between lab staff and the practice), are visible at audit and in referral-concentration data; urine hormone/specimen-validity codes billed alongside UDT are a bundling violation catchable by a code-pair edit.
482.features_to_create: Build a lab-plus-referrer unit of observation: compute the share of that referrer's patients receiving both presumptive and definitive UDT on the same date and the reflex-to-definitive rate, and prepay-deny or pend definitive UDT above the calibrated peer percentile pending signed, individualized orders documenting why presumptive was insufficient. Add an NCCI-style bundling edit rejecting specimen-validity/urine hormone assays billed with UDT on the same specimen, and cap UDT frequency per beneficiary per period.

483.ways_to_identify: Reported staffing on cost reports and PBJ/state staffing submissions can be reconciled against payroll tax records, wage data, and licensure files: names listed as direct-care staff who have no payroll entry, no active license, or who are simultaneously reported at another facility are detectable before payment of the period's claims. Administrative/kitchen staff counted as direct care is visible by comparing job codes to hours claimed.
483.features_to_create: Build an automated PBJ-to-payroll reconciliation: for each facility-quarter, join reported staff hours to employer payroll/tax filings and state license files, and compute the share of reported hours with no payroll or license match and hours for individuals reported at multiple facilities in overlapping shifts. Fire a compliance hold and condition-of-participation review (with payment suspension for repeated variance) when unmatched hours exceed the calibrated threshold or when reported ratios sit just above the minimum every period.

484.ways_to_identify: Member-submitted out-of-network reimbursement invoices can be validated against the named provider: verify the practice's TIN/NPI, confirm the invoice number/format and that the provider has any record of the patient, and check whether the same member submitted multiple invoices with sequential or reused numbers and round-dollar totals. Repeat manual reimbursements to one member with no corresponding provider-side claim is the core signal.
484.features_to_create: For member-reimbursement claims, build a provider-verification step that matches the billing entity on the receipt to registry data (NPI/TIN/address) and auto-pends any receipt from a provider with no submitted claim history for that member. Add a member-level velocity/aggregate rule (count and dollars of self-submitted receipts per rolling period, duplicate invoice numbers, identical templates) that fires an investigator review and direct provider confirmation before payment.

485.ways_to_identify: At enrolment, attested projected income can be cross-checked against IRS/SSA and state wage data; applications that attest income just above the subsidy-eligibility floor while the trusted-data check returns no or near-zero income are the core signal. Broker-level clustering - one NPN/agency submitting many applications sharing addresses, phone numbers, or shelter addresses, with mismatched SSN/name, all at maximum subsidy - is visible before any APTC is paid.
485.features_to_create: Build broker/agency-level enrolment analytics: for each writing agent, compute the rate of applications with income attested within a narrow band above the eligibility floor, the rate of data-matching inconsistencies, address/phone reuse across unrelated enrollees, and the share of zero-premium plans; suspend the agent's marketplace access and hold APTC pending DMI resolution when above the calibrated percentile. Add a per-application rule requiring documentary income proof before subsidy payment when trusted data shows income below the attested figure.

486.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic: attested income clustered just above the subsidy floor while IRS/SSA/state wage data show none, plus reused or shelter addresses, mismatched SSNs, and abandoned Medicaid applications used to manufacture special-enrolment periods. Agent-level concentration of these features, and enrollees with zero claims utilization after enrolment, are all observable before subsidies are disbursed.
486.features_to_create: Implement an income-plausibility edit that pends APTC when attested projected income is within a narrow band above the floor and trusted data returns no earnings, requiring documentation before disbursement. Layer an agent scorecard (data-match failure rate, duplicate contact/address clusters, SEP-via-denied-Medicaid rate, commission per enrollee) that triggers agent suspension and retroactive APTC recovery, and flag SEP claims where the Medicaid application was never completed.

487.ways_to_identify: The Medicaid side is catchable at eligibility determination: employment/income letters from multiple applicants that are near-identical in wording and layout, signed by the same 'manager', and reporting income conveniently below the limit, can be matched against employer payroll/quarterly wage filings and against SSA death records for the signer. The city-contract invoice fraud is a procurement matter - certified payroll names/SSNs can be matched to wage records - not a claims-adjudication control.
487.features_to_create: At Medicaid eligibility, auto-verify attested employer income against state quarterly wage and IRS data and pend cases with a variance beyond tolerance; add document-forensics rules that hash/fuzzy-match uploaded employment letters across applications to detect templates and flag reused signer names, plus a check of signer identity against death-master and licensing files. For contract invoicing, run certified-payroll SSN/name validation against wage records before disbursement.

488.ways_to_identify: No health care payer is involved - this is municipal procurement/wire fraud. It would be caught by vendor-side controls: beneficial-ownership disclosure showing the 'suppliers' were shell companies owned by the prime's principals, and price benchmarking of invoiced parts against retail catalog prices. Altered retailer invoices are detectable by requesting confirmation directly from the retailer rather than accepting contractor-supplied copies.
488.features_to_create: Build a vendor-graph control on invoice payment: match subcontractor/supplier entities against the prime's registered officers, addresses, bank accounts and corporate filings, and block payment on pass-through markups from related parties. Add a line-item price benchmark against reference catalog pricing that pends invoices whose unit prices exceed the benchmark by more than tolerance and requires retailer-sourced verification. Nearest payer analogue: related-party ownership screening in provider enrolment.

489.ways_to_identify: This is benefit-eligibility fraud on self-reported service history, catchable at claim/entitlement adjudication by verifying the asserted combat deployment against DoD personnel records (DD-214, deployment and non-deployable status data) before service-connection and treatment authorization. The signal is a diagnosis and rating narrative built solely on patient self-report of an IED blast with no corroborating record.
489.features_to_create: Require automated DoD/DMDC record matching for any claim or clinical encounter whose diagnosis basis is combat exposure: compute a flag when the record shows no OCONUS deployment or non-deployable status while the claim/encounter documents combat trauma, and pend the entitlement decision for corroboration. Route matched discrepancies to the OIG queue and hold retroactive compensation.

490.ways_to_identify: Claims listing service dates when the only licensed practitioners at the clinic were out of state are detectable by cross-checking rendering-provider claim dates against travel/absence indicators - most practically, against the provider's own claim activity elsewhere, clinic closure days, and geolocation-independent signals like billing on holidays or dates with implausible daily volume. Smoking-cessation and short office-visit codes billed to every patient in an OBOT panel on the same dates, with no supporting notes, is the other signal.
490.features_to_create: Build a rendering-provider day-level impossibility check: for each NPI-date, count claims and computed service minutes and flag dates exceeding a plausible workday or dates where the NPI is also billing far-away service locations; pend and request signed notes with time stamps. Add a panel-uniformity rule flagging counseling/E-M add-on codes billed to an abnormally high share of a clinic's patients on identical dates versus same-specialty peers.

491.ways_to_identify: No payer claims involved - this is DEA registrant diversion/recordkeeping. It is detectable from ARCOS/wholesaler distribution data: a small veterinary practice ordering thousands of hydrocodone and oxycodone dosage units is far above species-and-practice-size peers, and the absence of biennial inventory and dispensing logs is confirmable on inspection. Post-hoc 'records' produced after inspection can be tested for internal inconsistency against euthanasia/appointment logs.
491.features_to_create: Build a registrant-level purchase surveillance feed from wholesaler/ARCOS data: compute per-registrant annual dosage units by schedule normalized to practice type and patient volume, and fire an inspection referral when above the calibrated peer percentile or when purchases exist with no reported dispensing records. Add a wholesaler suspicious-order rule that blocks shipment pending justification. No payer claim edit applies.

492.ways_to_identify: Not a health claims case: it is a false self-certification of small-entity status to obtain reduced regulatory fees. It is catchable at certification intake by cross-referencing the certifying entity against corporate ownership/affiliation records, IRS revenue and employee-count data, and M&A filings showing the licensee is now a subsidiary of a larger parent.
492.features_to_create: Build an affiliation-aware size test at fee certification: resolve each licensee to its ultimate parent via corporate registry and ownership disclosures, aggregate parent revenue/employee counts, and auto-reject or pend Form 526 small-entity claims where aggregated size exceeds the regulatory limit. Re-run the test annually and on any change-of-ownership filing. The payer analogue is enrolment-time ownership/affiliation disclosure verification.

493.ways_to_identify: This is an omnibus round-up, but the recurring adjudication-visible signals are: one prescriber signing orthotic-brace orders for thousands of beneficiaries with no corresponding E/M encounter and beneficiaries geographically remote from the ordering NPI; behavioral-health claims using client identities with overlapping service times and no session documentation; and pharmacy claims for prescriptions lacking a valid prescriber relationship plus misreported manufacturer rebate/DIR amounts detectable by reconciling reported rebates to manufacturer data.
493.features_to_create: Prepay DME edit: deny or pend brace claims where the ordering NPI has no evaluation claim for that beneficiary within a look-back window, and flag ordering NPIs whose order counts, beneficiary counts and telehealth-only patient share exceed same-specialty peers - suspend payment above the calibrated percentile. For behavioral health, add duplicate-identity and overlapping-time-slot edits per client and staff NPI; for Part D sponsors, automate rebate/DIR reconciliation against manufacturer-reported amounts with recoupment on variance.

494.ways_to_identify: Facility-level billing of per-diem and group/individual therapy units can be tested against staffing rosters and census: billed therapy hours exceeding the clinician hours actually on shift, or every client billed the identical daily service bundle regardless of level of care, indicates undelivered or undocumented services. The controlled-substance side is caught through DEA registrant inventory reconciliation at the facility, not through claims.
494.features_to_create: Build a facility-day reconciliation: sum billed therapy units per site-date and divide by credentialed clinician hours available (from rosters/credentialing files), pending payment when the implied per-clinician workload exceeds a plausible ceiling or when service bundles are identical across the census. Add a documentation-request edit for residential/IOP per-diems lacking a signed daily note, and require periodic controlled-substance inventory attestation for licensed sites.

495.ways_to_identify: RPM coverage requires a device that auto-transmits at least the minimum days of readings; the payer can require device identifiers and transmission-day counts on or supporting the claim and detect practices billing the monitoring code with no accompanying device supply claim, no device serial, or implausibly perfect monthly billing for every patient. Practices billing RPM to nearly the whole panel every month with no setup/device code is the prepay signal.
495.features_to_create: Prepay edit on RPM codes: require a linked device-supply/setup claim or a submitted device identifier plus attested transmission-day count for the billing period, and deny when absent or below the coverage minimum. Add practice-level analytics on the share of panel billed RPM monthly and the ratio of monitoring-treatment-management codes to device codes versus peers, triggering a records request for raw transmission logs.

496.ways_to_identify: Surgeon-level utilization profiling shows an OB-GYN performing hysterectomies, pelvic-floor repairs, slings and urodynamics at rates far above same-specialty peers, often stacked on one patient in short succession and preceded by urodynamic/ultrasound testing on nearly every patient. Prior-authorization review of the submitted records would reveal symptom documentation appearing identically across patients and diagnoses unsupported by the testing.
496.features_to_create: Build a surgeon-procedure profile per NPI: rates of hysterectomy and pelvic-floor procedures per 1,000 unique patients, share of patients receiving urodynamics/ultrasound before surgery, and multi-procedure stacking per patient; when above the calibrated peer percentile, place the NPI on prepay medical review with mandatory prior authorization and records submission. Add a template-detection check flagging near-duplicate history/symptom text across different patients' submitted notes.

497.ways_to_identify: The exclusion is a hard, pre-payment fact: screening the rendering and employed-staff NPIs/SSNs against the HHS-OIG LEIE and state exclusion lists monthly (and at hire/credentialing) would have blocked every claim. Session-level fraud shows as billed psychotherapy units overlapping in time, sessions on dates with implausible daily totals, and telehealth claims with no corresponding platform connection log.
497.features_to_create: Implement a mandatory prepay exclusion edit that matches every rendering, supervising and employed individual on a claim against LEIE/state exclusion files at adjudication and denies with a group-level notice; re-screen the group's full roster monthly and suspend payments if an excluded individual is found. Add telehealth session-integrity edits: overlapping time units per rendering NPI, daily unit ceilings, and a documentation request for platform session logs.

498.ways_to_identify: Standing-order abuse is visible in claims: a single referring provider or residential program generating a fixed cadence of presumptive plus definitive UDT per client (e.g., three times weekly for a year) with unchanged diagnosis codes and near-100% definitive reflex rate. Requisition forms with pre-checked recurring panels and a residential facility rather than a treating clinician as the effective orderer are catchable at prepay review of the order documentation.
498.features_to_create: Compute per-beneficiary UDT frequency and per-referrer definitive-reflex rate, and prepay-pend definitive UDT beyond a calibrated frequency per period or where the same order date recurs mechanically, requiring an individualized, signed order dated near the collection. Flag labs whose referrals concentrate in one residential program and whose beneficiaries all share identical test cadence; deny testing used for program monitoring rather than treatment.

499.ways_to_identify: Time-based psychotherapy codes are directly auditable at adjudication: summing billed service minutes per rendering NPI per day exposes days exceeding 16 hours, and the code mix shift toward longer/complex codes (e.g., 60-minute over 45-minute, add-on crisis codes) is measurable against same-specialty peers. Both are computable before payment from the claim's own units and dates.
499.features_to_create: Build an NPI-day minute accumulator across all payers/lines: convert each time-based code to its minimum minutes, sum per rendering provider per date, and auto-deny or pend claims once the daily total exceeds a plausible workday ceiling. Add a code-distribution monitor comparing the provider's long-session/high-complexity share to same-specialty peers, placing outliers on prepay review with a request for time-stamped progress notes.

500.ways_to_identify: Referral concentration is visible at adjudication: nearly all of Noah Associates' UDT volume traced to a single SUD clinic owner, and the ordering NPI on the claims either did not match any physician with an active treatment relationship or showed no corresponding E/M or treatment-plan claim for the same beneficiary near the collection date. Definitive/presumptive UDT units per patient per month and panel breadth also sat far above same-specialty peers. Ownership and sham 'consulting' contracts surface at enrolment/credentialing via common addresses, officers and 1099 flows.
500.features_to_create: Build a lab-level referral-concentration monitor: per billing lab per quarter, compute share of UDT dollars from the top one or two ordering entities and the count of UDT claims lacking any companion E/M/SUD treatment claim for the same beneficiary within a lookback window; when both exceed calibrated percentiles, apply a prepay edit requiring the signed physician order and medical-necessity documentation and route to a kickback review. Add a per-beneficiary-per-month cap edit on definitive UDT drug classes with documentation request above the cap.

501.ways_to_identify: Attendant-level hour accumulation is fully visible prepay: 1,970.5 hours billed for two recipients implies impossible daily/weekly hour totals for one aide and overlapping service windows. Cross-check billed visit times against EVV check-in/out records, and against the recipients' authorized plan-of-care hours and any concurrent institutional or hospital claims for those beneficiaries.
501.features_to_create: Implement an aide-NPI/employee-ID daily and weekly hour aggregator across all recipients and agencies, firing when total hours exceed a physiologically plausible ceiling or when two recipients' service intervals overlap for the same aide; deny or pend those lines prepay. Add an authorization-reconciliation edit that rejects units above the approved plan-of-care hours and an EVV-absent edit that pends claims with no matching telephony/GPS visit record.

502.ways_to_identify: EDTA/chelation claims are covered only for lead toxicity, so the diagnosis code is the hook: look for J0600 (edetate calcium disodium) and chelation administration codes carrying lead-poisoning diagnoses with no supporting blood-lead or heavy-metal laboratory claim history for that beneficiary. A single practice reporting lead poisoning in a large share of its panel is statistically implausible versus same-specialty peers and versus state public-health lead prevalence.
502.features_to_create: Build a diagnosis-substantiation prepay edit on chelation drug and infusion codes: require a paid blood-lead or heavy-metal lab claim (or submitted result) for the beneficiary within a defined lookback, else pend for records. Add a provider-level monitor of the share of that provider's beneficiaries with lead-toxicity diagnoses versus peers; above the calibrated percentile, place the provider on prepay review of all chelation claims.

503.ways_to_identify: This is retail card/EBT skimming with no provider claim component, so no health-claim adjudication edit applies; detection sits with the card processor and the EBT program via common-point-of-purchase analytics linking compromised cards to a shared merchant terminal, plus out-of-pattern EBT balance drains and out-of-state ATM/POS use. For the benefit agency, post-compromise the route is card-replacement and transaction-reversal workflows.
503.features_to_create: For EBT: build a common-point-of-compromise engine that clusters fraud-reported cards by shared prior terminal/merchant ID and time window, auto-flags that terminal, and forces reissue of all cards that transacted there. Add velocity/geography rules on EBT authorizations (rapid full-balance withdrawals, transactions far from the household's usual merchants) that hold the transaction and trigger cardholder verification.

504.ways_to_identify: Pure employment-tax fraud with no health claims; the payer is the IRS. The observable signal is a mismatch between very large cash withdrawals from business accounts (and BSA/CTR filings) and the wages reported on Forms 941/W-2, plus workers' compensation payroll and certified-payroll filings inconsistent with reported wages.
504.features_to_create: No payer-side claims control applies. Nearest applicable control is an IRS/state-workforce cross-file analytic: per EIN per quarter, compare reported 941 wages to bank cash-withdrawal aggregates from CTRs, state unemployment wage records and industry revenue-to-payroll ratios, and open an employment-tax examination when the ratio falls below the calibrated peer percentile.

505.ways_to_identify: The Medicaid piece is income-eligibility fraud, detectable at enrolment and redetermination rather than in claims: the applicant reported near-zero income while operating a licensed roofing/paving business, used a UPS-mailbox address, and appeared as payer on 1099s issued in relatives' names. Automated wage/asset matches (state wage records, IRS 1099/1040 extracts, business registration and contractor licence files, bank/asset verification) would show self-employment and business receipts absent from the application.
505.features_to_create: Build an eligibility-verification rule set: at application and each redetermination, match applicant SSN/name against secretary-of-state and contractor-licence registries, 1099-MISC/NEC payer and payee data, and commercial-address databases; fire when self-attested income is near zero but the applicant is a registered business principal or the mailing address is a commercial mail drop, and suspend enrolment pending documentary income proof. Add an alias/identity-linkage check on shared SSNs, addresses and phone numbers across applications.

506.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic as the companion case: concealed self-employment income used to obtain low-income Medicaid, catchable at enrolment/redetermination via wage, 1099, business-registration and commercial-mailbox matches rather than in claim adjudication. Zero reported income alongside an active contracting business and alias-linked filings is the observable signal.
506.features_to_create: Implement automated income and identity verification at application and redetermination: cross-match to state wage files, IRS 1099/return extracts, contractor licensing and business registries, and commercial-address databases; fire when declared income is inconsistent with matched business activity and hold eligibility pending proof. Periodically re-run matches on the active enrolled population and generate overpayment-recovery referrals where income appears retroactively.

507.ways_to_identify: Duplicate-source billing is visible prepay through duplicate-claim logic keyed on beneficiary, specimen/DOS, and test code across Medicare, the state COVID program and, via clearinghouse/all-payer data, commercial payers; the same test billed to a federal program and to a state uninsured-testing fund is a hard duplicate. Phantom codes show up as claim volumes exceeding the lab's reported specimen accessions and instrument throughput, and as add-on/panel codes reported at implausible ratios to the base test.
507.features_to_create: Build a cross-payer duplicate detector: hash beneficiary+DOS+test code and reject the second payment path (federal versus state uninsured fund versus commercial) prepay, with attestation that no other payer has been billed. Add a lab-capacity check comparing billed test counts per day to reported CLIA capacity/accession logs, and suspend payment where billed volume exceeds capacity pending an on-site or records audit.

508.ways_to_identify: The signal is a sudden clustered adoption of specific electrical-stimulation and ENFD punch-biopsy code combinations by unrelated small practices, all coinciding with one manufacturer's distributor footprint, billed with acute-pain and neuropathy diagnoses outside the device's cleared/covered indication. Marketing-driven waves show up as new-to-code providers with near-identical code triplets (E-stim + vitamin injection + biopsy), and provider-owned distributorships appear in ownership disclosures and 1099/commission records at credentialing.
508.features_to_create: Build a code-cluster diffusion monitor: per HCPCS combination, detect statistically abnormal cohorts of providers newly billing the same triplet within a short window and sharing a device supplier, and place that cohort on prepay documentation review for coverage-indication proof. Add a non-covered-technology edit that denies electrical nerve stimulation and photoplethysmography-style codes when the underlying device/technology is not covered, plus an ownership-disclosure edit flagging provider-owned distributor relationships with the referred lab.

509.ways_to_identify: Both strands are prepay-detectable code-logic and authorization failures: DME claims without a matching physician order/face-to-face encounter claim, rentals continuing after the beneficiary died, moved to a facility or after the item was returned; and clinic claims with mutually exclusive E/M pairs, telehealth POS/modifier on visits also billed as in-person, and therapy codes clinically inconsistent with the member's diagnosis/equipment history. Duplicate billing across Medicare, Medicaid and VA for the same DOS is visible with cross-payer matching.
509.features_to_create: Implement a DME order-linkage edit requiring a paid physician encounter and written-order record before paying rental/purchase, plus continuous-rental termination logic tied to death, institutional stay and equipment-return data. For clinic claims, build mutually-exclusive/NCCI pair edits, a telehealth-consistency edit (deny when POS/modifier indicates telehealth but an in-person claim exists for the same DOS), and a diagnosis-to-service plausibility edit; combine with cross-payer duplicate DOS matching and place high-scoring providers on prepay review.

510.ways_to_identify: Hospice ineligibility is inferable prepay and near-real-time from the certification and utilization record: long stays with no decline in level of care, repeated recertifications, live discharges, absent or boilerplate physician narratives, and non-specific 'debility/failure to thrive' terminal diagnoses. Concurrent claims history showing curative treatment, active dialysis or aggressive workups for the same beneficiary contradicts a six-month prognosis.
510.features_to_create: Build a beneficiary-episode monitor computing length of stay beyond the calibrated peer percentile, recertification count, live-discharge rate and share of episodes with non-specific terminal diagnoses per hospice; when thresholds trip, apply prepay medical review of the certification and narrative for continued episodes. Add a contradiction edit flagging hospice episodes with concurrent curative/aggressive treatment claims and pend those periods for records.

511.ways_to_identify: No health-plan claims were submitted; this is an investor-loan Ponzi based on fabricated purchase orders, so no adjudication edit applies. Detection routes are securities/lender-side: verifying purported purchase orders directly with the named provider customers, confirming no corresponding revenue or inventory, and observing bank flows where new investor money pays earlier investors and casinos.
511.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control for a payer or lender doing supplier due diligence: automated verification of claimed purchase orders/contracts against the named counterparty's confirmation and against the supplier's actual claim/shipment history, plus a bank-flow rule flagging deposits from individual investors immediately disbursed to prior investors or gaming merchants.

512.ways_to_identify: This is a DEA recordkeeping violation, not a billing scheme, so claim edits will not catch it; the signal is a reconciliation gap between controlled-substance purchases reported by distributors (ARCOS) for the registrant and dispensing/administration records or claims. A registrant with contrast/sedation purchases but no corresponding administration documentation or biennial inventory is the flag.
512.features_to_create: Build a registrant-level purchase-to-dispense reconciliation: per DEA number per period, compare ARCOS/distributor purchase quantities to documented administrations (claims with sedation/anesthesia codes or dispensing records) and flag unexplained variance for inspection scheduling. For the payer, add a documentation request on controlled-substance administration codes from registrants with open DEA compliance findings.

513.ways_to_identify: This is a capitation-rate and overpayment-retention issue on the payer's own side: the rate-setting actuarial recalculation showed the paid PMPM diverged from the correct basis, and the plan kept invoicing at the stale rate. Signals are invoiced rate versus the authoritative contracted rate table, enrollment-count reconciliation, and the absence of a self-report after the plan was notified of the error.
513.features_to_create: Build an invoice-to-rate-table validation that recomputes each capitation invoice as authoritative rate x verified eligible member-months and auto-rejects or withholds any line where the billed rate differs from the current approved rate; retain version history so retroactive rate corrections generate automatic recoupment schedules. Add a 60-day self-report clock: once an overpayment is identified in the rate file, open a receivable and offset future capitation payments automatically.

514.ways_to_identify: No claims were paid; this is fiduciary/elder financial exploitation involving a trust and diverted Social Security payments, so payer claim edits do not apply. Observable signals are a representative-payee/trustee change followed by redirection of benefit deposits to an account controlled by an unrelated third party, and payments from a nonprofit to a fiduciary's personal or church accounts.
514.features_to_create: No health-claims control applies. Nearest control at the benefit agency: a rule that flags any change of direct-deposit routing or representative payee where the new account is not in the beneficiary's name, or is shared with multiple unrelated beneficiaries, and holds the change pending beneficiary contact; add monitoring for a single payee account receiving benefits for unrelated recipients.

515.ways_to_identify: Street resale is not visible in adjudication, but the upstream supply is: PDMP data would show the crew's members and straw patients obtaining oxycodone from multiple prescribers and pharmacies with short intervals, high MME, cash payment, and long travel distances, and would show a small set of prescribers accounting for the pills. Payer claims (if any) would show early refills and pharmacy/prescriber shopping.
515.features_to_create: Build a beneficiary-level PDMP/claims shopping score using distinct prescribers and pharmacies for opioids in a rolling window, cumulative MME, early-refill overlap and cash-versus-insurance mix; above the calibrated percentile, lock the member to a single prescriber/pharmacy and require prior authorization. Pair with a prescriber-level monitor of opioid volume and share of cash-paid, out-of-area patients, triggering prepay review and referral.

516.ways_to_identify: The signal is mass billing of vascular-study CPT codes (93922/93923/93924) by primary-care and risk-assessment providers who own no vascular lab, in tight clusters tied to one device vendor's rollout, often on the same encounter as annual health-risk assessments. Coverage policy excludes photoplethysmography, so the technology-to-code mismatch is checkable if the device/technology is captured, and abnormal per-provider PAD-testing rates versus peers are visible prepay.
516.features_to_create: Build a code-versus-technology edit requiring, for 93922/93923/93924, attestation of an ankle-brachial-index-capable modality and supplier/device identification, denying claims where the registered device performs only photoplethysmography. Add a diffusion monitor detecting cohorts of non-vascular specialties newly billing these codes at rates above the calibrated peer percentile within a short window, and place that cohort on prepay documentation review with recovery referral for prior paid claims.

517.ways_to_identify: No health claims involved; this is stolen-identity pandemic UI fraud plus deed/escrow fraud. The UI side was highly detectable prepay: 120 applications for 76 identities across ten states, sharing IP addresses, phone numbers, bank/debit-card mailing addresses and device fingerprints, with claimant identity data not matching state wage records.
517.features_to_create: No payer-side health control applies. For benefit agencies: build a cross-state identity-and-device deduplication service that clusters UI applications by SSN, mailing address, IP/device fingerprint and card-delivery address, holds payment when a cluster exceeds one claimant per identity or a shared address serves multiple unrelated claimants, and requires documentary identity proofing plus wage-record match before first disbursement.

518.ways_to_identify: Fabricated patients are detectable at the pharmacy and PDMP layer prepay: prescriptions from one Virginia clinic filled in dozens of far-flung states, patient names/addresses failing identity and address verification, repeated use of the same phone or address across many 'patients,' and one prescriber generating extreme volumes of promethazine-codeine and Tussionex relative to peers. Cash payment and geographic dispersion between prescriber and pharmacy are the strongest markers.
518.features_to_create: Build a prescriber-level controlled-substance profile computing volume of opioid/cough-syrup units, number of distinct patients per day, and the geographic spread between prescriber address and dispensing pharmacies; when the out-of-area fill share and volume exceed calibrated percentiles, suspend claim payment for that prescriber's controlled-substance scripts and refer to licensing/DEA. Add a patient-identity validation edit at the pharmacy claim level (address/DOB/SSN verification and duplicate-demographic clustering) that pends fills failing verification.

519.ways_to_identify: No health claims; the payers are the IRS and SBA. The trust-fund piece is visible as withheld amounts on W-2s with no matching 941 deposits for the quarter; the PPP piece was verifiable at underwriting by matching the applicant's certification of tax compliance and payroll figures against IRS transcripts and 941/W-2 filings, and by monitoring disbursement use against payroll bank activity.
519.features_to_create: No payer-side claims control applies. Nearest controls: an IRS rule matching per-EIN W-2 withholding totals to 941 deposits each quarter and auto-opening a trust-fund case on unexplained gaps; and an SBA underwriting edit that blocks disbursement until IRS transcript match confirms filed/paid employment taxes and the stated payroll matches reported wage data, with post-disbursement monitoring for absence of payroll outflows.

520.ways_to_identify: At claim adjudication, these schemes leave arithmetic footprints: EIDBI/HSS/ICS units billed on nearly every calendar day for the same client (447 consecutive service days), overlapping service hours for the same staff or same client across programs, service dates after a beneficiary's date of death, and billing under an NPI whose rendering provider never logged an encounter. At enrolment/credentialing, new EIDBI and Housing Stabilization agencies with out-of-state owner addresses (Philadelphia principals billing Minnesota HSS), no prior program history, and rapid ramp to full authorization amounts are visible before the first payment. Kickbacks to parents scaled to the DHS authorization are only detectable post-pay, via bank-record subpoena and beneficiary interviews, but the tell-tale prepay proxy is authorization amount consumed at or near 100% for every client in a clustered geographic/kinship recruitment pool.
520.features_to_create: Build a beneficiary-day engine that flags (a) any claim with service date > date of death from the MMIS eligibility/death file, (b) rendering-staff hours summed across all clients/programs exceeding a feasible workday, (c) clients with consecutive-service-day streaks and authorization-utilization ratios above the calibrated percentile versus same-program peers - each firing a prepay suspend and a records request for signed session notes with staff credentials. Add a credentialing rule that scores new EIDBI/HSS/ICS enrolments on out-of-state principal address, shared address/phone/bank account with other new enrolments, and owner overlap with previously sanctioned entities, placing them on 100% prepay review of the first N claims. Add a staff-qualification cross-check that matches each billed behavioral technician to a registry/training record and age, denying claims rendered by unverifiable staff.

521.ways_to_identify: RUG/PDPM distribution is the signal: a facility whose share of Ultra-High therapy RUGs sits far above same-state SNF peers, with therapy minutes clustering just past the Ultra-High threshold and uniform across clinically dissimilar residents, is visible from MDS assessments matched to claims before payment. On the hospital side, individual therapy codes (97110/97530 one-on-one) billed for many patients in the same time block by the same therapist is arithmetically impossible and detectable from rendering-therapist plus date/time-on-claim data. Absence of a physician-signed plan of care is a documentation condition of payment testable by targeted prepay records request at the three outpatient clinics.
521.features_to_create: Compute per-facility monthly Ultra-High/High therapy RUG mix and minutes-just-above-threshold density versus same-state peer distribution; fire prepay review with MDS and therapy-log request when both exceed the calibrated percentile. Build a therapist-day concurrency edit: sum billed one-on-one therapy units per rendering therapist per date; when implied minutes exceed available worked minutes, deny or downcode to group therapy pending logs. Add a plan-of-care attestation edit for outpatient therapy at new or flagged sites requiring physician signature date on file before payment.

522.ways_to_identify: A chiropractic clinic billing thousands of OTC COVID test kits is an immediate specialty/service mismatch - the service has no plausible relationship to the billing taxonomy - and volume ramping from zero to millions in six months is visible in weekly paid-trend monitoring. The referring NP appeared on thousands of claims across a state she had no relationship with; comparing the referring provider's own claim/encounter history (no corresponding office visit, no other referrals, licence status/retirement) to the volume attributed to her exposes credential misappropriation prepay. Beneficiary geography scatter far from the clinic's service area, and beneficiaries with no other claims from that provider, are further prepay signals.
522.features_to_create: Build a taxonomy-vs-service edit that hard-denies OTC test kit/DME-type codes billed by specialties with no plausible scope (chiropractic, etc.) absent explicit program authorization. Build a referring-provider plausibility check: per referring NPI per month, count distinct billing NPIs and claim volume, and require a matching evaluation encounter by that NPI within a lookback window; fire prepay suspension and provider outreach/attestation when the referring NPI's attributed volume exceeds the calibrated percentile or the provider is inactive/retired. Add a beneficiary-distance and new-patient-share monitor with velocity trip-wires that cap payment and trigger review on explosive first-year growth.

523.ways_to_identify: One ordering physician appearing on CGx orders for hundreds of geographically scattered beneficiaries, with no corresponding telehealth or office E/M claim for those beneficiaries by that physician, is fully visible in claims prepay. The referring NPI's cross-state beneficiary footprint, licensure states, and the concentration of his orders in a handful of labs are all adjudication-time data. Per-order payments of ~$30 from telemedicine marketing companies are only provable post-pay via bank records, but the ordering pattern alone justifies prepay suspension.
523.features_to_create: Per ordering NPI per month, compute distinct CGx-billing labs, distinct beneficiary states, order count, and the share of orders with no companion E/M/telehealth encounter by that NPI within a lookback window; fire prepay suspension of all CGx claims carrying that NPI and a documentation request for the encounter record when the no-encounter share and volume exceed calibrated percentiles. Add a lab-side edit requiring the ordering physician's licence state to include the beneficiary's state. Escalate ordering NPIs whose orders concentrate in a single lab to payment suspension and referral.

524.ways_to_identify: Identical mechanic to the companion case: a single physician signs CGx orders for beneficiaries he never contacted, so the diagnostic signal is orders without any companion encounter claim by the ordering NPI, extreme beneficiary-state dispersion, and order volume concentrated into one or two labs - all present in claim data before payment. Cancer-genetic testing ordered with no oncology diagnosis history or prior workup in the beneficiary's claim history is an additional prepay medical-necessity flag. The $30-per-order kickback is a post-pay bank-record finding.
524.features_to_create: Implement an ordering-provider integrity score per month (distinct labs, beneficiary-state count, order volume, share of orders lacking an E/M by that NPI, share of beneficiaries lacking any cancer/oncology diagnosis history) and suspend prepay all CGx claims bearing NPIs above the calibrated composite percentile pending encounter documentation. Add a beneficiary-level edit denying CGx when no qualifying diagnosis or treating-oncologist relationship exists in claim history. Feed flagged ordering NPIs and their linked labs to a shared watchlist that triggers prepay review of the lab's entire CGx line.

525.ways_to_identify: This is a lending/eligibility case, not a claims-payment case: no payer adjudication exists, so detection sits with the SBA/lender at application, by testing the stated affiliate group against corporate-ownership data (SBIC portfolio filings, EIN and common-control links, prior PPP loan records) to enforce the $4 million second-draw corporate-group cap. The observable signal is the applicant's ownership chain overlapping entities that already drew PPP. Post-award, forgiveness review could have aggregated loans across all entities with a shared controlling parent.
525.features_to_create: For payer-side analogues, build an affiliation-aggregation check for any enrolment or funding application: resolve applicant EIN/owner/officer/address to a corporate-group graph and sum prior awards or capitated payments across the group against the programme cap, blocking disbursement and forgiveness when the group total exceeds it. Require a signed affiliate-disclosure schedule and auto-compare it to the resolved ownership graph, flagging any undisclosed affiliate for manual underwriting.

526.ways_to_identify: Again a loan-eligibility case rather than claim adjudication, but the payer already holds the disproving data: Medicare/Medicaid SNF enrolment and cost-report files record common ownership and control across a chain and employee/staffing counts (PBJ payroll-based journal data), so an entity-by-entity 'fewer than 500 employees' certification could be tested against the chain's aggregate PBJ headcount at application. The observable signal is many separately certifying facilities sharing officers, managers, and a single management company.
526.features_to_create: Build a common-ownership aggregation service that keys facility CCNs to owner/officer/management-company records from enrolment and cost reports, then sums PBJ-derived employee counts across the resolved group; fire an ineligibility flag whenever an entity certifies a size standard that the group total contradicts. Expose this graph as an API to grant/loan programmes and as a prepay risk factor for chain-wide payment review.

527.ways_to_identify: There is no health-care claim here - it is a HUD construction grant with a false certification of completed work, so the control belongs to the grant administrator's invoice-approval step: paying draw requests only against independent inspection evidence (geotagged photos, sump-pump serial numbers, third-party inspector sign-off) for scope items in flood-plain homes. The observable signal is invoices certifying installed drainage systems with no matching inspection record or materials-purchase documentation.
527.features_to_create: For the nearest applicable payer control, build a pay-for-verified-deliverable rule: hold invoice lines for high-risk scope items until a matching independent inspection artifact (photo with geotag/timestamp, serialized equipment record) is linked, and sample-audit a calibrated share of certified units before final payment. Flag contractors whose certified-completion rate outpaces their materials purchases or inspection submissions for full documentation review.

528.ways_to_identify: Respiratory pathogen panels billed in bulk for nursing-home residents nationwide by one lab with no ordering-physician relationship is visible prepay: RPP claims lacking an ordering NPI who has any encounter with that beneficiary, an RPP-to-COVID-test ratio far above peer labs, and claims with service dates after the beneficiary's date of death. Facility-level clustering (whole census tested the same day at one SNF) and the lab's explosive volume ramp are adjudication-time signals from claim headers.
528.features_to_create: Build a lab-claim edit chain: deny RPP/large-panel codes when the paired COVID test is the documented purpose and no ordering physician with a beneficiary relationship exists; deny any service date after date of death; and compute per-lab monthly panel-to-basic-test ratio and same-facility same-day mass-testing density, suspending prepay above calibrated percentiles pending physician orders and specimen/result records. Add a facility-consent/order attestation requirement for nationwide SNF sweep testing before payment.

529.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic as the companion indictment: high-cost respiratory pathogen panels attached to nursing-home COVID screening with no treating-physician order, many tests never performed, and some beneficiaries already deceased. All three are prepay-testable from claim data: missing/implausible ordering NPI, date-of-death conflicts, and per-lab panel-versus-simple-test mix far above peers. Explosive month-over-month growth from a new lab enrolment adds an enrolment-time risk flag.
529.features_to_create: Implement date-of-death and eligibility-window hard denials on all lab claims, plus an ordering-provider relationship edit requiring an encounter by the ordering NPI within a lookback window for high-cost panels. Compute per-lab RPP share of total volume and growth velocity versus peer labs; when above the calibrated percentile, apply prepay payment suspension and request signed orders, specimen logs and result reports. Route new labs billing SNF populations across many states into first-N-claims full prepay review.

530.ways_to_identify: Angioplasty without any diagnostic workup shows as a missing-precursor pattern in claim history: PTA/peripheral intervention claims with no preceding non-invasive vascular study (ABI, duplex ultrasound, angiography) and no qualifying PAD/claudication or critical-limb-ischemia diagnosis for that beneficiary. Provider-level concentration - one practice performing hundreds of PTAs with per-beneficiary repeat interventions well above same-specialty peers - is visible before payment. Necessity itself is confirmed only by chart review, sought via prepay documentation request.
530.features_to_create: Build a precursor-diagnostics edit: for each PTA/peripheral intervention claim, require a qualifying diagnosis plus a non-invasive vascular study by any provider within a lookback window; otherwise pend the claim and request the diagnostic report and procedure note. Add provider-level metrics (PTAs per 100 patients, repeat interventions per beneficiary per year, share of cases without prior imaging) benchmarked to same-specialty peers, placing outliers above the calibrated percentile on prepay medical-necessity review.

531.ways_to_identify: Hospice enrolments harvested by door-knocking at retirement homes produce distinctive prepay patterns: election dates clustering within days for many beneficiaries from a few residential addresses hundreds of miles from the hospice's service area, patients with no prior claims evidencing terminal illness, and unusually long lengths of stay with no decline. Forged physician certifications are catchable at the ADR stage by verifying the certifying physician's signature, NPI status and attesting directly with that physician rather than accepting the submitted form. Beneficiary-side confirmation via a hospice-election notification letter is also a prepay control.
531.features_to_create: Build a hospice-election screen that geocodes beneficiary residence against the hospice's approved service area and clusters elections by shared facility address and election date; fire prepay review when out-of-area or address-cluster share exceeds the calibrated percentile. Require, before first payment, a verified certification: match certifying/attending NPI to an active licence and to a prior encounter claim with that beneficiary, and auto-contact the physician to confirm authorship on flagged records. Send election-confirmation letters to beneficiaries/representatives and suspend payment on non-response or denial.

532.ways_to_identify: Prescription-level red flags were all in the data the payer holds: MME per day above the calibrated high-dose threshold, concurrent opioid-benzodiazepine (and carisoprodol) combinations, early refills, and beneficiaries travelling implausible distances to a single prescriber. Cash payment despite coverage is visible as pharmacy fills for the same patients falling outside the drug benefit while medical claims continue. Prescriber-level concentration within one hospital's employed staff is detectable at adjudication and at pharmacy point-of-sale.
532.features_to_create: Build a prescriber-patient risk engine on pharmacy and medical claims computing per-patient daily MME, overlapping opioid/benzo/muscle-relaxant days, early-refill ratio, prescriber-patient distance and cash-fill share; fire point-of-sale prepay edits requiring prior authorisation on high-MME and dangerous-combination fills. Aggregate to prescriber level versus same-specialty peers and place outliers on prepay review with medical-record requests, notifying the employing hospital as a compliance obligation. Escalate persistent outliers to payment suspension and licensure/DEA referral.

533.ways_to_identify: A cash-only clinic that bills nothing leaves its footprint downstream at the pharmacy: one prescriber accounting for enormous oxycodone/oxymorphone volumes, uniform high-quantity high-dose scripts, patients clustered far from the practice address, and a practice location that is a warehouse with no legitimate clinical claim history. Payers and PDMPs can see prescriber volume and patient travel distance before paying the fills; the absence of any E/M claims for those patients from that prescriber is itself the giveaway. Kickback payments per prescription are post-pay bank-record evidence.
533.features_to_create: Build a 'prescriber with no encounters' detector: for each prescriber, compare controlled-substance fill volume against E/M/encounter claims for the same patients; when fills are high and encounters near zero, block pharmacy payment pending prior authorisation and chart request. Add prescriber-level oxycodone/oxymorphone dosage-unit volume, mean MME and mean patient-prescriber distance benchmarked to same-specialty peers, plus an address-validation check flagging practice locations that are non-clinical (warehouse/industrial) parcels. Route trip-wires to PDMP and DEA referral alongside the prepay edit.

534.ways_to_identify: For the insurers, the enrolment side is testable at underwriting: many ACA applications sharing a facility's address, phone, email domain or bank/payment instrument, all claiming qualifying life events and income just above Medicaid thresholds, then immediately incurring out-of-network residential treatment claims - a same-day enrol-and-admit pattern. On claims, comprehensive urinalysis panels billed at extreme per-patient frequency with ordering physicians who had already terminated employment (verifiable against licence/credential and employment dates) is a prepay conflict. Broker kickbacks disguised as marketing hours are post-pay, found through contract and payment-record audit.
534.features_to_create: Build an enrolment-integrity model that clusters applications by shared contact/address/payment identifiers and third-party assistor, and flags QLE-plus-income-attestation applications followed by out-of-network SUD admission within a short window for eligibility verification before claims pay. Build a UDS frequency and ordering-validity edit: cap definitive comprehensive panels per patient per period without documented rationale, and deny claims whose ordering NPI has no active relationship with the facility on the service date. Add a facility-level out-of-network billing monitor (claims per patient-day, panel spend per admission) that triggers prepay review and a records/contract request covering marketing agreements.

535.ways_to_identify: No claims-payment component - this is EIDL misuse of loan proceeds, detectable by the lender/SBA rather than by claim adjudication: post-disbursement transaction monitoring of the loan-funded account would show large luxury-vehicle and real-estate purchases inconsistent with permitted working-capital use. At application, revenue and injury figures could be cross-checked against tax transcripts. Payer-side, none of this touches claims.
535.features_to_create: Nearest applicable control: require disbursement into a designated account and run automated use-of-proceeds monitoring that flags MCC-coded luxury vehicle, brokerage and real-estate transactions above a threshold, freezing remaining draws and triggering a documentation request. Verify application revenue against IRS transcript data before funding. No payer claims edit applies.

536.ways_to_identify: The pattern is prescriber-level and visible in pharmacy claims and PDMP data before each fill is paid: a small set of patients receiving sustained opioid plus benzodiazepine plus sedative plus carisoprodol combinations over years, with early refills, escalating MME and overlapping days' supply. Concentration of a prescriber's controlled-substance volume in a handful of long-term patients, with no evidence of taper, referral or urine-drug monitoring claims, is measurable at adjudication.
536.features_to_create: Implement point-of-sale prepay edits denying or pending fills that create opioid+benzodiazepine or opioid+carisoprodol overlap, or push daily MME above the calibrated high-dose threshold, absent prior authorisation. Compute per-prescriber concentration metrics (share of controlled-substance dosage units to top patients, mean overlap days, early-refill rate) versus same-specialty peers and place outliers on prescriber-level prior authorisation plus medical-record request. Auto-generate PDMP/board referral packets when the pattern persists after outreach.

537.ways_to_identify: Purely internal corporate embezzlement via a company credit card - there is no payer claim and no adjudication touchpoint, so no payer-side control applies. Detection sits with the employer's expense controls: card transactions lacking receipts or business purpose, personal-merchant MCCs, and spend far above the cardholder's role benchmark, all visible in card-issuer data before reimbursement.
537.features_to_create: No payer control applies; the nearest analogue is a corporate card monitoring rule: per cardholder per month, flag personal-category MCCs, transactions without matched receipt/approval within a set period, and spend above role-peer percentile, auto-suspending the card and requiring documentation. Enforce segregation of duties so the cardholder cannot approve their own reconciliations.

538.ways_to_identify: Same as the companion charge: employee credit-card embezzlement with no health-care claim and no payer adjudication step, so this is outside payer controls. It is caught by card-level expense monitoring and reconciliation - unsupported charges, personal merchant categories, and approval by the spender herself.
538.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. The nearest applicable control is automated card-transaction surveillance (unmatched-receipt aging, personal-MCC flags, spend-versus-role-peer outliers) with automatic card suspension and mandatory independent approval of executive-assistant reconciliations.

539.ways_to_identify: This is trust-fund payroll tax fraud with no claims-payment component, so no payer adjudication control exists; detection belongs to the IRS by matching W-2/Form 941 reported withholding against actual EFTPS deposits and flagging accruing zero-deposit quarters in near-real time. The observable signal is filed returns reporting withheld amounts with no corresponding remittance over consecutive quarters.
539.features_to_create: No payer claims edit applies. Nearest control: an automated 941-versus-deposit reconciliation that fires after consecutive quarters of reported-but-unremitted withholding, triggering responsible-person identification and collection action; secondarily, flag employers whose payroll-based staffing data implies withholding far above deposits.

540.ways_to_identify: Compare the rendering/supervising NPI on claims against the physician's verifiable location and activity: Saggar was billed as personally performing services on dates he was out of town, detectable by cross-checking travel/absence indicators, simultaneous billing at two sites, and impossible same-day service volume for one NPI across two clinics. Credentialing data carries the rest: the state medical board's collaborative practice arrangement filings list assistant physicians and their collaborating physicians, and CPA rules restrict AP practice to underserved areas, so the practice's service ZIP can be scored against the state's shortage-area file. Also screen every servicing/ordering provider on claims against the OIG LEIE and the state Medicaid suspended/terminated-provider list, which would have flagged the co-conspirator with suspended billing privileges.
540.features_to_create: Build a 'personally performed' plausibility edit per rendering NPI per date: count distinct service locations, total timed/E&M minutes, and flag when one NPI bills as performer at two or more geographically separate sites the same day or exceeds a calibrated same-specialty daily-hours percentile; pend those claims for supervision documentation. Add an enrolment-time linkage that ingests state board collaborative-practice/supervision filings and mid-level rosters, maps each supervising physician to the number of APs and to the shortage-area status of each practice location, and blocks billing under the physician's NPI where the location is not eligible or the supervisor-to-AP ratio exceeds the licensure limit. Run a nightly rendering/ordering/supervising NPI screen against LEIE and state exclusion/suspension files with automatic prepay denial and post-pay recoupment.

541.ways_to_identify: Physician-lab ownership is visible at enrolment: Ali's ordering NPI and Central Diagnostic Laboratory shared ownership/address information in PECOS and state filings, so a self-referral link plus a spike in urine drug testing referrals concentrated from a handful of ordering NPIs is observable prepay. Billing under Dr. Malik's NPI for visits Ali performed shows up as annual wellness visits billed on dates Malik was out of state/country and as telephone-only encounters billed with in-person place-of-service codes; ketamine infusion and controlled-substance claims can be matched to the performing provider's DEA registration status.
