Absence/location evidence for the physician is partly post-payment, but POS/modifier inconsistency, pre-signed prescription patterns and DEA validation are all prepay signals.
541.features_to_create: Build an ownership-graph edit that links ordering physician NPIs to lab TINs via PECOS owner names, addresses and bank data, then computes each lab's share of volume from owner-affiliated orderers and each orderer's toxicology-per-patient rate versus same-specialty peers, pending claims above the calibrated percentile for medical-necessity documentation. Add a place-of-service/modifier consistency edit that denies in-person POS or wellness-visit codes when the only supporting contact is telephonic, and a same-day conflict edit flagging one NPI billed as performer at multiple locations. Validate the performing provider's active DEA registration and scope for any controlled-substance or ketamine infusion claim as a hard prepay edit.

542.ways_to_identify: Long-term-care pharmacy claims should be traceable to a valid, current prescriber order; the observable signal is dispensing after the last valid fill/authorization has lapsed - refills beyond the authorized quantity, dispensing on rolling 'standing order' or facility-cycle files with no new prescriber authorization, and prescriber DEA/NPI or prescription dates missing or stale on the claim. At adjudication the payer can compare fill dates to prescription written date and refill authorization count, and check that the prescriber NPI is active and has an encounter relationship with the resident. Full proof requires chart/prescription audit, so the prepay route is targeted documentation requests on the lapsed-authorization subset.
542.features_to_create: Build a prescription-validity engine at the claim line: for each dispense, validate presence and currency of prescriber NPI, written date, days-supply and remaining authorized refills, and deny or pend fills that exceed authorized refills, fall outside the state prescription-validity window, or lack a documented prescriber order. Add a pharmacy-level monitor computing the share of fills that are auto-refill/cycle-fill without a new authorization and the share of residents with no prescriber encounter in the lookback, and trigger prepay documentation review or payment suspension for pharmacies above the calibrated percentile versus LTC pharmacy peers.

543.ways_to_identify: A brand-new entity billing $17.3 million of pediatric early-intervention therapy is detectable at enrolment and first-billing: no verifiable clinical site, no licensed therapist roster, residential/virtual address, and a billing ramp far above same-specialty new-provider peers. Phantom services show up as claims for members with no other corroborating utilization, identical unit counts across members, and therapy minutes exceeding what the credentialed therapist headcount could physically deliver. Identity misuse is visible when member IDs appear on this provider's claims with no referral, no IFSP/early-intervention authorization, and geographic distance from the member's home.
543.features_to_create: Add a new-provider velocity control: for entities within their first year, compute weekly billed amount, distinct members and minutes-per-licensed-therapist, and auto-pend claims above the calibrated new-provider percentile pending site visit and therapist license verification. Build a rendering-capacity edit comparing billed therapy units per day to the number of licensed rendering NPIs on file, and a corroboration edit that pends claims for members with no referral/authorization and no other provider contact in the period, with member outreach verification letters before payment.

544.ways_to_identify: This is a product-diversion/misbranding case with no claim-adjudication footprint, so the payer signal is indirect: gray-market devices reach payers through DME suppliers whose acquisition invoices, serial numbers and lot codes do not trace to authorized U.S. distributors, and whose unit costs sit far below the market for the billed HCPCS. Detection is largely post-payment and regulatory (FDA/customs), but payers can require and audit invoice/serial documentation for high-cost device claims and check supplier accreditation and product-listing status at credentialing.
544.features_to_create: Build a device-provenance check on high-cost DME/implant HCPCS: require serial/lot and acquisition invoice on the claim or in the audit file, validate the manufacturer/model against the FDA listing and against authorized-distributor lists, and pend claims where provenance is missing or the invoice price falls below the calibrated low percentile for that HCPCS. At credentialing, verify supplier accreditation and add periodic invoice sampling with recoupment for non-U.S.-labeled product.

545.ways_to_identify: The signal is procedure-rate outliers within one specialty: endometrial ablation/biopsy, ultrasound, vaccination and STD/blood panel counts per unique patient far above OB/GYN peers, plus repeat ablations on the same patient (an anatomically implausible repetition) and ultrasounds billed on nearly every visit. Upcoding is visible in the E&M level distribution skewed to high levels for both office and telehealth visits, and in telehealth claims billed at levels whose time requirements exceed the documented session length. Falsified records only surface on audit, so the prepay route is targeted record requests on the outlier code families.
545.features_to_create: Build per-provider, per-code-family utilization scoring (procedures per unique patient, ultrasound-per-visit ratio, lab panels per patient) benchmarked against same-specialty peers, and pend claims for providers above the calibrated percentile pending records. Add member-history edits: deny/pend repeat endometrial ablation for the same member within the clinically implausible window, and pend where a procedure claim has no supporting diagnosis history or consent documentation. Add an E&M level-distribution monitor by provider and modality that triggers prepay level-of-service review when high-level share exceeds the peer-calibrated threshold.

546.ways_to_identify: Overbilling of residential/ID waiver services is visible as billed units exceeding the authorized service plan and exceeding calendar feasibility - more than 24 hours of billed care per resident per day, units billed while the resident was hospitalized or absent, and staff-to-resident ratios that cannot support the billed hours. Cross-check claims against the state's waiver authorization file, facility census/attendance logs and concurrent institutional claims. Representative-payee/SSA benefit misuse is not a claims signal; that requires referral to SSA-OIG.
546.features_to_create: Build an authorization-versus-billed reconciliation for waiver/personal-care lines: compute billed units per member per day against the approved plan of care and hard-deny units exceeding authorization or 24 hours/day, and pend units overlapping inpatient, ER or other facility claims for the same member. Add a facility-level staffing feasibility check comparing total billed direct-care hours to payrolled staff hours reported at enrolment/revalidation, with prepay documentation request or payment suspension when the ratio exceeds the calibrated peer threshold.

547.ways_to_identify: Percentage-of-profit marketing arrangements show up as an abrupt concentration of TRICARE compounded-cream claims at one pharmacy sourced from a small set of out-of-area prescribers, near-identical formulas and ingredient/quantity patterns across beneficiaries, and average reimbursement per claim far above peer pharmacies. Enrolment/contract data can be probed by requiring disclosure of marketing contracts and their compensation basis. Beneficiary contact showing they were cold-called and never examined by the prescriber is also available prepay.
547.features_to_create: Build a compound-drug prepay edit: for each pharmacy, compute share of revenue from compounded topical/scar creams, average paid per prescription, distinct-prescriber concentration and prescriber-to-patient geographic distance, and pend or suspend when multiple indicators exceed calibrated peer percentiles. Require signed attestation and disclosure of any marketing/referral arrangement with per-claim or percentage compensation as an enrolment condition, and flag pharmacy-marketer TIN/address/bank-account linkages for prepay review.

548.ways_to_identify: Foreign out-of-network self-pay reimbursement claims are a narrow, high-risk lane: the tells are multiple unrelated members submitting claims routed through the same submitter, email, address or bank account, dramatic injury narratives (stabbings, gunshots, hit-and-run) from the same foreign facilities, and receipts/police reports with reused formatting or sequential numbering. Payers can verify prepay that the member was actually abroad by checking travel/entry records or asking for passport stamps and boarding passes, and by cross-checking domestic claim activity on the same dates that proves the member was in the U.S.
548.features_to_create: Build a member-reimbursement clustering feature that links foreign-claim submissions by shared bank account, address, phone, email, IP, notary or foreign facility name and fires when a cluster exceeds a small number of unrelated members. Add a presence-conflict edit: pend any foreign-treatment reimbursement where the same member has domestic claims or pharmacy fills within the claimed treatment window, and require documentary proof of travel plus direct facility verification before payment; route matched clusters to SIU rather than paying.

549.ways_to_identify: This is a pure exclusion-screening failure and is fully catchable prepay: the rendering counselor's name/NPI/SSN appears on the HHS-OIG LEIE and state exclusion lists, so any claim naming him as rendering provider is non-reimbursable regardless of supervision. The gap is that telehealth group claims often carry only the group NPI or the owner's NPI, hiding the actual renderer, so the payer must require rendering-provider identification on every behavioral-health line and screen the group's full employee roster monthly.
549.features_to_create: Require a rendering-provider NPI on every professional/behavioral-health line and hard-deny lines where the rendering, supervising, ordering or billing entity's owner matches LEIE, SAM, or the state exclusion/termination file, refreshed monthly with name/DOB/SSN fuzzy matching. Add an employment-roster attestation at enrolment and revalidation for group behavioral-health providers, screen every listed clinician and contractor, and suspend payments to the group when an excluded individual is found on the roster pending remediation.

550.ways_to_identify: Time-based psychotherapy codes have minimum-duration requirements, and telehealth platforms generate objective session-duration metadata (connection start/stop) that can be compared prepay to the billed code tier. Provider-level tells: nearly all sessions billed at the longer tier, back-to-back sessions whose billed minutes exceed the clinician's available workday, and identical documented durations across all patients. Payers can require session start/stop times on telehealth behavioral claims and reconcile aggregate billed minutes against clinician capacity.
550.features_to_create: Build a timed-code duration edit: require start/stop time on time-based telehealth psychotherapy lines, deny or downcode when documented duration falls below the code's minimum, and pend when the field is absent. Add a clinician-day capacity check summing billed minutes per rendering NPI per day (including travel/facility rounds) and a distribution monitor on the share of sessions at the longest tier versus same-specialty peers, triggering prepay record and platform-log requests above the calibrated percentile.

551.ways_to_identify: CGx claims driven by telemarketing show a distinctive signature prepay: high-cost hereditary cancer panels ordered for beneficiaries with no cancer diagnosis or family-history documentation, ordering physicians located hundreds of miles from the patient with no prior or subsequent treating relationship, and a handful of ordering NPIs feeding many labs. Ownership concealment is catchable at enrolment by verifying 5%-plus owners against identity data, cross-matching owner SSNs/addresses/bank accounts to other enrolled entities and to individuals with prior sanctions, and requiring notarized disclosure with identity proofing.
551.features_to_create: Build a prepay medical-necessity edit for hereditary cancer panels requiring a qualifying diagnosis or documented family history and evidence of a treating relationship (prior E&M by the ordering NPI within a lookback), denying or pending otherwise. Add ordering-physician concentration and patient-distance features per lab, plus an enrolment identity/ownership verification that scores owner identity documents, matches owner PII and bank accounts across enrolled entities, and blocks or revokes enrolment where disclosed ownership conflicts with verified identity data; suspend payment on labs whose orders concentrate in telemarketing-linked NPIs.

552.ways_to_identify: Unsolicited mailed COVID test kits are catchable prepay with three deterministic checks: date of service after the beneficiary's date of death in the eligibility/DMF file, no ordering-provider relationship or physician order for the kit, and mass-identical claims (same code, same units, thousands of members) from a lab with no matching specimen-processing footprint. Kickback-sourced beneficiary lists show up as member cohorts clustered geographically or by marketer-linked ordering NPIs, and audit responses consisting of templated 'authorizations' with identical wording are a further tell on documentation review.
552.features_to_create: Implement hard prepay edits: deny lines with DOS after date of death using daily-refreshed eligibility/DMF, and deny lab/test-kit claims lacking a valid ordering NPI with a documented patient relationship. Add a lab-level mass-mailing detector computing distinct beneficiaries per day, single-code concentration, share of members with no other claims from the ordering NPI, and duplicate authorization-document hashes on audit responses, with automatic payment suspension and beneficiary verification mailings when thresholds are exceeded.

553.ways_to_identify: No payer-side control applies: this is a commercial receivables/bank fraud on fictitious ethanol invoices with no health care claim component. The analogous financial-institution control is invoice and counterparty verification - confirming shipments and independent counterparty confirmation before purchasing receivables, and flagging circular buy/sell flows between two related parties.
553.features_to_create: No health-plan claims control applies. The nearest analogous control, if the payer purchases or factors receivables, is a counterparty-circularity check that detects offsetting invoice pairs between the same two entities, requires third-party proof of delivery before funding, and suspends funding on concentration or default-rate outliers.

554.ways_to_identify: The mechanic is a fabricated chronic diagnosis driving high-cost recurring services, which is visible prepay as an extreme rheumatoid arthritis diagnosis rate and infusion/injection volume per unique patient versus rheumatology peers, plus near-universal RA coding across the panel with no supporting serology or imaging claims. Additional prepay tells: infusion units exceeding drug-acquisition purchases, imaging billed for more patients per day than equipment capacity allows, and duplicate/reused ultrasound image files identified on documentation review. Fabricated records and staff-image reuse are audit findings, so the prepay action is a documentation request plus prior authorization on biologic infusions.
554.features_to_create: Build a diagnosis-concentration feature per provider (share of panel with the same high-reimbursement chronic diagnosis, and infusion/injection lines per unique patient) benchmarked to same-specialty peers, firing prepay review above the calibrated percentile. Require diagnosis corroboration for biologic infusion claims (supporting lab/serology or imaging claim history) via prior authorization, and add a drug-inventory reconciliation comparing billed J-code units to distributor purchase data, with payment suspension when billed units exceed documented acquisition.

555.ways_to_identify: The pass-through mechanic is visible in claim data: small rural hospitals billing high volumes of specialized cardiovascular lipid panels for patients who never appear in their inpatient/outpatient encounter data and who live far outside the hospital's service area, with the actual testing done by an out-of-state reference lab. The observable signals are outpatient lab revenue as a dominant share of a critical-access hospital's billing, referring-physician geography, and hospital-outpatient rates billed for tests performed elsewhere. Kickbacks routed through MSO 'investment returns' surface at credentialing through physician financial-interest disclosures and in ownership/payment records; the laundering trail is post-payment.
555.features_to_create: Build a lab pass-through edit for facility claims: for each facility, compute the share of billed lab lines for members with no other encounter at that facility, the referring-physician distance distribution, and the ratio of reference-lab-performed to in-house tests, and pend or deny facility-rate lab claims where the specimen was neither collected nor analyzed at the facility. Add mandatory disclosure of MSO/management-company financial relationships at credentialing, link referring-physician NPIs to MSO payee entities, and suspend payment on referral streams where a referring physician holds an undisclosed financial interest in the billing chain.

556.ways_to_identify: No payer-side claims control applies: this is PPP loan fraud, detectable by the SBA/lender through payroll-tax records - no IRS 941 filings or state wage reports matching the claimed 14 employees and $88,000 monthly payroll, an entity with no filing history, and identities of insurance prospects appearing as employees. The health-plan-adjacent signal is a broker misusing customer PII, which a plan can detect through unusual broker access to member/prospect identity data.
556.features_to_create: No claims-payment control applies. The nearest applicable controls are lender-side payroll verification (cross-match applicant payroll to IRS 941/state wage filings before disbursement, deny on mismatch) and, on the payer side, broker/agent access monitoring that flags bulk export or reuse of prospect PII and SSNs by a single broker account and suspends the broker's appointment pending review.

557.ways_to_identify: Forged controlled-substance prescriptions using stolen DEA numbers are catchable at the point of dispensing: the prescriber's DEA registration can be validated in real time for active status, state, and schedule authority, and the patient identity can be checked against eligibility/PDMP records. Cross-pharmacy, cross-state signals are decisive - the same prescriber DEA number appearing at pharmacies in five states within days, patients with no prior claim or PDMP history, and cash-pay codeine fills clustered by presenter. PDMP and switch-level data carry these signals before the fill is completed.
557.features_to_create: Build a real-time prescriber-validation edit on controlled-substance claims that verifies active DEA registration, schedule authority and state of practice, and rejects mismatches. Add a cross-pharmacy velocity detector on prescriber DEA number and patient identity: fire when one DEA number appears across pharmacies in multiple states within a short window, or when a patient with no verifiable eligibility/PDMP history presents schedule II-V opioid or codeine prescriptions, generating a hard reject plus PDMP/board alert.

558.ways_to_identify: Compounded pain creams billed at up to $16,000 per prescription are catchable prepay on price and formula: reimbursement per prescription orders of magnitude above the ingredient cost, high-cost bulk ingredient NDCs, and identical multi-ingredient formulas across unrelated injured workers. Referral concentration is the second signal - a small group of prescribers generating nearly all of a pharmacy's compound volume, often with no examination and with patients geographically remote from the prescriber. Kickback payments are visible through required disclosure of marketing/consulting arrangements and, post-payment, through financial flows to shell entities.
558.features_to_create: Implement a compounded-drug prepay control: require ingredient-level NDCs and quantities, cap or pend claims where paid amount per prescription or per-gram cost exceeds the calibrated peer percentile, and require prior authorization with documented failure of commercially available alternatives. Add prescriber-pharmacy concentration and prescriber-patient distance features per pharmacy, with payment suspension when both exceed thresholds, and mandate disclosure of percentage-based marketing contracts as a condition of participation.

559.ways_to_identify: This is a business email compromise against a health department's accounts-payable function, not a claims fraud, so the signal lives in vendor-master and payment operations: an emailed request to change a known vendor's bank account, sent from a lookalike domain, with new account details not matching the vendor's tax ID or historical banking. It is preventable prepayment by out-of-band callback verification to a phone number on file and by dual approval of any banking change.
559.features_to_create: Build a vendor-master change control: any bank account, address or remittance-email change triggers a hold on all payments to that vendor until out-of-band verification against previously stored contact data plus dual authorization is recorded. Add automated detection of lookalike sender domains and of new payee accounts receiving first-time payments above a threshold or accounts already linked to other payees, routing those disbursements to manual review before release.

560.ways_to_identify: Bilateral knee injection claims split across two dates of service for the same beneficiary within a short window are visible at adjudication: pair the same HCPCS (e.g., viscosupplement injection/arthrocentesis) with LT and RT modifiers on separate claims days apart and flag the repeating pattern practice-wide rather than one-off. Contrast/drug waste is auditable prepay by summing billed units of single-use vials (JW-modifier discarded units plus administered units) against vials purchasable per the provider's 340B/wholesaler purchase records and per-patient dosing limits.
560.features_to_create: Build a beneficiary-level edit that detects same-code opposite-laterality injection claims separated by fewer days than the calibrated clinical norm and, when the provider's share of split-laterality pairs exceeds same-specialty peers, deny the second date pending records. Build a provider-month drug-waste reconciliation: total billed units (administered + JW discarded) of single-use contrast/viscosupplement divided by distinct patients and compared to vial size and to purchase-invoice volumes; overage triggers prepay suspension of the J-code line and an invoice documentation request.

561.ways_to_identify: Cross-payer price comparison catches the dual fee schedule: compare the supplier's charged/allowed amount per breast pump HCPCS against the same supplier's Medicaid-charged amount and against peer suppliers for the identical code, since TRICARE rules bar charging more than other payers. Unbundling is visible at adjudication because accessory HCPCS codes are billed on the same date or shortly after the pump code even though the kit includes them, and 'replacement part' billing appears before any plausible wear interval.
561.features_to_create: Build a supplier-code price parity check that joins TRICARE claim lines to the same NPI/TIN's Medicaid or commercial charge data for identical HCPCS and fires when the TRICARE charge exceeds the lowest other-payer charge, suspending payment above the parity amount. Add a kit-bundling edit that denies accessory/replacement-part codes billed within the kit's included-contents list on or near the pump dispense date absent documentation of loss or defect.

562.ways_to_identify: Several mechanics here are pure enrolment/credentialing controls: nightly screening of every owner, officer, managing employee and W-2 clinician against the LEIE/SAM exclusion and state-exclusion lists would have surfaced Alonso, and beneficial-ownership verification against corporate filings, bank signatory records and IRS data would have exposed straw owners Anzivino and Ramirez-style figures. New DME NPIs that bill high volumes of braces to beneficiaries clustered far from the supplier's service area, with orders traceable to purchased leads and to prescriber NPIs whose other claims never touch orthotics, are detectable prepay; identity-theft-based ordering shows as prescriber NPIs whose ordering pattern breaks from their historic specialty mix, and cross-program benefit duplication (Maine Medicaid/SNAP plus New York SNAP) is found by interstate identity matching.
562.features_to_create: Build a continuous exclusion and ownership monitor that re-screens all disclosed and inferred owners/managers/clinicians against LEIE, state exclusion and death-master files daily and auto-suspends billing privileges plus prepay-holds all claims on a hit. Build a new-supplier surveillance score (months since enrolment, beneficiary geographic dispersion from supplier ZIP, share of claims from prescribers with no prior same-item ordering history, brace-per-beneficiary counts, denied-then-resubmitted claim ratio) that routes above-percentile suppliers to prepay review and requires signed order and delivery-proof documentation; separately run interstate beneficiary identity dedupe on SSN/DOB across state Medicaid and SNAP files.

563.ways_to_identify: Compare billed medical-food HCPCS for inherited metabolic disorders against each recipient's diagnosis history: claims for metabolic formula on members with no PKU/organic-acidemia diagnosis, no metabolic geneticist or specialty-clinic claims, and no prior-authorization from a metabolic specialist are a prepay red flag. Supplier-level acquisition reconciliation also works: the DME's purchase invoices from the metabolic formula manufacturer will not support the billed units, and multiple NPIs/business names sharing one address, bank account or owner conceal volume.
563.features_to_create: Build a diagnosis-and-specialist concordance edit that denies specialized metabolic-formula codes unless the beneficiary has a qualifying metabolic diagnosis on a claim from a metabolic/genetics specialist within the lookback window and a valid prior authorization. Add a supplier-level units-versus-invoice reconciliation requiring manufacturer purchase documentation when billed metabolic-formula units per month exceed the calibrated peer percentile, and link NPIs sharing address/EIN/bank account so the aggregate is scored as one entity.

564.ways_to_identify: This is a plan-and-broker marketing-compensation scheme rather than a claim-level fraud, so the detection surface is the MA plan's broker payment ledger, marketing agreements and enrolment outcomes, reviewable by CMS before capitation flows. Signals: broker-organization payments exceeding regulated commission caps or booked as 'co-op advertising'/'admin fees' with volume-based terms, and enrolment mix by broker showing a deficit of disabled/under-65 or high-risk enrollees versus the market, plus rapid disenrollment and low plan-suitability match.
564.features_to_create: Build a broker-compensation audit feed: per plan-broker-year, compute total compensation per enrolment across all payment categories and flag amounts above the regulatory cap or contracts with volume/quality-of-life-of-plan contingencies, triggering marketing-material and contract production. Build a broker-level enrolment-mix monitor comparing the share of disabled/ESRD/high-CMS-risk enrollees and 90-day disenrollment rates against the broker's local market baseline, with above-percentile deviation escalating to a compliance investigation and potential enrolment suspension.

565.ways_to_identify: Phantom counseling is visible prepay from time-and-capacity arithmetic: sum billed timed psychotherapy units per rendering clinician per day and flag days exceeding feasible working hours, plus weekend/holiday volumes and identical session lengths for every patient. Cross-check with member-side signals — no other claims contact, deceased or out-of-state members, and members who deny receiving services on verification letters — and request the notes, since fabricated notes are typically cloned with near-identical text.
565.features_to_create: Build a clinician-day capacity edit that converts each timed psychotherapy code to minutes, sums per NPI per date, and prepay-suspends claims on dates exceeding the calibrated maximum service hours or where the same member is billed concurrent sessions. Add a solo-provider anomaly score (billed minutes per week, share of patients with no corroborating claims from any other provider, note-text similarity across records obtained) that triggers a documentation request and beneficiary verification mailing before further payment.

566.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic as the companion case: a single social worker's billed therapy minutes per day exceed any feasible schedule, and the members billed show no other clinical footprint, so the fraud is catchable at adjudication from timed-unit totals per NPI per date. Fabricated notes are exposed by a targeted prepay documentation request plus template/text-similarity comparison and beneficiary verification letters asking members to confirm the sessions.
566.features_to_create: Implement a per-NPI per-date minute accumulator across all timed psychotherapy codes with a prepay suspension when totals exceed the calibrated clinician workday and when concurrent-session overlaps occur. Pair it with a solo-behavioral-health monitor scoring growth in billed minutes, patient-panel size versus peers, and share of members with no other provider claims; above-percentile providers move to 100% prepay review with records requested and note-similarity scoring.

567.ways_to_identify: Forged controlled-substance prescriptions on stolen DEA numbers are detectable at pharmacy claim adjudication: the prescriber NPI/DEA is out of state or far from the pharmacy and member, has no prior treating relationship with the member, and suddenly appears as prescriber of Promethazine-Codeine/hydrocodone at a rate inconsistent with that prescriber's specialty and history. Cross-referencing DEA registration status, licence specialty, PDMP dispensing records and member-prescriber-pharmacy distance triangles catches it before payment; the PPP/EIDL/PUA loan and unemployment fraud is not a payer claims matter and is only addressable by the lending/labor agencies' own identity and payroll verification.
567.features_to_create: Build a prescriber-integrity edit on controlled-substance pharmacy claims that validates DEA registration, state licence, and prescribing-authority scope, and fires when a prescriber's cough-syrup/opioid claim volume or geographic dispersion breaks from that prescriber's own 12-month baseline — action is prepay reject plus an alert to the listed prescriber to confirm authorship. Add a member-level triangulation rule (distinct prescribers, distinct pharmacies, prescriber-member and pharmacy-member distance, early refills) that locks further controlled-substance fills pending review; no payer control applies to the PPP/PUA counts.

568.ways_to_identify: At the pharmacy claim level the payer can validate the prescriber's DEA/NPI status and treating relationship: forged scripts show as prescribers with no prior claims for the member, out-of-area prescriber-pharmacy-member geography, and a spike of Promethazine-Codeine/hydrocodone attributed to a prescriber whose specialty and history never included them. PDMP linkage and prescriber-confirmation callbacks resolve it prepay; the PPP/EIDL and multistate PUA components have no payer-side claims control and belong to lender and workforce-agency identity/payroll verification.
568.features_to_create: Build a controlled-substance prescriber-authentication edit (live DEA registration/schedule authority check, licence-specialty plausibility, no-prior-relationship flag) that rejects prepay and notifies the prescriber of record for attestation. Add a pharmacy-level monitor of the share of controlled-substance fills written by prescribers outside the pharmacy's normal referral network and by prescribers with sudden volume breaks, escalating above-percentile pharmacies to prepay review and on-site audit; state the loan/UI counts are out of payer scope.

569.ways_to_identify: Billing under a proxy prescriber is visible prepay: the elderly father's NPI/DEA suddenly appears as rendering provider on thousands of OTP/Suboxone claims at a clinic where his co-located, credentialing-barred relative works, with implausible daily service volumes and no travel/presence evidence, and the barred individual appears in ownership or payroll disclosures. Upcoding is detectable from the clinic's code-level distribution — near-universal high-complexity E/M and counseling codes versus same-specialty peers — and from time-unit totals per NPI-day exceeding a feasible schedule.
569.features_to_create: Build a rendering-provider plausibility check per NPI-day: total timed/E-M minutes, patient counts, and age/licence status of the NPI, plus a shared-address/shared-owner link to any excluded or credential-denied individual; a hit triggers prepay suspension and an in-person attestation/site visit. Add an OTP code-distribution outlier model (share of high-complexity codes, counseling units per patient-month, buprenorphine prescriptions per prescriber-day) that pushes above-percentile clinics to prepay documentation review.

570.ways_to_identify: There is no health care claim in this case — it is pure PPP loan fraud, so no payer adjudication control would have caught it; detection sits with the lender/SBA, via matching the applicant's claimed payroll to IRS Form 941/W-2 filings and to state wage records, and validating submitted bank statements directly with the depository. Multiple entities sharing owners, addresses or bank accounts each claiming separate payroll is the strongest pre-disbursement signal.
570.features_to_create: The nearest applicable control is an enrolment/payment-integrity identity module: before disbursing any program funds, cross-verify applicant-reported payroll against authoritative tax and state wage data and cluster applications by owner SSN/EIN, address, phone and bank account, holding funds where a cluster claims duplicative payroll. For payer systems, apply the same clustering to provider enrolment applications so related shell entities are scored as one; otherwise no payer-side claims control applies.

571.ways_to_identify: This is device-manufacturer/FDA misbranding, not claims fraud, so a payer would not catch it at adjudication; the detectable payer-side signal is post-payment analytic — an implausible shift in result distributions from labs using LeadCare devices, i.e. venous lead results clustering below the reference threshold versus capillary results and versus labs on other platforms. Complaint/recall feeds (FDA MedWatch, MAUDE, Class I recalls) and the manufacturer's own customer-complaint volume are the earliest external signals.
571.features_to_create: Build a device/assay-level result-distribution monitor where lab results are reported (state lead registries, HEDIS/lab-result feeds): per test platform and specimen type, compute mean and percent-elevated rates and alert when a platform diverges from all others, triggering payer notification and re-test coverage. Add an automated FDA recall/MAUDE ingestion that flags claims for tests or devices under active recall and suspends payment for the affected device/specimen-type combinations.

572.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic as the companion case: concealment from FDA and customers about a venous-sample defect is outside claim adjudication, so a payer could only detect it post-payment by comparing lead-result distributions across testing platforms and specimen types, where the defective analyzer produces anomalously low venous results. Recall and adverse-event feeds plus state childhood-lead registry data provide the external trigger.
572.features_to_create: Build a platform-stratified result-distribution surveillance job over reported lead results (percent elevated by device model and specimen type, by lab, over time) that alerts on a single platform diverging from peers and triggers member re-test outreach and recovery from the manufacturer. Ingest FDA recall/MAUDE feeds nightly and auto-flag claim lines for recalled device/test combinations for payment hold and coverage-policy update.

573.ways_to_identify: The prescriptions are forged against real member IDs, so adjudication-time signals are strong: fills for members with no prior relationship to the prescriber, fills at pharmacies far outside the member's home region and scattered across multiple states, high-value drug fills clustered on the same prescriber or same courier pickup, and pickups not by the member. Non-emergency transport claims billed for the same dates and members with no accompanying medical visit at the destination is a second, independent prepay flag.
573.features_to_create: Build a member-level geographic-plausibility edit for pharmacy claims: compute distance from member address to dispensing pharmacy and to prescriber, count distinct states of fill in a rolling window, and prepay-reject or hold fills exceeding the calibrated dispersion with a member-contact verification requirement. Build a transport-to-service linkage edit that denies NEMT/rideshare claims lacking a matching same-day covered service claim at the destination provider, and cluster pharmacy fills by pickup-agent/delivery pattern for investigation referral.

574.ways_to_identify: This is vendor-procurement self-dealing and kickbacks inside a grantee organization, not claim submission, so payer claim edits would not see it; detection sits with grant/cost-report oversight and vendor-payment auditing — comparing the intermediary's invoices to underlying vendor invoices for markup, and matching officer/manager names and home addresses against vendor corporate filings and bank signatories. Payments to a vendor with no employees, no other customers, and an owner who is also an executive of the payer organization are the auditable signal, plus a contract returning 50% of fees to an executive-controlled entity.
574.features_to_create: Build a related-party procurement check for organizations submitting cost reports or receiving grant/FQHC funds: match vendor EINs, registered agents, officers and addresses against employee/officer rosters and disclosed ownership, and flag any vendor payment stream to a matched entity for mandatory conflict-of-interest documentation before cost reimbursement. Add an invoice-markup test comparing intermediary invoices to third-party vendor invoices for the same work and a no-substance vendor test (no payroll filings, single customer), each triggering payment hold and audit referral.

575.ways_to_identify: Phantom private-duty nursing and personal care hours are catchable prepay through EVV: claims with no matching electronic visit verification record, visits with identical start/stop times, hours exceeding the authorized plan of care, and caregiver-day totals exceeding feasible working hours across overlapping members. Pre-signed blank notes surface when requested documentation shows identical handwriting/signature blocks, notes completed by staff who have no EVV check-in, and guardians receiving cash — the latter only via post-payment interview, but the hour arithmetic is prepay.
575.features_to_create: Build an EVV-to-claim reconciliation edit that denies or holds any PDN/personal-care/respite line without a matching verified visit at the member's address, and a caregiver-day aggregator that flags overlapping or over-24-hour totals per employee across members. Add an authorization-versus-billed-hours edit per member-month and a documentation request/prepay review for agencies whose share of unverified or authorization-exceeding units is above the calibrated peer percentile.

576.ways_to_identify: Enrolment screening should have caught the straw officer: verify the disclosed President/CEO against tax filings, bank signatories, lease and corporate records, and interview/site-visit new high-risk DME suppliers, while linking the hidden true owner through shared addresses, phone numbers and payment flows. At adjudication the scheme shows as a new supplier billing braces/DME nationwide to beneficiaries with no prior treating relationship to the ordering prescriber, high denial-then-resubmission rates on the same claims, and money movement to an unrelated shell (Sharp Ventures) visible in payment-address changes.
576.features_to_create: Build an enrolment verification module that cross-matches disclosed owners/officers to IRS, banking and corporate-filing data and requires in-person verification for new DME suppliers, auto-holding billing privileges on mismatch. Build a claim-behavior monitor per supplier: beneficiary geographic dispersion, share of orders from prescribers with no prior same-item history or no prior member encounter, and resubmission-after-denial ratio; above-percentile suppliers go to 100% prepay review requiring signed physician orders, proof of delivery and beneficiary confirmation, and any payment-address/EFT change triggers re-verification.

577.ways_to_identify: Billing for drugs never stocked is provable prepay by reconciling billed NDC units against the pharmacy's wholesaler purchase data — a pharmacy cannot dispense what it never bought. Additional adjudication signals: nearly all claims tied to one claimant population (FECA/USPS injured workers) via a small set of prescribers, high-cost compounds and topicals per claimant, and no valid prescription on file when records are requested.
577.features_to_create: Build an NDC-level purchase-to-dispense reconciliation per pharmacy per month using wholesaler/ARCOS or 340B purchase feeds; when billed units exceed purchases beyond a calibrated tolerance, suspend payment for those NDCs and require invoices. Add a concentration edit (share of revenue from a single payer/claimant cohort and single prescriber, average cost per claimant versus peer pharmacies) that routes outlier pharmacies to prepay review with mandatory prescription-image submission.

578.ways_to_identify: The prescriber-patient relationship gap is visible at adjudication: high-cost compounded prescriptions written by a family-practice physician for members who have no prior or subsequent office-visit claims with him, all originating from one marketer, with per-prescription cost and refill counts far above peer norms. Concentration of one prescriber's compound scripts at a single compounding pharmacy, plus long automatic refill chains without any interval visit, are prepay flags; the physician's false audit attestation is caught by comparing his claim history to the scripts and by requesting chart notes.
578.features_to_create: Build a compounded-drug prior-authorization edit requiring an office-visit claim between the prescriber and member within the lookback period and denying refills beyond the calibrated count without a documented re-evaluation. Add a prescriber-pharmacy concentration model (share of a prescriber's high-cost compound scripts flowing to one pharmacy, average allowed per script versus specialty peers, share of members outside the prescriber's normal panel) that triggers prepay hold, chart-note requests and direct prescriber attestation rather than a pharmacy-mediated audit response.

579.ways_to_identify: Unbundling is a pure adjudication-time catch: the component CPT codes of a defined respiratory or UTI PCR panel billed on the same date for the same member should be recoded to the panel code, and providers whose component-to-panel billing ratio diverges from same-specialty peers are identifiable in claim history. Medical necessity is testable prepay from diagnosis linkage — large multiplex panels ordered on members whose only documented presentation is COVID-19 symptoms, or reflex panels ordered on nearly every urgent-care visit.
579.features_to_create: Build a panel-rebundling edit that groups component molecular CPT codes by member-date-provider and, when the count of components meets the panel definition, reprices to the single panel code and denies the excess lines. Add a utilization/necessity edit limiting large multiplex respiratory or UTI panels to claims with qualifying diagnoses and no prior same-panel test within the calibrated interval, plus a provider-level monitor of panel-per-visit rate versus urgent-care peers that triggers prepay documentation review.

580.ways_to_identify: Panel unbundling is visible at adjudication: the same claim or same-day claims for one patient carry the individual PCR component CPT codes whose combination equals a defined respiratory or UTI panel code, and the aggregate allowed amount exceeds the panel rate. Reimbursement-per-encounter for respiratory/UTI testing at this urgent care would sit far above same-specialty peers, and diagnosis linkage (COVID-19 symptoms only) fails to support a multi-pathogen or comprehensive UTI panel.
580.features_to_create: Build a claim-family rebundling edit: group all molecular pathogen component codes for the same beneficiary, DOS and TIN, and if the count of components meets the panel-definition threshold, deny/reprice the components to the single panel code prepay. Add a medical-necessity edit that flags panel-tier codes where the only supporting diagnosis is a single-pathogen or generic symptom code, and a provider-level outlier report on components-per-specimen versus urgent care peers triggering documentation request.

581.ways_to_identify: This is a Medicare Advantage enrolment-integrity and data-misuse scheme, detectable in CMS enrolment transaction data rather than claims: bursts of enrolment submissions from one plan/agent ID in a single day, enrolments with no recorded scope-of-appointment or call recording, and beneficiaries whose applications originate from pharmacy-sourced data rather than beneficiary contact. Rapid disenrolment/complaint (CTM) rates and enrolments clustered by the same pharmacy referral source are the strongest pre-payment signals; kickbacks per referral show as per-enrolment payments in the plan's vendor ledgers.
581.features_to_create: Build an enrolment-velocity monitor at agent/plan/upstream-referral-source level: count applications per submitting user per day and per pharmacy referral code, and suspend batch submissions above the calibrated percentile pending beneficiary verification callbacks. Add an audit control matching every enrolment to an authenticated beneficiary consent artifact and flag enrolments whose beneficiary demographic data trace to pharmacy dispensing records; screen plan marketing vendor contracts for per-enrolment compensation.

582.ways_to_identify: No payer-side claims component: this is corporate income tax evasion via successor entities and diverted gross receipts, detected through IRS collection and bank-records analysis, not claim adjudication. The transferable signal is a tax-delinquent entity ceasing operations while new entities with common ownership, addresses, and assets continue the same business.
582.features_to_create: Nearest applicable control is enrolment/vendor screening: link entities by owner SSN/EIN, officers, address, phone and bank account, and flag new applicants that are successors to an entity with outstanding federal debt or revoked billing privileges, holding the application for verification. Otherwise no payer-side claims control applies.

583.ways_to_identify: Stimulant pill-mill prescribing is visible in Part D/Medicaid pharmacy data before payment: one prescriber's share of Schedule II amphetamine claims, patients per day, adult new-start ADHD volume, and average daily MME-equivalent dosing all far above same-specialty peers. Corroborating signals are patients traveling long distances, cash-pay office visits with no supporting E/M claim, and clustering of the prescriber's patients at a few pharmacies.
583.features_to_create: Build a prescriber-level controlled-substance profile computing Schedule II stimulant claim counts, distinct beneficiaries, beneficiary travel distance and share of patients with no corresponding evaluation claim; fire when multiple metrics exceed the calibrated peer percentile. Action: prepay prior authorization on that prescriber's stimulant claims plus a records request, and pharmacy-side edit denying stimulant fills with no billed office encounter in the lookback window.

584.ways_to_identify: This is unemployment-benefit adjudicator corruption and embezzlement, not medical claims, but it is a classic insider-override pattern detectable in the benefit system's audit logs before disbursement: a small set of adjudicator IDs approving claims that failed wage-verification or identity checks, approvals concentrated in a few claimant clusters, and payments routed to repeated bank accounts or addresses. Embezzlement shows as payments the adjudicator created and approved without a claimant of record.
584.features_to_create: Build adjudicator-level override analytics: for each examiner compute approval rate on claims lacking employer wage records, count of approvals sharing a bank account/address/IP, and self-created-plus-self-approved payment counts; fire above the calibrated percentile and suspend disbursement pending supervisory review. Enforce maker-checker separation so no single user can both create and approve a payment, and match every payment bank account against employee banking data.

585.ways_to_identify: Direct-to-consumer sale of counterfeit imported drugs is largely outside the claims stream, so payer detection is indirect: no NDC-level dispensing claims exist for these units, and the tell is patients with high-cost oncology drug claim histories showing therapy gaps while clinically progressing, plus specialty-drug claims for product acquired outside the legitimate supply chain. Post-payment routes are FDA/CBP import interdiction, pedigree/DSCSA verification and manufacturer serial-number checks.
585.features_to_create: Build a supply-chain provenance edit for high-cost specialty and biologic products: require the dispensing NDC plus serialized lot/pedigree data from an authorized distributor on the claim, and deny or pend claims where the product cannot be matched to an authorized trading-partner transaction record. Add member-level alerting where an oncology or specialty drug is administered with no corresponding paid dispensing claim, prompting product-source investigation.

586.ways_to_identify: The core signal is a coding impossibility: surgically implanted neurostimulator codes billed by chiropractor-owned entities and physician offices with no operating-room facility claim, no anesthesia, no surgical implant supply, and no NPI with surgical privileges. Auricular electroacupuncture devices are non-covered, so the volume of implant claims per patient and repeat 'implants' at short intervals for the same beneficiary are further prepay flags.
586.features_to_create: Build a site-of-service and specialty edit that denies implantable neurostimulator procedure/device codes when the billing/rendering provider taxonomy is not surgical, place of service is office, and no facility or anesthesia claim exists for the same beneficiary and date. Add a per-beneficiary lifetime frequency edit on implant codes and a referral-concentration report flagging physicians whose Stivax/neurostimulator referrals concentrate in one supplier, triggering documentation request and payment suspension.

587.ways_to_identify: Enrolment screening would have caught it: newly enrolled hospices with nominee foreign-national owners, shared addresses/leases, sequential bank accounts, and attending/certifying physician NPIs belonging to deceased or non-consenting doctors. At adjudication, hospice election periods with no visit records, certifying physician NPIs flagged deceased in the death master file, and beneficiaries simultaneously receiving full curative Part A/B services are all pre-payment signals.
587.features_to_create: Build enrolment-time controls: validate owner identity documents, cross-link new hospice applicants by address, phone, bank account and IP to other enrollees, and place newly enrolled hospices under prepay review with a 100% claim hold for an initial period. Add adjudication edits rejecting any claim whose certifying/attending NPI is deceased, inactive, or has never billed for that beneficiary, and flag hospice election overlapping curative treatment claims.

588.ways_to_identify: OTC COVID test-kit claims were mass-submitted for beneficiaries with no relationship to the lab, so prepay signals are stark: claim volume per lab spiking from zero to national scale within weeks, beneficiaries spread across all states with no local ordering provider, duplicate kit claims exceeding the per-beneficiary monthly benefit cap, and claims for beneficiaries with dates of death before service. Nominee foreign-national owners and shared addresses/bank accounts across labs are visible at enrolment.
588.features_to_create: Implement a hard prepay edit rejecting OTC test-kit claims that exceed the per-beneficiary period quantity cap, that post-date the beneficiary's date of death, or that duplicate another supplier's kit claim for the same period. Add new-supplier ramp-rate monitoring (billed dollars per week versus enrolment age and peer labs) with automatic payment suspension above the calibrated percentile, plus enrolment link analysis on owners, addresses, bank accounts and IPs.

589.ways_to_identify: Multiple prepay-checkable contradictions exist: the beneficial owner was an excluded/previously convicted individual operating under a pseudonym, so OIG/state exclusion and criminal-history screening against owners and managers at enrolment should have blocked participation. In claims, BCBA supervision codes billed with no same-day technician direct-service line, ABA services billed on dates the member has an inpatient hospital claim, and service hours exceeding paid staff hours in payroll are all detectable at adjudication or via targeted audit.
589.features_to_create: Build an enrolment control that screens all owners, officers and managers against exclusion lists, state fraud convictions and alias/SSN matching, and denies or revokes on match. Add prepay edits: deny supervision/direction codes lacking a paired technician service line for the same member and date; deny outpatient ABA on dates overlapping an inpatient stay; and run a rendering-staff capacity check comparing billed service hours per NPI/technician per day against a feasible maximum, pending claims above it for documentation.

590.ways_to_identify: Reimbursement-driven compounding leaves a distinctive fingerprint at adjudication: a single pharmacy's compound claims cluster on a handful of high-cost ingredient NDCs, average paid per claim far above peers, refills auto-generated without patient contact, and prescriber NPIs writing high volumes with no corresponding office-visit claims and no geographic proximity to the patients. Test claims submitted under patients' data with no prescription of record, and TRICARE/plan member complaints about unrequested creams, are further prepay flags.
590.features_to_create: Build a compound-claim edit set: flag claims whose ingredient mix matches high-margin formulas, require prior authorization for compounded topical/vitamin claims above the calibrated cost percentile, and deny where no evaluation encounter by the prescriber exists in the lookback or where prescriber-patient distance exceeds a calibrated bound. Add pharmacy-level monitoring of average paid per claim and refill-without-contact rate with payment suspension, plus beneficiary verification calls before paying first fills.

591.ways_to_identify: Telemarketing-plus-telehealth DME schemes are visible prepay: a small set of telehealth NPIs ordering braces and CGMs for thousands of beneficiaries nationwide, no prior treating relationship or associated E/M claim, orders for multiple braces per beneficiary across body regions in a short window, and CGM claims without diabetes diagnosis or insulin history. Common ownership across seven supplier NPIs sharing address, bank account and marketing vendor is detectable at enrolment.
591.features_to_create: Build an ordering-provider concentration edit: for each ordering NPI compute distinct DME beneficiaries, states, and share of orders with no prior encounter with that provider; when above calibrated peer percentiles, pend all downstream supplier claims for documentation. Add beneficiary-level edits denying multiple-brace combinations within a short window and CGM claims lacking diabetes diagnosis/insulin evidence, and link suppliers by owner/address/bank for coordinated suspension.

592.ways_to_identify: Pass-through lab billing shows as a small rural hospital's outpatient lab volume for advanced lipid/cardiovascular panels exploding beyond its inpatient census, service area population and on-site capability, with specimens originating from physicians hundreds of miles away and no corresponding hospital encounter. Referring physicians participating in the MSO 'investment returns' appear as a tight set of high-volume orderers whose lab referrals concentrate almost entirely in these two hospitals; ownership/compensation disclosures at credentialing would show the MSO interests.
592.features_to_create: Build a facility-based lab edit: for each hospital outpatient lab claim require an associated hospital encounter and a referring provider within a calibrated service radius, and pend claims where the specimen-collection site or referring provider is remote or the test is not on the facility's CLIA/capability profile. Add hospital-level ratio monitoring of outpatient advanced-lab dollars to total facility volume versus rural peers, and a referral-concentration/Stark-AKS screen flagging orderers whose volume concentrates in one facility for financial-relationship disclosure review.

593.ways_to_identify: Both parts are prepay-detectable: E/M and telephonic discussion claims from practitioners whose daily claim counts and per-beneficiary contact records are implausible and unmatched by any other claim for those beneficiaries, and thousands of brace orders signed by a practitioner with no billed encounter and no geographic relationship to the beneficiaries. High volume of orders per signing day is a direct capacity impossibility.
593.features_to_create: Build a signer-capacity check: count DME orders attributed per ordering NPI per day and the share lacking any billed encounter with that NPI in the lookback window; above the calibrated threshold, suspend downstream supplier claims and demand records. Add a prepay edit denying telehealth/telephonic E/M claims where the practitioner's same-day claim count exceeds a feasible-minutes-per-day model, and cross-check that ordering practitioners are licensed in the beneficiary's state.

594.ways_to_identify: This is procurement/insider bribery inside a VA facility, catchable in vendor-master and purchasing controls before payment: a newly created supplier onboarded by the same employee who approves its invoices, prices above federal supply schedule benchmarks, quantities exceeding surgical case volume, and employee financial-disclosure filings that omit an ownership interest in a vendor. Overbilling shows as unit-price and quantity variance against contract catalogs.
594.features_to_create: Build vendor-onboarding segregation-of-duties controls: flag any vendor whose master-file creator, requisitioner and invoice approver overlap, and require independent verification before first payment. Add invoice-line price/quantity variance edits against FSS/contract catalogs and against facility surgical case counts, and run automated matching of employee disclosure and payroll/HR identity data (names, addresses, bank accounts) against vendor ownership and payment records, holding payment on match.

595.ways_to_identify: Prescriber-credential takeover is visible prepay: e-prescribing traffic from a physician's NPI originating from new IPs/EPCS accounts, sudden appearance of high-cost HIV regimens outside the prescriber's historical drug mix and specialty, and patients with no prior claim history for that prescriber or condition. Copay-card usage patterns cluster the sham patients into a few pharmacies with abnormal HIV-drug volume, and quantities/units far exceed one-patient needs.
595.features_to_create: Build a prescriber-behavior-shift detector: per NPI, compare new claims against the prescriber's historical therapeutic-class profile, specialty, and geography, and pend claims for high-cost specialty drugs that are out-of-profile or come from a newly registered e-prescribing credential pending prescriber confirmation. Add member-level edits for first-fill high-cost HIV/oncology drugs with no supporting diagnosis or lab claim history, plus pharmacy-level monitoring of copay-card-assisted specialty volume for suspension.

596.ways_to_identify: No claim-adjudication component; this is PPE procurement fraud and price gouging, catchable in supplier vetting: the NIOSH approval number and test report submitted did not correspond to the model shipped, and the certificate could have been verified against the NIOSH Certified Equipment List before payment. Price benchmarking against prevailing market rates and the absence of any prior respirator-manufacturing history for the vendor are further pre-payment flags.
596.features_to_create: Build a procurement document-verification control: for respirator and PPE purchases, programmatically match the claimed NIOSH approval number, manufacturer and model on the certificate to the official certified-equipment database and reject mismatches before payment release. Add unit-price screening against a rolling market benchmark with escalation above the calibrated percentile, plus mandatory sample lot testing and vendor-history checks for new PPE suppliers.

597.ways_to_identify: Drug diversion into the pharmacy supply chain is detectable via pedigree and inventory reconciliation before payment: pharmacies acquiring high-cost HIV/oncology product from unregistered or newly formed 'wholesalers' whose DSCSA transaction histories cannot be traced to a manufacturer, and dispensing volumes exceeding documented purchases. On the beneficiary side, patients with repeated early fills and no corresponding lab/visit evidence indicate prescription-selling upstream.
597.features_to_create: Build an acquisition-source control: require dispensing pharmacies to report supplier DEA/wholesaler license and match every high-cost NDC dispensed against verified purchase records from licensed distributors; pend or deny claims where dispensed units exceed verified purchases or the supplier is unlicensed. Add pharmacy-level inventory reconciliation analytics and a beneficiary early-refill/no-clinical-evidence flag routing to investigation.

598.ways_to_identify: Classic pill-mill signals sit in claims and PDMP data prepay: one practice writing near-uniform oxycodone 30 mg 30-day-supply prescriptions at extreme volume, prescriptions signed on days the physician did not bill any encounter or was absent, patients traveling far and clustering at a handful of commonly owned pharmacies, and cash-plus-insurance dual billing for the same fills. Members with no chronic-pain diagnosis history and stolen-identity members with no other utilization are further flags.
598.features_to_create: Build a prescriber-pharmacy dyad monitor: compute share of a prescriber's claims that are high-dose Schedule II with identical day-supply, beneficiary travel distance, and the concentration of fills into pharmacies with common ownership; fire above the calibrated percentile and impose prepay prior authorization plus payment suspension. Add edits denying opioid fills with no billed encounter by that prescriber in the lookback window or no supporting pain diagnosis, and duplicate-fill detection across commonly owned pharmacy NPIs.

599.ways_to_identify: The same dyad pattern, plus a pharmacy-ownership network signal: roughly twenty pharmacies controlled by one pharmacist all filling identical oxycodone 30 mg 30-day scripts from a single Brooklyn practice, with beneficiaries who have no other utilization or whose identities were stolen, and prescriptions issued on dates with no billed physician encounter. Uniform quantity/day-supply, distance between prescriber and pharmacies, and purchase-versus-dispense reconciliation at the wholesaler level are all checkable before payment.
599.features_to_create: Build pharmacy-network link analysis (shared owners, pharmacist-in-charge, addresses, bank accounts, DEA order data) and aggregate controlled-substance volume across the network versus peers, suspending payment and referring for site visits above the calibrated percentile. Add prepay edits denying Schedule II opioid claims lacking a corresponding billed encounter or supporting diagnosis, flagging identical-quantity/day-supply prescribing concentration by prescriber, and requiring beneficiary verification for members with no other claims history.

600.ways_to_identify: Both mechanics are visible at adjudication: claims billed under Malik's NPI for face-to-face services (inpatient visit, ketamine infusion, in-person AWV) on dates when Malik was demonstrably absent — cross-check against travel/border data only post-pay, but prepay you can test place-of-service and modality consistency (telephone-only encounters billed as in-person E/M, no telehealth modifier/POS 02), and rendering-vs-supervising provider mismatch where a second physician's schedule shows the same time slots. Kickbacks for urine specimens show as a lab whose UDS referral volume is concentrated in a few ordering NPIs with payments disclosed nowhere, and pre-signed controlled-substance scripts appear as PDMP prescriptions issued on dates with no corresponding encounter claim for that patient.
600.features_to_create: Build a provider-day activity edit: per billing NPI per date of service, count in-person-only codes and flag when the same NPI has concurrent telehealth-origin encounters, impossible same-day multi-site activity, or a rendering provider whose claims all originate from another practice's patient panel; suspend and request appointment logs/attestation. Add a prescriber-encounter reconciliation job matching PDMP controlled-substance fills to an E/M or telehealth claim for the same patient within a window, and a lab UDS concentration monitor (share of specimens from top ordering NPIs, plus payment relationships) that triggers prepay review of that lab's UDS claims.

601.ways_to_identify: No payer claims component — this is commercial wire fraud on supplement customers using forged GMP and FDA Certificate of Free Sale documents, so no claim edit would have caught it. The applicable control is credentialing/vendor due-diligence: verify certification documents directly with the issuing auditor or FDA rather than accepting supplier-provided PDFs, and check whether the 'certifying' consultancy is beneficially owned by the audited party. Detection is otherwise post-hoc via customer or regulator complaint.
601.features_to_create: For any payer or PBM that contracts with manufacturers/suppliers, build a certificate-provenance check: every GMP/FDA certificate uploaded during vendor onboarding is validated against the issuer's registry or by direct issuer callback, and the certifying entity's ownership is screened against the vendor's own beneficial-owner list for overlap. Fire on unverifiable issuer, ownership overlap, or a document version differing from the issuer's copy, and hold contracting until resolved.

602.ways_to_identify: Hospice enrolment of non-terminal patients shows prepay as a benefit-period pattern: high share of live discharges clustered near the end of the second benefit period, patients with no hospice-appropriate diagnosis, low medication/symptom burden in prior claims history, and re-admission to a commonly-owned home health agency after discharge. Certification integrity is testable by concentration — a single nurse practitioner or two attending physicians certifying nearly all admissions, with assessment content boilerplate. Kickbacks to marketers are visible on payroll/1099 and per-patient-per-month payment structure, usually only on audit or via ownership-linkage analysis of the hospice, HHA, and marketing entities.
602.features_to_create: Build a hospice admission-integrity score at the agency level: live-discharge rate, share of discharges in months 5-7, share of discharges to a commonly-owned HHA/hospice (via ownership graph from enrolment records), and certifier concentration; agencies above the calibrated percentile go on prepay documentation review requiring the full certification and face-to-face assessment. Add a beneficiary-level edit that flags admissions where the preceding 12 months of claims show no terminal-trajectory indicators and requires the physician narrative before payment.

603.ways_to_identify: At enrolment: the ownership/managing-employee disclosures can be validated against corporate registries, bank signatories, and exclusion/criminal-history screening — a straw-owner filing plus an undisclosed prior bank fraud conviction is a prepay denial of enrolment. At adjudication: telehealth E/M claims that are systematically followed within days by high-cost hereditary cancer panels from a small set of labs, with no treating relationship (no prior or subsequent claims from that provider for the patient) and no use of results, are the signature; marketer-driven referral funnels show as beneficiaries geographically dispersed far from the telehealth entity.
603.features_to_create: Build an enrolment integrity check that resolves each applicant's disclosed owners/managers against secretary-of-state filings, bank account signatories, shared addresses/phones with previously revoked entities, and criminal/exclusion databases, and refers mismatches for revalidation before billing privileges issue. Add a prepay link edit: for each telehealth encounter that precedes a genetic test order, compute the ordering provider's rate of order-only encounters (no follow-up care) and lab concentration; above the calibrated percentile, deny or pend both the telehealth claim and the linked lab claim pending records showing a treatment relationship.

604.ways_to_identify: The prior-authorization file itself carries the fraud: PA requests asserting a cancer/breakthrough-cancer-pain diagnosis can be reconciled prepay against the beneficiary's claims history for any oncology encounter, chemotherapy, or cancer diagnosis — TIRF claims with no cancer footprint should never have paid. Prescriber-level signals: sudden step-change in Subsys volume and dose escalation after a date, non-oncologist specialty, and payments received from the manufacturer visible in Open Payments/speaker-program disclosures. Cross-referencing top-decile TIRF prescribers with manufacturer speaker-fee recipients is a prepay-actionable overlay.
604.features_to_create: Build a TIRF eligibility edit that requires an on-file cancer diagnosis and an opioid-tolerance regimen in the member's own claims/pharmacy history before paying, and auto-rejects PA assertions contradicted by claims history, routing the call center's stated diagnosis to audit. Add a prescriber monitor joining Open Payments/speaker honoraria to the prescriber's TIRF volume, dose trajectory, and specialty; prescribers in the top calibrated percentile on both payments and volume go to prepay review of all their branded-opioid claims.

605.ways_to_identify: This is an annual collections round-up, not one scheme, and the components (defense procurement fraud, PPP forgiveness fees) are largely outside claims adjudication. The one payer-relevant mechanic is the Teva co-pay foundation kickback: manufacturer funding of a 'charity' that covers copays only for that manufacturer's drug is detectable by correlating foundation grant flows with a drug's Part D volume and by seeing beneficiaries whose cost-sharing is always covered by a single disease-specific fund tied to one product. Loan-forgiveness fee fraud is a lender-side, post-payment audit matter.
605.features_to_create: Build a copay-support linkage analysis: per manufacturer and per drug, track the share of federal-program claims where third-party cost-sharing comes from a foundation the manufacturer funds, and flag single-drug or single-manufacturer disease funds for AKS review and potential claim recoupment. No prepay claim edit applies to the procurement or PPP components.

606.ways_to_identify: Stark/AKS financial-relationship cases are detectable prepay only through disclosure and referral-pattern data: the hospital's physician-compensation arrangements (directorships, service-line management, leases) can be tested for fair market value and for whether the arrangement is in writing and current, and DHS claims from physicians with a financial relationship can be flagged when the arrangement is expired or undocumented. Referral concentration — a share of the hospital's surgical volume coming from the two paid groups far above peers — is visible in claims. Otherwise the route is post-payment FCA/qui tam.
606.features_to_create: Require hospitals to submit a physician financial-arrangement register (party NPI, term dates, compensation basis, time-record requirement) and build an edit that denies or pends DHS claims referred by a physician whose arrangement is expired, missing, or lacks required time documentation. Add a referral-concentration monitor per facility-specialty pair flagging groups whose referred volume and paid compensation both exceed the calibrated peer percentile for FMV/Stark audit.

607.ways_to_identify: This is an annual collections announcement covering unrelated crop insurance, employee theft, and health care matters; there is no single scheme with an identifiable claim signature, so nothing here is catchable by a specific prepay edit. The generic payer-side route is post-payment FCA recovery and qui tam intake, which is what produced these numbers.
607.features_to_create: No case-specific control applies. Nearest applicable payer control is a recovery-pipeline capability: route qui tam allegations and OIG referrals into a case-management system that automatically pulls the named provider's claim history and places new claims on prepay review while the allegation is open.

608.ways_to_identify: No scheme is described — this is a working-group meeting and fraud-reporting announcement, so there are no claims to adjudicate and no signal to detect.
608.features_to_create: No payer-side detection control applies. The nearest useful build is an intake/triage feature: normalize hotline and multi-agency referral tips into provider identifiers and auto-attach them to the provider's risk score so future claims from tipped providers can be pended for review.

609.ways_to_identify: Amniotic/skin-substitute allograft billing is highly visible prepay: per-square-centimeter units far above wound size, application counts per beneficiary and per applying clinician per day exceeding what is clinically feasible, extreme dollar concentration in a handful of nurse practitioners, and product/HCPCS billed at a price point where a single distributor dominates. Kickbacks from the distributor to appliers appear as 1099/consulting payments, generally only post-pay, but the volume anomaly alone justifies prepay suspension. Also check whether wounds have any prior wound-care history or debridement claims supporting a graft.
609.features_to_create: Build a skin-substitute utilization edit: per rendering NPI per day, compute applications and total cm² billed, and per beneficiary compute cumulative graft cm² and application count versus documented wound size/diagnosis; pend claims above the calibrated peer percentile and require wound measurements, photographs, and the treatment plan. Add a distributor-linkage monitor tying HCPCS/product to supplier and to appliers' outside payments, and place high-velocity appliers on payment suspension pending review.

610.ways_to_identify: Speaker-program kickbacks are detectable by joining Open Payments honoraria, meal, and travel records to the same prescriber's Part D/Medicaid/TRICARE volume for the sponsor's drug: prescribers with repeat honoraria at the same venue, implausible attendee patterns, and step-change increases in branded HIV prescribing after payments are the signature. Brand-share skew — a prescriber whose HIV regimen mix is almost entirely one manufacturer's products versus same-specialty peers — is visible in pharmacy claims prepay. Full proof of intent comes post-payment via FCA/qui tam.
610.features_to_create: Build a payment-to-prescribing correlation job at prescriber-drug-quarter granularity that merges Open Payments (speaker fees, meals, travel) with claim volume and computes post-payment volume lift and manufacturer brand-share versus peers; prescribers above the calibrated percentile on both are flagged for prepay review and referral. Add a program-level test on sponsors: repeat-attendee and repeat-speaker concentration across events, triggering AKS review and potential claim taint analysis.

611.ways_to_identify: This is fully visible in the pharmacy claim: reported days-of-supply that equals the plan maximum while the metric quantity dispensed (five insulin pens) implies a longer supply is an internal inconsistency the adjudicator can compute from quantity, NDC package size, and directions. The downstream symptom is refill-too-soon: cumulative dispensed quantity per member per drug exceeding elapsed days at the prescribed daily dose. Chain-level patterns — one chain's insulin claims clustering exactly at the plan day cap — make it detectable prepay.
611.features_to_create: Build a days-supply plausibility edit: recompute expected days-of-supply from NDC unit strength, metric quantity, and sig-derived daily dose, and reject or pend any claim where reported days-of-supply is materially below the computed value or sits exactly at the plan cap while quantity implies more. Layer a cumulative-supply refill edit per member-drug (total dispensed units versus elapsed days at prescribed dose) that denies premature refills regardless of the reported days-supply field, and report chain-level clustering at the cap for audit.
