612.ways_to_identify: The tell is administrative rather than clinical: medical-directorship and service-line management payments continuing after the written agreements expired in 2016, with no time records supporting the hours paid — verifiable at contract/credentialing review of the hospital's Stark arrangement register. On the claims side, oncology referral volume from that single practice as a share of the hospital's oncology admissions, and IORT/melanoma-center service volume, can be compared to peers; DHS claims referred by a physician with an expired or undocumented compensation arrangement should be blockable. Full detection here came post-payment via qui tam.
612.features_to_create: Implement a Stark arrangement register with mandatory term dates and time-attestation requirements, and an edit that pends or denies designated health service claims where the referring physician's arrangement with the billing facility is expired, unsigned, or missing time records for the paid period. Add an annual FMV/commercial-reasonableness review trigger when compensation per arrangement plus referred DHS revenue from that physician group both exceed the calibrated peer percentile.

613.ways_to_identify: Never-dispensed prescriptions are detectable prepay/near-pay by reconciling adjudicated claims to actual pickup: claims with no corresponding dispense-completion or return-to-stock event, and members with paid fills but no refill continuity or no encounter history for the drug. Inflated AWP for compounding ingredients is detectable by benchmarking submitted ingredient prices against independent pricing sources and against other compounders' submissions for the same NDC. Lab-referral payments from a hospital CEO to physicians appear as referral concentration plus undisclosed financial arrangements.
613.features_to_create: Build a dispense-reconciliation control requiring pharmacies to transmit pickup/return-to-stock status and auto-reversing or recouping claims lacking a pickup event within the plan window, with chains above the calibrated non-pickup percentile placed on prepay review. Add an ingredient-price outlier edit comparing submitted AWP/ingredient cost per NDC against external benchmarks and peer submissions, pending claims above the outlier threshold; and a lab referral-concentration monitor tied to declared physician financial arrangements.

614.ways_to_identify: Each sub-scheme has a distinct prepay signal: nerve-block plus ultrasound-guidance pairs billed at near-100% frequency by one practice using an unapproved drug/device (no valid J-code/NDC for ozone) versus peers; Medicaid environmental-modification claims priced above subcontractor invoices, testable by requiring the underlying invoice; group-home/residential per-diem or service claims overlapping inpatient hospital, incarceration, or absence dates — a direct date-overlap edit against institutional claims and correctional/eligibility files; HBOT claims where the rendering NPI did not authorize use and patients cluster as family members sharing addresses/phones; drug diversion detectable via Pyxis dispense-versus-administration reconciliation and patient pain-response anomalies rather than claims.
614.features_to_create: Build a beneficiary-day conflict edit that denies residential/day-service and outpatient therapy claims overlapping inpatient stays, incarceration, or out-of-state periods using institutional claims and eligibility feeds. Add an NDC/device validity edit rejecting injection claims lacking an approved drug code, a fixed-pair frequency monitor (e.g., guidance always billed with the procedure) for prepay review, an NPI-consent check flagging rendering NPIs whose claims originate from an unaffiliated biller with shared-address patient clusters, and require subcontractor invoices before paying home/vehicle modification claims. For diversion, require facilities to submit automated-dispensing-cabinet-to-MAR reconciliation exception reports.

615.ways_to_identify: Not a fraud matter — this is a personnel announcement with no claims, provider, or loss, so no payer-side signal exists.

616.ways_to_identify: Chelation is covered only for documented heavy-metal toxicity, so the prepay signal is a claim for chelation infusion codes with no supporting toxicity diagnosis and, critically, no confirmatory heavy-metal laboratory result in the member's claims history. Practice-level concentration — one physician accounting for an outsized share of a payer's chelation volume, with repeated long infusion series per patient — is visible in claims and far above same-specialty peers.
616.features_to_create: Build a medical-necessity edit that pends chelation drug/infusion claims unless the member has a coded heavy-metal toxicity diagnosis and a prior qualifying lab result on file, and requires the lab report as documentation. Add a provider-volume monitor for chelation series length and patients-per-provider versus peers; providers above the calibrated percentile go on prepay documentation review of all chelation claims.

617.ways_to_identify: Not a fraud case: this is a personnel announcement of a U.S. Attorney's resignation, with no scheme, defendant, claims, or loss amount described. There is nothing for a payer to detect.

618.ways_to_identify: Purchased/duped physician orders leave fingerprints in claims: a supplier whose orders come from a small number of distant physicians who have no other treating relationship with the beneficiary, identical CMN language across patients, and braces/equipment shipped in standardized bundles. The strongest available signal here was ignored — hundreds of beneficiary complaints about orders they never requested; complaint volume per supplier NPI is a directly actionable prepay trigger. New/recently enrolled suppliers with rapid claim ramp-up add to the risk profile.
618.features_to_create: Build a supplier risk engine keyed on beneficiary complaint counts, ordering-physician concentration and geographic distance, absence of any prior encounter between ordering physician and beneficiary, and claim-velocity ramp since enrolment; crossing calibrated thresholds triggers prepay review or payment suspension. Add a per-claim edit requiring a verifiable treating-relationship encounter for the ordering NPI within the lookback window and beneficiary contact verification before paying high-value DME.

619.ways_to_identify: No health care payer is involved — this is employee travel/time reimbursement fraud against a federal contractor, so no claims edit applies. The detectable signal is internal: expense claims lacking receipts or business purpose, and claimed labor hours conflicting with travel dates, badge/access records, and project charge codes.
619.features_to_create: Not a payer control; the nearest analogue is an internal expense-and-timecard reconciliation rule that cross-checks claimed hours against travel itineraries, badge/system access logs, and receipt presence, auto-holding reimbursements with missing documentation or hour/location conflicts for supervisor and audit review.

620.ways_to_identify: Veterinary-issued Schedule II prescriptions dispensed at retail pharmacies and billed to a human plan are visible at adjudication: prescriber DEA/taxonomy is veterinary, patient name is non-human or has no eligibility/claim history, and the prescription is for human-dosage oxycodone/hydrocodone. PDMP data would show a single DEA number writing high volumes of Schedule II with no corresponding animal-owner records, and the same DEA number used from locations/prescribers other than the registrant. The self-fill (a pharmacy employee filling her own dextroamphetamine and billing Medicaid) is caught by matching claim member ID to the dispensing pharmacy's employee/owner roster; diversion from inventory is caught post-payment by dispensed-versus-purchased reconciliation.
620.features_to_create: Build a prepay edit at the pharmacy claim level that denies/pends any controlled-substance claim where the prescriber's DEA registrant business activity is veterinary, or where prescriber NPI taxonomy is absent from the human-provider registry, and a second edit where the billed member is not found in eligibility or the member's name matches an animal-name pattern or a deceased-file record. Add a prescriber-level PDMP monitor computing Schedule II MME volume and unique-patient counts per DEA number versus same-registration-type peers, firing a payment suspension and DEA referral above the calibrated percentile; add a claim-level conflict-of-interest edit when member ID appears on the billing pharmacy's employee/ownership file, and a monthly dispensed-versus-wholesaler-purchase reconciliation by NDC.

621.ways_to_identify: Exclusion screening should be run not just on the billing NPI but on all owners, officers, managing employees and indirect/beneficial owners disclosed at enrolment and revalidation, and cross-checked against corporate registry filings, bank signatory records, lease and payroll data — Hill's continued control would surface as an undisclosed managing employee matching LEIE/state exclusion lists. Common addresses, phone numbers, prior NPIs and bank accounts shared with the previously convicted entity are a strong pre-enrolment linkage signal. The phantom counseling itself is testable at adjudication: billed counseling units per rendering clinician per day and licensure/credential status of the named counselors.
621.features_to_create: Build an enrolment/revalidation feature that fuzzy-matches every disclosed and inferred associate (owner, officer, managing employee, authorized official, bank signatory, address, phone, EIN) against LEIE, state exclusion and prior-adverse-action files, plus a linkage graph that flags a new provider sharing address/phone/bank/staff with a previously excluded or terminated entity; a hit triggers enrolment denial or a payment hold pending an ownership audit. Add a claim-level edit that requires a valid, currently licensed rendering-clinician NPI on every behavioral-health/SUD counseling line and a provider-level monitor of counseling units per clinician-day and per client-day against licensure hours, firing prepay documentation requests above the calibrated percentile.

622.ways_to_identify: Annual Wellness Visit claims (G0438/G0439) are highly rule-bound and testable at adjudication: prior AWV within the preceding 12 months, presence of an initial-versus-subsequent code mismatch, IPPE overlap, and same-day billing of a problem-oriented E/M without documented distinct service. A hospital/system billing AWVs at a rate far above same-specialty peers, or with AWVs clustered on days with implausible per-provider visit counts, indicates the wellness elements (HRA, personalized prevention plan) were not actually performed. Whether the record supports the required AWV elements is only verifiable through medical-record review, so use targeted prepay documentation requests plus post-payment probe sampling with extrapolation.
622.features_to_create: Build a claim-level AWV edit set: deny when a prior AWV exists inside the 12-month window or when G0438 is billed for a beneficiary with prior AWV/IPPE history, and pend same-day AWV+E/M pairs lacking modifier and distinct diagnosis. Add a provider/TIN-level monitor computing AWV share of all visits and AWVs per rendering NPI per day versus same-specialty peers, and auto-trigger a prepay documentation request for the wellness record (HRA, prevention plan, risk factors) on a rotating sample once a provider exceeds the calibrated percentile, escalating to prepay review of all AWV lines.

623.ways_to_identify: This is an annual collections round-up spanning several unrelated matters, so there is no single mechanic; the payer-relevant threads are urgent-care/pain-management billing for services not rendered, chiropractors manufacturing disability documentation, and a physician taking telemedicine-company kickbacks to sign orders. The catchable signals at adjudication are urgent-care/pain E/M and injection volumes per provider-day versus peers, and telehealth-sourced orders where the ordering physician has no prior or subsequent treating relationship with the beneficiary and signs orders across many distant states. Disability-certification fraud sits with the disability program rather than the claims system, and is detected by cross-matching a small set of certifying chiropractors to a disproportionate share of approved claimants.
623.features_to_create: Build an ordering-physician feature that, per NPI per month, computes the count of orders/prescriptions for beneficiaries with no other claim from that physician, the geographic spread of those beneficiaries, and the concentration of orders arriving from a single telehealth vendor's roster; above the calibrated percentile, prepay-suspend the downstream DME/lab/pharmacy claims tied to that orderer and request the encounter record. Add a provider-day service-intensity monitor for urgent care and pain management (units and procedures per rendering NPI per day) firing prepay review, and a certifier-concentration report for disability/attending-physician statements that flags certifiers whose share of approved claims exceeds peers for investigative referral.

624.ways_to_identify: The release gives only an asset-sale collection against an existing settlement, so nothing is identifiable from the facts stated; the payer-side control is on the back end — tracking settled/convicted providers' assets and ownership interests so restitution is collectible, and ensuring the provider and any successor practices are flagged in enrolment. Prospectively, the practical prepay hook is that a provider under FCA settlement or corporate integrity obligations should be on a heightened-review list, and any new NPI sharing his address, staff or bank account should be linked to him.
624.features_to_create: Maintain a settled/sanctioned-provider registry that automatically places the provider's NPI/TIN on prepay review for the settlement term and links, via a shared-identifier graph (address, phone, bank account, billing agent, staff NPIs), any newly enrolling entity to that provider for enrolment scrutiny. Pair it with a debt-offset feature that withholds current-claim payments against outstanding FCA/restitution balances for the same TIN or successor entity.

625.ways_to_identify: Classic order-mill kickback pattern: a physician (here supplied through a locum-tenens staffing company) signs DME and diagnostic lab orders for beneficiaries he never treated, so the ordering NPI appears on DME/lab claims with no corresponding E/M claim, and orders cluster in remote geographies and arrive through one or two supplier/marketing entities. At adjudication the payer can see order-to-treating-relationship gaps, brace/orthosis and panel-test volume per orderer versus same-specialty peers, and identical code combinations across unrelated beneficiaries. Kickback payments themselves surface only post-payment through financial records or whistleblowers, but the billing footprint is prepay-visible.
625.features_to_create: Build an ordering-provider risk score at NPI-month level: share of ordered DME/lab claims for beneficiaries with no prior/subsequent E/M by that provider, count of distinct downstream suppliers and states, and order volume versus same-specialty peers; above the calibrated percentile, prepay-suspend affected DME/lab lines and issue documentation requests for medical necessity and the treating encounter. Add a supplier-side concentration edit that flags any DME supplier or lab whose orders concentrate on a small set of orderers or a single staffing/telehealth vendor, and route those claims to prepay review.

626.ways_to_identify: For the telehealth psychology network, the prepay signals are billed therapy units per rendering clinician per day (impossible session counts), identical session lengths/codes across members, unlicensed or non-credentialed staff behind a supervising NPI, and clusters of related corporate entities sharing addresses and billing agents. For the dental patient-recruiter scheme, the signals are Medicaid patients travelling implausible distances to one practice, sudden surges of new members from specific ZIP codes or group-home/recruiter addresses, and members sharing an address or phone with practice-affiliated recruiters. Actual kickback payments to recruiters are provable only post-payment via financial records and interviews.
626.features_to_create: Build a rendering-clinician-day capacity edit for psychotherapy codes (total timed units and distinct members per licensed NPI per day, cross-entity within the network graph) that denies or pends lines exceeding a feasible workday and validates licensure/credential status on every line. For dental, build a member-origination monitor per practice computing new-patient volume by ZIP, member-to-practice distance, and shared member address/phone clusters versus same-specialty peers, firing prepay review plus a marketing/transportation-arrangement disclosure request when concentration exceeds the calibrated percentile.

627.ways_to_identify: The release is a collections recap and gives no billing detail, but the mechanic — paying kickbacks that induce claims to TRICARE, VA, DOL-OWCP and Medicare — leaves the standard cross-payer footprint: the same beneficiaries and the same small set of prescribers/marketers generating high-margin items across multiple federal programs simultaneously. Because DOL/VA/TRICARE adjudicate separately, the signal is best seen by cross-program matching of beneficiary+prescriber+product combinations. Kickback payments themselves require post-payment financial investigation.
627.features_to_create: Build a cross-program matching job keyed on beneficiary ID (SSN hash) and ordering NPI that flags beneficiaries with concurrent high-cost DME/compound/lab claims in two or more of Medicare, TRICARE, VA and DOL-OWCP within a short window, and prescribers appearing in that pattern above the calibrated percentile; fire prepay suspension and a medical-necessity documentation request. Add a marketer-entity linkage feature (shared phone, address, bank account, billing agent between suppliers and telemarketing firms) to place linked suppliers on prepay review.

628.ways_to_identify: Insider misuse of patient identifiers to generate billings shows up as claims for members whose only recent utilization comes from one provider or billing agent, with members who never appear at the location, plus a spike in new-member claims traceable to the employee's access account. Access-log analytics (which staff account viewed which member records, versus which members were subsequently billed) is the discriminating data, and it lives with the provider/plan rather than the claim, so combine it with beneficiary-verification mailings and EOB/explanation-of-benefits response rates. Concealment of proceeds is post-payment; asset-tracing follows conviction.
628.features_to_create: Build a beneficiary-verification loop: for provider-month cohorts of newly billed members with no prior relationship to the provider, sample and mail/IVR service-verification notices and treat non-response plus beneficiary denial as a trigger for prepay suspension of that provider's claims. Add an identity-integrity edit flagging claims where member demographics conflict with service location distance, where many members share a contact phone/address, or where a member's identifiers were recently accessed by a staff account under investigation, and require documentation before payment.

629.ways_to_identify: This is an annual district collections announcement with no health care claims component: the underlying matters are a cybersecurity-testing FCA settlement on a rental-assistance website, estate theft, and lender fraud. No claims-adjudication signal exists. The nearest applicable federal control is contract/grant oversight — verifying that contractually required deliverables (here, security testing artifacts) were actually performed before invoices are paid.
629.features_to_create: No payer-side claims control applies; instead build an invoice-to-deliverable verification gate for federally funded contracts that withholds payment on any invoice line tied to a required test/certification until the artifact (penetration-test report, attestation, scan output) is uploaded and validated. Add contractor-level flags for repeated missing-deliverable invoices to trigger audit.

630.ways_to_identify: Grossly substandard SNF care is measurable pre-payment by joining payroll-based staffing data to daily census: nurse and aide hours per resident-day falling below required minimums on many days, in the same periods the facility bills full skilled per-diems. Corroborating claim-side signals include facility-acquired UTI, pressure-ulcer and fall-related diagnoses and transfers appearing on resident claims at rates above same-size peers, plus survey deficiency history and high staff turnover. The quality failure is detectable from the payer's own PBJ, MDS, survey and claims data before per-diem payment cycles close.
630.features_to_create: Build a facility-day feature joining payroll-based journal hours to census to compute HPRD by discipline, and a facility-month rate of resident harm indicators (UTI, stage 2+ pressure ulcer, fall with injury, weight loss, dehydration transfers) risk-adjusted against same-size peers; fire when HPRD is below the required minimum on a sustained share of days or harm rates exceed the calibrated percentile. Action: place the facility on prepay review with medical-record/MDS documentation requests for the affected stays, notify the survey agency, and condition continued payment on a quality-of-care corrective plan.

631.ways_to_identify: For the D.C. Medicaid aide, the payer already holds the disproving data: EVV check-in/out GPS and timestamps show the aide away from the client's home and overlapping shifts with different clients, and the same person billing simultaneously as a personal care aide and community support worker creates same-time-different-place conflicts detectable at adjudication. For the AFLAC disability claims, the signals are forged physician statements — provider NPIs/signatures that don't match the licensing registry or that appear across many claimants from one employer — plus clusters of claimants sharing an employer, work unit and bank/address, and kickback-sized transfers between claimants.
631.features_to_create: Build an aide-level overlap edit that rejects any personal care or community-support claim line whose service interval overlaps another line by the same rendering caregiver, and a geofence edit that denies or pends lines where EVV GPS distance from the client's registered address exceeds tolerance or where EVV is missing/manually keyed above the calibrated percentile. For disability/supplemental claims, build a certifier-verification check against the state licensure and NPPES registries with automated flagging of duplicate or reused excuse-note templates, and an employer-cluster monitor that pends claims when claimants from one employer unit spike or share contact/bank identifiers pending document authentication with the treating provider.

632.ways_to_identify: Each thread has its own prepay signal: AWP-based compounding-ingredient pricing can be validated against independent acquisition-cost benchmarks and invoice audits before reimbursement; hospice claims for non-terminal patients show up as long lengths of stay, live discharges, absent decline in functional/diagnostic data and non-hospice-typical diagnoses; inflated acupuncture and oncology billing shows as units per patient-day and add-on test volumes above same-specialty peers with kickback-linked referral concentration; and controlled-substance prescribing is testable against MME/day, distance travelled and prescriber-pharmacy pair concentration. PPP false certifications are not a claims matter and are checked by matching applicant EINs against common-ownership and employee-count data.
632.features_to_create: Build (a) a drug-pricing validation feature comparing manufacturer-reported AWP/WAC for compounding ingredients to independently surveyed acquisition cost, pending claims priced above tolerance; (b) a hospice election-level monitor of length of stay, live-discharge rate, and absence of decline markers versus peers, firing a certification/medical-record request before continued-period payment; (c) provider-day unit-intensity edits for acupuncture and oncology add-ons with referral-concentration scoring; and (d) prescriber MME and prescriber-pharmacy concentration monitors triggering prepay suspension. For PPP-type programs, add an affiliation check joining applicant EINs by common ownership before disbursement.

633.ways_to_identify: Billing a physician as rendering provider while he was out of the country is directly testable: cross-check claim service dates against the provider's own absence markers — no other claims, no e-prescribing/PDMP activity, hospital privilege logs, and (post-payment) travel records — and against implausible daily volumes for one NPI when non-physician staff actually saw patients. Pill-mill prescribing shows in PDMP as high MME/day, uniform drug cocktails, short visit intervals, cash-heavy patient mix and patients travelling long distances to one clinic and a few pharmacies. Clinic-level signals include one physician's NPI attached to visits at multiple sites simultaneously.
633.features_to_create: Build a rendering-provider attribution edit that pends claims when the billed rendering NPI exceeds a feasible patient-count/units-per-day threshold, when the same NPI is billed at overlapping times across locations, or when the NPI shows a continuous multi-day service run with zero independent corroborating activity (no e-prescribe, no facility encounter) — requiring attestation and schedule/sign-in documentation before payment. Add a prescriber-level controlled-substance monitor (MME/day, same-cocktail share, patient travel distance, pharmacy concentration) that triggers prepay review of the clinic's E/M and drug claims and a PDMP/DEA referral above the calibrated percentile.

634.ways_to_identify: This is an annual district statistics release with no identified defendant, payer or scheme, so there is nothing to detect pre-payment; the only substantive payer-relevant element is the recurring category of providers paying civil penalties for Controlled Substances Act recordkeeping/dispensing violations. Those are detectable from dispensing and inventory data rather than claims narratives.
634.features_to_create: No case-specific control applies; the nearest useful build is a registrant-level dispensing-integrity monitor that reconciles billed/dispensed controlled-substance quantities to wholesaler purchase (ARCOS-style) data by NDC per pharmacy per month and flags unexplained gaps or excess for audit. Feed CSA penalty and settlement outcomes back into the provider risk registry so affected NPIs are placed on prepay controlled-substance review.

635.ways_to_identify: Not a claims-payment scheme — this is benefit eligibility fraud against DOL workers' compensation, and it is catchable by automated periodic matching of the claimant's certified dependents against the Social Security Death Master File and state vital records (spouse died 2014) and against divorce/marital-status records or IRS filing status. The augmented-rate flag persisted for a decade because dependency was self-certified and never re-verified.
635.features_to_create: Build an annual dependency-recertification job that matches every augmented-rate claimant's listed dependents (SSN/name/DOB) against the Death Master File, state marriage/divorce indices and tax filing status, and automatically suspends the augmentation and issues a verification demand on any death or marital-status mismatch. Add a rule that the augmented percentage cannot be paid without a dated recertification inside the current cycle.

636.ways_to_identify: Not a claims scheme but a loan-eligibility one, and it was detectable at application: the applying entities shared common ownership and control, and the payer/agency already holds the linkage data — Medicare/Medicaid enrolment ownership disclosures (PECOS), shared owners, officers, addresses, EINs and management companies — which aggregate to well over the employee cap. Aggregated payroll reported across affiliated entities in the same chain would also exceed the size standard.
636.features_to_create: Build a pre-disbursement affiliation check that resolves each applicant EIN into an ownership graph using provider-enrolment ownership disclosures, state corporate filings and shared address/officer/bank identifiers, sums employees and payroll across the resolved group, and blocks or holds the application when the aggregate exceeds the program size standard. Retain the same graph for forgiveness review and for Medicare/Medicaid chain-level risk scoring.

637.ways_to_identify: The disproving data is inventory: billed dispensed quantities by NDC exceeded what the pharmacy ever purchased from wholesalers, a reconciliation the payer/PBM can run monthly against wholesaler and 340B/ARCOS-style purchase reporting. Supporting prepay signals include very high per-beneficiary drug costs, refills without patient contact, high-cost NDC concentration versus same-region pharmacy peers, and beneficiaries living far from the pharmacy. Beneficiary verification letters on high-dollar fills provide independent confirmation.
637.features_to_create: Build a pharmacy-NDC-month reconciliation feature computing billed dispensed units minus verified wholesaler purchase units (plus opening inventory), flagging any negative balance and immediately suspending payment on that NDC pending invoice production. Add a prepay edit requiring purchase-invoice documentation for high-cost NDCs when a pharmacy's cost-per-beneficiary or single-NDC share exceeds same-region peer percentiles, plus sampled beneficiary receipt verification.

638.ways_to_identify: Textbook CGX swab-mill footprint visible at adjudication: high-dollar cancer genetic panels ordered for beneficiaries with no cancer diagnosis or family-history documentation, orders signed by a handful of telemedicine physicians who have no other claims for those members, beneficiaries clustered by recruitment location and spread across multiple states, and near-identical panel code combinations per member. Beneficiary inducement (cash for swabs) surfaces through complaint lines and verification calls; the marketing contracts and kickback flows require post-payment financial investigation.
638.features_to_create: Build a claim-level CGX edit that denies or pends hereditary-cancer panel claims lacking a qualifying diagnosis/family-history indicator or where the ordering NPI has no prior treating-relationship claim with the member, and cap/pend duplicate panels for the same member across labs. Add a lab-month monitor of orders-per-ordering-physician concentration, member geographic dispersion, telehealth-sourced order share and average allowed amount per test versus peers, auto-suspending payment and triggering ordering-physician attestation plus beneficiary verification when the calibrated percentile is exceeded.

639.ways_to_identify: This is an annual district collections statistic with no named defendant, payer or scheme, so nothing is detectable pre-payment from the release itself; the recurring components are FCA recoveries involving Medicare/TennCare and large Controlled Substances Act civil penalties. Detection would depend on the underlying individual matters, not on this announcement.
639.features_to_create: No case-specific control applies; the nearest applicable payer control is a feedback pipeline that ingests FCA settlements, CSA penalties and exclusions into the provider risk registry, automatically placing named NPIs/TINs and their ownership-linked affiliates on prepay review and offsetting outstanding debts against current payments. Pair with a controlled-substance dispensing reconciliation monitor for penalized registrants.

640.ways_to_identify: Inpatient rehab facility (IRF) claims carry the signals needed prepay: the admission's pre-admission screening, post-admission physician evaluation, individualized overall plan of care, and the 3-hour therapy rule are all documentation-verifiable, and case-mix group/tier assignment plus the referring physician's NPI are on the claim. A payer could rank IRFs on share of admissions with low-acuity primary diagnoses (e.g. debility, joint replacement without complications), short pre-transfer acute stays, and discharge home without ongoing therapy, and rank the certifying physician on the concentration of IRF certifications they alone sign.
640.features_to_create: Build an IRF-level and certifying-physician-level profiling job: per quarter compute share of admissions in low-acuity CMGs, mean therapy minutes documented per day, share of admissions transferred internally from the same corporate acute hospital, and readmission/discharge disposition mix, all versus same-region IRF peers. Above the calibrated percentile, place the facility and the certifying physician on prepay medical-review with mandatory submission of the pre-admission screening, post-admission evaluation and therapy logs before payment.

641.ways_to_identify: No payer-side control applies to this document: it is a press release about a U.S. Attorney's departure with no defendant, conduct period or billing mechanic. The mixture of provider types mentioned (hospitals, telemedicine, DME, physicians, therapists) reflects the office's caseload, not a single scheme.
641.features_to_create: Nearest applicable control is generic: maintain a cross-payer referral-linkage monitor that joins telehealth ordering NPIs to DME and lab billing NPIs and flags order clusters concentrated on a handful of ordering providers, feeding prepay review. Otherwise no case-specific check can be derived.

642.ways_to_identify: Not a fraud case for claims purposes: this is a resignation announcement referencing a Controlled Substances Act settlement with eBay, an EHR vendor (NextGen) recovery and defense-contractor matters. No billing scheme or claim stream is described, so nothing was detectable at adjudication.
642.features_to_create: Nearest applicable payer control is EHR-vendor exposure mapping: record the certified EHR product on attestation/claims metadata and, when a vendor is found to have induced coding behavior, run a retrospective cohort comparison of coding distributions among that vendor's users versus other vendors to target post-payment review. No prepay edit derives from this document.

643.ways_to_identify: Not a specific case: this announces the creation of a prosecutorial section, with no defendant, dates or dollars, so there is no claim stream a payer could have screened.
643.features_to_create: Nearest applicable control is standing coding-integrity surveillance: monthly provider-level E&M level distribution, unbundling (NCCI pair) rates and modifier override rates versus same-specialty peers, with above-percentile outliers routed to prepay documentation requests. No case-specific check exists.

644.ways_to_identify: This is customs duty evasion via double invoicing, not health care claims; no payer adjudication event exists. The detectable route is on the import side: comparing declared unit values on CBP entry summaries against the importer's own purchase ledgers and against industry unit-value benchmarks for the same garment HTS codes and country of origin, plus the existence of a third-party audit warning that went unremediated.
644.features_to_create: No payer-side control applies. The analogous control for a purchasing agency is a supplier price-integrity job: for each vendor and item, compare invoiced/declared unit values against contract price files and peer-vendor unit-value distributions for the same commodity code, and hold payment on entries where the same shipment appears at two different values across document sets.

645.ways_to_identify: This is detectable in plan-side data rather than claim lines: enrollment records tie each beneficiary to a broker/agent ID, and the plan's own general-ledger payments to broker organizations can be compared against regulated commission and administrative-payment caps, with excess labeled 'marketing', 'co-op advertising' or 'technology fees'. Signals include broker organizations whose per-enrollee total compensation from a plan exceeds allowable commission structures, and enrollment mix by broker showing under-representation of disability-eligible or high-risk beneficiaries versus the plan's service-area demographics.
645.features_to_create: Build a broker-compensation reconciliation: per plan-year and per broker entity, sum all payments of any label divided by net new enrollments and flag where non-commission payments exceed allowable compensation, requiring documentation of bona fide services and fair market value. Second, a broker-level enrollment-mix check computing share of disability-eligible/ESRD/high-risk-score enrollees versus service-area eligible population, firing when a broker's mix is below the calibrated percentile across multiple plans; escalate to marketing-misconduct review and payment suspension of the broker arrangement.

646.ways_to_identify: Every element is on the claims: the ordering NPI on high-cost molecular/CGx lab claims, whether that NPI has any prior or subsequent evaluative claim history with the beneficiary, and whether the telehealth visit was a brief low-level code billed the same day as the order. A payer can flag ordering physicians whose CGx orders vastly exceed their own patient panel, whose ordered tests concentrate at one or two labs, and where no result-driven follow-up service appears in the following months.
646.features_to_create: Prepay edit at the lab claim level: deny or pend high-cost genetic panels where the ordering NPI has no evaluation/management or specialty claim for that beneficiary within a lookback window, or where the only linked encounter is a brief telehealth code billed on or within days of the order. Add an ordering-provider counter — distinct beneficiaries with CGx orders per month, share of orders routed to a single lab TIN, and share lacking downstream management — and suspend the ordering NPI's lab-order authority for documentation review above the calibrated percentile.

647.ways_to_identify: The mechanic is visible in code distributions: surgical debridement CPTs versus non-surgical/active wound care codes, per rendering physician and per group, plus a near-universal Modifier 25 rate on same-day E&M with a global-period procedure. A payer can also compare the physician's specialty/credentialing record (no wound care training) with a practice consisting almost entirely of surgical debridement, and compute debridements per patient per month across nursing-home rosters, which shows scheduled targets rather than clinical need.
647.features_to_create: Provider- and group-level monthly profiling: ratio of surgical to non-surgical debridement codes, Modifier 25 append rate on E&M paired with global-period wound procedures, and debridements per resident per month, each versus same-specialty peers. Fire a prepay edit denying Modifier 25 E&M when append rate exceeds the calibrated percentile and requiring the operative note (depth, tissue removed, instrument) for surgical debridement claims; escalate group-wide when the pattern is uniform across many rendering NPIs sharing one EMR/TIN.

648.ways_to_identify: Two prepay signals: the billing agent's identity and the ordering-physician linkage. Claims from many unrelated labs sharing one billing agent's submitter ID, IP geography outside the U.S., and identical claim templates are visible at the clearinghouse layer; separately, the ordering NPIs on Selecta's genetic claims had no treating relationship with the beneficiaries, checkable against the beneficiary's own claim history and geography (patient state versus ordering physician state versus lab state).
648.features_to_create: Build a submitter/billing-agent risk profile: cluster claims by EDI submitter ID and originating IP/geolocation, compute total billed genetic-test dollars and number of distinct billing TINs per submitter, and flag submitters with concentrated high-cost CGx volume for prepay review of all downstream labs. Pair with an ordering-relationship edit that pends genetic panels where the ordering NPI has no prior claim for the beneficiary or is more than a calibrated distance from the beneficiary's residence, and suspend payments to a new-ish lab whose CGx billing ramps above the calibrated percentile within months of enrollment.

649.ways_to_identify: This is a managed-care MLR/medical-loss reporting issue, detectable at settlement rather than at claim adjudication: the state can reconcile the plan's reported 'allowed medical expense' line items back to encounter data and to provider contracts. Red flags are large lump-sum 'incentive' payments to providers with no encounter-level basis, retroactive rate increases outside the contract, payments booked in the reporting period but dated or approved after period close, and pass-through payments whose ultimate recipients are consultants or IT vendors.
649.features_to_create: Build an MLR attestation audit engine: for each plan-year, require line-item mapping of every claimed medical expense to either an encounter record or a contractually documented value-based arrangement, and flag any incentive/withhold pool whose dollars per attributed member exceed the calibrated percentile or that lacks pre-period written quality metrics. Add a backdating detector comparing general-ledger entry/approval timestamps and contract amendment execution dates to period end, and withhold surplus-refund settlement pending documentation for flagged pools.

650.ways_to_identify: Same mechanic as the companion matter: retention of Medicaid expansion surplus by relabeling administrative, consultant and technology spending as provider incentive payments. Detectable at the state's 85% minimum-spend reconciliation by tracing reported medical expenses to encounter data and to executed contracts, and by testing whether provider payments were passed through to non-provider vendors or dated after the close of the measurement period.
650.features_to_create: Implement a surplus-reconciliation control that requires encounter-level or contract-level substantiation for every dollar counted toward the minimum medical-expense floor, rejecting lump sums with no member attribution, no pre-established metric, or an amendment executed after period end. Compute per-provider incentive dollars per attributed member versus peer plans and flag above the calibrated percentile; hold the refund determination and issue a documentation request before accepting the plan's certification.

651.ways_to_identify: Staffing and assessment data expose this before per-diem claims are paid: payroll-based staffing hours per resident-day versus reported acuity, MDS-reported care needs (pressure ulcers, weight loss, feeding assistance) versus care-plan and treatment documentation, and survey/complaint history. Claims that bill full skilled nursing per-diems while nurse-hours-per-resident-day sit below the calibrated percentile and MDS shows worsening weight loss and new-onset facility-acquired wounds are the observable signal; charting-time metadata showing block-entry documentation is a second signal available on audit.
651.features_to_create: Facility-level monthly job joining payroll staffing data, MDS assessments and claims: compute nursing hours per resident-day adjusted for case mix, incidence of facility-acquired pressure ulcers and significant unplanned weight loss, and MDS-versus-claim acuity mismatch. When multiple indicators fall/rise past calibrated percentiles, place the facility on prepay review requiring individualized care plans and treatment records for a sampled census, and escalate to payment suspension where documentation contradicts staffing capacity.

653.ways_to_identify: Two adjudication-time signals: impossible-day/volume tests on time-based psychotherapy codes (summed service minutes per rendering NPI per day exceeding a plausible workday) and provider-absence evidence, which appears as claims dated when the physician has no other footprint or as service locations far from the beneficiary. Rendering-versus-supervising NPI mismatch is also checkable, since services actually delivered by other practitioners were billed under his NPI without incident-to/supervision requirements met.
653.features_to_create: Build a time-based-service accumulator: per rendering NPI per date of service, sum required minutes for all timed psychotherapy/E&M codes and fire a prepay edit when the total exceeds a plausible-day threshold or when the same NPI bills at two locations that are geographically incompatible. Add a cross-check against the practice's licensed staff roster and scheduling data via documentation request when one NPI's rendered volume exceeds the peer percentile while other practitioners at the same TIN bill almost nothing.

654.ways_to_identify: The signature is a therapy-intensity distribution piled at the highest payment tier: share of stays at the top RUG/PDPM therapy or high-acuity case-mix category, therapy minutes clustering just above tier boundaries, and uniform intensity regardless of resident diagnosis or age. Record-integrity signals are also available: EHR audit trails showing assessment fields edited by a non-clinical or out-of-scope executive, and claims submitted with service dates preceding the completion timestamp of the supporting assessment/therapy note.
654.features_to_create: Facility-level monthly profiling of top-tier therapy share, minute clustering at tier thresholds, and therapy minutes per resident-day versus same-state SNF peers; above the calibrated percentile, apply prepay review requiring therapy logs and MDS support. Add a claim-level sequencing edit that pends any SNF or MassHealth long-term-care claim whose submission predates the finalization timestamp of the required assessment, and an authorship edit flagging assessment fields signed or altered by a user whose license scope does not permit that entry.

655.ways_to_identify: Both prongs are visible in claim mix: rapid strep and influenza test volume per urgent-care visit approaching one-to-one with no supporting symptom diagnosis codes (pharyngitis, fever, ILI) on the same claim, and an E&M distribution skewed to the highest levels for a COVID-era visit population. Comparing each site's test-per-visit ratio and high-level E&M share against same-type urgent-care peers in the same period would have surfaced this before payment.
655.features_to_create: Claim-level edit: pend or deny strep/influenza rapid tests billed without a companion symptom diagnosis on the same encounter, and compute per-site test-per-encounter ratios monthly versus urgent-care peers. Separately profile each site's and clinician's high-level E&M share and time-based code use for respiratory encounters; above the calibrated percentile, route to prepay documentation request for the visit note substantiating time and complexity.

656.ways_to_identify: The release is an annual collections round-up and does not describe the billing mechanic or even the payer for the health care fraud count, and the accompanying Cleveland Clinic matter concerns federal grant applications rather than claims; there is nothing specific a payer could have screened prepay. The grant prong is detectable only through grant-office review of progress reports against effort reporting and payroll.
656.features_to_create: No case-specific payer control derives. Nearest applicable: for grant-funded entities, reconcile reported personnel effort and progress-report milestones against payroll and subaward ledgers before drawdown approval; for the health care count, standard provider-level billing-outlier profiling versus same-specialty peers.

657.ways_to_identify: No claims adjudication is involved; this is benefit eligibility fraud on annual workers' compensation self-certifications. It is catchable before each benefit continuation by matching the claimant's SSN against state wage/new-hire records, commercial-driver licensing and DOT/CDL medical certification files, and employer quarterly wage filings, all of which would show earnings and a CDL while he certified no employment.
657.features_to_create: Build a recertification cross-match: before approving each annual EN-1032 certification, run the claimant's identifiers against the National Directory of New Hires, state UI wage files, and CDL/DOT registries, and flag any earnings record or occupational license inconsistent with the certified non-work status. Firing suspends further benefit payments pending an eligibility interview and documentation request.

658.ways_to_identify: The Uninsured Program was payer-of-last-resort, so every claim should have failed an insurance check first; the fraud is visible by re-running eligibility (Medicare/Medicaid/commercial via clearinghouse 270/271 and state Medicaid eligibility files) against the beneficiary identifiers on the submitted claims. Additional signals: the provider's own intake records already contained verified insurance for many of these patients, and per-provider rates of paid-uninsured claims that later match an active coverage record are far above peers.
658.features_to_create: Prepay edit on every uninsured-program claim: automated 270/271 eligibility ping plus Medicare/Medicaid enrollment match on name, DOB and identifiers; deny if any active coverage exists on the date of service and require documented denial or non-coverage otherwise. Add a submitter-level monthly rate of retroactively-matched insured claims and, above the calibrated percentile, suspend further uninsured-program payment and require the provider's intake insurance fields to accompany each claim.

659.ways_to_identify: This is a contract-pricing overcharge, detectable at invoice adjudication by comparing each line's charged price against the awarded contract/schedule price file and any negotiated discount terms for that ordering agency. Signals include the same catalog item invoiced at different prices across federal customers, credits issued to complaining customers but no corresponding correction for identical overcharges elsewhere, and price variances that persist after a known system defect is identified.
659.features_to_create: Build a contract price-compliance edit in accounts payable: for each invoice line, join item/SKU to the active contract price file and reject or hold lines priced above the contract ceiling, including lease-schedule equivalents. Add a variance-recidivism monitor that, whenever a vendor issues a pricing credit, automatically re-prices all other federal invoices for the same SKU in the lookback window and generates a refund demand; escalate to contract review when overcharge rate exceeds the calibrated percentile.

660.ways_to_identify: The signal is order-origin concentration: thousands of braces and compounded pain cream claims across many unrelated suppliers all trace to a small set of telemedicine prescribers who have no prior treating relationship with the beneficiary, no other claims for that patient, and impossible cross-state ordering volume in a single day. At adjudication this is visible by joining the DME/pharmacy claim's ordering NPI to that NPI's own E/M claim history, beneficiary geography, and per-day order counts. Marketing origin is also visible in beneficiary complaint logs and in bilateral-brace-set combinations ordered for the same patient across multiple suppliers.
660.features_to_create: Build an ordering-prescriber surveillance job: per NPI per day, count distinct beneficiaries with DME/compound orders, share with no prior or subsequent E/M encounter by that NPI, and number of distinct states and distinct billing suppliers; fire when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers and route all downstream claims from that NPI to prepay documentation review for the face-to-face encounter. Add a beneficiary-level edit rejecting multi-joint brace sets and topical compound kits ordered by a telehealth-only prescriber within a short window, and an enrolment-side link analysis flagging suppliers sharing addresses, bank accounts or ordering platforms.

661.ways_to_identify: This is HSA/benefits-administrator account funding fraud rather than claim adjudication, but the payer-side signal is at enrolment: a newly registered employer group with no verifiable EIN wage history, 57 enrollees whose SSNs and addresses do not match the employer's state, and dozens of pre-funded debit cards mailed to a handful of common Vicksburg addresses. Card spend at gift-card and retail merchants rather than health merchant category codes is a second, near-real-time signal. Repetition with a second administrator in another state would be caught by an industry shared-fraud registry.
661.features_to_create: At group onboarding, verify the employer against state wage/UI filings and EIN registration and score the census for identity anomalies (address clustering, mismatch between enrollee state and employer state, SSN-name mismatch on eCBSV/consumer-data match); hold card issuance and funding pending verification when the score exceeds the calibrated threshold. Post-issuance, monitor MCC codes and block/suspend cards with non-qualified-merchant spend, and add cross-administrator negative-file sharing keyed to mailing address, device and bank account.

662.ways_to_identify: Balloon sinus dilation billed on the maximum number of sinuses per patient, and repeatedly staged on separate dates for the same beneficiary, stands out in claim-line counts of sinus-dilation codes per patient per year versus same-specialty ENT peers. Absence of supporting diagnosis history (documented chronic sinusitis, failed medical management) and absence of prior imaging claims in the beneficiary history is checkable at adjudication. Billing CPT 31235 alongside dilation codes at near-100% frequency is an unbundling/never-performed pattern visible in code-pair ratios.
662.features_to_create: Prepay edit: for each beneficiary, sum sinus-dilation units across all dates within a rolling year; when units reach the anatomic maximum or the same sinus is billed twice, or when there is no antecedent chronic sinusitis diagnosis plus CT/imaging claim, pend the claim for operative note and medical-management documentation. Add a provider-level ratio monitor for 31235 billed with dilation and for staged same-patient sessions, flagging outliers versus ENT peers for prepay review.

663.ways_to_identify: The kickback shows up as extreme referral concentration: a handful of ordering physicians in two states account for the bulk of one lab's volume, with per-physician test ordering far above same-specialty peers and panels ordered uniformly regardless of diagnosis. Cross-referencing CMS Open Payments and the lab's disclosed medical-director/consulting arrangements against those same physicians' referral volume exposes payments tracking referrals. Marketer commissions are visible only in the lab's books, so post-payment audit or CID is the route for that element.
663.features_to_create: Build an ordering-physician/lab dyad monitor computing each lab's share of a physician's total lab orders, the physician's rank in that lab's revenue, and growth after the first Open Payments transfer from that lab; fire when concentration and payment coincidence exceed calibrated thresholds and place the lab's claims from those NPIs on prepay medical-necessity review. At enrolment/revalidation, require attestation and disclosure of all medical-director and consulting agreements with ordering providers and reconcile against actual referral volume.

664.ways_to_identify: The mechanic is a near-invariant coding profile: excisional debridement billed at essentially every visit for every nursing-home patient, with the surgical-debridement code chosen at a rate approaching 100% of wound encounters, far above same-specialty peers, and repeated debridements on the same wound without documented improvement or wound-measurement change. Facility-level clustering (one group billing debridement for most residents of a SNF) and E/M billed with the procedure add signals. All of this is visible in claim-line code mixes and per-beneficiary longitudinal series at adjudication.
664.features_to_create: Provider-level edit: compute the excisional-versus-non-excisional debridement ratio and debridements per beneficiary per 90 days per rendering NPI and per group TIN; when both exceed the calibrated percentile versus wound-care peers, apply prepay documentation requests requiring operative note with tissue level, instrument, and wound measurements. Add a same-wound repeat-debridement counter that pends after the calibrated number of sessions absent documented size change, and a bundling edit denying E/M billed with the debridement on the same visit.

665.ways_to_identify: Because the demonstration paid a fixed amount per test, the only real evidence of delivery is shipment; claims can be matched against carrier tracking/proof-of-delivery data, and here 136,491 January claims had ship dates months later. A prepay signal is a single pharmacy billing the per-beneficiary monthly maximum for enormous numbers of beneficiaries, many out of its service area or with no other dispensing history at that pharmacy. Retention after internal acknowledgment is a 60-day overpayment issue reachable post-payment via self-disclosure and audit.
665.features_to_create: Require submission of a shipment tracking identifier on each OTC test claim and hold payment until a delivery-confirmation feed validates a ship date on or before the date of service; auto-deny when ship date postdates service date. Add pharmacy-level monitors for share of beneficiaries at the monthly cap, beneficiary-to-pharmacy distance, and share of beneficiaries with no other claims at that pharmacy, with payment suspension and full prepay review above calibrated thresholds.

666.ways_to_identify: This is SBA loan fraud with no health care claim component, so no claim-adjudication control applies. The lender-side signals were verifiable at underwriting: employee counts and payroll on the application versus IRS transcripts (Form 941/W-2/W-3) obtained by consent, and bank statements validated through direct account-data feeds rather than uploaded PDFs. Clusters of applications sharing a preparer, IP address, or identically formatted wage forms are the network signal.
666.features_to_create: No payer-side claims control applies; nearest control is an underwriting verification service that requires IRS transcript matching of reported payroll and API-based bank-account verification before disbursement, auto-declining or pending when reported payroll exceeds transcript payroll beyond tolerance. Add document-forensics and application-clustering checks (same preparer, device, IP, template metadata) that route grouped applications to manual review.

667.ways_to_identify: Usual-and-customary reporting fraud is detectable by comparing the U&C submitted on Medicaid claims for a given generic/NDC/quantity against the chain's own cash and discount-generic program prices for the same drug in the same store and period, which payers can obtain via price-list submission or secret-shopper price surveys. A prepay signal is a store's Medicaid U&C sitting well above the discount-program price and above other pharmacies' U&C for the same NDC. Full quantification typically needs post-payment audit of the pharmacy's cash transaction file.
667.features_to_create: Build a U&C reasonableness edit: for each pharmacy/NDC/quantity, compare submitted U&C to the pharmacy's registered discount-program price and to the same-chain and market median; pend or reprice to the lower amount when the submitted value exceeds the calibrated deviation. Require periodic attestation and upload of discount-program price schedules at contracting and audit-sample cash claims to validate, with recoupment of the differential.

668.ways_to_identify: Invalid-prescription red flags are computable from the payer's own pharmacy claim stream and PDMP data: early refills before the calculated days-supply exhaustion, cumulative MME above thresholds, and 'trinity' co-dispensing of an opioid, benzodiazepine and muscle relaxant, often across multiple prescribers and pharmacies. Prescriber-level concentration (one prescriber generating most of a store's controlled dispensings, long patient travel distances, cash-alongside patterns) is visible at adjudication. Store- and chain-level rates of these flags versus peers identify where volume pressure overrode review.
668.features_to_create: Prepay edits at the pharmacy claim: reject or pend refills submitted before the calibrated percentage of days supply has elapsed, pend claims that push cumulative daily MME above the calibrated level, and pend trinity combinations pending prescriber consultation documentation. Add store- and prescriber-level dashboards of flag rates and multi-prescriber/multi-pharmacy patient counts, with prepay review, PDMP cross-check requirements and referral where rates exceed peers.

669.ways_to_identify: Identical mechanic to the companion case: the payer's own claim history supports detection of early refills, high cumulative MME, and trinity combinations, and PDMP linkage shows multi-prescriber/multi-pharmacy shopping before the fill is paid. Withholding prescriber red-flag data from pharmacists is an internal control failure, but the payer can supply the missing view by feeding prescriber-level risk scores back into adjudication. Chain-level comparison of red-flag rates and fill-speed metrics per store versus peers highlights the pressure effect.
669.features_to_create: Implement controlled-substance prepay edits (early refill against calculated days supply, cumulative MME ceiling, trinity concurrency, duplicate-therapy across prescribers) that pend for documented prescriber verification rather than auto-pay. Publish a prescriber risk indicator to pharmacies at point of sale and monitor store-level red-flag override rates, escalating outlier stores to prepay review, targeted audit and corporate-integrity reporting.

670.ways_to_identify: This is embezzlement from resident patient-trust funds and stolen stimulus checks, not claim submission, so it is not detectable at claim adjudication; the payer/regulator route is patient-trust-fund audit. Observable signals include ~500 checks with a single signature pattern, cash-disbursement volume per resident far above facility norms, ledger debits without resident signature receipts, and continued insurance deductions for a cancelled policy. Bank data plus trust ledger reconciliation surfaces it.
670.features_to_create: Require facilities to submit periodic resident trust-fund reconciliations and build an audit analytic on the ledger extract: per-resident cash disbursement frequency and amount versus facility and statewide norms, checks lacking dual signature or resident acknowledgment, and deductions for terminated coverage; fire for on-site audit and license action. Enforce segregation of duties and dual authorization as a survey/condition-of-participation check at the facility level.

671.ways_to_identify: No claims were billed; this is grant-fund embezzlement, so the control sits with the grantor's financial monitoring rather than claim adjudication. Signals available pre-disbursement include cost reports and drawdown requests containing unallowable categories (appliances, travel, timeshare fees, spa charges, donations), vendor payments to consumer retailers and resorts, and expenditures authorized solely by the executive director. Single-audit findings and bank/credit-card level transaction review would surface these.
671.features_to_create: Build a grant expenditure screening rule over the grantee's general-ledger/drawdown detail: classify vendors by merchant category and flag any spend in personal-consumption categories, any single-approver transaction above the calibrated amount, and any card spend outside approved cost categories; hold the next drawdown pending documentation. Require annual independent audit submission and dual-approval attestation as a condition of continued funding.

672.ways_to_identify: Phantom NEMT trips are testable against the member's own service claims: a paid trip on a date with no corresponding methadone-clinic or medical encounter, or trips for members whose clinic dosing records show self-transport. Group-ride upcoding is detectable when a claimed group trip has only one member billed for that vehicle/time slot, or when the same vehicle is billed as group for overlapping single passengers. Kickbacks to recipients typically require post-payment interviews, though gaps between paid trips and any provider encounter give the lead.
672.features_to_create: Prepay edit: for each NEMT claim, require a matching same-day medical encounter claim or authorized standing order for the member; deny or pend when absent. Add a group-ride validator that requires two or more distinct member trip legs sharing vehicle, driver and time window before the group modifier/rate pays, plus GPS/trip-log submission and provider-level monitoring of group-ride share and trips-per-vehicle-hour feasibility.

673.ways_to_identify: Multiple independent cross-checks were available before payment: ABA claims on dates when no staff were on payroll, BCBA supervision codes billed without the paired technician session code, and service dates overlapping inpatient hospital stays visible in the same Medicaid claim history. Owner/agency licensure and rendering-staff credential status are checkable at enrolment. Provider-level billed hours per rendering staff member exceeding feasible working hours is a further adjudication-time signal.
673.features_to_create: Prepay edits: deny ABA supervision codes with no matching technician direct-service claim for the same member/date; deny any outpatient ABA claim overlapping an inpatient facility claim; require rendering-provider NPI with active credential on every line and reject unlicensed/uncredentialed renderers. Add an agency-level capacity check comparing billed service hours per rendering staff to reported payroll/roster hours, suspending payment and requesting payroll and session notes when billed hours exceed reported hours.

674.ways_to_identify: This is disability/supplemental insurance claim fraud detectable at the carrier's claim intake: multiple claimants from a single employer and single agent-of-record, doctors' statements and excuse notes with matching template text and signatures that do not match the physician's file signature or come from practices with no corresponding treatment claim. Direct provider verification (calling the NPI's office) and checking for any medical claim history for the alleged treatment would have failed. Kickbacks to the organizer are only visible post-payment through banking records among claimants.
674.features_to_create: Build a claim-cluster detector keyed to employer, policy writer/agent, and attesting physician: fire when claimant counts per employer-agent-physician triple exceed calibrated norms, and require independent verification of the physician statement (direct-to-office callback or portal attestation) before benefit payment. Add document forensics on submitted notes (signature match against verified physician signature, template/metadata duplication, sequential note numbering) and pend payment on any positive hit.

675.ways_to_identify: CCM codes are time-based, so the payer can require the reported cumulative clinical-staff minutes and compare them against the practice's own time-logged EHR data; a practice billing the code for nearly all enrolled patients every month, with total implied staff minutes exceeding available staff hours, is an adjudication-time outlier. Absence of any documented care-plan or interim contact claim/encounter in the month is a second signal. Precise per-encounter minute shortfalls generally require post-payment record review.
675.features_to_create: Build a CCM capacity edit: per TIN per month, multiply billed CCM units by the code's minimum minutes and compare with reported clinical-staff FTE minutes; fire and pend when implied minutes exceed available capacity or when the share of enrolled patients billed each month exceeds the calibrated percentile versus peers. Also require beneficiary consent and care-plan attestation on file and sample-request time logs for flagged practices.

676.ways_to_identify: The core signal is credential impersonation, catchable at enrolment and at adjudication: the rendering BCBA's certification number can be verified live against the BACB registry, and the real certificant's other billing footprint, address, and taxpayer identity would conflict with the agency's roster. Impossible service volume attributed to a single BCBA across 12 children, and a rendering NPI whose demographics do not match the agency's employment records, are visible before payment. Identity-theft confirmation comes from contacting the certificant of record.
676.features_to_create: At enrolment/revalidation and on every claim line, validate rendering-provider certification number, name, DOB and NPI against the certifying-board registry and NPPES, rejecting mismatches and pending claims where the same certificant is billed by multiple unrelated agencies. Add a per-certificant capacity monitor (billed service hours per day/week versus feasible maximum) with payment suspension and identity verification outreach to the certificant when exceeded.

677.ways_to_identify: The mechanic is add-on panel testing beyond the order: a lab where nearly every COVID-19 screening specimen also generates a high-cost respiratory pathogen panel, with panels billed for asymptomatic congregate-setting and school populations and no symptomatic diagnosis on the claim, is a clear adjudication-time outlier versus lab peers. Requisition/order documentation would not support the RPP. Duplicate billing across Medicare, the HRSA Uninsured Program and a commercial payer for the same specimen is detectable by cross-program matching on beneficiary, date and specimen.
677.features_to_create: Prepay edit: pend or deny multiplex RPP codes billed with a COVID-19 test on the same specimen/date absent a symptomatic diagnosis, and require submission of the signed requisition showing the panel was ordered. Add lab-level ratio monitors (RPP-to-COVID-test ratio, share of claims from congregate/school settings, panel rate versus lab peers) triggering payment suspension, plus a cross-payer/HRSA duplicate-claim match on beneficiary-date-specimen.

678.ways_to_identify: Skin-substitute graft claims carry size units, so the payer can compare billed graft square centimeters against the documented wound surface area and flag grafts far exceeding wound size, multiple grafts per wound, and repeat applications without wound closure progress. Overlap with an active hospice election or a terminal-diagnosis palliative population is directly visible in the same beneficiary's Medicare history and is clinically incompatible with aggressive grafting. Extreme cost concentration in one product/wholesaler across a few NP rendering NPIs, and rendering volume per NP exceeding feasible visits per day, are adjudication-time outliers; the distributor kickbacks require post-payment financial audit.
678.features_to_create: Prepay edits: deny or pend skin-substitute claims where billed graft area exceeds documented wound area beyond tolerance, where units per wound per session exceed the calibrated maximum, or where the beneficiary has an active hospice election; require photographs, wound measurements and prior conservative-care documentation. Add provider/product monitors for grafts per rendering NPI per day, applications per wound, single-manufacturer concentration and per-beneficiary allowed amounts versus wound-care peers, with prepay review and payment suspension above calibrated thresholds.
